title: Stepmother Supreme (AKA Yunchu's Vengeance)
author: Zhao Yunzi
synopsis:
[Film/TV rights already sold. Drama titled  Yunchu's Vengeance to be released 2026]

In her past life, Yun Chu assisted her husband, raised his illegitimate children, and helped the Xie family rise to prominence. In the end, it led to the entire Yun family, over a hundred lives, being executed, and she was forced to drink poison by the very child she had raised with her own hands!

As the poison seeped into her veins, she opened her eyes to find herself back at twenty years old.

A line of Xie family children stood before her, each affectionately calling her "Mother."

These very culprits who had doomed the Yun family; she would not let a single one escape!

The eldest loved studying? Then she would ruin his path to officialdom!

The second son adored martial arts? Then he would never set foot in a military camp!

The eldest daughter coveted power? Then she would be married off to a nobleman only to become a widow!

The youngest was useless? Then she would let him fend for himself!

On the path of vengeance, Yun Chu would show no mercy!

But—

"Mother!"

"You are our mother!"

Two little dumplings surrounded her, burrowing into her arms.

A man stood before her: "I raised them for four years. Now it's your turn."

chapters.title: Kneel in the Ancestral Hall
chapters.content:
A splitting headache.

Pain pierced her heart and lungs.

Yun Chu struggled to open her eyelids.

A face slowly loomed before her, Xie Shian, the eldest son of the Xie family.

The scenes before she had fainted in agony replayed in her mind: the Yun family being raided, her grandfather taking his own life, her parents thrown into prison, over a hundred members of the Yun family sentenced to execution...

All of this was the doing of the man before her.

Without a second thought, she raised her hand and slapped him hard across the face.

Xie Shian, caught off guard, stumbled and fell to the ground.

"Mother?" His face was filled with disbelief.

Yun Chu was equally stunned.

She realized that the Xie Shian before her was young and immature, with none of the imposing presence and authority he had held in his later years.

At twenty-six or twenty-seven, how could he look so young?

She looked down at her own hands, fair and smooth, without a single scar from burns.

A ridiculous thought surfaced in her mind.

Xie Shian got up from the floor and cupped his hands in respect. "What have I done wrong? Please, Mother, enlighten me."

Yun Chu's lips trembled. "How old are you this year?"

Xie Shian didn't understand why she asked, but he answered obediently, "Twelve."

Yun Chu's hand tightened into a fist.

She was only eight years older than this son of hers. So... had she returned to the year she was twenty?

Her gaze fell on Xie Shian's face. That slap had used all her strength, and his face was red and swollen.

Yet, it still couldn't erase even a fraction of the hatred in her heart.

"At twelve years old, and you still don't know what you did wrong?" She suppressed the overwhelming hatred and spoke calmly. "Go to the ancestral hall and kneel. Think carefully about where you went wrong!"

Xie Shian's eyes widened in shock.

He had been raised by her for four years. She had never laid a hand on him, let alone spoken harshly to him.

But today...

He opened his mouth to say something but met Yun Chu's terrifyingly cold gaze.

He lowered his head. "Yes."

A mother's command could not be disobeyed.

He turned and walked out.

Yun Chu wearily waved her hand.

The two maids in the room didn't dare breathe, keeping their heads down as they quietly retreated.

She sat on the edge of the bed, looking out at the courtyard. The begonia flowers by the courtyard wall were ones she had planted in her first year after marrying into the Xie family.

Thinking back on her past life, she was pitiful, laughable, and even more pathetic.

She was the legitimate eldest daughter of a general's household, born with a golden spoon in her mouth.

Her grandfather was a grand general, her father was a grand general. The Yun family was deeply loved by the people. Fearing their power might threaten the throne, her marriage had been chosen with extreme care.

Her mother had spent two years selecting, finally settling on a good match: Xie Jingyu, that year's top scholar.

The Xie family was of humble origins, so this was considered marrying beneath her station. Her family believed this match was perfect; it wouldn't draw the emperor's suspicion, nor would she be bullied by her in-laws.

After their wedding night, she became pregnant. Every day, she fantasized about what her child would look like.

But she never expected that at eight months pregnant, she would fall and suffer a miscarriage, losing the child. The physician said she would never bear children again.

Barren was one of the seven grounds for divorce, yet the Xie family not only did not divorce her but also took good care of her, giving her the respect due to a legitimate wife.

At that time, she had been deeply grateful to the Xie family.

So, when she learned that Xie Jingyu had children before their marriage, she did not dare harbor any resentment.

When Xie Jingyu suggested placing all his illegitimate children under her name, she was grateful that her husband allowed her to have a place in the Xie family.

A bitter smile appeared on Yun Chu's face.

She had died at thirty-four. By then, the Xie family had numerous descendants, a flourishing clan.

These children; she had personally raised and educated them, devoting all her heart and soul. The scars on her hands were from saving them... She, a general's daughter, had learned to be a virtuous wife, shouldering the responsibilities of a legitimate mother. She had given everything, hoping only that the children would grow up safely and bring honor to the family.

And they had.

But after the Xie family became the new power in the court, they turned their spears toward the Yun family.

The eldest son had orchestrated the Yun family's rebellion.

The second son had hidden evidence in the Yun residence.

The third son had personally handed her, the legitimate mother, the poison.

The fourth, fifth, and youngest sons... those children had watched coldly as she drank the poison.

The poison entered her body, the pain piercing her to the bone.

She had thought she was dead.

But she had returned to the year she was twenty, with Xie Shian having been by her side for four years.

If not for her schemes and paving the way, how could Xie Shian have achieved his later success? How could he have had the chance to plot against the Yun family?

In the end, it was she who had doomed the Yun family.

Yun Chu forced back her tears.

The Yun family's downfall was more than a decade away. Since she had been reborn, she would never let that happen again.

The Xie Shian who would later top the imperial examinations, enter the cabinet, and wield great power was now just a twelve-year-old child.

There was still time.

Yun Chu sorted her thoughts and slowly fell asleep.

When she awoke again, the orange light of dusk streamed through the window, as if she were in a dream.

"Madam, you're awake?"

Hearing the movement, a maid lifted the curtain and entered.

"Half an hour ago, Old Madam's maid, Zhou Mama, came by. She asked Madam to go to Anshou Hall when you wake up."

Yun Chu looked at the two maids who entered.

Of the four personal maids she had brought from the general's household to the Xie family, only Tingfeng and Tingxue had stayed by her side.

Tingyu, in the year she was pregnant, had become Xie Jingyu's concubine, Rain.

Later, Tingshuang had died in the great fire at the Xie residence while saving her, crushed by a falling beam.

Yun Chu looked at the mirror. Tingshuang was combing her hair, her face filled with worry. "Madam, Old Madam must be here about Young Master. You had him kneel in the ancestral hall, and before even a quarter of an hour had passed, Old Madam had him get up. Now she's probably here to demand an explanation."

Yun Chu smiled. "I'm a little hungry. Bring some food."

In her past life, because she was barren, she had felt guilty. Whenever Old Madam summoned her, even if she was ill, she would force herself to go.

Now that she had been reborn, if she still acted with the same caution, putting the Xie family first in everything, then what was the point of living again?

Tingshuang quickly ordered food to be brought in.

Looking at the table full of dishes, Yun Chu's appetite returned.

After eating, she changed her clothes and then went to Anshou Hall.

In her past life, Old Madam had passed away after Xie Shian entered the cabinet. The number of people who came to pay their respects had nearly worn down the threshold, her funeral was unparalleled in grandeur.

But now, Xie Jingyu was only a minor fifth-rank official, and Xie Shian was just twelve years old.

The Xie family was still just an insignificant small clan in the capital.

---

chapters.title: The Sinner of the Xie Family
chapters.content:
Anshou Hall.

Old Madam Xie sat in the seat of honor, with the cheek of Xie Shian, still red and swollen, seated below her. Around them stood a group of servant women and maids.

"Mother."

Xie Shian stood up and greeted Yun Chu.

"Shian is a good child, filial and respectful to you in every way," Old Madam began reproachfully. "How could you bear to slap his face? How could you bear to make him kneel in the ancestral hall... Look at his face, how swollen it is! The physician said it would take three days for the swelling to go down..."

"So Old Madam summoned me for this?" A strange smile appeared on Yun Chu's lips. "Shian, didn't you tell Old Madam why I punished you?"

Xie Shian lowered his head. "This son does not know."

Yun Chu's voice turned cold. "Kneeling in the ancestral hall is to make you think carefully about where you went wrong. If you haven't figured it out, then continue kneeling."

"Chu, you have always been kind and gentle. Why are you so harsh today?" Old Madam frowned. "What did Shian do?"

Yun Chu smiled.

Yes, she had been kind and gentle to the illegitimate children, generous to the concubines. She had managed the household affairs and built connections outside, supporting half of the Xie family.

But how had these people treated her all along?

Old Madam, the main wife, and Xie Jingyu, on the surface, they respected her, but in reality, they had used her to squeeze the Yun family dry.

Those illegitimate children called her "Mother," but in truth, they had never truly considered her as their mother.

So many concubines, including her own maid, Tingyu, who had become Concubine Rain, how many of them had not secretly mocked her for her inability to bear children?

This so-called kindness and generosity was the Xie family's way of controlling her, as well as her own oppression of herself.

She spoke softly, "Tingshuang, go to Qingsong Pavilion and bring Young Master's recent calligraphy and paintings."

Tingshuang accepted the order and left immediately.

Old Madam frowned. Since she was sending for calligraphy and paintings, it must be related to his studies.

Shian had been clever since he was young, excelling in his studies, and was praised by everyone. She truly couldn't think of what could be wrong in this regard.

Soon, Tingshuang returned with the calligraphy and paintings.

Yun Chu flipped through them and took out one piece of calligraphy, handing it to Xie Shian. "Read it yourself."

Xie Shian's expression had already changed. His lips pressed tightly together in a straight line. He spoke softly, "To seek the growth of a tree, one must strengthen its roots; to wish for a long flow..."

Old Madam was not some ignorant old woman. Her husband had been a scholar, her son a Jinshi, and her grandson Xie Jingyu a Zhuangyuan (top scholar). She often boasted of being from a scholarly family. After years of influence, she naturally understood that this was a memorial written hundreds of years ago by a minister to the emperor, advising the emperor to be cautious in times of peace and accumulate virtue and righteousness.

She frowned. "What's wrong with this remonstrance?"

"There's nothing wrong with the remonstrance itself," Yun Chu said coldly. "But at the end of the article, he wrote words of great disloyalty."

Old Madam snatched the paper away.

"... Emperor Yang of Sui exploited the people, and Heaven's mandate was hard to preserve. Present medicine to Your Majesty, and do not accept bribes..." Reading this, Old Madam was horrified. "Shian, what did you write this for?"

Yun Chu sneered.

In Xie Shian's study, such words could be seen everywhere, enough to show that he had great grievances against the current emperor.

That was why, after entering the cabinet, the first thing he did was to find a way to eliminate the loyal Yun family and support the prince in usurping the throne...

She had never understood how a twelve-year-old boy could harbor such resentment toward the emperor.

"Shian, do you know what the consequences would be if outsiders saw this?" Yun Chu said sternly. "You are registered under my name, which makes you the legitimate eldest son of the Xie family. Every word and action of yours represents the Xie family!"

A powerful aura suddenly radiated from her. "You denounce the current emperor as debauched and untrustworthy of his ministers..."

Xie Shian's face darkened. "I didn't—"

"This is not something you can deny with a simple 'I didn't'!" Yun Chu's expression became even more severe. "Black on white is the evidence. If someone reports this, at best, your father will be demoted; at worst, the Xie family will be imprisoned. Whether light or severe, you cannot bear it! The Xie family's ancestors for three generations have been scholars, and it was only in your father's generation that they entered the court. And with these few lines, you will waste the efforts of generations. You will become the sinner of the entire Xie family!"

She slammed the paper onto Xie Shian's face.

Old Madam sat in her chair, stunned as if struck by lightning. She truly hadn't expected the consequences to be so severe.

No wonder her usually gentle daughter-in-law had suddenly flown into a rage; it turned out Shian had indeed made a huge mistake.

Yun Chu lowered her eyelids.

This matter sounded serious, but in reality, even if it blew up, it would only result in a few months' salary deduction at most.

Moreover, her husband, Xie Jingyu, was so clever; he would have countless ways to cover this up.

Now that she had been reborn, many things needed to be carefully planned.

She spoke softly, "Since Shian was acknowledged and returned to the family, I have raised him with the utmost care. In these four years, this is the first time I have been angry, and it has already caused such a commotion with Old Madam. It seems that as a mother, I am not allowed to discipline my own child... Or perhaps, even though Shian is registered under my name, I still don't have the right to discipline him strictly? If that's the case, then I dare not keep this son."

Just now, she had been furious, but now her expression was heartbroken, as if she was deeply hurt.

Old Madam immediately panicked. "Chu, I didn't mean to blame you."

If Yun Chu didn't want Shian anymore, then Shian would be an illegitimate son. Illegitimate sons were always looked down upon and would have a hard time in officialdom.

Although he was already in the family registry, it wasn't as if Yun Chu could just disown him, but only if Yun Chu truly accepted him would the Yun family accept him.

The Yun family was a first-rank general's household, not something their fifth-rank Xie family could compare to...

Old Madam turned her head. "Shian, why are you still standing there like an idiot?"

Xie Shian walked over. "The books say, 'A strict mother raises a talented child; a kind mother raises a failure.' Mother is strict with her son, hoping he will amount to something. I failed to understand Mother's kind intentions. It was my fault. I will continue to kneel in the ancestral hall."

Yun Chu curled her lips.

From the beginning, Xie Shian had not accepted her punishment, so he had involved Old Madam.

It was only when the evidence was placed before him, when he could no longer refute it, that he lowered his head and made the choice most beneficial to himself.

This child was like Xie Jingyu, deep in thought and scheming, good at studying. Otherwise, how could he have topped the imperial examinations and entered the cabinet at such a young age?

She spoke indifferently, "Shian, don't kneel anymore. Old Madam will worry."

Old Madam was indeed worried.

After all, since the Xie family had established their household, there had never been a precedent of kneeling in the ancestral hall.

But it was a mother's duty to educate her son. If she, as the great-grandmother, interfered, wouldn't that be heartless?

She had to say against her will, "If he should kneel, then he must kneel."

"Since Old Madam has said so." Yun Chu sighed. "The spring chill is heavy. There's no need to kneel for too long. Two days should be enough."

Old Madam's eyes nearly popped out of her head.

She thought even two hours was too much, but two days? That could cost a life!

But Xie Shian had already agreed. "Yes. I will come to pay my respects to Mother again after two days."

Yun Chu's eyes were unfathomable.

Only two days...

Before her death, she had knelt for more than two months, not to plead for the Xie family to intercede for the Yun family, but to receive a cup of poisoned wine...

Leaving Anshou Hall, Tingshuang spoke worriedly, "Madam, punishing Young Master like this may cause a rift between him and Madam."

Yun Chu smiled.

Xie Shian had never been on the same side as her. Where did this talk of a rift come from?

In her past life, all her heart and soul had been devoted to them, only to be repaid with schemes and betrayal. There was no need to give her heart again.

chapters.title: The Child Stopped Breathing
chapters.content:
By the time she returned to Yushang Residence, the sky had already turned completely dark.

Lamps were lit inside the house. As soon as she stepped in, she saw a man sitting in the side hall, drinking tea.

This was Xie Jingyu, twenty-eight years old.

Years ago, when her mother had sought a marriage for her, she had secretly met Xie Jingyu. He was a graceful and accomplished top scholar, flawless in every way.

But if she had known that Xie Jingyu already had children, she would never have married into the Xie family.

She looked at the woman standing behind Xie Jingyu.

Everyone in the Xie household knew that this woman was the most capable steward by Xie Jingyu’s side. Everyone called her Mama He.

Only after the Yun family fell in her previous life did she learn that this woman was actually the birth mother of Xie Shian.

Four years ago, when Xie Jingyu had brought the three Shian siblings back to the Xie family, he had personally told her that the children’s mother was already dead.

At that time, her own child had died in infancy, and the Shian siblings had also lost their mother. Naturally, the three children were raised under her name and called her mother.

To prevent the Yun family from harboring resentment, to make the children of a concubine legitimate, and to ensure she devoted herself to raising them, she had been deceived for so many years...

"Husband."

Yun Chu called out indifferently.

After their wedding, Xie Jingyu had never entered her bedchamber again.

At first, when she was pregnant, she had been grateful for her husband’s consideration.

But as night after night, year after year passed without his presence, she gradually gave up hope and poured all her energy into the children.

If Xie Shian had single-handedly caused the downfall of the Yun family, then the tragedy of her life had begun with Xie Jingyu.

"Did my husband come because of Anguo?" Yun Chu asked with a composed expression.

She sat down at the table and said coldly, "Anguo did such a rebellious thing. Does my husband think I shouldn’t punish him?"

At these words, Xie Jingyu was somewhat shocked.

After her premature child had died, Yun Chu had lost the grandeur of a general’s daughter. She had gradually become silent and obedient.

This was the first time in four years he had felt that the former Miss Yun seemed to have come back to life.

"Of course, my lady should punish him." Seeing that Xie Jingyu remained silent, Mama He, standing behind him, spoke up. "It’s just that spring has only just begun, and the nights are still cold. The young master has a weak constitution..."

Before she could finish, she felt a cold glare.

Yun Chu’s expression was frigid: "In our Yun family, when the master speaks, if a servant interrupts, they are to be slapped."

"Mama He was only concerned about Anguo." Xie Jingyu spoke. "Anguo was indeed wrong. Kneeling in the ancestral hall for two days will make him realize the gravity of his actions. I came to ask that my lady not let the Yun family know of this matter."

He also hoped the Yun family would continue to support Anguo, so naturally, he couldn’t let Anguo’s mistakes be used against him.

"Husband, rest assured. I understand everything." Yun Chu took a sip of tea, her lips curling into a smile. "Speaking of which, I still don’t know Mama He’s real name."

Mama He lowered her head deferentially: "This servant is of low status. My humble name is unworthy of my lady’s ears."

"Are you not yet thirty, Mama He? I’ve heard you’re still unmarried." Yun Chu continued to stare at her. "I happen to have a good marriage prospect for you."

"Your servant is terrified!" Mama He bowed deeply. "My fate is poor, and I will never marry. Besides, I’m already past the age for such thoughts. I appreciate my lady’s kindness."

Xie Jingyu stood up: "I still have official business to attend to. I’ll take my leave. My lady, don’t tire yourself out."

Watching the two of them leave Yushang Residence one after the other, Yun Chu’s eyes narrowed.

She could sense that He had no intention of becoming the mistress of the household.

Any woman who bore a man’s children and tried every means to stay by his side, wouldn’t she want to become his lawful wife?

Why was this He willing to remain a servant, without a single word of complaint?

In her previous life, she had been so preoccupied with the Yun family’s affairs until her dying breath that she had never given He’s identity a second thought.

Now, with a second chance, she couldn’t afford to be so muddle-headed again.

That night, Yun Chu repeatedly recalled every event from her past life until dawn before finally falling asleep.

She even dreamed of her wedding night.

The intimacy of that night had seeped into her bones.

She also dreamed of herself during pregnancy. Unable to do embroidery, she had learned to stitch many tiger-head shoes while carrying the child.

The dream suddenly shifted.

A pool of fresh blood spread out. Around her were all kinds of voices.

"Something’s wrong! The mistress is bleeding heavily. The child is premature. Someone, come quick!"

"The young master is finally born... Why isn’t the young master crying? It’s as if he’s not breathing!"

"There’s another child in the mistress’s womb. It seems... it’s not breathing either..."

"The mistress will go into shock if she sees the stillborn children. Take them away at once!"

"No! Don’t!"

Yun Chu jolted awake.

When she was pregnant, her belly had been very large. It was only during childbirth that she learned she had been carrying twins, a boy and a girl.

But she, their birth mother, hadn’t even caught a glimpse of her own flesh and blood before the children were taken away, lifeless.

She never knew where her children were buried, not even until her death.

"Mistress, what’s wrong?"

Hearing her voice, Tingshuang rushed in. Seeing her drenched in sweat, she quickly brought water for her to wash up.

Yun Chu soaked in the bath for a long time before finally suppressing the emotions from her dream.

By then, dawn had broken.

After dressing, the people who had come to pay their morning respects had also arrived.

"Mistress."

"Mother."

Seeing her emerge, everyone stood up and bowed in unison.

Yun Chu’s gaze swept over the crowd.

Xie Jingyu was not a man of excessive desire; he had only three concubines.

Her eyes settled on one of them, Ying, her former maidservant who had come as part of her dowry. Now she was Concubine Yu in the Xie household.

Five years ago, when she was pregnant, Ying had secretly climbed into Xie Jingyu’s bed behind her back.

Her own child had died in infancy, while Ying had smoothly given birth to the Xie family’s third young master. Xie Jingyu had then placed Ying’s child under her care.

She had personally named the child Xie Shiyun.

If Xie Shian was the eldest son she had poured the most effort into, then Xie Shiyun was the apple of her eye, the child she doted on the most.

This child had healed her grief over losing her own son, pulling her out of boundless despair and giving her life purpose again.

She had truly treated Xie Shiyun as her own flesh and blood. But later...

"Mother."

Xie Shiyun buried his head in Yun Chu’s arms, clinging to her affectionately.

Yun Chu’s smile did not reach her eyes: "Yun’ge is four years old now. He should understand some rules."

Ying looked up.

The mistress had always doted on Yun’ge the most. Whenever Yun’ge acted cute, the mistress would hold him in her arms, showering him with affection.

But now, the mistress hadn’t even touched the child. There was distance and guard in her eyes.

If she hadn’t served the mistress since childhood, she wouldn’t have noticed this subtle change in emotion.

"The east side of the Xie residence has an empty courtyard. From now on, it will belong to Concubine Yu and Yun’ge." Yun Chu said with a smile.

Ying froze.

After becoming a concubine, she had always lived in the mistress’s courtyard. Yun’ge had also lived here, which was why her relationship with the mistress had been so close.

If she moved to the east side, it would be difficult to visit the mistress in the future. Would the mistress still dote on Yun’ge then?

---

chapters.title: Jujube Trees Are Hardy
chapters.content:
Yun Chu no longer looked at Ying.

Her gaze fell on the children.

The eldest daughter, Xie Pin, was thirteen years old, graceful and poised.

The eldest son, Xie Shian, was still kneeling in the ancestral hall.

The second son, Xie Shiwei, was eight years old and hadn’t come to pay respects, probably still asleep.

The three oldest children were all born to He.

The third son was Xie Shiyun.

The second daughter, Xie Yan, was born to Concubine Jiang and was only three years old.

Concubine Tao was pregnant, carrying the future fourth young master...

Yun Chu glanced at each of them before saying indifferently, "I have other matters to attend to. You may all go about your business."

After marrying into the Xie family, she had taken over the management of the household’s affairs. Thus, the old madam and the madam had exempted her from the daily morning greetings.

As soon as the people paying respects left, the Xie family’s stewardesses arrived.

The stewardesses reported matters one by one.

Yun Chu blew on her tea to cool it.

The Xie family could be considered a scholarly and farming family. After Xie Jingyu’s father passed the imperial examinations, the neighboring villages had registered their land under the Xie name to avoid taxes, earning the family a considerable amount of silver.

When Xie Jingyu entered the imperial court as an official, his father used that silver to buy some farmland and shops in the outskirts of the capital.

The annual income from those shops was about five thousand taels of silver. Most of it was used by Xie Jingyu to grease the wheels of his official career. The remaining silver was far from enough to support the extravagant lifestyle of the entire Xie household.

In her previous life, she had always felt indebted to the Xie family and wanted to do what she could.

Thus, her dowry had been gradually depleted.

By the time the Yun family met with disaster and she wanted to use silver to bribe the prison guards, her dowry had been reduced to less than a thousand taels...

"Mistress?"

Seeing that she only drank tea without speaking, the reporting stewardess felt uneasy.

Yun Chu regained her thoughts and asked indifferently, "Where were we just now?"

The stewardess hurriedly replied, "Spring has arrived. The flowers in the courtyard should be replaced. Should we plant orchids or azaleas this year?"

Yun Chu let out a soft laugh.

The Xie family was of humble origins. They still had dirt on their legs, yet they wanted to imitate the noble families of the capital, who changed flowers every season and hosted flower-viewing banquets.

Every spring, they planted orchids; every autumn, chrysanthemums. It seemed simple, but it cost a lot of silver.

For the past four or five years, she had used her own dowry to maintain the Xie family’s dignity.

But now...

She set down her teacup. "Changing flowers back and forth is nothing special. It’s too troublesome. This year, we’ll plant fruit trees instead."

The stewardess thought she had misheard. "Fruit... fruit trees?"

Yun Chu pondered for a moment. "Jujube trees are hardy and easy to care for. Let’s go with jujube trees."

The stewardess was stunned.

The ladies of the capital all loved flowers. Every spring, the various mansions competed to host flower-viewing banquets. The Xie family didn’t want to lag behind; it was a good opportunity to network.

At first, when the mistress mentioned fruit trees, she had thought it might be peach or pear trees. After all, peach blossoms and pear blossoms were also a sight to behold.

But jujube flowers were small and unattractive, hidden beneath the leaves. She had never heard of any mansion in the capital planting jujube trees.

This was unheard of!

"Anything else?" Yun Chu’s voice was very calm. "If not, you may all leave."

The stewardesses had already heard that the mistress had flown into a rage yesterday and punished the eldest young master. None of them dared to say more. They bowed their heads and retreated.

"Tingfeng, go invite Old Chen to come see me." Yun Chu ordered. "Tingshuang, Tingxue, the two of you go through my dowry. Note down what’s missing, what’s been used, and which items have been given to the Xie family members. Be thorough with every single entry."

Tingfeng quickly went outside to fetch the person.

Tingshuang hesitated. "Mistress, has something happened?"

Since yesterday, the mistress had been acting strangely. Punishing the eldest young master was justified, but then ordering Concubine Yu and the third young master to move out was odd. And now she wanted to take stock of her dowry... Something serious must have happened.

Yun Chu looked at Tingshuang.

Among the four maidservants who had come with her dowry, Tingshuang was the most intelligent and steady. But Tingshuang had died early in that great fire.

If Tingshuang had lived, with her sharpness, she might have discovered the wolf in sheep’s clothing that was Xie Shian...

Yun Chu looked at her warmly. "Nothing’s happened. Don’t overthink it. Go attend to your tasks."

Tingshuang suppressed the worry in her eyes and, along with Tingxue, headed toward the storeroom where the dowry was kept.

A quarter of an hour later, Tingfeng returned with Old Chen.

Old Chen, whose full name was Chen Defu, was also someone Yun Chu had brought into the Xie family. He was nearly fifty years old and had been specifically put in charge of her dowry.

After she took over the Xie family’s household affairs, she had also entrusted the management of the Xie family’s several shops to Chen Defu.

Her father-in-law was a scholar, not good at business. Under his management, the Xie family’s shops had only brought in a little over a thousand taels of silver per year.

Under Chen Defu’s management, the annual income had increased to four or five thousand taels.

"Greetings to the mistress." Chen Defu entered. "The mistress has urgently summoned this old servant. Is there something important?"

Yun Chu spoke. "Old Chen, do you have a small steward under you by the name of He?"

"Yes, there is one. His name is He Xu." Chen Defu looked up. "Is there a problem with this person?"

Yun Chu lowered her gaze.

In her past life, after the Yun family’s downfall, she had learned that the He Steward of the Xie family was actually He’s elder brother.

When she had knelt at the door of Xie Jingyu’s study, begging for a chance to save the Yun family, He Xu, relying on the fact that he was Xie Shian’s maternal uncle, had repeatedly harassed and insulted her...

However, she was still the legitimate wife of the Xie family, so He Xu had only dared to make verbal advances.

Tingxue and Tingfeng were just maidservants with no power to resist. They had been violated by He Xu... Later, when she had taken poison to end her life, these two maids had surely followed her in death...

Seeing Yun Chu’s ugly expression, Chen Defu realized the matter was serious.

He clenched his fists. "Mistress, just give the order!"

"Actually, there’s no need to do anything special." Yun Chu concealed the coldness in her voice. "Give him opportunities. Let him climb higher. The higher he climbs, the harder he’ll fall when the time comes."

Chen Defu was a man of the business world and naturally understood the implication. He immediately accepted the order.

Yun Chu set down her teacup and stood up. "Old Chen, take me to see my dowry shops."

In her past life, her dowry shops had been sold off one by one. The silver obtained had mostly been used for Xie Jingyu’s official career.

The seven or eight dowry estates in the capital’s outskirts had been split, half given to Xie Shian’s wife, the other half to Xie Pin as her dowry...

All of these had been carefully prepared for her by her mother, costing the Yun family most of its fortune. In the end, everything had fallen into the hands of the Xie family.

Only after experiencing the despair of the Yun family’s ruin did she realize how wonderful money was.

With a second chance at life, she not only had to guard her dowry but also make it triple, tenfold, even a hundredfold!

chapters.title: You Owe Me a Cricket
chapters.content:
The streets of the capital were bustling with activity.

Yun Chu did not take a carriage; instead, she walked through the crowded streets, watching the lively crowds. Once again, she confirmed that her rebirth was not a dream.

Chen Defu took her on a tour of the dowry shops.

There were tea shops, silk shops, rice shops, blacksmith shops... a total of eleven large and small shops.

Chen Defu managed these shops well, earning over ten thousand taels of silver each year. But it was still too little.

The Emperor feared the Yun family. Even without Xie Shian pushing from the middle, the Yun family would eventually face trouble.

She had to earn enough silver before the Yun family was in danger...

"Madam, it's raining, and it's a bit cold." Tingfeng took out a cloak and draped it over Yun Chu's shoulders. "Let's go sit in a teahouse for a while."

Yun Chu looked up at the sky.

If she remembered correctly, this year was a cold spring. It wouldn't warm up until May, and then the heat would become unbearable, lasting until October.

If one asked what business was the most profitable, it would naturally be hoarding and selling ice.

With this idea in mind, Yun Chu felt more at ease. She stepped into the teahouse, sat by the window on the second floor, and enjoyed the rain with tea and conversation.

"What? Madam, you want to do the ice business?" Chen Defu stood behind her, looking surprised. "Nobles and high-ranking officials have their own ice cellars, and other major clans start purchasing ice at this time of year. But this spring is so cold, and summer definitely won't be too hot. Many families have only bought a third or even a fifth of what they usually do. This business probably won't make much profit."

Yun Chu smiled. "Uncle Chen, just listen to me. Whatever ice is available in the market, we'll buy it all."

Seeing her confident expression, Chen Defu knew he couldn't persuade her.

He followed Yun Chu's words. "How much silver does Madam plan to use to buy ice?"

Yun Chu spoke. "Use all the available funds from the accounts. I will give you more silver later."

Chen Defu was shocked. "But Madam, didn't you say before that the silver in the accounts was for a great use?"

Yun Chu gave a cold laugh.

The so-called great use was because Xie Jingyu would soon attend a superior's birthday banquet, and this money was to be used to buy a birthday gift for the superior.

She would never spend a single copper on the Xie family again.

As they were speaking, a luxurious carriage stopped at the entrance of the teahouse.

Before the carriage had even come to a complete stop, the curtain was lifted, and a chubby, fair-skinned little child quickly jumped out.

The child's maids and nannies behind him couldn't keep up with their young master at all, shouting loudly, "Young Master, slow down! Be careful not to fall!"

Yun Chu's gaze fell on the child.

The child was small and thin, probably only a little over three years old, but he ran exceptionally fast, disappearing in a flash.

She withdrew her gaze and continued talking to Chen Defu.

As they talked, she suddenly felt as if something had fallen into her hair.

"Madam, don't be afraid!" Tingfeng was startled. "A cricket has jumped onto your head. Let me take it off for you!"

Yun Chu was so scared that she straightened her body.

She was the eldest daughter of a general's mansion and had been bold since childhood, fearing neither heaven nor earth, but she was terribly afraid of bugs and crickets.

Her scalp tingled, and she didn't dare to move.

"Don't touch my Jump Jump!"

A soft, sticky voice came, followed by a small cannonball crashing into Yun Chu.

She looked up in shock and saw the little young master from downstairs rushing towards her.

In the blink of an eye, he climbed onto her lap.

Then, he clapped his hands towards the top of her head.

All of this happened in an instant.

Yun Chu was caught off guard, and her body fell backward.

Instinctively, she protected the little child in her arms, and they both fell to the ground.

"Madam!"

Tingfeng was extremely regretful. Not only had she failed to stop this inexplicable child, but she had also let Madam fall in public.

She quickly helped Yun Chu to her feet and straightened her hair and clothes.

"Waaaaah, !"

The little child in luxurious clothes suddenly lay on the ground and cried loudly.

For some reason, Yun Chu's heart suddenly ached.

She lifted her skirt and squatted down, softly asking, "Where did you get hurt? Let me blow on it for you."

"You're a bad person! You're a bad person!" The little guy, with tears in his eyes, looked at her accusingly. "You squished Jump Jump to death. Waaaaah, I hate you..."

Yun Chu looked.

A cricket was squished on the ground. The little guy ignored the fluid on the body, picked up the cricket with both hands, and held it in his palm.

Yun Chu was so scared that she quickly stepped back.

"You owe me Jump Jump!" The little guy cried, glaring at her. "You have to compensate me with an identical cricket!"

Yun Chu: "..."

Had she gone out without checking the almanac? How could she encounter such a troublesome matter?

"Young Master, why are you crying?"

"Little ancestor, we told you to be careful. Did you get hurt?"

A large group of servants only now rushed upstairs, surrounding the little ancestor and asking about his well-being.

The little child cried even louder. "She... she squished my Jump Jump to death!"

The nanny, who had just been gently coaxing the young master, heard this and immediately changed her expression, glaring at Yun Chu menacingly. "Where did this blind thing come from? How dare you squish our Young Master's treasure! You..."

Before she could finish her sentence, the little young master, who had been crying fiercely, suddenly stopped.

His round, black eyes stared at her, looking displeased. "Who allowed you to scold her? Apologize!"

The nanny looked confused.

This woman had squished the young master's favorite cricket. She had only said a few words to vent for the young master, but the young master actually wanted her to apologize?

But when she met her young master's displeased gaze, she had no choice but to step forward and say, "This madam, I was rude just now. Please don't take it to heart."

Yun Chu's expression was calm. "It's fine."

Although she was the legitimate eldest daughter of a first-rank general's mansion, after marriage, her first identity was Madam Xie.

Even if she wasn't wrong, as the wife of a fifth-rank minor official, she had to lower her head in front of any noble.

She continued, "I will find an identical cricket to compensate the young master. May I ask where your residence is?"

"I live in the Pingxi Prince's Mansion." The little guy lifted his chin. "Remember, Pingxi Prince's Mansion. Once you find the cricket, send it over quickly!"

Yun Chu was stunned.

This child was actually the child of the Pingxi Prince?

The Pingxi Prince was the current Third Prince, who had once led troops to repel the enemy invaders in Xichuan, thus earning his title.

Four years ago, the Pingxi Prince suddenly had a pair of children. Despite the censure from civil and military officials, he insisted on conferring the title of heir to his son, whose mother was unknown, causing a huge uproar in the capital...

"Little ancestor, it's time to return to the mansion." The nanny whispered, "If the Prince returns and doesn't see the young master..."

The little guy's face showed fear. "Let's go, let's go! Hurry back!"

The nanny picked up the little guy in one go, and the large group of people surrounded him as they went downstairs, got into the carriage, and the carriage sped away.

"Madam, leave this matter to this old servant." Chen Defu spoke, "By tomorrow morning, I will bring a cricket for Madam to inspect."

Yun Chu nodded.

Sitting in the carriage on the way back to the mansion, she recalled the events of her previous life.

The Pingxi Prince had gone to the battlefield at the age of fifteen and was a close friend of her father. After the Yun family was convicted, the Pingxi Prince had also helped to intercede.

However, before the Yun family's case could be resolved, the Pingxi Prince was exposed for secretly storing weapons, with intentions of rebellion...

She didn't know what happened to the Pingxi Prince later because she had already died from a cup of poisoned wine...

---

chapters.title: Dowry Used for Public Expenses
chapters.content:
Yun Chu had just returned to the Xie Mansion.

Old Madam's maid, Zhou Mama, invited her to Anshou Hall.

Old Madam Xie sat in the main seat, with Xie Mansion's eldest daughter, Xie Pin, sitting to her lower left.

"You're here." Old Madam spoke calmly, "Have a seat first."

Yun Chu sat down, and Zhou Mama served tea.

She took a sip. This was the tea that the Emperor had bestowed upon the Yun family several years ago. Her mother had sent it to her, and she had respectfully presented it to Old Madam.

Old Madam had kept it for many years before finally taking it out to drink.

She put down her tea cup. "I wonder, Old Madam, what did you call me here for?"

"Chu'er, the manager of the courtyard, Li Pozi, said that this year the entire courtyard is planting jujube trees?" Old Madam asked indifferently, "Was this your idea?"

Yun Chu nodded. "I ordered it."

"Mother!" Xie Pin couldn't contain herself and spoke up, "Every spring, our family hosts a flower appreciation banquet. This year, with jujube trees planted, won't the flower appreciation banquet be impossible to hold?"

Old Madam frowned.

Thanks to the status of the legitimate daughter of a first-rank general's mansion, many noble families' madams and daughters came to join in the fun at the annual flower appreciation banquet.

For this year's flower appreciation banquet, she had prepared a lot in private. But now, without flowers, what kind of banquet could be held?

Unless they appreciated jujube blossoms, which would be a laughingstock.

But in her heart, she knew that Yun Chu was not someone who did things without a plan. She softened her tone. "Chu'er, why is this?"

"Does Old Madam know how much silver our Xie family spends every day with so many masters and servants?" Yun Chu sighed. "We spend a lot and earn little. If we don't reduce expenses soon, life will become difficult in the future. The reason I asked Li Pozi to plant jujube trees is that they are cheap and easy to maintain. In the future, we won't need to replace flowers with the seasons, which can save five or six hundred taels of silver a year. Furthermore, when the jujube trees bear fruit, we can sell them, which will be an additional income."

Old Madam looked surprised. "Our Xie family's shops have excellent business. How can it be that we earn so little?"

Xie Pin chimed in, "The Xie family's cosmetic shop is the best business in Osmanthus Alley. The shopkeeper said it earns more than a thousand taels of silver a year. How can we not even afford to plant flowers?"

"A thousand taels of silver..." Yun Chu smiled. "Sister Ping, you don't manage the household, so you don't know how expensive daily expenses are. A thousand taels of silver can't even cover the Xie family's monthly expenses. Where would there be extra money to plant flowers? If it weren't for me using my dowry to fill the gap, how could the flower appreciation banquets of the past few years have been so lively?"

Xie Pin said incredulously, "Mother used her own dowry to cover the Xie family's deficit?"

Old Madam heavily placed her tea cup down. "This is impossible. Our Xie family would never use a daughter-in-law's dowry. Chu'er, you mustn't say such things recklessly."

In their scholarly family, face was extremely important. If this matter spread, how could Jingyu maintain his position in the officialdom?

Yun Chu raised her hand. "Tingshuang, the account books."

Tingshuang quickly presented the neatly organized account books.

"This is the Xie Mansion's account book. Every month's expenses and income are clearly recorded." She had Tingshuang place the account books on the table in front of Old Madam. "Every month, expenses exceed income. I didn't mention it before because I didn't want Old Madam to worry about these trivial matters. Today, since the topic came up, it's better to clarify everything rather than be questioned."

Old Madam, influenced by her upbringing, could only understand the Four Books and Five Classics and was not very knowledgeable about business matters.

As for Xie Pin, a thirteen-year-old girl with no one to teach her, naturally knew nothing about it.

"Call An Ge." Old Madam said, "His teacher said An Ge is very good at accounting. Let him take a look at the family's account books."

Using a daughter-in-law's dowry was a very shameful matter. They couldn't just take Yun Chu's word for it.

Since they couldn't understand, they would invite someone who could.

Zhou Mama took the order and immediately went to the ancestral hall to invite someone.

Xie Shian was still kneeling in the ancestral hall and had nothing else to do, so he quickly followed.

On the way, he already understood what was going on. After arriving, he greeted his elders and quickly picked up the account books to examine them.

"Our Xie family is indeed spending more than we earn..." Xie Shian said slowly. "Last year alone, the total income was 5,600 taels of silver, but the expenses amounted to 13,000 taels of silver."

Old Madam was shocked. "How can there be such a big difference?"

Yun Chu might be lying to her, but An Ge wouldn't.

Xie Shian held the account books. "The Xie family only has income from the shops, Father's salary, and the farmstead in the suburbs of the capital. These sources of silver are not recorded in the accounts."

Old Madam didn't speak because this was the truth, and she had no way to refute it.

Tingfeng stood behind Yun Chu and muttered softly, "Master and Madam's silver should be contributed to the public accounts. Instead, it seems like only Madam's dowry as an outsider has been used for public expenses..."

Although her voice was very low, everyone present heard it clearly.

Before Old Madam could speak, Yun Chu stood up.

She walked to the center and slightly bent her knees. "Since marrying into the Xie family, whether it was serving the elders, raising the children, helping my husband build connections, or managing the various affairs of the Xie family, big or small, I have done my best without any mistakes. Now, for the sake of saving some expenses by planting jujube trees, I have to endure so many questions... Old Madam, my abilities are limited. I return this household management authority to you today."

Tingshuang stepped forward and placed the box containing the tally tokens in front of Old Madam.

Old Madam frowned.

Initially, the Xie family had only seven or eight maids and nannies, which she found easy to manage.

But now, with her grandson in office, the Xie family had grown in size and business. Managing such a large mansion with so many people was not a simple task.

"Chu'er, you're overthinking." Old Madam had various thoughts in her mind, but her face was full of kindness. She took Yun Chu's hand and spoke earnestly. "Over the past four or five years, it is because of you that our Xie family has prospered. You are the great benefactor of our Xie family. Today's matter was my mistake. I apologize to you. Please don't say such things in anger."

"Old Madam, I am not speaking in anger." Yun Chu lowered her head. "An Ge has seen the account books and should know the current state of the Xie family. If I continue to manage the household, my dowry will eventually be exhausted. Then, I would have to go back to the Yun family to ask my mother for silver. Old Madam, you wouldn't want to cause trouble for the Yun family, would you?"

Old Madam felt somewhat embarrassed.

If the Yun family found out that the Xie family had used Yun Chu's dowry, the consequences... at best, they would no longer support the Xie family; at worst, they would submit a memorial to the throne to impeach them.

The Xie family had taken three generations to reach the capital and could not afford any mistakes.

Thinking of this, Old Madam spoke. "An Ge, calculate how much dowry your mother has used over the years."

Xie Shian had someone bring an abacus. With a clatter, he quickly calculated, "A total of 21,235 taels."

Old Madam's heart ached.

But she clearly understood that, no matter how reluctant she was, this money had to be repaid.

The only thing that consoled her was that her daughter-in-law had taken good care of the children, and this money would eventually return to the Xie family.

She waved her hand, and Zhou Mama, standing behind her, took the order, went into the inner room, and brought out a thick stack of silver notes.

chapters.title: After This, It Shall Be Called Shengju
chapters.content:
Yun Chu let out a self-deprecating laugh.

In her past life, she had thought the Xie family was poor, so she had voluntarily added to her dowry, and to avoid hurting the Xie family’s pride, she had never brought it up.

But the old madam had been able to take out twenty thousand taels of silver in one go, proof enough that the Xie family had some wealth.

Now, looking back, her father-in-law was the only *juren* (scholar) for a hundred *li* around, and Xie Jingyu was the youngest *zhuangyuan* (top scholar). Though the Xie family held little influence in the capital, they were highly respected locally. With so many landowners and gentry registering their properties under the Xie name, their annual income must have been substantial.

Mama Zhou presented the silver notes.

Yun Chu took a step back and curtsied. "This silver is meant for the household’s daily expenses, so the old madam should take it back."

The old madam felt that something about her granddaughter-in-law seemed different.

Ever since Yun Chu had lost the child in her womb, she had become unusually obedient, respectful, and deferential to her elders.

This was the first time she had used the tactic of retreat to advance, trying to manipulate her.

*Manipulate?*

The moment the word crossed her mind, the old madam immediately shook her head.

Yun Chu was barren; she would never have a child of her own. So, it was only the Xie family who could control *her*.

"Chu’er, you’re making me look bad," the old madam said. "I didn’t know before. If I had, we wouldn’t have this mess today. Add this money back to your dowry list. Later, I’ll have Mama Zhou put all the income from your father-in-law’s estate into the household accounts. From now on, if you need money, come to me. Don’t use your own private funds anymore. Understood?"

Yun Chu turned and took the old madam’s hand, her face filled with emotion. "As expected, the old madam still dotes on me. Earlier, my mother asked about a hundred-*li* peony screen in my dowry. I was still thinking of an excuse to brush her off. Now, with this silver, I can just buy a similar one…"

Hearing this, the old madam broke out in a cold sweat.

Fortunately, she had generously returned the silver. If Lady Yun had grown suspicious and come to the Xie household herself, the truth would have been impossible to hide.

"Good child…" The old madam patted Yun Chu’s hand. "With the Xie family in your hands, I can rest easy. You’ve worked hard."

Yun Chu hesitated before speaking. "Normally, I handle the household affairs alone, so it’s only natural that the old madam has some doubts. How about this, Baojie is grown now and will soon be looking for a marriage match. Let her help me manage the household."

Old Madam Xie did not respond immediately. If she agreed too quickly, it would seem as if she didn’t trust Yun Chu.

Mama Zhou, who was attending at the side, spoke up for her. "The eldest miss will be the mistress of another household someday. She needs to learn these things."

The old madam took a sip of tea before saying, "Baojie, what do *you* think?"

Xie Baojie smiled. "I’m willing to learn!"

Her mother managed the Xie household so well; if she could learn her mother’s skills, marrying into a high-ranking family would be much easier.

Yun Chu smiled. "Tomorrow after you pay your respects, stay at Yushengju and learn from me."

After settling the matter, she rose to take her leave.

Tingshuang held the steward’s tally and a stack of silver notes, following behind her.

The old madam sighed. She had called Yun Chu over to reprimand her, but in the end, *she* was the one who had lost over twenty thousand taels of silver.

Xie Shian’s gaze darkened. He truly felt that his mother had changed…

Yun Chu slowly walked back to Yushengju.

As she reached the courtyard gate, she saw several maids gathered there.

It turned out that the first character of the plaque above the courtyard gate, *Yu* (玉), was missing a dot, and the maids and servants were trying to fix it.

"Madam, it’s strange that Yushengju has turned into Wangshengju," Tingxue said. "Shouldn’t we ask the master to rewrite the plaque?"

Yun Chu looked up at the three characters.

This courtyard had existed even before she married into the family. Originally, Xie Jingyu had lived here alone, but after she moved in, he had relocated to the neighboring courtyard.

She spoke. "We won’t use *Yu* anymore. From now on, it shall be called Shengju."

The maids and servants exchanged glances, each seeing disbelief in the other’s eyes.

The *Yu* in Yushengju was a character from the master’s name. Was it really alright to remove it just like that?

Tingshuang coldly remarked, "Didn’t you hear Madam’s words? What are you still standing around for?"

The group quickly fetched ladders and tools to get to work.

As soon as Yun Chu sat down, a servant from her mother-in-law Yuan’s courtyard arrived with two thousand taels of silver. "Madam has been managing both the inner and outer affairs of the Xie family. The mistress knows this, so she sent this old servant with silver for Madam to buy some jewelry or fine fabric you like."

Yun Chu pressed her lips together.

After she had married in, her mother-in-law, who had been bedridden for over a decade, had suddenly recovered.

So her mother-in-law had always believed that she brought good fortune.

Her mother-in-law did have a bit of genuine care for her.

But that bit of care had vanished after the fall of the Yun family…

Yun Chu gathered all the silver together and handed it to Tingshuang. "Take this to Old Chen. Tell him to buy as much ice as he can. If the silver isn’t enough, he can borrow from the money shop."

Tingshuang left under the cover of night.

That night, Yun Chu slept fairly well.

She woke before dawn, dressed, and went out. Xie Shian was already waiting in the side hall to pay his respects.

Seeing her emerge, he quickly stood. "Mother."

Yun Chu asked gently, "Have you eaten?"

Xie Shian shook his head. "After leaving the ancestral hall, I came straight here. These past few days, I’ve come to understand many things. Thank you for your teachings and punishment, Mother."

"Understanding is good." Yun Chu smiled. "Sit down and have a meal with me."

Xie Shian subtly let out a breath.

His mother still treated him with the same kindness as before. It seemed he had overthought things.

Halfway through the meal, Yun Chu set down her chopsticks and said, "Yesterday, I read a story. Would you like to hear it?"

Xie Shian also set down his chopsticks, assuming an attentive posture.

In the past, Yun Chu had occasionally shared interesting stories from the court or battlefield with him, so this sudden offer of a story didn’t strike him as odd.

Yun Chu began slowly, "There was a woman who raised three children. But when they grew up, they killed her over a small conflict. Do you think the children were right to do so?"

"Of course not!" Xie Shian’s face darkened with indignation. "Those three are heartless and unworthy of being called sons!"

Yun Chu asked, "What if the three children weren’t her biological children?"

Xie Shian replied, "The debt of raising a child is greater than that of giving birth. That woman raised them, so she was their mother. No matter what, they shouldn’t have killed her!"

Yun Chu nodded. "And what if the woman might have been involved in a rebellion, and the three children killed her only to protect themselves and their entire family? Would you still think they were wrong?"

Xie Shian didn’t answer as quickly this time.

He pondered for a moment before lifting his head and speaking softly, "The life of an entire family, compared to that of one woman, naturally the family is more important. If the woman knew her children killed her for the family’s prosperity, I think she would be willing to die."

Yun Chu smiled. "Thank you."

Xie Shian suddenly realized something was off. "Mother, what are you thanking me for?"

Yun Chu’s lips curved.

Of course, she was thanking him for making the same choice as he had in her past life.

Thanking him for being the same as he was before; so that when she took action, she would have no hesitation.

---

chapters.title: Bring the Family Punishment
chapters.content:
After paying his respects, Xie Shian still had to go to school.

He always arrived more than half an hour early, where he would read and practice calligraphy diligently.

He was just about to leave when a commotion suddenly erupted in the courtyard.

Yun Chu’s brows furrowed.

Tingfeng hurried in from outside. "Madam, the second young master has taken a fancy to the cricket in Old Chen’s hands. What should we do?"

At the mention of the cricket, Yun Chu’s mind flashed back to the chubby, fair-skinned little boy from yesterday.

Though the child had been ill-mannered, jumping on her and causing trouble, for some reason, she couldn’t bring herself to feel any disgust toward him.

She stood and walked toward the courtyard.

Daylight filled the sky. The concubines had brought their children to pay respects, and the courtyard was lively.

Just then, Chen Defu arrived with the cricket cage, and the two groups ran into each other. That was how Xie Shiwei spotted the cricket.

Eight-year-old Xie Shiwei lifted his chin and ordered, "Give me the cricket!"

Chen Defu looked troubled. "In response to the second young master, this cricket was specially ordered by Madam for—"

"Just give it to me if I tell you to! Why so much nonsense?" Xie Shiwei huffed through his nose. "Mother is always generous; how could she possibly begrudge one cricket?"

"Wow, this cricket looks really strong!" Four-year-old Xie Shiyou, eyes wide, exclaimed, "Second Brother, can I play with the cricket too?"

Xie Shiwei looked displeased.

Mother always doted on Third Brother the most. Whatever Third Brother wanted, he got. And now he even had to compete for a little cricket…

"You’re just a little brat. What do you know? Scram!"

He glared at Xie Shiyou before turning back to Chen Defu.

Chen Defu was just a servant, and he knew that Madam always spoiled these young masters.

He wasn’t sure if Madam would give the cricket to the second young master and have him find another one…

While he hesitated, Xie Shiwei snatched the cage from his hands.

Xie Shiwei immediately opened the cage, and the cricket leaped out, scurrying toward a nearby clump of grass.

"It dares to run!"

Xie Shiwei dropped the cage and gave chase.

At eight years old, he was at his most agile. With a pounce, he trapped the cricket beneath his palm.

He climbed to his feet and, lifting his gaze, saw Yun Chu standing on the steps not far away.

He quickly bowed. "Mother."

Only then did the others in the courtyard notice Yun Chu’s presence, and they all lowered their heads to pay their respects.

Yun Chu’s gaze settled on Xie Shiwei.

The second young master of the Xie family had not inherited Xie Jingyu’s intelligence or diligence. By nature, he was unruly and disliked studying. At eight years old, he still refused to attend school.

He slept until noon every day, and it was already good if he came to pay respects three or four times a month.

Though Xie Shiwei was not her most favored child, she had never shown favoritism. She had done her best to raise and educate every child…

Since Xie Shiwei had no talent for academics, she had her brother use the Yun family’s influence to send him to the military camp… And it was precisely this wrong decision that had given Xie Shiwei free access to the Yun family’s military camp. The evidence that sealed the Yun family’s treason had been personally hidden by Xie Shiwei in her father’s correspondence…

Her thoughts churned, and a chilling aura radiated from her.

Standing behind her, Xie Shian keenly sensed the shift in her mood.

"Shiwei." Xie Shian stepped forward, speaking with the authority of an elder brother. "Taking something without permission is not the act of a gentleman. Our Xie family values scholarship above all else. Your behavior brings shame to the Xie name. If Grandfather and Father find out, they will surely punish you to reflect in solitude. Return the cricket to its cage and apologize to Mother at once!"

Xie Shiwei first glanced at Yun Chu.

Normally, Mother would say it was just a cricket, nothing serious, and let him take it.

But now, Mother’s face was stern, her eyes intimidating.

He had no choice but to open his hand.

"Huh? Why isn’t the cricket moving?" Xie Shiyou cried out from the side. "Oh no, it looks like Second Brother squished it to death!"

Xie Shiwei poked at it. The cricket didn’t move.

He frowned. "How did it die so easily…"

"Kneel!"

Yun Chu coldly spat out the two words.

Xie Shiwei could hardly believe it. "Why?"

"Over the years, I’ve been too lenient with you, and that’s why you’ve become so lawless!" Yun Chu’s voice was sharp. "Taking without asking is theft. Our dynasty’s laws are clear, thieves are branded on the forehead, a lifelong disgrace. How can your father maintain his standing in the official circles? How can your eldest brother pursue his studies and career…?"

"I didn’t steal anything!"

Xie Shiwei panicked. Even at his most unruly, he knew he couldn’t allow himself to be branded as a thief.

"Mother, I was just being playful. I was wrong. I won’t do it again…"

In the past, he had taken Mother’s things like this before, and she had just smiled and let him have them.

Why was she making such a big deal out of it this time?

But he didn’t dare ask. He could only admit his mistake and hope she wouldn’t hold it against him.

Yun Chu slightly tilted her head, looking at Xie Shian beside her. "An’ge, what do you think should be done about this?"

Xie Shian lowered his head. "To know one’s mistake and correct it is the greatest virtue. Since Shiwei understands his error, let him compensate with an equivalent cricket."

Xie Shiwei’s face twisted in bitterness.

His eldest brother shared the same mother, why wasn’t he helping him plead his case? Instead, he was suggesting compensation!

He had spent all his money on food, drink, and entertainment. Where would he get the money to compensate Mother? Wasn’t this deliberately making things difficult for him?

Yun Chu smiled. "An’ge, do you know who this cricket was meant for?"

Xie Shian shook his head.

"It was a gift for the young heir of the Prince of Pingxi’s residence." Yun Chu’s smile vanished, her voice turning icy. "If it were my own things, and Wei’ge took them, well, we’re all family, I wouldn’t mind! But the Prince of Pingxi, do you know his status? The young heir of the Prince of Pingxi’s residence, can our Xie family afford to offend them? Today, Wei’ge can crush the Prince of Pingxi’s cricket to death. Tomorrow, he might ruin some noble lady’s dress. The day after, who knows, he might pluck a flower painstakingly cultivated by a princess… If we don’t punish him severely, do you think Wei’ge will ever learn his lesson?"

Xie Shian was stunned.

Mother had actually connected with a family as noble as the Prince of Pingxi’s; she must have gone to great lengths.

The cricket she had painstakingly obtained to please the young heir had died in Shiwei’s hands. No wonder Mother was so furious.

Xie Shian spoke slowly, "Then… family punishment is in order."

Yun Chu’s lips curved. "As expected, An’ge understands the bigger picture. Servants, bring the family punishment."

"No!" Xie Shiwei’s eyes widened in terror. "I don’t want the board! I don’t! Can’t I just compensate for the cricket…?"

In the Xie family, the rule had been set when the household was established: serious offenses were punishable by family law, starting with twenty strikes of the board.

Previously, a servant woman had colluded with an outside servant to embezzle the Xie family’s silver, and the old madam had her beaten so severely that she was bedridden for life.

This had left a deep psychological shadow on Xie Shiwei.

He was afraid of being flayed, afraid of never being able to walk again…

chapters.title: How to Cut Expenses
chapters.content:
At Yun Chu’s command, the servants immediately carried long benches into the courtyard.

Xie Shiwei was pressed onto the bench by the servants. He struggled desperately, "Mother, I was wrong, I was really wrong, please, Mother, spare me this once..."

Yun Chu coldly ordered, "Begin."

Two sturdy servants stood on either side, each holding a thick wooden board.

*Crack!*

A heavy board struck Xie Shiwei’s backside.

He let out a wail of agony.

"Stop!"

He Jin, dressed in a servant’s green attire, suddenly rushed into the courtyard from outside, pushing aside the man wielding the board.

She lowered her head to hide her anxious expression, walked up to Yun Chu, knelt, and said, "Madam, using family punishment is a serious matter. Shouldn’t Madam ask for the opinions of the Old Madam and the Mistress? Besides, the Second Young Master is still young, he might not survive twenty strikes. If he’s injured, the Old Madam will hold you accountable..."

Yun Chu smiled faintly, "How is it that Mama He seems to care more for Wei Ge’er than I, his own mother? It’s as if Mama He is the birth mother, while I, the legitimate mother, am treated like a stepmother."

He Jin’s face paled suddenly, "Madam, this servant didn’t mean that. I was only worried the Old Madam would blame you for injuring the Second Young Master..."

Yun Chu’s voice turned icy, "The affairs of the masters are none of a servant’s concern. Step back!" Then, to the others, "Continue!"

The two servants stepped forward. *Crack!* Another strike landed, and Xie Shiwei screamed in pain again.

He Jin bit her lip.

Sure enough, since he wasn’t her own child, she didn’t feel the slightest pity.

She turned and ran toward Anshou Hall.

Yun Chu watched indifferently as the servants delivered the strikes. At first, Xie Shiwei could still scream, but his cries grew weaker with each blow.

By the tenth strike, he passed out.

"Wei Ge’er!"

The Old Madam, leaning on her cane, arrived late and was horrified by the scene.

"Quick, quick! Send for a doctor!"

She was so flustered that she ordered someone to carry Xie Shiwei back to his room immediately.

"If I hadn’t come, were you planning to beat Wei Ge’er to death?" The Old Madam fixed Yun Chu with a glare, speaking each word deliberately. "It was just a cricket! If it died, we could’ve bought another. Was it necessary to beat the child like this? Even if punishment was needed, there are a hundred other ways. Who gave you permission to use family punishment? You’re trying to take Wei Ge’er’s life!"

Xie Shian stepped forward, "Great-Grandmother, this was my idea."

The Old Madam was stunned.

He Jin had rushed over breathlessly to report that Yun Chu was going to beat Wei Ge’er to death. She had assumed it was Yun Chu’s order.

But it was actually An Ge’er?

Xie Shian spoke, "Wei Shi’s temper really needs to be reined in. Otherwise, who knows what kind of trouble he’ll cause in the future? Father’s transfer is coming soon. If we anger the Prince of Pingxi’s household, who knows what the consequences will be? These twenty strikes, Wei Shi must endure them."

The Old Madam tightened her grip on her cane.

The Prince of Pingxi was the current Third Prince, a man of great military merit and imperial favor, someone the Xie family could never hope to associate with in their wildest dreams.

But her daughter-in-law had made the acquaintance of the young heir of the Prince of Pingxi’s household.

Yun Chu lowered her gaze, "Whether it’s punishing An Ge’er by making him kneel in the ancestral hall or punishing Wei Ge’er with a beating, the Old Madam always worries I’ll harm the children. In the end, it’s because I’m not their birth mother. Perhaps, in the future, I’ll have to indulge and spoil them, giving them whatever they want, just to keep the household peaceful."

The Old Madam was left speechless.

Over the past few days, she had confronted Yun Chu several times, and each time, she had been the one in the wrong.

"Yun Chu, these children are under your name, which makes them your own. Whether you punish or scold them is your right. As a great-grandmother, I truly shouldn’t interfere." She sighed, "Let’s go, back to Anshou Hall."

He Jin, standing behind the Old Madam, pressed her lips tightly together.

If the Old Madam wouldn’t intervene, and the Mistress wouldn’t either, then her children would be at Yun Chu’s mercy.

But what could a servant like her do?

As she left Yusheng Hall, she heard Yun Chu order the servants, "There are still ten strikes left. Wait until Wei Ge’er has recovered before continuing."

He Jin staggered, nearly falling to the ground.

The concubines in the courtyard exchanged glances, each lowering their heads to minimize their presence.

Yun Chu waved her hand, dismissing them all, but kept Xie Pin behind.

"Mother," Xie Pin said, a little nervously.

In the past, she had found her mother easy to get along with, but now, she no longer dared to think so.

She stood by Yun Chu’s side, looking obedient.

Yun Chu ordered Chen Defu to buy an even better cricket to send to the Prince of Pingxi’s household, then had Xie Pin study the account books.

Xie Pin had also received an education. She could read and write, but she wasn’t very good at accounting. She listened as Shuang taught her step by step how to keep the books clearly.

For someone who had been educated, this task wasn’t difficult as long as there was guidance.

Xie Pin quickly picked it up. She took last year’s account book and calculated, then gasped in shock, "I never realized that our Xie family, with such a modest status, could have such high expenses in a year. If we relied solely on these shops, the whole family would starve. Fortunately, we have Mother."

Yun Chu set down her work and said gently, "So the most important thing now is to increase revenue and cut expenses. As a young lady from a boudoir, you may not understand how to increase revenue, but you can help your mother think about how to cut expenses."

Xie Pin felt a sense of being entrusted with responsibility. She nodded confidently, "Mother, rest assured. I will come up with a plan."

For the entire afternoon, Xie Pin stayed in Yun Chu’s side hall, poring over the account books.

As dusk fell, she excitedly reported to Yun Chu, "Mother, our Xie residence has more than twenty rough-working servant women. Every afternoon, tea and snacks are arranged for them, costing about a dozen coins per person. That’s over two hundred coins a day, nearly ten taels of silver a month. If we cut this expense, we could save nearly a hundred taels of silver a year."

Yun Chu smiled, "Although a hundred taels isn’t much, if we find several areas to cut expenses, the savings will add up. Over a year, it will be a considerable sum. Pin Jie’er, I’ll leave this matter to you. Can you handle it?"

Xie Pin was encouraged, "I will do my best."

Yun Chu nodded, "You’re young. Even if you make a mistake, it’s fine. If there’s anything you don’t understand, come ask me."

"Thank you, Mother."

Xie Pin was full of determination.

While Shian and Shiwei were being punished, she had received her mother’s praise. She was determined to handle the task her mother had assigned her.

She carried a stack of account books back to her own courtyard to continue studying.

Yun Chu curled her lips and continued to lower her head, examining the account books.

She wasn’t looking at the Xie family’s accounts, but at the ledgers for her own shops and businesses.

The Xie family’s matters were just for show. What truly mattered was carefully planning the businesses in her own hands...

She worked until the sky was completely dark. Tingshuang gently reminded her that it was time for dinner.

The dishes had just been served when Tingxue entered from outside, "Madam, Elder Chen has just returned to the residence. He said the young heir of the Prince of Pingxi’s household refused to accept that cricket..."

---

chapters.title: If That Night
chapters.content:
Yun Chu took a sip of tea.

Tingxue explained carefully, "Elder Chen went to the Prince of Pingxi’s household twice. The first time, the young heir received him personally and said the cricket was too small. So Elder Chen quickly bought a larger, stronger cricket and sent it over. But this time, the young heir didn’t even come out. He had someone drive Elder Chen away, saying that if a satisfactory cricket wasn’t delivered, the matter wouldn’t be settled..."

Tingfeng frowned, "How can the young heir of the Prince of Pingxi’s household be so difficult?"

"Enough nonsense," Tingshuang reminded her, "It’s fine to say these things in front of Madam, but you must never repeat them outside and bring trouble upon Madam."

Yun Chu ate a little more before setting down her chopsticks, "The young heir has seen countless fine things. Naturally, he wouldn’t be impressed by an ordinary cricket from the market. Tingxue, go and have Elder Chen take a few people to the mountains and wild fields outside the city to look for crickets. Only unusual ones might catch the young heir’s eye."

Tingxue was about to accept the order.

Suddenly, the curtain of the flower hall was lifted.

A tall, jade-like man walked in.

It was Xie Jingyu.

He sat down at the dining table, "Set another place."

Tingfeng was overjoyed.

The Master hadn’t come to Madam’s place for a meal in a very long time.

If the husband and wife could eat together, perhaps they could reconnect. Maybe he would even stay in Yusheng Hall tonight.

She quickly took a set of bowls and chopsticks and respectfully placed them in front of Xie Jingyu.

Yun Chu had originally wanted to eat more, but the moment she saw Xie Jingyu, she lost her appetite entirely.

Her voice was calm, "Why have you come, Husband?"

"The Prince of Pingxi is busy with official duties and has not yet married a princess consort. The young heir has no one to guide him, so his temper is bound to be a little arrogant," Xie Jingyu said slowly. "Sending a servant like Elder Chen to him would be seen as disrespectful. Naturally, he would make things difficult for Elder Chen. If you trust me, Madam, tomorrow is a rest day. Why not let me handle this matter for you?"

A faint, almost imperceptible cold smile curled on Yun Chu’s lips.

Xie Jingyu was like this; even though he was clearly trying to ingratiate himself with the Prince of Pingxi, he made it sound as if he were sacrificing himself to help her.

But could a single cricket really help them connect with the Prince of Pingxi’s household?

She suppressed her mockery and said, "Thank you, Husband, for resolving this for me."

Xie Jingyu looked at her, "We are husband and wife, one family. There’s no need for thanks between us."

Suddenly, he felt that his wife’s fair face had taken on a beauty that didn’t belong to Madam Xie.

The first time he had seen her at the General’s residence, she had looked just like this; as if she had absorbed all the light, possessing an inexplicable, breathtaking beauty.

His throat rolled, and uncontrollably, he reached out and took Yun Chu’s hand.

In that instant, it was as if a venomous snake had slithered up from his palm. Yun Chu’s entire body broke out in goosebumps. Instinctively, she tried to pull her hand away.

But Xie Jingyu let go first.

His gaze darkened.

He had once imagined a life of marital bliss with her, filled with children and grandchildren, growing old together.

But who could have foreseen what happened that night...

*If that night...*

Xie Jingyu stood up, "I have some matters to attend to. I’ll take my leave."

He left in a hurry.

As he reached the door of Yusheng Hall, he turned back and saw Tingshuang place a basin of water on the table. Yun Chu was frantically washing her hands.

His expression darkened instantly.

He hadn’t rejected her for losing her virtue, so how dare she...

He looked up and noticed that Yusheng Hall had somehow become Sheng Hall at some point.

An indescribable emotion surged in his heart...

"Master."

He Jin’s figure suddenly appeared in the night.

Seeing him emerge from Yusheng Hall, He Jin said with some bitterness, "Did Master come straight to Madam’s place as soon as you returned to the residence?"

Xie Jingyu clasped his hands behind his back and walked forward, "What’s wrong with me visiting my wife?"
