"Does Master know what Madam did today?" He Jin bit her lip and said, "Madam used family punishment and beat Wei Ge’er unconscious. His backside was split open, bleeding heavily. The doctor said it would take at least ten days or half a month to recover... Madam isn’t Wei Ge’er’s birth mother, so she showed no mercy in beating him. But I care, Master. Can’t you control Madam and stop her from—"

"He is their legitimate mother. Disciplining them is her duty!" Xie Jingyu’s sharp eyes swept over her. "Whether An Ge’er can find a good teacher, whether Wei Ge’er can amount to anything, whether Pin Jie’er can marry into a noble family, all of this depends on her. What can you, as their birth mother, provide for them?"

He Jin lowered her head, her face filled with bitter smiles.

She turned and went to Xie Shiwei’s courtyard.

Before she even entered, she heard pitiful cries of pain from inside.

"All of you, leave."

She dismissed all the servants, closed the door, and rushed to the bedside in one swift motion, "Wei Ge’er, does it hurt?"

"Mother, Mother! I’m in so much pain!" Xie Shiwei threw himself into He Jin’s arms. "Why do I have to have that woman as my mother? I hate her! I hate her the most!"

He Jin quickly covered his mouth, "Wei Ge’er, she is your legitimate mother. You must respect her. Never say such things again!"

No matter how much she disliked Yun Chu, she had to admit that acknowledging Yun Chu as their mother was the best choice for the children.

Xie Shiwei bit He Jin’s hand and said hatefully, "She wouldn’t even give me a cricket. She doesn’t treat me like a son at all. Why should I respect her? I hate her to death!"

Before he could finish, the door to the room was suddenly pushed open.

He Jin opened her mouth, ready to scold the servant for their rudeness.

But when she turned, she saw Tingshuang and Tingxue enter from the left and right. The door swung open, and then Yun Chu stepped inside.

She was so frightened that her face turned pale. She lost her balance and fell to her knees.

"M-Madam!"

She knelt in greeting, silently praying in her heart that Madam hadn’t heard Wei Ge’er call her "Mother."

"Mama He, why do you bow to me with such a grand gesture? You are the Master’s woman. I cannot accept such a greeting from you." Yun Chu ignored her and looked at the person lying on the bed, "Did Wei Ge’er just say he hates me the most?"

Xie Shiwei pressed his lips together and remained silent.

He had said those words, but in truth, he didn’t hate his mother that much.

Before the age of four, he had lived with his birth mother in a modest farmhouse outside the city, enduring hardship.

After turning four, he returned to the Xie family to live with his father and mother. In every aspect, clothing, food, shelter, his life had improved immeasurably.

He knew he shouldn’t offend his mother, but after enduring so many strikes, he was truly aggrieved...

"It seems Wei Ge’er still hasn’t learned his lesson." Yun Chu shook her head indifferently. "I was planning to spare you the remaining ten strikes, but since you still don’t understand the rules, then after your injuries heal, we’ll continue with the family punishment."

Xie Shiwei’s eyes widened in shock.

He had thought his mother had come to comfort him, but instead, she was still determined to punish him further.

He didn’t dare say anything disrespectful again. He flipped over and got off the bed, grabbing Yun Chu’s sleeve, "Mother, I really know I was wrong. I’ve learned my lesson. I truly remember this punishment. Please, Mother, spare me the remaining strikes. I beg you, Mother!"

He Jin’s lips parted, but she forced herself to swallow her plea.

Yun Chu bent down and helped Xie Shiwei lie back on the bed. Her voice was gentle, "That was the most expensive cricket on the market, worth five hundred taels of silver. In comparison, twenty strikes are nothing."

Xie Shiwei broke down and shouted, "I’ll compensate Mother for the five hundred taels! If five hundred isn’t enough, then a thousand! I’ll pay it all!"

chapters.title: What Was Gained
chapters.content:
Yun Chu smiled faintly.

She looked around the room. Apart from the four walls belonging to the Xie family, everything else had been arranged by her.

These things, even if fed to dogs, would be better than giving them to this pack of ungrateful wolves.

She spoke, "Since Wei Ge'er has said so, if I, as his mother, still insist on punishing you, that would indeed be too heartless. But, can you come up with a thousand taels of silver?"

Xie Shiwei was immediately at a loss for words.

He received a few taels of silver each month as his allowance. The old madam and his grandmother would also give him some. Altogether, it added up to twenty or thirty taels, all of which he had squandered. He didn’t have a single coin left.

Yun Chu raised her hand slightly, "If you can't come up with it, then we'll have to scrape it together somehow."

Listening Shuang and Listening Xue stepped forward and began moving things.

Several servants and maids entered from outside to help.

The originally exquisite bedroom was soon emptied.

Xie Shiwei endured the pain and restrained himself as he asked, "Mother, what are you doing?"

"First, these things are worth a bit of silver, so consider this as compensation for the cricket," Yun Chu said slowly. "Second, the books say that when Heaven is about to place a great responsibility on someone, it must first torment their mind, exhaust their muscles and bones, and starve their body... When Wei Ge'er first entered the Xie household, he was obedient and sensible. But now, he’s becoming more and more undisciplined. I suppose it’s because I’ve spoiled him too much. Starting today, your food, clothing, and expenses will all be halved. When you show improvement, then we’ll restore them."

Xie Shiwei wailed loudly, "Mother, no, I know I was wrong!"

Yun Chu turned around and left with her people.

"Mother, don’t go! I really will change, I promise I will! Please, Mother, don’t do this to me..."

Xie Shiwei crawled off the bed, moving on his hands and knees, but was stopped by He Shi, who picked him up.

"He Shi, the madam is doing this for your own good..." He Shi struggled to advise.

Compared to An Ge'er, Wei Ge'er was indeed far too unruly.

This time, she wouldn’t go to the old madam to complain. She hoped that under the madam’s discipline, Wei Ge'er would truly improve.

He Shi comforted him for a long time before Xie Shiwei finally stopped crying and fell asleep.

She walked into the courtyard and sighed.

Too many things had happened these past few days, more than in the past four years combined. She felt overwhelmed.

As she walked outside, she overheard a few servant women whispering.

"Did you say that starting tomorrow, the afternoon melon seeds and tea will be gone?"

"Yes, the people from the young lady’s courtyard said so. Tomorrow morning, they’ll announce it. The young lady, on her first day assisting the madam with household management, is already targeting us?"

"Melon seeds and tea don’t cost much. The young lady really doesn’t treat us coarse servant women as people."

"If the young lady really won’t even give us a cup of tea, then in the future, I won’t do what she orders either."

...

"What are you all doing, gathered here in the middle of the night!" He Shi stepped out from the shadows, her voice cold. "Hurry up and disperse!"

Everyone knew she was the most trusted He Mama by the master’s side. None of them dared to say another word. They lowered their heads and quickly went about their tasks.

Under the cover of night, He Shi went to Xie Pin’s courtyard.

Xie Pin was still looking at the account books. When she saw He Shi approaching, her eyebrows immediately furrowed. "Didn’t I tell you not to come here often?"

She was now the legitimate eldest young lady of the Xie family and didn’t want to be too closely associated with a servant, even if that servant was her own mother.

He Shi chose her words carefully. "Pin’er, I..."

"Don’t address me like that!" Xie Pin said displeasedly. "You are the manager mama in the master’s courtyard. You should address me as Eldest Young Lady. Don’t make me remind you again."

"Yes, Eldest Young Lady." He Shi suppressed her disappointment and said, "I heard the servant women in the courtyard say that the Eldest Young Lady has canceled the afternoon tea and snacks?"

Xie Pin nodded. "Yes, what of it?"

"This won’t do." He Shi said slowly, "You’ve only just started assisting the madam with household management. Making such drastic changes will make the servants below resent you. In the future, when you give orders, they won’t obey. They’ll create many troubles for you. Don’t think that just because these coarse servant women are of low status, their opinions don’t matter. They..."

"That’s enough from you!" Xie Pin’s face was filled with impatience. "Mother said this approach is excellent. What qualifies you to say it won’t work? Mother is the eldest young lady of the Yun family; she understands everything. You’re just a coarse servant. Do you think I should listen to you or to Mother? I still have account books to look at. I don’t have time to talk to you. Someone, please escort He Mama out."

A maid entered and made a gesture of invitation.

He Shi wanted to say more, but Xie Pin gave her no chance. She hugged the account book and went straight into the inner room.

He Shi walked out of the courtyard, her eyes narrowing.

She replayed the events of the past few days in her mind.

Although the madam had reasons for each of her outbursts, for some reason, she vaguely felt that the madam seemed to be deliberately targeting her children.

The old madam and the madam listened to everything the madam said, and the master also allowed the madam to discipline the children. Even if the madam crippled the children, the Xie family would probably think it was for the children’s future...

Whether she was overthinking or not, she couldn’t just sit and wait for disaster.

An idea surfaced in He Shi’s mind.

---

The next morning, the spring rain pattered outside the window. The fresh air improved Yun Chu’s mood slightly.

As Listening Shuang combed her hair, she whispered, "Last night, He Mama sent a pot of flowers to Tao Concubine on behalf of the master."

Tao Concubine was Xie Jingyu’s third concubine, a gifted concubine from Shang Feng. She was currently pregnant and due in a little over three months.

Yun Chu selected a hairpin and put it on. "Keep an eye on He Shi."

She had expected that, with her recent actions, He Shi would make a move.

In her previous life, something had happened to Tao Concubine’s child... All evidence had pointed to her, saying she had attempted to harm Tao Concubine’s child.

Originally, the Xie family had respected her, but after that incident, her status in the household had plummeted...

Tao Concubine’s child had not died, but had been brain-damaged, unable to speak or walk, appearing foolish. It was she who had searched everywhere for famous doctors to treat the child. It was she who had begged her grandfather and grandmother to bring in that divine doctor. It was she who had taken care of the child without rest... But after the child was cured, what had she gained?

Yun Chu let out a cold laugh.

In this life, He Shi had acted a month earlier than in the previous one. She wondered if the Xie family’s fourth young master would have the fortune to be born alive.

Just as she finished her toilet, Xie Shian came to pay his respects.

Because he had to study, he was always the first to arrive, standing properly in the side hall waiting for Yun Chu to come out.

Yun Chu chatted with him briefly and, seeing that he wasn’t in a hurry to go to school, asked, "Is there something else?"

"I’m waiting for Father." Xie Shian replied, "Father is going to the Prince of Pingxi’s residence and wants me to go with him. Does Mother have anything to instruct?"

Yun Chu said gently, "Just be careful on the road."

Xie Jingyu valued this eldest son the most. Starting so early to pave the way for his eldest son, this deep paternal love truly moved her.

It was a shame that Xie Shian would never achieve what he had in his previous life.

---

chapters.title: Let Her Come Herself
chapters.content:
The morning in the capital was bustling.

Xie Jingyu and Xie Shian sat in the carriage. Father and son looked as if they had been carved from the same mold, even their temperaments were similar.

Passing through the busiest streets, the carriage entered the most prestigious area of the capital. Those who lived here were all high-ranking officials and nobles, the lowest being second-rank officials.

"When we enter the prince’s residence, be sure to watch your words and actions." Xie Jingyu instructed, "The prince’s residence has strict rules. You’re young, so don’t speak out of turn."

Xie Shian nodded. "Father, I remember."

The two arrived at the prince’s gate. Just as Xie Jingyu was about to step onto the stairs, the guards stationed on both sides of the gate shouted harshly, "Who are you? What are you here for? Do you have a calling card?"

Xie Jingyu cupped his hands. "I am Xie Jingyu, a Langzhong in the Ministry of Revenue. The other day, my wife offended your honorable residence’s young master. I have come specially to apologize and make amends."

"So, you don’t have a calling card?" The guard raised his chin, looking down on him. "Wait here at the gate. I’ll go in and ask first."

Xie Jingyu’s face darkened slightly.

He was, after all, a fifth-rank official in the imperial court. How could this guard look at him with such disdain and make him wait at the gate? This was far too disrespectful.

"Ah, so this is what they mean by 'before the prime minister’s gate, even a third-rank official is nothing.'" Xie Shian said softly. "Our great-grandfather was a Xiucai, our grandfather a Juren, and our father passed the imperial examination as a Zhuangyuan. In just over five years, he has become a fifth-rank official in the imperial court. By my generation, I will certainly make the Xie family a new noble family in the court. But at that time, I won’t allow the Xie family’s servants to look down on anyone."

Xie Jingyu’s face was full of comfort. "I have not raised you in vain."

As they spoke, footsteps approached. The two stopped talking and assumed a respectful waiting posture.

A small, fair-skinned child came out of the prince’s gate. It was the four-year-old young master of the Prince of Pingxi’s residence.

As soon as he saw the two people waiting at the gate, the expectation on his delicate little face turned into anger.

"Greetings, Young Master." Xie Jingyu lifted the cage in his hand and presented it with both hands. "This is an extremely rare iron-headed green-backed fighting cricket. It has a fierce temperament and is very aggressive. Please, Young Master, take a look."

The little fellow stomped down the steps, took the cage, and then suddenly smashed it to the ground.

"This cricket is ugly! I don’t like it!" The young master’s face was full of anger as he pointed at Xie Jingyu’s nose. "Go back and tell that woman to come to the prince’s residence herself!"

What good cricket hadn’t he seen? He only wanted the cricket that woman brought personally.

As he thought of the woman he had seen at the teahouse that day, his eyes suddenly reddened. He didn’t know why, but he just wanted to see her.

The more aggrieved he felt, the angrier he became. He shouted, "Tell her, if she doesn’t come, I’ll go find her myself!"

"Who do you want to find?"

A cold voice suddenly rang out.

Immediately afterward, a sweating blood horse stopped at the gate of the residence. A man in a purple-black court robe dismounted.

Xie Jingyu turned around, bowing deeply. "This official greets Your Highness! Wishing Your Highness good health!"

This was the first time he had been so close to the Prince of Pingxi.

This was a great opportunity to get to know the Prince of Pingxi.

However...

The Prince of Pingxi didn’t even glance at him. He stepped forward and picked up the little boy with one hand.

His voice was extremely deep. "You just said, who do you want to find?"

"Father..." The little fellow shrank his neck. "I, I didn’t want to find anyone. Father, you heard wrong."

The man gave a cold laugh and, with a wave of his hand, tossed him into the arms of a nearby servant. "If he takes one step out of the prince’s residence, none of you servants will ever set foot in the prince’s residence again."

Having said that, he turned to Xie Jingyu. "Childish words. Official Xie, don’t take it too seriously. Don’t come again in the future."

Before Xie Jingyu could say anything, the Prince of Pingxi had already strode into the residence.

The two guards at the gate closed the prince’s gate.

Xie Jingyu’s face was filled with disappointment.

Such a good opportunity, and he had failed to seize it.

Xie Shian spoke up, "What if we let Mother..."

Xie Jingyu tightened his lips. "No need."

He was a grown man. If he couldn’t handle this small matter, it would be too embarrassing to have his wife step in.

However, Yun Chu was not the kind of fool who was kept in the dark.

The carriage driver who had taken Xie Jingyu and Xie Shian to the prince’s residence was a man from the Yun family whom she had brought into the household. He had recounted everything that happened at the prince’s gate to her in full detail.

"Let our madam go to the prince’s residence in person?" Listening Shuang’s face was full of shock. "The prince’s residence has no princess. It would be highly inappropriate for the madam to visit. How could the young master make such a request?"

The carriage driver lowered his head. "The Prince of Pingxi scolded the young master severely and ordered the Xie family not to visit again."

Listening Xue sighed in relief. "It seems this matter is settled. The Prince of Pingxi is indeed reasonable. He knows it was the young master’s fault and isn’t making things difficult for our madam."

Yun Chu nodded.

The Prince of Pingxi had always been a reasonable man. In her previous life, when the Yun family was in prison, only the Prince of Pingxi had been willing to help...

As they were speaking, Listening Yu entered from the doorway. "Madam, this is the soup I specially made for you. Please drink it while it’s hot."

Yun Chu’s voice was very calm. "I’ve already had soup. Take it away."

Listening Yu’s lips trembled. She hesitated before saying, "Madam, has this concubine done something wrong, or has Yun Ge’er broken any rules?"

These past few days, the madam had severely punished the eldest young master and the second young master. She was afraid that Yun Ge’er had also done something wrong and displeased the madam, which was why she had moved them out of Yusheng Courtyard.

When they had lived in Yusheng Courtyard, she had served the madam closely and had a lot of face in the Xie residence.

Since moving out, not only had their food, clothing, and expenses worsened, but even the senior maids and servants dared to give her dirty looks...

So, she had mustered the courage to come and ask the madam what was going on.

Yun Chu looked at her. "Ever since you gave birth to Yun Ge’er, you’ve never served the master again. After thinking it over, it’s still better for you to live separately in your own courtyard. It will also be more convenient for the master to stay overnight."

Listening Yu bit her lower lip.

Yun Chu picked up an account book and opened it. She knew the madam was about to get busy, so she could only lower her head and retreat.

As soon as she stepped out of the courtyard, she heard a cold laugh.

"Oh, isn’t this our Concubine Yu?" Listening Feng sneered. "Concubine Jiang and Concubine Tao stay quietly in their own courtyards, but you like to get close to the madam. Don’t tell me you think that because you served the madam growing up, you’re different from the other concubines. Ever since the day you climbed into the master’s bed behind the madam’s back, the madam hasn’t taken you seriously. The only reason she tolerates you now is for the sake of the third young master. You should be grateful you gave birth to a good son..."

Listening Yu struggled to explain, "That night, I really didn’t do it on purpose... The master was drunk..."

"Don’t explain your bedchamber affairs to me, a pure and innocent young lady." Listening Feng tugged at the corner of her mouth. "I’m just a maid, unworthy of your explanations, Concubine Yu. Slow walk, no need to see you off."

Listening Yu bit her lip in humiliation and turned to leave the Sheng Courtyard.

Yun Chu sat on the couch, somewhat lost in thought.

Listening Shuang was twenty this year, and the youngest, Listening Feng, was sixteen. It was time to find them husbands.

In her previous life, after Listening Shuang’s death, Listening Feng and Listening Xue had sworn never to marry, spending their lives in lonely solitude. In this life, she couldn’t let these maids follow her in such loneliness again.

chapters.title: Madam He’s Thoughtfulness
chapters.content:
Chen Defu acted very quickly. The more than 20,000 taels of silver Yun Chu gave him, along with some revenue from the shop, were all used to purchase ice blocks.

In an ordinary summer, ice cost about one or two taels of silver per jin. In spring, ice was cheaper, around 500 to 600 wen per jin. This spring was unusually cold, and everyone believed the summer would not be too hot, so the price of ice kept dropping. Chen Defu took advantage of this and bought ice at 350 wen per jin, renting all the ice cellars around the capital...

Yun Chu still remembered that in her previous life, that summer was so scorching hot that the price of ice soared to nearly that of gold, making it unaffordable.

The ice blocks she bought for over 30,000 taels of silver could be sold for at least 200,000 to 300,000 taels.

With money, many future problems could be solved.

She had stayed up late the night before, so she woke up a bit later the next morning. When Yun Chu came out, the concubines had already arrived.

"Madam."

"Mother."

They all greeted her in unison.

Yun Chu raised her hand slightly, and only then did the people in the room dare to sit down.

They certainly did not want to be severely punished by Madam for not following the rules.

Yun Chu glanced around and asked, "Why isn’t Concubine Tao here?"

Jiang Concubine and Tao Concubine lived next door. Jiang Concubine quickly stood up and replied, "Last night, Concubine Tao had diarrhea and vomiting. Early this morning, she said she felt unwell and would come to pay her respects later. Please do not blame her, Madam."

Yun Chu frowned. "A pregnant woman indeed has various discomforts. Concubine Tao is due in three months. If her body is too weak, the child will not be easily delivered."

She looked at the maid beside her and ordered, "Tingxue, take some tonics for pregnancy from my storage and send them to Concubine Tao’s courtyard."

Tingxue nodded and went to do as instructed.

Yun Chu’s gaze fell on the little girl beside Jiang Concubine. This was Xie Xian, the second young lady of the Xie family, who had a very low presence in the household.

She vaguely remembered that before her death, when Xie Shiyun forced her to drink poison, it was Xie Xian who rushed over in tears and knocked over the bowl containing the poison.

In the entire Xie family, only Xian Jie cried bitterly over her death.

Seeing her looking over, Xie Xian hid behind Jiang Concubine and softly called out, "Mother."

Yun Chu smiled and said, "Xian Jie is a bit too timid. She is three years old and can start her education. Let Xian Jie go to school with the others."

The Xie family had hired a teacher to teach the children to recognize characters. After the initial education, they would go to the imperial academy like Xie Shian.

Jiang Concubine had actually wanted to send her child to school for a long time.

But the eldest young lady, Xie Pin, only started learning to read and write at the age of five. She was afraid that if Xian Jie started school too early, the eldest young lady would dislike her...

However, since Madam had given her permission, she naturally agreed enthusiastically, pulling Xie Xian forward. "Hurry and thank your mother."

Yun Chu waved her hand. "No need for thanks among family. Don’t stand here, all of you go back to your tasks."

The crowd withdrew.

Xie Pin stayed behind to continue learning household management from Yun Chu.

After teaching her for a while, Yun Chu said, "Early this morning, Old Servant Li brought several carts of jujube trees into the residence. Take the account book and verify them. Handle minor issues yourself, and come back to me for major ones."

Xie Pin stood up. "Yes, Mother."

She took the account book and left.

As soon as she left, Tingshuang approached and whispered, "Madam, the tonics you ordered have been sent to Concubine Tao’s courtyard. The maid stewed some bird’s nest, and Concubine Tao had just taken a few sips when Madam He brought several bolts of brocade and said that the master had sent them for Concubine Tao to make some new clothes."

Tingfeng muttered, "When our Madam was pregnant, the master never showed this much care..."

She stopped halfway, realizing that saying this might upset Madam, and immediately covered her mouth.

Tingshuang lowered her head. "The master is busy with official duties and cannot be expected to care about such small matters. It should be said that Madam He is thoughtful."

Yun Chu took a sip of tea.

It seemed that Madam He could no longer wait to make her move.

She had done her best to cooperate. She hoped that Madam He would not disappoint her.

At this moment, a commotion suddenly arose in the courtyard.

Soon after, Xie Pin ran in with a terrible expression. "Mother, those old servants completely disregard me as the eldest young lady. They keep saying infuriating things. You must punish them..."

Outside, the voices of the old servants could be heard. "Madam, you must stand up for us! Although we are rough servants, we are still people. How can the Xie family treat us so harshly..."

Xie Pin’s face turned red with anger.

Yun Chu patted her hand, signaling her to calm down, then stepped outside.

The old servants spoke one after another, clearly explaining what had happened.

The matter was simple. Earlier, Xie Pin had gone to check the accounts. The jujube trees matched the records, so there was no problem. After finishing, she was about to leave.

Suddenly, one of the old servants said she was thirsty and asked if the Xie family’s kitchen could prepare some tea for everyone.

This old servant had clearly heard about the cancellation of the afternoon tea and was deliberately testing the waters.

Xie Pin, not thinking much, announced the cancellation of the daily afternoon tea and snacks.

This statement was like pouring oil into hot water, instantly causing an uproar.

"Madam, we do the hardest and most tiring work every day, earn the least wages, and now we don’t even have tea to drink. How can we not feel disheartened?"

"The maids in the courtyard earn so much monthly allowance and can drink the tea and eat the snacks given by the masters. Why not cut their allowances instead?"

"As soon as the eldest young lady started managing the household with Madam, our days have become difficult. What will happen in the future?"

"In my opinion, the eldest young lady is simply not suitable for managing the household!"

"The eldest young lady is born of a concubine. Only a concubine’s daughter would pinch pennies with us old servants..."

Xie Pin tightly clutched the handkerchief in her hand.

What she hated the most was when the servants said she was born of a concubine. This was more painful than a slap to her face.

Yun Chu heavily placed her teacup on the table, and the crowd of old servants finally quieted down.

"You old servants still have your contracts held by the Xie family, yet you dare to disregard the Xie family’s masters like this?" She exuded a cold aura. "The Xie family’s eldest young lady is registered under my name, making her a legitimate eldest young lady. If I hear you say such nonsense again, I will sell you off immediately!"

The old servants, who had been chattering away, suddenly fell silent like cicadas in winter.

They were not afraid of the eldest young lady because of her questionable status, but Madam was different. She was a legitimate daughter of the General’s residence...

Xie Pin looked at Yun Chu with gratitude.

These past few days, her mother had been quick to anger. She had thought her mother would blame her, that her mother would take away her household management rights just like she had punished An Ge and Wei Ge...

"However..." Yun Chu’s voice softened. "I gave Ping Jie the authority to manage the household. Since she proposed removing the afternoon tea and snacks, I naturally will not oppose it."

The old servants’ faces were filled with disappointment.

Even Madam would not stand up for them. Did that mean they just had to accept it?

"But you have indeed worked hard." Yun Chu’s voice became gentle. "How about this: the monthly allowance for all rough servants will be increased by 50 wen. Do you have any objections?"

Upon hearing this, the old servants’ eyes widened in disbelief.

A few cups of tea and some melon seeds and snacks every afternoon would be gone once eaten, but the monthly allowance was real copper coins. Having them in their pockets was extremely reassuring.

"No objections, no objections at all!" The old servants beamed with joy. "Thank you, Madam. We will continue with our work."

After they left, Yun Chu turned to Xie Pin. "The implementation of any new measure will encounter resistance. Don’t be scared by those old servants. Feel free to do what you must. I will always be here."

Xie Pin gratefully replied, "I understand, Mother."

---

chapters.title: Concubine Tao’s Incident
chapters.content:
The monthly wage for the rough servants in the Xie family was not high, just over 500 wen.

An increase of 50 wen per month meant they would earn nearly one tael more per year. How could this not make people happy?

"Madam is still the one who understands us servants."

"Our Madam is the legitimate daughter of the General’s residence. She wouldn’t care about such a small amount of money."

"I really don’t understand why Madam insists on having the eldest young lady manage the household. If the eldest young lady continues like this, the entire residence will be in chaos."

"Anyway, the eldest young lady will marry out sooner or later. This residence is managed by Madam. What is there to fear?"

"I hope the eldest young lady gets married soon."

...

Standing not far away, He Shi was so angry that smoke seemed to rise from her head.

By canceling the afternoon tea, Ping Jie saved 300 wen per month per servant. But Madam increased their wages by 50 wen. Wasn’t this taking Ping Jie’s credit to win favor?

Madam was too cunning. She was using Ping Jie’s efforts to build her own reputation in the residence.

If word got out that Ping Jie was incapable of managing the household, which noble family would still want to marry her as the mistress of the household?

Wei Ge was still injured and bedridden. Now, Ping Jie’s reputation was about to be ruined. What exactly did Madam want to do?

She could not wait until things reached an irreversible point before taking action. By then, it would be too late.

He Shi’s eyes darkened as she turned and left.

Soon, a young servant from the outer courtyard came to Shengju Hall to report, "Madam, just now, Madam He personally went to the pharmacy..."

Yun Chu smiled. "Bring the chicken soup stewed at noon. Let’s go to Anshou Hall."

It was now evening, and twilight was beginning to fall. The servants coming and going in the courtyard would stop to respectfully greet Madam.

Soon, they arrived at Anshou Hall. Two old servants stood guard at the entrance, two maids were sweeping the courtyard, and two maids stood at the door of the main house, lifting the curtain. Inside, two more maids and old servants were attending to the sides.

Just in Anshou Hall alone, there were more than a dozen people serving the old madam.

Without the financial means, yet insisting on such grandeur.

Yun Chu curled her lips slightly and stepped inside.

The old madam was seated in the main position, with Madam Yuan Shi sitting beside her. The two were chatting idly.

"So Mother is also here." Yun Chu smiled. "I only brought one bowl of chicken soup. This puts me in a difficult position."

The old madam said, "When your mother came, she brought me a bowl of rock sugar bird’s nest soup. I couldn’t finish it, so I had your mother drink it."

Tingshuang placed the chicken soup in front of Yuan Shi.

Yuan Shi took a few sips and praised the soup for being fragrant, sweet, and tender. Then she said, "Chu’er, how has Ping Jie been managing the household these past few days? I’ve heard some rumors..."

"Mother, have you forgotten how I experienced the same when I first took over the household affairs?" Yun Chu said. "When Ping Jie becomes the mistress of the household in the future, she will inevitably face deliberate difficulties from the servants. With me supporting her and teaching her personally in the Xie family, what else do you have to worry about, Mother?"

Yuan Shi’s face was filled with relief. "Jingyu’s greatest talent is not passing the imperial examination, but marrying a capable wife like you."

Yun Chu looked up at the old madam. "Soon, it will be Old Madam’s birthday. This year, I plan to have Ping Jie handle the arrangements. What do you think, Old Madam?"

The old madam slightly furrowed her brows. "Can Ping Jie handle it?"

"Isn’t Chu’er here to help?" Yuan Shi said reassuringly. "If Ping Jie does something wrong, Chu’er can guide her. Nothing will go wrong."

The old madam thought for a moment before saying, "Alright."

Ping Jie’s marriage was very important. If she married well, it would be a great help to the Xie family. She must learn household management well.

Yun Chu took a sip of tea and looked up. "Old Madam, I heard from the servants that you sent some things to Wei Ge’s courtyard this morning?"

The old madam was at a loss for words.

Previously, she had sworn she would not interfere with Yun Chu’s discipline of the children, but now she had slapped her own face.

"Wei Ge has been spoiled. His temper must be suppressed." Yun Chu said. "The things Old Madam sent to his courtyard, I will take back for now. When Wei Ge improves, I will send them to him on your behalf."

Those things were originally gifts Yun Chu had given to the old madam, so taking them back was justified.

The old madam’s face darkened.

The things sent to Wei Ge’s place were extremely rare and precious, yet her granddaughter-in-law had taken them away just like that.

As the three were talking, an old servant suddenly rushed in from outside. "Old Madam, it’s not good!"

The old madam, having been upset by Yun Chu, took out her anger on the old servant, shouting, "I am sitting here perfectly fine. How is it not good? You have no manners at all!"

The old servant slapped her own mouth and then said, "Concubine Tao is in trouble. She has lost a lot of blood. This old servant has already taken the initiative to call for a doctor!"

The old madam suddenly stood up. "The child is only six or seven months along. How could there be bleeding? Let’s go see!"

Yun Chu and Yuan Shi quickly stood up and followed her to Concubine Tao’s courtyard.

As soon as the people in charge of the household arrived, Concubine Tao’s maid quickly greeted them. "Old Madam, Madam, Madam Yun, Concubine Tao started feeling unwell last night, but it was just some diarrhea and vomiting. Just now, she suddenly said her stomach hurt, and then she started bleeding..."

It was not yet time for delivery. Everyone present knew what bleeding at this stage meant, and their expressions were all grave.

As they spoke, the doctor finally arrived. The maid quickly led the doctor into the room to diagnose.

After a while, the doctor came out. "The concubine probably ate something that caused the fetus to move. Fortunately, she did not eat much, and most of it was vomited up. With some medicine to stabilize the fetus and proper care, the child should be saved."

The old madam let out a sigh of relief.

As people aged, they cherished having many children and grandchildren around them. The more descendants, the more prosperous the family, and the more face they would have when meeting their ancestors after death.

Therefore, she could not allow anything to happen to any child.

The old madam said, "Bring everything Concubine Tao ate today. Let the doctor see what exactly she ate wrong."

The maid quickly went to fetch the items. The leftovers were brought out, and the things that were finished were recorded for the doctor to review.

"This chicken soup..." The doctor’s gaze fell on the remaining chicken soup. He dipped his finger in and tasted a bit, his expression suddenly changing. "Did the pain start after drinking this soup?"

The maid nodded. "The concubine drank a few sips and felt even more unwell, so she put it down. As soon as she lay down on the bed, she started having stomach pains and bleeding..."

"There is safflower in this soup." The doctor said gravely, "Old Madam, you had better investigate this thoroughly. If this happens again, the child will definitely not be saved."

After leaving the prescription, the doctor picked up his medical case and left.

The old madam had someone give the doctor some silver, clearly hoping he would not spread the Xie family’s dirty laundry.

Yuan Shi stepped forward, her voice filled with disbelief. "Isn’t this the same chicken soup that Chu’er brought earlier?"

The old madam’s gaze fell on Yun Chu, filled with doubt and scrutiny.

Yun Chu did not avoid it. "This soup was indeed sent by me. One bowl was sent to Anshou Hall, and another was sent to Concubine Tao’s place."

The old madam’s face darkened. "The doctor said there was safflower in the soup you sent. What is your explanation?"

chapters.title: Fear of Father’s Wrath
chapters.content:
Dusk fell.

The lanterns in the courtyard were lit one by one.

After the incident with Concubine Tao, everyone from the Xie family except Xie Jingyu had come, Concubine Jiang, Concubine Yu, Xie Shian, and Xie Pin. The small courtyard was packed with people.

Everyone’s gaze fell on Yun Chu.

Yun Chu stood composed. "So, Old Madam suspects that I wanted to cause Concubine Tao to miscarry?"

"It’s not that I suspect you, but the evidence points to you." Old Madam spoke. "Chu’er, you know how much I trust you. Otherwise, I wouldn’t have placed all the household authority in your hands. Is this how you repay my trust?"

"This..." Concubine Jiang spoke cautiously. "This servant only wishes to speak a fair word. The mistress has no motive to do such a thing."

If the mistress had her own child, it would make sense for her to resent a concubine’s child.

But the mistress had no children of her own, and never would. Moreover, the master had declared that any child born to a concubine must be registered under the mistress’s name. Whether she raised one or many, it made no difference. Deliberately causing Concubine Tao to miscarry would serve no purpose.

Madam Yuan nodded. "Chu’er has always been kind and magnanimous. She would never do something so cruel as to harm an unborn child."

Old Madam let out a cold laugh.

Yun Chu had indeed been kind before, but lately, she had grown increasingly harsh and difficult. Doing such a thing was not impossible.

At that moment, Concubine Tao called out from inside the house, "Old Madam, I know why the mistress wanted to harm the child in my womb..."

Old Madam had the door pushed open. Concubine Tao’s voice became clearer. "These past few days, the master has been sending me things, potted flowers, bolts of fabric, even jewelry and hairpieces. The mistress must have seen how attentive the master is to a mere concubine like me and feared that he would favor me over her. That’s why she acted against the child in my womb..."

Madam Yuan sighed.

Four or five years ago, when Chu’er was pregnant, Jingyu had indeed not been so attentive. It was no wonder Chu’er had grown jealous enough to do such a thing.

Tingyu pressed her lips together.

When she had been pregnant, she had hidden it from the mistress, fearing that the mistress might do something desperate. But in the end, her worries had been for nothing...

"Jealousy is one of the seven grounds for divorce." Old Madam’s face was filled with disappointment. "Chu’er, you are the legitimate eldest daughter of the Yun family, the mistress of the Xie household. How could you be so foolish?"

Yun Chu surveyed everyone in the courtyard, taking in all their expressions.

She smoothed her dark hair and spoke. "The Xie family is also a scholarly clan. Is it really so easy to convict someone based on mere words in a book?"

Her calm and detached demeanor made Old Madam feel a pang of irritation.

She preferred the Yun Chu from before, the one who had lost her child, the obedient and silent mistress, the granddaughter-in-law who could be molded at will.

She had to catch Yun Chu in the wrong this time to make her return to being an obedient and compliant daughter-in-law.

With that thought, she ordered, "Someone, go search Yushang Residence."

Madam Zhou bowed slightly to Yun Chu. "Mistress, this old servant must offend you."

With that, she led seven or eight servant women and maids toward Yushang Residence.

It wasn’t far, and soon, Madam Zhou returned, shaking her head. "Old Madam, we found nothing."

Old Madam frowned. "How could that be? Did you check the storeroom?"

Madam Zhou lowered her head. "That is the mistress’s dowry storeroom. Without the mistress’s permission, this old servant dare not..."

Old Madam’s expression darkened.

Perhaps Yun Chu had already disposed of the evidence...

"Even if you searched my dowry storeroom, you wouldn’t find what Old Madam wants, because—" Yun Chu paused, "you searched the wrong place."

Old Madam’s eyes narrowed. "What do you mean?"

Yun Chu looked toward the courtyard entrance. "Since Madam He has arrived, why is she standing outside?"

Madam He was startled.

She had been standing in the shadows where no one could easily spot her.

Yet, while the mistress was being questioned, she had somehow noticed her presence.

She lowered her head and stepped forward. "This servant was afraid that when the master returns and asks, I would have no answers, so I..."

Before she could finish, Yun Chu clapped her hands.

Tingshuang, who had been standing at the courtyard gate, entered with two people, a man dressed like a shopkeeper and a beggar boy of seven or eight years.

After they entered, they looked around at everyone present, and their gazes settled on Madam He.

In that moment, Madam He’s breath caught in her throat.

"It was her who gave me twenty copper coins and told me to buy medicine at Shande Hall." The beggar boy pointed at Madam He. "I’m very good at recognizing people. I couldn’t be wrong."

The shopkeeper-like man spoke. "Half an hour ago, this beggar boy came to my shop for medicine. He had no prescription, only the names of a few herbs. I gave him a little of each, including safflower."

As soon as these two spoke, everyone in the courtyard wore expressions of disbelief.

"It wasn’t me! He’s mistaken!" Madam He struggled to keep her composure. "I left the residence to buy an inkstone for the master. I beg Old Madam to investigate clearly."

Old Madam gripped her cane tightly. "Madam He is just a servant. She couldn’t possibly harm the master’s child. This is impossible."

Yun Chu’s voice was calm. "Of course I wouldn’t follow Old Madam’s example of accusing someone without evidence. Now we have witnesses. All that’s missing is physical evidence. Tingshuang, take a few people to search Madam He’s room thoroughly."

"Mother!" Xie Pin couldn’t help but speak up. "Madam He has been loyal to Father. She would never harm Father’s child. You won’t find anything even if you search."

Xie Shian stepped forward. "Madam He is Father’s trusted servant. If Mother searches her room without permission, I fear it will anger Father."

A faint smile curved Yun Chu’s lips. "I am Father’s lawfully wedded wife. Why would searching my courtyard anger him? Or is it that in Father’s eyes, a mere servant who manages the courtyard is more important than me, his legitimate wife?"

Xie Shian fell silent.

Yun Chu shook her head. "An’ge, you would rather believe a servant than your own mother. You’ve broken my heart."

She made a gesture.

Tingshuang immediately led people toward Madam He’s room.

No one in the courtyard spoke.

Old Madam clenched her cane tightly. Though the evidence had not yet been found, she already understood what had happened.

Her cloudy eyes, sharp as blades, raked over Madam He.

She truly had not expected Madam He to dare harm an unborn child and frame the mistress!

Back then, she should never have allowed Madam He to stay in the Xie household for the sake of An’ge and his siblings.

Tingshuang acted quickly. In less than a quarter of an hour, she returned with several people, presenting a few herbs. "These were found under Madam He’s bed."

The shopkeeper stepped forward and took a look. "Yes, the beggar boy asked for these herbs and safflower. I wouldn’t be mistaken."

"Thank you both for making this trip." Yun Chu took out two money pouches and handed them to the two. "As for today’s matter, consider it as if it never happened. Thank you."

The money was essentially a bribe for their silence. The shopkeeper and the beggar boy understood.

But after leaving the Xie residence, when they opened the pouches, they found only a few dozen copper coins. The shopkeeper’s expression changed. He hadn’t intended to gossip about the private affairs of a noble household, but to dismiss them with such a paltry sum was an insult...

---

chapters.title: Like Rain from the Heavens
chapters.content:
All the servants were dismissed from the courtyard.

Madam He stood in the middle, head bowed, repeatedly saying, "This servant truly did not do it. The evidence was planted..."

"It definitely wasn’t Madam He." Xie Pin spoke with difficulty. "Madam He is just a servant. Why would she harm Father’s child? There must be a mistake. It must be a misunderstanding!"

She clenched the handkerchief in her hand tightly, her heart filled with resentment.

She couldn’t understand. An’ge was already so old, the master’s most prized eldest son. An unborn illegitimate child posed no threat to An’ge’s position. Why would Madam He take such a risk?

Unless... it was because the master had been too attentive to Concubine Tao lately, and Madam He had grown jealous, leading her to do such a reckless thing?

Even if she was resentful, Xie Pin knew she had to protect Madam He. She couldn’t allow Madam He to be sold out of the household or sent to the authorities under such a serious charge...

Xie Pin gave Xie Shian a meaningful look.

Xie Shian pressed his lips tightly together.

Earlier, because he had trusted Madam He, he had hurt his mother’s feelings.

If he spoke up for Madam He now, his mother would be even more hurt and might never be close to him again.

Four years ago, Madam He had been allowed to stay in the Xie household to prevent Xie Pin and her siblings from being mistreated by their mother. But in reality, their mother had treated them as if they were her own.

Now that they were older, it wouldn’t be a problem to let Madam He leave the Xie household.

Over the years, he had used the silver given by his elders to purchase a small courtyard outside, which would be perfect for Madam He to live in.

Old Madam Xie took a deep breath. "Madam He indeed has no motive to harm the child. This matter needs to be investigated further."

Yun Chu raised her hand. "Because Madam He has no motive, you all think it isn’t her. If that’s the case, then let’s have someone present the motive."

Madam He froze.

What was her motive? Even she couldn’t say for sure.

Was it to prevent the children from being mistreated by the mistress? Or to secure An’ge’s position in the Xie household? Or was it simply jealousy toward the mistress?

Tingxue entered with a tray holding a dozen or so envelopes.

Yun Chu casually opened one and handed it to Xie Shian. "We found these while searching for the herbs. An’ge, why don’t you read it aloud?"

Xie Shian’s heart lurched.

Could it be that Madam He’s secret correspondence with outsiders had been discovered...

When his eyes fell on the words on the paper, his heart, which had been stuck in his throat, finally settled back into his stomach. He slowly read aloud, "You are like rain from the heavens, I am like a well beneath the eaves. With no way to flow together, I wish to be your shadow..."

Everyone in the courtyard was literate enough to understand. This was a love poem written by a woman to a man.

Xie Shian’s voice caught in his throat. He couldn’t read any further. His face turned a mottled red, a truly spectacular sight.

Yun Chu spoke. "If we compare this with Madam He’s usual handwriting, we’ll see that this letter was written by her. As for whom it was written to, look at the very beginning, it addresses someone as ‘Yu Lang.’ I need not say more. Old Madam, Madam, you must know who Yu Lang is."

Madam Yuan looked as if she had swallowed a fly, utterly disgusted. "Madam He, how dare you have such filthy thoughts..."

Concubine Jiang covered her mouth. "No wonder Madam He has never married, even at her age. So that’s the reason..."

"Madam He, you’re not even a concubine! What right do you have to be jealous? And to harm an unborn child!" Concubine Tao wailed from inside the house. "If anything happens to my child, I will never let you off!"

Madam He suddenly raised her head, looking toward Yun Chu.

She suddenly realized, this was all a trap.

When she had acted against Concubine Tao, the mistress had already known of her plan and had people watching her. That was how she had obtained the witnesses and evidence so quickly.

Had the mistress discovered the letter she had written to the master, feared her presence, and set this trap to ensnare her?

With all the evidence laid out before her, she had no way to refute it.

"Madam He, as a servant, it’s bad enough that you harbor improper feelings for your master, but to poison an unborn child!" Yun Chu spoke each word deliberately. "The Xie family cannot keep you. Someone, take Madam He to the authorities!"

"Mother!" Xie Shian clenched his fists. "This is, after all, a family matter. If it becomes public knowledge, it will be a scandal. Father’s evaluation is coming up soon. It’s best not to create unnecessary complications."

Yun Chu looked at him. "Then, An’ge, what do you suggest we do with Madam He?"

Xie Shian unclenched his fists. "Perhaps we should just send her away."

"But she almost killed the child in my womb! Is sending her away enough?" Concubine Tao’s voice rang out. "Even if we can’t report her to the authorities, we can’t let her off so easily! Old Madam, Madam, Mistress, I beg you to seek justice for the child in my womb!"

Old Madam’s temples throbbed with visible veins.

This Madam He was truly a troublesome creature. Sending her away would be for the best.

But was sending her away really the best solution? Such a shameless woman; she should never have been involved in the first place...

Yun Chu turned to Old Madam. "Where is Madam He’s contract of servitude?"

Old Madam didn’t know how to respond.

Because Madam He didn’t have a contract of servitude. On the surface, she was a servant of the Xie household, but in reality, she was a free woman...

"Wait until Jingyu returns and ask for his opinion." Old Madam closed her eyes. "For now, have Madam He confined. Everyone else, disperse."

Yun Chu turned and left with the people of Yushang Residence.

After everyone had dispersed, Old Madam picked up her cane and struck Madam He’s back with force. "Back then, I allowed you to enter the household as a concubine, but you refused. And now, you write such disgusting things! I was kind enough to let you stay in the Xie household, to let you stay by An’ge’s side. How dare you harm the Xie family’s child? Who gave you the audacity!"

She struck again with her cane.

Xie Shian blocked the blow for Madam He and knelt to the ground with a thud. "Great-Grandmother, please let my mother go..."

"No, I won’t leave!" Madam He sobbed. "If I leave, what will happen to my three children? I’d rather die than leave the Xie household..."

Old Madam seethed. "Do you want to become a concubine to Jingyu at your age?"

"No, I don’t want to be a concubine either." Madam He prostrated herself on the ground. "Old Madam, as long as I can stay in the Xie household, I will accept any punishment!"

Old Madam wished she could beat Madam He to death.

She refused to leave, refused to be a concubine, and couldn’t be sent to the authorities. So what was to be done with her?

Xie Pin snapped angrily, "If you want to stay in the Xie household, then behave yourself and stop causing trouble for us! If people find out you’re our real mother, how will An’ge, Wu’ge, and I face the world!"

Xie Shian spoke each word deliberately. "I can persuade Father to let you stay in the Xie household. But remember, this is your only chance."

chapters.title: Missing the Children
chapters.content:
The night deepened.

After finishing the last account book, Yun Chu looked up toward the door and, as expected, saw Xie Jingyu enter.

He was dressed in official robes, clearly having just returned home from his duties without even changing clothes before being summoned by the old madam, then coming straight to her.

"Has my husband come regarding the matter of He Shi?" Yun Chu stood up. "He Shi nearly took a life. Not sending her to the authorities is already an act of mercy from the Xie family. I hope my husband does not break Aunt Tao's heart."

Xie Jingyu's face was filled with exhaustion. He took a sip of the clear tea Ling Shuang had served, his voice hoarse. "An Ge, Ping Jie, and Wei Ge were raised by her. If we sell her off, I fear it will leave a thorn in the hearts of the three children..."

Yun Chu scoffed. "Does my husband not fear that the child in Aunt Tao's womb will have a thorn in its heart?"

Xie Jingyu fell silent.

Could an unborn child be compared to An Ge?

An Ge was his eldest son, just like him when he was young, exceptionally talented in his studies. One could even say he had surpassed his father.

The future of the Xie family depended on An Ge.

"Then how about this," Yun Chu said with a smile. "Since the children care so much for He Shi, and my husband trusts her so deeply, let her become Concubine He."

Xie Jingyu's expression changed. "I have no such intentions toward her. My lady, do not joke."

Yun Chu's gaze darkened.

At this point, the best solution would be for Xie Jingyu to admit to a secret affair with He Shi to protect her.

But Xie Jingyu had firmly refused to make He Shi a concubine?

Could it be that he wanted to wait until she died, then let He Shi directly become the mistress of the household?

But would someone who aspired to be the mistress of the household be willing to remain a servant until then?

"There is a small temple in the southeast corner of the Xie residence. Let He Shi take refuge there," Xie Jingyu said, rubbing his temples. "I will confine her there. She is not to set foot outside the temple for three years."

Yun Chu pretended to hesitate before nodding after a long while. "Then we shall follow my husband's suggestion."

From the very beginning, she had never intended to drive He Shi out of the Xie family.

Only by keeping He Shi under her watch, forcing her into a corner, could she uncover what she wanted to know.

"Thank you, my lady," Xie Jingyu said, his eyes on her. "You have worked so hard for the Xie family. This husband is deeply grateful."

He took a step forward, approaching Yun Chu, about to place his hand on her shoulder.

Suddenly, Yun Chu stepped back, avoiding his touch.

The scene of her frantically washing her hands that day flashed through his mind. Once again, he realized, she despised him.

That was why she could so easily suggest he take He Shi as a concubine.

This realization filled Xie Jingyu with an indescribable emotion.

He withdrew his hand and said gently, "I heard the Empress is ill and is seeking a divine physician to treat her. If the opportunity arises, I will invite the physician to diagnose you and see if your infertility can be cured."

Yun Chu lowered her gaze. "I am probably fated to be childless. My husband need not trouble himself."

Perhaps because Xie Jingyu had mentioned children, that night she dreamed of two children.

A boy and a girl, both four years old, fair and delicate, surrounding her and calling her "Mother." The happiness overflowed from the dream.

But it did not last long. The two children suddenly disappeared.

The white mist around them turned into a red blood mist.

"Mother, why don’t you want us anymore!"

"Mother, I miss you so much. Come pick us up, please!"

"Mother, it’s so cold here..."

Their cries echoed in her ears.

Yun Chu’s heart shattered. "Children, where are you? Tell Mother where you are..."

The children’s cries gradually faded away.

Yun Chu abruptly opened her eyes and sat up straight.

She looked outside; it was pitch black. It was just past midnight.

In these four years, she had never dreamed of her two deceased children. But recently, this was the second time.

In her past life, she had lived into her thirties. What couldn’t she let go of? She should have moved on, should have learned to face it. She should go see her children...

Yun Chu leaned against the headboard, sitting in silence until dawn.

Ling Shuang entered quietly and was startled to see her fully dressed and sitting at the edge of the bed. "My lady, when did you wake up? Why didn’t you call for this servant to attend to you?"

She hurriedly began to comb Yun Chu’s hair.

Sitting in front of the mirror, Yun Chu asked softly, "Where were my two children buried?"

Ling Shuang’s hand trembled, and the comb fell to the floor.

She quickly picked it up and whispered, "My lady, it’s all in the past. Please don’t dwell on it. Overthinking will harm your health..."

"The Qingming Festival is approaching," Yun Chu said with a smile. "I want to see my children, let them know what their mother looks like. I want to talk to them..."

Ling Shuang lowered her head. "After the young master and young miss passed away, it was the master who ordered their burial. This servant does not know the exact location."

Yun Chu felt a pang of sorrow.

After the children’s deaths, she had been unable to face it and dared not ask about the aftermath. Now, she wanted to see them but didn’t even know where to go.

She was such an unworthy mother.

No wonder the children had come to her in dreams...

After the morning greetings from the concubines, Yun Chu went directly to the old madam’s courtyard.

Madam Yuan thought she had come about last night’s matter and sighed. "That He Shi has been with Jingyu for many years. Jingyu kept her in the residence out of old feelings. From now on, she will be a nun in our family temple. She won’t cause any trouble. Don’t take it to heart."

Yun Chu said, "Mother, I came for another matter. Four years ago, my two children who were stillborn; do you know where they were buried?"

"Why bring up something from four years ago?" Seeing the redness in her eyes, Madam Yuan softened her voice. "I heard Jingyu say that the Empress is seeking a divine physician who specializes in treating women’s illnesses. Once that physician arrives in the capital, Jingyu will find a way to meet him. Maybe he can cure your condition..."

Yun Chu’s voice was bitter. "Mother, I just want to see my deceased children."

Madam Yuan sighed. "According to custom, children who have not come of age cannot be buried in the ancestral tomb, nor can a stele be erected. Too much attention might prevent them from reincarnating. Jingyu had He Shi take the children’s remains back to the Xie family’s old residence and bury them somewhere. If you want to see them, I can arrange for two servants to make the trip."

Yun Chu clenched her sleeves.

Her children had been buried by He Shi’s own hands.

The children had said it was cold in the dream; where had they been buried to feel such cold?

Her heart felt as if it were being torn apart by a knife, the pain unbearable.

Guilt, regret, remorse, all kinds of emotions surged within her.

Leaving Madam Yuan’s courtyard, Yun Chu went straight to the front courtyard and ordered a carriage to return to the Yun family.

The Xie residence was in the southern part of the city, while the Yun residence was in the prime area near the imperial palace. Because they were separated by half the capital, Yun Chu did not visit often.

In her past life, she had caused the deaths of over a hundred people in the Yun family. After reincarnating, she was ashamed before her family and had never thought of returning...

---

chapters.title: How Do You Want to Live
chapters.content:
The carriage stopped at the gate of the General’s Mansion.

"Eldest Miss!"

"It’s Eldest Miss returning!"

The two guards at the gate, upon seeing her, bowed and then ran inside to report.

As soon as Yun Chu entered, her mother, Lady Lin, and her sister-in-law, Liu Qianqian, came out to greet her.

Lady Lin took her hand, delighted. "Chu’er, why didn’t you send word that you were coming?"

"Your mother was just talking about you a few days ago," Liu Qianqian said with a smile. "If your elder brother knew you were coming today, he would have canceled all his engagements to be here."

At the mention of her elder brother, Yun Chu’s eyes suddenly reddened.

Their Yun family had been military for generations. Their great-grandfather had died on the battlefield. By their grandfather’s generation, only their grandfather remained. Their father had been injured defending the front lines.

Because many men of the Yun family had perished in war, by her elder brother’s generation, he was forbidden from learning martial arts. Instead, he pursued scholarly studies. Last year, he had passed the imperial examinations as a third-class scholar and was now a seventh-rank official in the court.

When the Yun family was accused of treason, her elder brother was the first to know. He immediately submitted a petition to defend the Yun family but was thrown into prison.

The day after her elder brother was imprisoned, word came from the prison to retrieve his body.

She hadn’t even seen her elder brother one last time...

"Why are you crying?" Lady Lin was startled. "Chu’er, has someone from the Xie family wronged you?"

Only then did Yun Chu realize her face was wet with tears. She hastily wiped them with her sleeve and threw herself into Lady Lin’s arms. "Mother, I haven’t been home for so long. I missed you, I missed home..."

"You silly child, if you miss home, just come home," Lady Lin said, patting her back. "Though there’s a saying that a married daughter shouldn’t visit often, the Xie family can’t control us. From now on, every few days, I’ll send someone to the Xie residence to bring you back."

Feeling the comforting presence of her mother, Yun Chu’s emotions gradually settled.

The Yun family’s downfall was still more than ten years away. In this life, such a thing would never happen. She need not grieve.

Her voice hoarse, she said, "I want to see Grandfather."

In his youth, Old General Yun had fought on the battlefield, his body covered in injuries. Now old, his legs were not as strong, and he spent most of his time lying in bed.

Originally, the old general could have retired with honor, but in the end, to prove his innocence, he had used the very sword he had wielded against the enemy to cut his own throat.

"Chu’er is back," the old general said, half-reclining on the bed. A smile on his face made the scar there more pronounced. "Come here, let your grandfather test if you still remember any moves."

Yun Chu felt a pang of guilt. "Grandfather, please spare me."

When she was young, the old general, injured and unable to return to the battlefield, spent most of his time at home. Her elder brother had to study, so the old general had focused on teaching her martial arts.

But she had been a playful child, unable to sit still. Back then, her grandmother was still alive and often protected her, forbidding the old general from teaching her.

So she had learned in fits and starts, barely mastering a few moves, and after marriage, she had forgotten them all.

"A person must have some skills to rely on," the old general said. "People can walk away, mountains can collapse, and money can be spent. Only talent and martial arts ingrained in your bones will stay with you for life."

"I’m sorry, Grandfather. I was too immature before," Yun Chu looked up. "Can Grandfather arrange someone to teach me martial arts?"

The old general studied her. "Are you serious, or just trying to make your grandfather happy?"

Yun Chu pouted. "Even if it’s to make you happy, I have to learn properly. Then, every few days, I’ll come to spar with you. You mustn’t find me annoying."

The old general laughed heartily and promised to find a suitable person to send to the Xie residence within three days.

Yun Chu had a meal with her family, then sat in the flower hall with her mother and sister-in-law, chatting about recent events, feeling quite cheerful.

Lady Lin sighed. "Your sister, Ran’er, was ill a couple of years ago, which delayed her marriage. Now she’s already seventeen. If we don’t find her a match soon, she’ll become an old maid."

Liu Qianqian said, "Tomorrow’s flower-appreciation banquet hosted by Princess Zhang will actually be a gathering for the major families in the capital to look for matches. At that time, we can find a good family for Ran’er. Mother need not worry about this."

Yun Chu’s fingers paused.

Yun Ran was her half-sister, but her birth mother had died in childbirth, so she had been raised by Lady Lin. They were as close as full sisters.

Because her half-sister had been frail, her illness two years ago had delayed her marriage. Now, with her age advancing, she had made a hasty and poor decision in choosing a match.

"Mother, can I go to the flower-appreciation banquet with you?" Yun Chu asked. "Since becoming Madam Xie, I haven’t seen my old friends in a long time."

As the wife of a fifth-rank official, she no longer moved in the same circles as the daughters of second and third-rank officials.

For example, Princess Zhang’s flower-appreciation banquet would certainly not invite her.

She could only tag along with the Yun family’s invitation.

Lady Lin nodded. "That’s fine. You can also help me look at the two families I’ve selected for your half-sister and give your opinion."

As they spoke, Yun Ze returned.

Yun Ze was the eldest young master of the Yun family, four years older than Yun Chu. Last year, at the age of twenty-three, he had passed the imperial examinations as a third-class scholar. In the entire capital, this was not particularly outstanding.

But Yun Chu knew her brother was excellent. He could have passed the examinations at eighteen and at least become a second-place scholar, but fearing the emperor’s suspicion toward the Yun family, he had deliberately waited five years before taking the exams...

"Your elder brother is back. You two siblings can chat for a while," Lady Lin stood up. "Qianqian, come with me to the kitchen to check on the refreshments."

She knew her daughter had returned this time for something important; otherwise, she wouldn’t have waited so long.

Yun Chu was indeed waiting for Yun Ze to return.

"Elder Brother, there’s something I need your help with," she said, pressing her lips together. "Can you arrange for someone to go to Ji Zhou?"

"Ji Zhou? Isn’t that where the Xie family’s ancestral home is?" Yun Ze looked at her. "Has something happened?"

Yun Chu lowered her head. "I dreamed of my deceased children. They said it was so cold... The children died at birth and couldn’t be buried in the Xie family’s ancestral tomb. They were buried in a random place in the old home. I want to ask Elder Brother to arrange for someone to bring the children’s remains back to the capital. I... I want to rebury my two children properly..."

Xie Jingyu had living children and would not care about two dead ones, so this matter she could only entrust to her elder brother.

"Don’t tell Mother and Grandfather," she whispered. "I don’t want to worry them... Elder Brother, don’t worry about me either. I just want to give the children a proper burial. Please fulfill this wish for me."

Yun Ze sighed.

He reached out and, as he had when they were young, ruffled her hair. His voice was gentle. "There’s been flooding in Ji Zhou. The court is about to send someone there. I’ll go myself to bring back my nephews and find a good feng shui burial site for them."

Yun Chu choked back a sob. "Thank you, Elder Brother."

"Chu’er, remember this: the Yun family will always be your strongest support. If the Xie family has wronged you, we can always divorce. It’s not your fault that you can’t have children. Don’t let this make you feel inferior in the Xie family. You are the eldest daughter of the Yun family, my proudest sister, the apple of our parents’ eyes. However you want to live, that’s how you should live."

As she left the Yun family and sat in the carriage, Yun Chu burst into tears.

chapters.title: The Grand Princess's Banquet
chapters.content:
Yun Chu let the carriage circle the streets twice before returning to the Xie residence.

Except for the slight redness around her eyes, there was no trace of her earlier sobbing.

As soon as she returned to the courtyard, Tingfeng entered to report, "Madam, after you returned to the General's residence, the eldest young lady secretly visited the ruined temple and delivered many things to He Mama..."

The madam treated the eldest young lady as her own daughter. She didn't understand why the eldest young lady would be so kind to a servant who had framed the madam...

Yun Chu sat on the couch and ordered, "Have Xie Pin come see me."

Since taking over some of the household affairs, Xie Pin had been busy, either reviewing account books or summoning the servants from the outer courtyard for reports.

While she was busy, she saw Tingxue come to invite her over.

Normally, it was she who took the initiative to see her mother; her mother had never sent a maid to summon her before.

Xie Pin put down the account book, feeling somewhat uneasy.

Could it be that her mother had found out she had sent things to He and was calling her to question?

If she had known, she shouldn't have softened her heart and gone to see He. Now, how could she explain this to her mother?

All the way there, Xie Pin's mind was filled with various thoughts.

Upon entering the Sheng Ju, she saw Yun Chu looking at her with a smile, "Xie Pin, sit."

Xie Pin sat down and took a sip of tea.

"Tomorrow is the Grand Princess's flower-appreciation banquet. Do you have time to accompany me?" Yun Chu asked with a smile, "If you don't want to go, it's fine."

Xie Pin could hardly believe it. Suppressing her excitement, she asked, "Did the Grand Princess invite Mother?"

Yun Chu shook her head, "The Grand Princess invited the Yun family. Your grandmother invited me to go with her. If you want to go, having one more person is fine. It's a good opportunity to see the world."

Xie Pin nodded firmly, "I'm willing to go."

Her father was a fifth-rank official. The young ladies she usually associated with were daughters of fifth or sixth-rank officials. At the Grand Princess's flower-appreciation banquet, most of the attendees would be wives and daughters of officials ranked third class and above.

Following her mother, she would definitely meet many noble ladies.

If she behaved cleverly and sensibly, those noble ladies might even consider her as a potential daughter-in-law...

At this thought, Xie Pin couldn't wait any longer. She stood up, "Mother, I'll go prepare now."

Watching her departing figure, a cold smile appeared on Yun Chu's lips.

In her previous life, at the spring banquet hosted by the Yun family, Xie Pin had met the Fourth Prince for the first time and fallen in love at first sight.

A fifth-rank official's daughter and the current Fourth Prince had absolutely no chance together. Even becoming a concubine would be out of her league. So, Xie Pin had come up with a foolish idea. She had found an opportunity and, while the Fourth Prince was not paying attention, she had drugged him, trying to force a marriage...

It was she who had accidentally discovered Xie Pin's scheme and prevented the farce from happening.

Not long after this incident, the Fourth Prince had met with a disaster...

She had arranged a good family for Xie Pin.

Although the man was only a seventh-rank minor official, his family was upright and had a promising future. However, Xie Pin had not been interested at all. Just as the marriage was about to be settled, Xie Pin had used the excuse of entering the palace to pay respects to her aunt. She had met the Emperor and then... become a new favorite of the Emperor...

The so-called aunt was Yun Chu's own aunt, who had been selected to enter the palace and was one of the Four Consorts, having given birth to the Eighth Prince for the Emperor.

Xie Pin had stepped on her own aunt to become the Emperor's favored concubine.

In her previous life, her aunt had suffered greatly at Xie Pin's hands...

Recalling the events of her past life, Yun Chu's expression turned sorrowful.

Given a second chance, she would not allow Xie Pin to enter the palace again, nor would she let her aunt be threatened by Xie Pin...

Xie Pin liked the Fourth Prince, didn't she? Then she would let her become the Fourth Prince's consort. The glory of being the Fourth Prince's consort would be as short-lived as it was honorable...

The night passed quietly.

At dawn, after Yun Chu had finished her morning routine, Xie Shian was already waiting to pay his respects.

"The imperial examinations are approaching. You don't need to come pay respects during this time," Yun Chu said gently. "Study hard and strive to bring honor to the Xie family."

Xie Shian cupped his hands, "Paying respects is part of filial piety. Propriety cannot be abandoned. Mother, rest assured. I am very confident about the imperial examinations. Becoming a Xiucai is not difficult."

Yun Chu knew he was not boasting.

Not only had he passed the Xiucai examination, but he had also ranked first as the top scholar. The following year, he took the provincial examination and again ranked first as the Jieyuan. Two years later, in the metropolitan examination, he once again took first place, becoming the Huiyuan. Immediately after, in the palace examination, he was personally selected by the Emperor as the Zhuangyuan.

He was the only one in the current dynasty to have achieved the rare feat of topping all three levels of the imperial examinations, and he was also the youngest Zhuangyuan...

With Xie Shian entering the cabinet, Xie Pin becoming a favored concubine in the palace, and Xie Shiyou joining the military, the Xie family's future momentum would be unstoppable...

After Xie Shian left, the people from the inner residence came to pay their respects.

Yun Chu's gaze fell on Xie Pin. She spoke indifferently, "Go back and change your clothes. Tingshuang, you go help her with her hair and makeup."

Xie Pin was somewhat at a loss, "Mother, what's wrong with my clothes?"

"Eldest Young Lady, your clothes are too gaudy," Tingyu said softly. Having stayed in the General's residence for so many years, she naturally understood these things. She continued, "The Grand Princess's flower-appreciation banquet is meant for appreciating flowers, not for young ladies to compete in beauty..."

Yun Chu spoke, "It's normal for Xie Pin to not understand these things since it's her first time attending a banquet with me. Go back and change into something else."

Tingshuang accompanied Xie Pin back to her courtyard and selected a light pink spring dress for her. She styled her hair in a simple bun, inserting a single jade hairpin at an angle and adorning her with a pair of pearl earrings the size of rice grains.

Xie Pin pursed her lips, "Isn't this too plain?"

Tingshuang lowered her hands, "Madam is attending the Grand Princess's residence under the Yun family's name, so naturally, we should be more low-key. This is the appropriate attire."

Xie Pin felt somewhat displeased.

Dressed so plainly, no one in the crowd would notice her. How could she make connections with the wives and young ladies of noble families?

But her mother had already given the order. If she insisted on doing things her own way, she might not be allowed to attend the Grand Princess's flower-appreciation banquet.

Yun Chu took Xie Pin in a carriage to the Yun residence first. After meeting up with the Yun family, they headed to the Grand Princess's residence together.

The Grand Princess was the Emperor's sister, sharing the same mother. She was a leading figure in the noble ladies' circle in the capital. Her banquets were almost always packed with guests.

The carriage stopped at the entrance.

Yun Chu helped Lin Shi alight.

Behind them followed two unmarried young ladies: the second young lady of the General's residence, Yun Han, and the eldest young lady of the Xie residence, Xie Pin.

The four of them walked in. There was no need to present an invitation; as soon as Lin Shi stood there, the servant at the door announced, "The General's madam has arrived!"

Immediately, a matron came out to greet them and led Yun Chu's group inside.

It was Xie Pin's first time visiting such a high-ranking residence. She looked left and right, unable to get enough of the sights.

Lin Shi frowned and reminded her in a low voice, "Xie Pin, why are you being so improper? Later, I'll have Qi Mama go to the Xie residence to teach you some manners."

Yun Chu smiled in response, "Such a small matter is not worth troubling Mother over."

If someone was going to lose face, it would be the Xie family. She had no reason to maintain the Xie family's reputation.

However, since Xie Pin had come with the Yun family this time, she had to give some guidance to avoid the Yun family being laughed at.

Yun Chu gave Tingshuang a look.

Tingshuang took a step back and walked to Xie Pin's side, reminding her softly.

---

chapters.title: Going Out for Some Air
chapters.content:
Yun Chu followed Lin Shi into the Grand Princess's residence.

By this time, many guests had already arrived in the courtyard. As soon as they entered, many people came forward to exchange greetings.

"Madam Yun, it's been a while since we last saw you."

"Is this Sister Chu? In the blink of an eye, she's grown so much. Time truly spares no one."

"And this must be Sister Han. If I recall correctly, she should be sixteen years old now. She's grown up to be so graceful and elegant."

The Yun family was a first-rank General's residence. The old General had achieved countless military merits, and the current General was stationed at the border. The Yun family's position in the court was unshakable.
