It was no wonder that so many people came forward to greet them.

These people spoke to Lin Shi with a touch of flattery, but when their gaze fell on Yun Chu, it carried a hint of sympathy.

The legitimate daughter of the General's residence had married into a humble family, and to make matters worse, she had lost the qualification to be a mother. As a result, she had no choice but to raise her stepchildren under her own name.

A madam's gaze fell on Xie Pin, "And who is this?"

Lin Shi smiled, "This is my granddaughter."

Xie Pin stepped forward and slightly curtsied, which served as her greeting to everyone.

The people present all showed surprised expressions.

They only knew that the General's legitimate daughter had raised a group of stepchildren and stepdaughters under her name, but they didn't know that the stepdaughter was already this grown up.

She was only half a finger shorter than Yun Chu. If it weren't for the youthful innocence still visible on her face, she would look like two sisters of similar age.

The sympathy in their eyes grew even stronger.

Lin Shi felt a lump of anger in her chest. Back then, she had married her daughter to a humble family for two reasons: first, to avoid the Emperor's suspicion, and second, because Xie Jingyu was indeed a good match.

But who could have anticipated that Xie Jingyu already had three children before the marriage... If it weren't for Chu losing the qualification to be a mother, she would have made trouble for the Xie family no matter what...

Lin Shi gave the crowd a faint smile and led Yun Chu in another direction.

"Chu, do you see those two madams over there?" Lin Shi asked. "One is Madam Zhang. Her husband is a seventh-rank Imperial Academy scholar. Her eldest legitimate son just passed the Xiucai examination last year. I've met that child; he knows his place and is quite good. The other is Madam Qian. Her husband is a fourth-rank Minister of Rites. She has two legitimate sons who are already married, and only one step-son of marriageable age..."

Upon hearing this, Xie Pin looked up in surprise.

She had been listening to Lin Shi and Yun Chu's conversation on the way, so she naturally knew that the main purpose of coming to the Grand Princess's residence was to find a suitable match for Yun Han.

Yun Han was, after all, the young lady of a first-rank General's residence. Listening to what Madam Yun was looking for, a Xiucai from a seventh-rank family and a step-son from a fourth-rank family, in her opinion, even a legitimate son from a fourth-rank family would not be a good match for the young lady of a first-rank General's residence.

But then, she thought, even the General's legitimate daughter, her own birth mother, had only married into the Xie family. With that in mind, it seemed acceptable.

Yun Chu's gaze fell on Madam Qian's face. In her previous life, this Madam Qian had been Yun Han's mother-in-law.

As for how Yun Han's husband was, that was another matter. But the evils committed by this Madam Qian were endless; ten days and nights would not be enough to recount them all.

Her stepsister had a gentle nature and was constantly tormented by Madam Qian's rules and discipline until she was unrecognizable.

In the fourth year after her marriage, when she had just become pregnant and no one knew, she was punished by her mother-in-law to kneel in the cold snow for three hours. Not only did she lose the child, but she also contracted a serious illness. She was bedridden for three or four years before she passed away...

"The Qian family is out of the question," Yun Chu said. "As for the Zhang family, we need to investigate further before making a decision."

Lin Shi had her heart set on the Qian family and couldn't help but ask, "Why?"

Yun Chu shook her head, "Mother, send someone to investigate Madam Qian, and you'll understand."

Lin Shi had originally planned to take Yun Han to meet Madam Qian. After hearing Yun Chu's words, she immediately abandoned this idea. The four of them took their seats.

As soon as they sat down, they saw the Grand Princess arrive.

Beside the Grand Princess were two men dressed in magnificent clothes: the Third Prince, Prince Pingxi, and the Fourth Prince, Prince Anjing.

Everyone stood up together to pay their respects.

"Greetings to the Grand Princess, Prince Pingxi, and Prince Anjing!"

The Grand Princess smiled and raised her hand, "There's no need for formalities at my residence. Please, everyone be seated."

The noble ladies who had come to the banquet all understood that the Grand Princess's banquet this time was likely mainly to find suitable princess consorts for Prince Pingxi and Prince Anjing.

Although Prince Pingxi had achieved remarkable military merits, because he already had a pair of children, he was not the first choice in everyone's minds. Therefore, everyone's gaze was eagerly fixed on Prince Anjing.

"Old Third, why did you bring Yu Ge here?" The Grand Princess looked at Prince Pingxi with some annoyance. "Are you afraid that people don't know you have a son, or that some madam might want to marry her daughter to you?"

Prince Pingxi picked up his wine cup and took a sip, "He insisted on coming. What could I do?"

The Grand Princess's gaze fell on the delicate and exquisite child. If it weren't for the fact that the child's eyebrows and eyes were exactly like Old Third's, she might not have felt the slightest liking for him.

"Yu Ge," the Grand Princess called out, "are you looking for someone?"

Chu Hongyu quickly withdrew his gaze and put on a harmless smile, "Royal Aunt, I just think it's lively here. Can I go play?"

"Then go play," the Grand Princess said, pointing to a matron beside her. "Be careful and follow the little worldly grandson. Don't bump into anything or fall."

The little fellow, having received permission, trotted off with his short legs.

Yun Chu's gaze involuntarily fell on the little fellow. Only when the child disappeared down the path did she realize she had been staring at him for a long time.

"Prince Pingxi went to war with your father when he was fifteen," Lin Shi said in a low voice. "He has always been a steady child. I don't know how he suddenly ended up with a pair of children. The mother of the children is unknown, and they were even made the worldly grandson. The great families in the capital probably won't easily marry their daughters to become Prince Pingxi's consort..."

Yun Chu nodded in strong agreement.

In her previous life, until she died, Prince Pingxi had never married.

Great families were unwilling to have their daughters marry him and become stepmothers, and the daughters of small families were beneath Prince Pingxi's notice.

As Yun Chu spoke with Lin Shi, she noticed out of the corner of her eye that Xie Pin's gaze was fixed on Prince Anjing, who was seated at the highest position.

She curled her lips slightly. Sure enough, just like in her previous life, Xie Pin had fallen in love with the Fourth Prince at first sight.

At this moment, the Fourth Prince suddenly stood up and left his seat.

Yun Chu sensed that Xie Pin was starting to get restless.

Since that was the case, she would give her a push.

She put down her chopsticks, "Mother, I feel a bit stifled here. I want to go out for some air."

Lin Shi quickly said, "Are you feeling unwell? I'll tell the Grand Princess, and we can leave now."

"Going out for some air will be enough," Yun Chu stood up. "Xie Pin can accompany me for a walk. We'll be back soon, Mother. There's no need to worry."

A look of joy appeared on Xie Pin's face.

Yun Chu took Xie Pin away from the table, with Tingshuang following behind them.

As soon as they reached a nearby courtyard, Xie Pin exclaimed, "Mother, my earring fell off. What should I do?"

Tingshuang lowered her head, "This slave will go back and look for it for the eldest young lady."

"How could I trouble Sister Tingshuang?" Xie Pin said. "It probably fell among the flowers and plants. I can look for it myself."

This time at the Grand Princess's residence, only Lin Shi and Yun Chu had each brought one maid. Xie Pin had no one to attend to her, so she went back alone to search.

Tingshuang felt this was somewhat inappropriate and was about to speak when she saw Yun Chu shake her head. She swallowed the words she was about to say.

chapters.title: Just Want to See Her
chapters.content:
After Xie Pin’s figure disappeared.

Yun Chu took Tingshuang to the crossroads and stood there admiring the flowers.

If someone came, she would know immediately, so no one would see Xie Pin trying to flirt with the prince.

She had gone to such lengths; she hoped Xie Pin wouldn’t disappoint her.

The begonia flowers were vibrant. As Yun Chu admired them, she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her ankle. She looked down and saw a small stone rolling away.

Tingshuang looked in the direction of the stone: "Who’s hiding there?"

A green, broad leaf rustled, and a short little figure emerged.

Yun Chu’s face showed disbelief.

It was actually the young heir of Prince Pingxi’s mansion.

The little fellow held a slingshot in one hand and a handful of smooth, round stones in the other.

He straightened his body, placed a stone in the slingshot, and aimed it at Yun Chu’s face.

Tingshuang quickly stepped in front of Yun Chu.

"Hmph!" The little fellow was furious. "You promised to compensate me for the cricket. Where is it?"

Yun Chu: "..."

Why was the cricket matter still not settled?

"You liar! You don’t keep your word!" The little fellow released the slingshot.

A stone whizzed toward Yun Chu but missed, landing in the grass by the roadside.

"Little Prince." Yun Chu took two steps forward, crouched down in front of him, and said calmly, "Three crickets have been sent to Prince Pingxi’s mansion, but the young prince wasn’t satisfied. Why doesn’t the young prince just say what kind of cricket he really wants?"

Chu Hongyu tightened his lips.

He didn’t want any cricket. He just wanted to see this woman.

He had schemed to follow his father to the flower-viewing banquet, originally planning to slip away unnoticed to find her.

Who would have thought that this woman would also be at Her Highness the Grand Princess’s residence?

His luck was truly good.

Seeing the little fellow remain silent, Yun Chu pondered for a moment: "Then I’ll give the young prince a one-of-a-kind cricket."

She walked to the roadside, picked two long, slender leaves, and quickly folded them. In no time, a green cricket appeared in her palm.

She held it out to the little fellow: "Do you like it?"

Chu Hongyu’s eyes widened: "How are you so amazing? Can you teach me?"

"It’s simple." Yun Chu patiently explained, "Place the two leaves like this, overlap them, then fold them this way, and then..."

In just a few words, the second cricket was folded.

Chu Hongyu followed Yun Chu’s steps, but what he ended up with didn’t look like a cricket; it looked more like a dog...

She couldn’t help but laugh.

"Don’t laugh!" The little fellow was annoyed. He picked two more leaves and continued practicing, determined not to stop until he learned.

Just then, a wet nurse hurried down the path: "Young Prince, this old servant has finally found you!"

Chu Hongyu’s face darkened: "I told you not to follow me. Why are you still looking for me? Go away!"

The old wet nurse bowed deeply as she approached, respectfully asking, "This old servant dares to ask, was it the Young Prince who shot the goldfish in the Clear Flower Pond?"

The little fellow’s expression suddenly changed. He humphed and continued fiddling with the leaves in his hands.

His attitude made it clear. The wet nurse bowed even lower: "Those goldfish were brought from the south at great expense by Her Highness the Grand Princess. If they died like this, Her Highness will surely demand an explanation... Please, Young Prince, come with this old servant and explain to Her Highness."

Chu Hongyu plopped down on the ground: "I won’t go. I’m not going."

The wet nurse was nearly in tears. Two goldfish had died. Not only would the maidservants who fed them suffer, but she, the wet nurse in charge of the Young Prince, would also be punished...

"Virtue lies not in being faultless, but in being able to correct one’s mistakes." Yun Chu’s voice was gentle. "Does the Young Prince understand what this means?"

Chu Hongyu shook his head in confusion. Although his father had hired tutors to teach him, he often fell asleep in class and hadn’t learned much.

"A person isn’t the best just because they make no mistakes. What’s truly precious is knowing one’s mistakes and correcting them." Yun Chu looked at him steadily. "If the death of the Grand Princess’s goldfish is related to the Young Prince, and the Young Prince bravely admits his mistake, I think the Grand Princess won’t blame him."

Chu Hongyu pursed his lips.

The Grand Princess certainly wouldn’t blame him. The problem was, his father was also there...

He looked up and met Yun Chu’s gaze. Under such a gentle look, he felt a pang of shame.

He stood up: "Let’s go, wet nurse."

The wet nurse looked at Yun Chu with immense gratitude: "Thank you, Madam."

Yun Chu glanced at the end of the path and saw Xie Pin emerge from the depths of the woods, her face flushed, the very picture of a lovestruck girl.

"Did Sister Pin find her earrings?"

Xie Pin’s heart raced with guilt. She quickly lowered her head to hide the spring in her eyes: "Yes, Mother. I found them."

"Then let’s return to the banquet." Yun Chu turned and walked forward.

Xie Pin glanced behind her, then quickly followed Yun Chu.

As soon as they reached the banquet area, Yun Chu saw the little fellow nestled in the Grand Princess’s arms, acting coy: "Aunt Royal Grandmother, I did something wrong. Can you forgive me?"

The Grand Princess’s heart melted. Initially, she hadn’t liked this child of uncertain birth, but the boy was sweet-tongued and good at winning people over. Over time, she had naturally grown fond of him.

She pinched the little fellow’s cheek: "What did our little Yu do wrong?"

"I was playing with my slingshot and... accidentally shot dead two goldfish in the pond..." Chu Hongyu lowered his head, fiddling with his fingers. "Aunt Royal Grandmother, I was wrong."

Before the Grand Princess could respond, Prince Pingxi, sitting beside her, had a cold glint in his eyes. He reached out and grabbed Chu Hongyu by the back of his collar.

"Old Three, what are you doing?" The Grand Princess shielded the child in her arms. "They’re just two fish. It’s not worth making such a fuss."

Prince Pingxi spoke coldly: "If he can shoot two fish dead today, tomorrow he might kill two people. Indulging him will only make him more lawless."

"When a child misbehaves, it’s the father’s fault for not teaching him properly. In the end, this is all your fault." The Grand Princess humphed. "If you don’t have time to discipline your child, you should marry a princess consort to do it for you, instead of always resorting to beatings and scoldings. Look at how scared the child is."

At these words, the ladies seated below all averted their gazes.

Only a legitimate daughter was worthy of Prince Pingxi, but none of them wanted their daughters to become a stepmother. Each feared being noticed by the Grand Princess.

The Grand Princess scanned the entire banquet, her gaze settling on Yun Chu.

She smiled: "I’ve heard that there’s a student at Huai De Academy who has greatly impressed his teachers, the eldest son of the Xie family. If all goes well, he will be the top scholar in this year’s imperial examination. The child is so outstanding precisely because of his mother’s good upbringing. So, Old Three, when you marry, you should marry a woman like Sister Chu."

Yun Chu quickly stood up: "Your Highness flatters me. I dare not accept such praise."

Prince Pingxi raised his eyes, his hawk-like gaze falling on Yun Chu.

---

chapters.title: It’s Not My Fault
chapters.content:
Prince Pingxi’s gaze fell on Yun Chu.

She was dressed as a married woman, her long black hair piled high and secured with a gold and jade hairpin. She wore a light purple dress embroidered with camellias.

He recalled many years ago, before she was married, when they had met once.

He had gone to the Yun residence to visit General Yun, and she had happened to be bringing tea to the old general.

Back then, she had worn a goose-yellow dress, looking delicate and lively, almost like a different person compared to now.

"I think she’s great too." Chu Hongyu blinked his big eyes. "Aunt Royal Grandmother, can she be my mother?"

The Grand Princess let out a soft laugh: "You really are a child, always talking like one. Sister Chu, don’t take what he says to heart."

Yun Chu lowered her head: "To receive praise from the Young Prince is a great honor for me."

When she was young, she often followed Lin Shi to the Grand Princess’s residence, where the Grand Princess would still call her "Sister Chu."

But now she was married, the wife of a fifth-rank official. When speaking to the Grand Princess, she naturally couldn’t be as casual as before.

The banquet ended quickly.

After Lin Shi and the Grand Princess took their leave, the group began to exit.

Before they even left the Grand Princess’s residence, at the second gate, Yun Chu heard a child crying. Looking in the direction of the sound, she saw two figures in a nearby pavilion, a large one and a small one.

Prince Pingxi had a cold expression as he stared at the child in front of him. The child was wailing and fearfully backing away.

"You said you’d behave, so I brought you to the Grand Princess’s residence." Prince Pingxi’s voice was icy. "It’s one thing to cause trouble at home, but to act wild here; who gave you the courage?"

The little fellow sobbed: "Father, I admit I was wrong! Aunt Royal Grandmother forgave me too. I won’t dare do it again..."

Prince Pingxi’s face darkened further.

Those goldfish were priceless. It had taken tens of thousands of taels of silver to transport them all the way to the capital, and only two had survived, only to be killed by this brat.

If he wasn’t disciplined properly, who knew what greater disasters he might cause in the future.

He grabbed the child and lifted him up.

"Let go of me! Let go!" Chu Hongyu kicked his legs, crying loudly. "Aunt Royal Grandmother said it wasn’t my fault! Waaah, it’s your fault for not finding me a mother consort..."

Prince Pingxi’s face turned even darker.

He had indeed neglected his son’s upbringing, too busy with official duties. It was his fault.

Without another word, he carried the sobbing child away.

The child’s cries grew louder and louder.

Yun Chu’s heart suddenly ached. Before she realized it, her legs had already moved toward Prince Pingxi.

"Chu!" Lin Shi grabbed her arm. "Where are you going?"

Yun Chu came to her senses and pursed her lips: "I was the one who convinced the Young Prince to admit his mistake. I told him that as long as he admitted and corrected it, it would be fine..."

Lin Shi asked: "Do you think you were wrong to convince the Young Prince to admit his mistake?"

Yun Chu shook her head.

Lin Shi continued: "Then is Prince Pingxi wrong for disciplining his own child?"

Yun Chu shook her head again.

"There you have it." Lin Shi patted her hand. "It’s only natural for a father to discipline his son. What are you going to do by going over there? Do you think Prince Pingxi will listen to you? He’ll only think you’re meddling. Besides, look up."

Only then did Yun Chu notice that many ladies and young misses had stopped along the path.

She understood: Prince Pingxi’s public reprimand of his child was meant to thoroughly discourage any thoughts these people might have of marrying their daughters to him as his princess consort.

Prince Pingxi, carrying the child, quickly disappeared from the Grand Princess’s residence.

Many noblewomen began whispering among themselves.

"Rumors of the Young Prince’s mischief have been around for a while, but today we truly saw it for ourselves."

"Wasn’t it said that the Young Prince’s mother is of questionable status, and the imperial family disapproves of the child? Yet I saw the Grand Princess doting on him."

"The Grand Princess dotes on Prince Pingxi, so naturally, she extends that affection to his son. Otherwise, why would she be so anxious about finding a princess consort for Prince Pingxi?"

"What a shame. With such a grown son, no noble lady would be willing to marry into that household."

"And if this son is the heir, any future legitimate sons born to the princess consort would be in an awkward position..."

...

After leaving the Grand Princess’s residence, Yun Chu’s mood remained unsettled.

For some reason, she couldn’t stop thinking about that child.

"Mother." Xie Pin suddenly spoke, breaking Yun Chu’s thoughts. "Earlier, I saw the Grand Princess speaking happily with Madam Li. Does the Grand Princess want Madam Li’s eldest legitimate daughter to marry Prince Pingxi as his princess consort?"

Yun Chu replied indifferently: "Why are you so concerned with royal family matters?"

Xie Pin felt a pang of guilt but forced a smile: "I was just curious what kind of woman would be worthy of becoming a princess consort."

"Currently, only two princes have taken official wives. The Crown Prince’s consort is the eldest legitimate daughter of the Grand Preceptor, and the Second Prince’s wife is the second daughter of the Grand Secretary." Yun Chu looked at her. "At the very least, the daughter of a second-rank official family would be worthy of the title of princess consort. The lowest acceptable would be from a third-rank family."

Xie Pin’s fingers tightened.

Her father had taken five years to rise to the fifth rank. The higher the rank, the harder it was to ascend. Who knew how many more years it would take to reach the third rank...

She lowered her head, afraid that Yun Chu would notice the disappointment in her eyes.

The carriage soon stopped at the Xie family’s gate. As soon as they stepped through the door, Mama Zhou ushered the two of them into An Shou Hall.

An Shou Hall was lively. Not only was Xie Shian there, but Xie Jingyu was also present, clearly waiting for their return.

Old Madam Xie smiled and asked: "Chu, how was the Grand Princess’s flower-viewing banquet? Which nobles were in attendance?"

"Prince San of Pingxi and Prince Si of Anjing were there as well." Yun Chu noticed the eagerness in the Xie family’s eyes. "The noblewomen present were all wives of first, second, or third-rank officials. I was the only exception."

"You are the daughter of a first-rank general’s family. You naturally belong at such events." The old madam smiled. "Chu, did you speak with Madam Yu?"

Xie Jingyu also looked at her.

Yun Chu forced a smile. Madam Yu’s husband was Xie Jingyu’s superior. With evaluations coming up, if Xie Jingyu wanted to advance further, he would need to win over Official Yu.

If Official Yu agreed, Xie Jingyu could rise from the fifth rank to the fifth rank upper division.

There was no practical difference between the fifth rank and the fifth rank upper division, but if an opportunity for promotion arose, officials from the upper division would be considered first.

In the five short years since passing the imperial examination as the top scholar, Xie Jingyu had risen from the seventh rank to the fifth, partly due to his connection to the Yun family, but mostly because of his own skill in networking...

In the past, no matter what banquet she attended, she would help him cultivate these relationships.

Madam Yu was the wife of a third-rank official and couldn’t enter the circle of first-rank noblewomen. She had always been on the periphery. Normally, Yun Chu would have taken the initiative to bring Madam Yu into the circle.

But at the Grand Princess’s banquet, she had only glanced at Madam Yu from afar.

Madam Yu, unable to join the circle of first-rank noblewomen, would surely be resentful. She would then whisper in her husband’s ear, and Xie Jingyu could forget about rising to the fifth rank upper division.

Yun Chu’s face broke into a smile: "Madam Yu and I did exchange a few words."

Xie Jingyu stood up and cupped his hands: "Thank you, Madam."

"Thank me for what? We’re family." The old madam’s face lit up. "When Jingyu becomes a fourth-rank official, our Xie family will truly be able to hold our heads high."

Yun Chu’s smile deepened.

That day would probably never come.

chapters.title: Nothing is Impossible in This World
chapters.content:
While Yun Chu was speaking in Anshou Hall,

Xie Pin was pulled into the small grove behind by He-shi.

"What are you doing?" Xie Pin was startled, looking left and right. Seeing no one, she said, "Didn't Father order you to be confined in the small temple? How did you come out?"

He-shi said nervously, "Why did the madam suddenly take you to the Princess's residence? Did something happen?"

Xie Pin's face was full of impatience: "Mother took me to see the world, what could happen?"

He-shi didn't believe it at all.

Recently, the madam had repeatedly targeted her children. She absolutely did not believe that the madam would be so kind as to take Pin to see the world.

"I saw the Fourth Prince, Prince Anjing." Xie Pin said what she dared not say to Yun Chu, "Do you think I can become the Princess Consort of Anjing?"

He-shi's eyes widened: "You, what nonsense are you talking about?"

The Fourth Prince was of such high status, how dare the daughter of a mere fifth-rank official's family have such thoughts?

Moreover, although Xie Pin was currently the legitimate eldest daughter of the Xie family, anyone who cared to inquire would know that Xie Pin was actually a concubine-born daughter.

The royal family valued status the most. With Xie Pin's background, she could never be presented on the royal jade platter.

Xie Pin bit her lip: "Nothing is impossible in this world, as long as one is determined."

"My dear Pin, you must not act recklessly." He-shi was so scared that her soul almost left her body, "Your marriage is to be decided by the old madam and the madam. Do not harbor improper thoughts."

As they were speaking,

a voice suddenly came: "Isn't this Mama He? Didn't the master punish you to be confined in the small temple for reflection? How did you come out? You have quite the nerve!"

The speaker was none other than Tao Yiniang. Having heard that the madam had returned from the Princess's residence, she had specially come to join in the excitement. Who would have thought she would see He-shi, who should have been confined in the small temple?

As soon as she saw He-shi, flames seemed to shoot from her eyes.

The child in her belly had almost lost its life, yet this lowly creature who had coveted the master was unharmed.

She raised her hand and slapped He-shi hard.

Xie Pin reacted quickly, blocking the slap.

Tao Yiniang's eyes narrowed: "What does Eldest Miss mean by this?"

"It was I who asked Mama He to deliver some things for me." Xie Pin spoke, "Tao Yiniang is with child, it's better not to get angry, for fear of harming the baby."

Tao Yiniang followed: "Eldest Miss, it's truly surprising how you protect this lowly servant who covets your father and frames your mother."

These days, Yun Chu had always been kind to Xie Pin. This was the first time she had spoken so harshly.

Xie Pin lowered her head and said softly: "Mother, I'm sorry. I shouldn't have secretly sent things to Mama He. I was wrong, and I won't do it again."

Yun Chu said indifferently: "He-shi committed a grave mistake. Not sending her to the authorities is the Xie family's mercy. It's impossible to let her continue enjoying the treatment of a first-class servant as before. Tao Yiniang, if you have time, go to the small temple. Take away what should be taken. There's no need to hand it over to the public treasury. You can keep it yourself. Consider it a gift to calm the baby in your belly."

Tao Yiniang was overjoyed: "Thank you, Madam!"

With Yun Chu's permission, Tao Yiniang took two sturdy servant women directly to the small temple of the Xie family.

Because the old madam believed in Buddhism, when the mansion was established, a temple was built. However, since they couldn't support many people, only a young nun lived in the temple. Now, He-shi also lived there.

He-shi lived in the west side room. She was sitting in the room lost in thought.

Suddenly, the door was kicked open.

Tao Yiniang, supporting her belly, walked in and looked around: "Tsk tsk, a servant who tried to harm the master can live in such a good room. I am not as charitable as the master and the madam. Come, take everything away!"

With her command, the two servant women outside entered and took away all the visible objects. Not only that, they also took away the clothes and shoes from the cabinet. Then, they rolled up the bedding and threw it into the courtyard...

"What are you doing..." He-shi widened her eyes, "Don't touch my things!"

As the bedding was rolled up, a money bag fell out.

Tao Yiniang bent down to pick it up and opened it. Inside, besides silver, there were several banknotes worth a hundred taels each.

"Good for you, He-shi, to hide so much money!" Tao Yiniang shouted angrily, "So you not only tried to harm the master but also stole silver. How dare you, after the master trusted you so much!"

He-shi rushed to grab the money.

This was her savings over the years, not stolen!

All her possessions were in this money bag!

She lunged at Tao Yiniang without regard.

"Someone, she's trying to harm me!" Tao Yiniang retreated, letting the two sturdy servant women step forward.

The servant women kicked He-shi, who fell to the ground with a miserable cry.

---

chapters.title: Rising at the Crow's Caw
chapters.content:
Yun Chu was looking at her dowry list, planning to sell unnecessary items for silver.

While busy, Tingfeng entered and said, "Madam, Tao Yiniang found 780 taels of silver in He-shi's place. How should we handle it?"

Yun Chu casually said, "Let Tao Yiniang keep it."

To make Tao Yiniang willing to be the knife, she naturally had to give some benefits. Only then would the knife become sharper.

Tingfeng continued, "Tao Yiniang ordered people to beat He-shi until she spat blood. Should we call a doctor?"

"It's just a few mouthfuls of blood, she won't die." Yun Chu's expression was quite cold.

He-shi had three biological children. She wanted to see who would be the first to lose their patience and send medicine to He-shi.

She paused and said, "Tao Yiniang was startled at He-shi's place. Take some cordyceps from the storeroom and send it to Tao Yiniang to nourish her body."

Receiving the tonics sent by Yun Chu, Tao Yiniang's suspended heart settled.

She knew that the madam also despised He-shi in her heart. It was just that the madam was like the clear moon in the sky, and He-shi, such a lowly creature, was unworthy of the madam's attention.

With the madam's permission, what else did she have to worry about?

Tao Yiniang beckoned and said a few words to the maid.

In the evening, the servant woman delivering food threw a bowl of moldy rice at the door of He-shi's side room.

"Stop!" He-shi called out to the servant woman, "Is this something for a person to eat? How dare you treat me like this?"

The servant woman spat: "Oh, do you still think you're the manager mama by the master's side? Now that you're confined in this broken temple, you're not even as good as the lowest rough servant girl. It's already good enough that we give you a bowl to eat. What more do you want?"

He-shi simply couldn't believe it. That cheap woman Tao-shi had taken all her savings, beaten her until she spat blood, and now was even cutting her food rations.

Truly, a tiger fallen on hard times is bullied by dogs!

"What's that look in your eyes?" The servant woman lifted her foot and kicked over the bowl of moldy rice, "You're given a face and you don't want it. If you despise it, then don't eat it. After almost killing the young master, you still dare to hope for a full stomach. You'll get what's coming to you!"

The servant woman cursed and left.

He-shi's blood surged, and she almost fainted.

The next day at the Chen hour, Old General Yun sent a woman with a graceful figure.

This woman was named Qiutong, about twenty years old, wearing a black short jacket, with a sword hanging at her waist.

"Greetings, Madam!"

Qiutong cupped her hands in salute, looking heroic and spirited.

Yun Chu, being the daughter of a military family, knew at first glance that this woman had excellent martial arts skills.

She said, "From now on, you will be my martial arts teacher. Place yourself in the position of a teacher, and we will train as you see fit."

Qiutong agreed and stepped forward to check Yun Chu's pulse, pressing her muscles and bones, and shaking her head repeatedly: "Madam actually has some foundation, but it's been too long since you've exercised, and your muscles and meridians have become stiff. The most urgent thing now is to restore your body to its former flexibility..."

Yun Chu was immediately taken to the courtyard.

Although Qiutong was a woman, the strength in her hands was not at all inferior to Yun Chu's grandfather. When she was unblocking Yun Chu's acupoints and meridians, she almost made Yun Chu cry out in pain.

After an hour, Yun Chu didn't even have the strength to stand.

Qiutong, with no change in expression, said: "At the crow's caw tomorrow morning, I will wait for Madam in the courtyard."

Yun Chu's vision went black.

The crow's caw was around the You hour, just after midnight.

She felt as if she had just fallen asleep when Tingshuang woke her up: "Madam, it's time to get up. Sister Qiutong is already waiting outside."

Yun Chu quickly got out of bed.

This path was one she had chosen herself, so she must walk it with unwavering determination.

Her grandfather had said that only the skills one had learned truly belonged to oneself.

The courtyard was lit with lamps, and Qiutong stood solemnly. She demonstrated the standard horse stance and had Yun Chu squat in the horse stance for a quarter of an hour, then gradually increase the time.

When Yun Chu was a child, she had also squatted in the horse stance, but whenever her grandfather wasn't paying attention, she would start to slack off.

The laziness stolen in childhood was the bitterness that had to be endured in adulthood.

"You few come over and accompany Madam as well." Qiutong looked at the maids standing to the side, "If you really encounter any danger, you can help Madam."

Hearing this, Tingshuang, Tingsnow, and Tingwind immediately walked over and lined up to squat in the horse stance.

After a quarter of an hour, the three maids, who had never been exposed to martial arts, were sweating profusely. Qiutong let them rest temporarily.

Yun Chu, having some foundation, managed to squat in the horse stance for more than half an hour before starting to wobble.

After practicing for nearly an hour, she went back to bed and immediately fell asleep, sleeping for more than an hour before dawn.

The people who came to pay their respects arrived one by one.

"Mother, the old madam's birthday is coming up soon." Xie Pin held a few lists, "I want to make the old madam's birthday banquet grand, inviting all the noblewomen of status in the capital to liven things up. What do you think, Mother?"

Yun Chu looked at the lists she handed over: "You plan to invite the wives of the Minister of Revenue, the Grand Preceptor... These are all first-rank noblewomen. With the Xie family's status, we cannot invite them."

Xie Pin said, "Our grandmother and these madams are on good terms and have watched Mother grow up. If Mother invites them, I think those madams will definitely give Mother face..."

Tao Yiniang let out a laugh: "Eldest Miss is still too young and doesn't understand these social niceties."

Being mocked by a concubine made Xie Pin feel quite embarrassed.

Tingyu spoke up: "If it were Madam's birthday, it might be possible to try inviting these madams, but for the old madam, it's still somewhat inappropriate."

"Pin, rewrite the guest list." Yun Chu looked at her, "Also, the menu you've set is exactly the same as last year's. It should be changed. There should be some new ideas, shouldn't there?"

Xie Pin felt a bit disheartened.

Previously, no matter what she did, Mother would praise her a little.

But ever since she secretly sent things to He-shi, Mother's attitude towards her seemed to have changed.

She lowered her head: "Yes, Mother. I'll go and reconsider."

Yun Chu no longer concerned herself with the birthday banquet, leaving it entirely to Xie Pin. She only made minor, insignificant suggestions during the daily greetings.

She devoted herself entirely to learning martial arts from Qiutong.

What she hadn't expected was that for three or four consecutive days, none of He-shi's three children, Xie Pin, Xie Shian, or Xie Shiyou, had sent medicine to the small temple.

Yun Chu smiled.

These three ungrateful wolves not only had no affection for her, their foster mother, but also clearly had no deep feelings for He-shi, their biological mother.

He-shi was having a very hard time.

She had coughed up several mouthfuls of blood, and her body ached terribly every day. In addition, she hadn't had a proper meal, so she rapidly lost weight.

She knew that she couldn't go on like this. She had to find a way to save herself, otherwise, if she starved to death in the small temple, no one would know.

After the only young nun in the temple fell asleep, under the cover of night, she slipped out of the temple, avoiding maids and servant boys, and arrived at Xie Jingyu's study.

Xie Jingyu returned home very late every day.

As soon as she reached the study door, she saw a tall figure approaching from a distance.

chapters.title: The Xie Family Deceived You
chapters.content:
He’s wife was feeling somewhat disheartened.

She and Xie Jingyu were the same age, yet while he remained the same dashing young master, she had already grown old.

"Why are you here?" Xie Jingyu’s exhausted face showed anger when he saw her standing at the courtyard gate.

He’s wife lowered her head. "Master, I did wrong and accept my punishment, but that doesn't mean I'm willing to be tortured to death... Madam Tao, with your tacit approval, has cut off the food supply to the small temple. This is an attempt to cut off my means of survival..."

Xie Jingyu pinched the space between his eyebrows.

He had just returned from Lord Yu’s residence, where he had spent most of the day without even catching a glimpse of Lord Yu.

In the past, Lord Yu had treated him quite well. No matter what social events they attended, he would always bring Xie Jingyu along, allowing him to meet many influential figures in the official circles.

With the evaluation approaching, Lord Yu had suddenly started avoiding him.

He truly didn’t understand what he had done wrong.

A day of frustration with no one to confide in, and upon returning home, he was accosted by He’s wife with these trivial matters.

He wasn’t someone who easily lost his temper, but at this moment, he couldn’t hold it in any longer. He coldly said, "It was your own choice to stay in the Xie family. Whatever treatment you receive is your own choice. Furthermore, I ordered you to stay confined in the small temple, yet you appeared at my study door. Since you don’t take my words seriously, I will have to arrange for someone to guard the entrance of the small temple."

He’s wife’s lips suddenly stiffened.

She thought of their first meeting a long, long time ago, when his eyes held admiration as he looked at her.

She thought of the heartache in his eyes after she gave birth to An Ge’er.

She thought of many years ago, when she lived with her three children in the outskirts of the capital, and he would visit once a month, full of tenderness and affection.

Ever since she moved into the Xie family, she and he had become master and servant. Her address for him had changed from "Yu Lang" to "Master"...

Until this moment, she realized that they might never return to how things were before.

"Still not leaving?" Xie Jingyu’s voice was filled with impatience.

Tears suddenly welled up in He’s wife’s eyes.

She had racked her brains to have her children recognized by the family, she had tried every means to stay by Xie Jingyu’s side, she was even willing to be a servant just to keep the family together... Had this man truly seen her sacrifices?

"Yes, Master, I will leave now."

He’s wife curtsied, turned around, and tears streamed down her face.

Watching her back, Xie Jingyu couldn’t help but sigh. Keeping her in the Xie family was already out of consideration for their past relationship.

If he did more for He’s wife, it would surely arouse Yun Chu’s suspicion. He still needed to rely on the Yun family’s influence to rise in rank. How could he fall out with Yun Chu?

Back in the small temple, He’s wife’s heart was as dead as ashes.

She still had to watch An Ge’er pass the imperial examinations and become an official, she still had to personally send Pin Jie’er off to marry, she still had to see Wei Ge’er make something of himself... She absolutely could not die in this small temple.

Since Xie Jingyu was unreliable, she could only rely on herself.

She wrote a letter and gave the only bracelet on her wrist to a young nun, begging the nun to help her send it out.

"Oh, she wants to send a letter to Manager He in the outer courtyard?" Yun Chu looked at the young nun who had come to report, "Then you should deliver it for her."

The young nun agreed and took the letter to the outer courtyard.

Tingshuang was somewhat surprised. "He’s wife and Manager He in the outer courtyard share the same surname. Could they be related?"

Yun Chu nodded. "They are probably siblings. To find out He’s wife’s true identity, we need to start with He Xu."

He’s wife’s identity was definitely not ordinary. Otherwise, she would have surely coveted the position of the main wife. Even if she couldn’t become the main wife, she would have been willing to be a concubine.

A vague guess formed in her mind, but without evidence, no one would believe her if she spoke of it.

Whether she could completely ruin Xie Shian’s official career depended on He’s wife’s identity.

At this moment, a young servant from the front courtyard came to report: "Madam, I went to the Yun residence, and the Yun family said that the eldest young master will return to the capital tomorrow morning."

Yun Chu suddenly stood up.

The distance between Ji Province and the capital was not far, but her eldest brother needed to handle official business in Ji Province. It was unexpected that he would return to the capital so soon.

The rest of the day was agonizingly slow. The next morning, she took a carriage back to the Yun residence.

However, after Yun Ze returned to the capital, he first went to the imperial city to report for duty. It wasn’t until noon that he returned, exhausted. His sister-in-law, Liu Qianqian, took him to change his clothes.

Lin Shi curiously asked, "Chu’er, do you and your eldest brother have something important to discuss?"

Ever since her daughter returned home, she had been absent-minded, frequently looking outside. Only when Yun Ze returned did her anxious emotions ease slightly.

Yun Chu quickly forced a smile. "The Xie family’s old residence is in Ji Province. My husband hasn’t returned there in many years. I wanted to ask my eldest brother about the situation there."

Lin Shi nodded thoughtfully.

When Yun Ze had changed his clothes and returned, Lin Shi took Liu Qianqian and left the flower hall, leaving the space for the siblings.

"Eldest brother." Yun Chu’s voice was hoarse as soon as she spoke, "The children... have they returned?"

Yun Ze opened his mouth but couldn’t say a word.

If he had brought back those two poor children, he would have told his sister immediately, rather than using the time to change clothes to think about how to brush this off.

The light in Yun Chu’s eyes slowly faded, and her voice became even hoarser. "Eldest brother?"

Yun Ze sighed. "Chu’er, I personally went to the Xie family’s old residence in Ji Province and asked the clan members about the children’s burial place. But the elders of the clan told me that four years ago, the Xie family in the capital had never sent anyone back, and they had never heard that Xie Jingyu’s legitimate son and daughter had already died in infancy. The Xie family lied to you..."

Boom.

Yun Chu felt as if her head had exploded.

Her body swayed, and she steadied herself by holding onto the table to avoid falling.

She closed her eyes and took several deep breaths before gradually calming down.

"Thank you... thank you, eldest brother!" she managed to say with difficulty, then turned and walked out.

"Chu’er." Yun Ze, disregarding the impropriety between siblings, grabbed her wrist.

"I’ll go back with you, Chu’er."

Yun Chu pressed down on Yun Ze’s arm, her voice hoarse to the extreme. "I can handle this myself. If I really can’t, I’ll come back and ask eldest brother for help."

She turned around and walked out with quick steps.

Normally, she would go to say goodbye to her mother and sister-in-law before leaving.

But now, she no longer had the mind for that.

Tingshuang supported her as she quickly walked out of the Yun residence, got into the carriage, and urged the coachman to go faster, even faster.

The carriage sped through the streets and soon returned to the Xie residence.

She entered swiftly and sat weakly in the flower hall, her voice carrying a deep chill. "Bring He’s wife here."

The two servant women had never seen the mistress like this. They exchanged a glance and hurried to the small temple to fetch her.

He’s wife was lying weakly on the bed, her body frail from untreated injuries and days without a proper meal. She had just closed her eyes when the door to her room was kicked open.

She was startled and thought it was Madam Tao leading people in. Looking up, she saw the coarse servant women from Yu Sheng residence.

These were people sent by the mistress.

The mistress had always been hypocritical. Even if she wanted to deal with her, she would have Madam Tao do it. Why would she personally send people?

Before she could think further, He’s wife was lifted by the two servant women and dragged out.

---

chapters.title: Early Death Means Inauspiciousness
chapters.content:
Yun Chu sat on a rattan chair in the courtyard.

She had drunk four or five cups of cold tea in a row, but still couldn’t calm her emotions.

Every time she thought about not knowing where the children were buried, her heart felt as if it were being cut by a knife.

In her previous life, she had never asked about the children. Until she died, the children had never truly rested in peace. She hated her past self to death.

He’s wife was dragged in from the entrance.

The pain in Yun Chu’s heart turned into hatred, and her eyes, sharp as blades, mercilessly fixed on He’s wife.

He’s wife couldn’t help but shiver.

The Yun Chu she had seen was always gentle and dignified. Even when dealing with the lowest servants in the residence, she had always been kind and pleasant.

Even when He’s wife had framed her last time, the mistress had never shown such an expression.

One of the two servant women behind her kicked her leg, and her knees buckled, causing her to kneel on the ground.

Yun Chu coldly looked at her. "Four years ago, my children in my womb died. But Mama He took the children back to their hometown for burial. I ask you, where were the children buried?"

He’s wife’s mind went blank. Why would the mistress suddenly ask about something that happened four years ago?

She lowered her brows and eyes. "Master was busy with official duties, so he ordered this slave to go instead. This slave took the young master and young miss back to the old home in Ji Province for burial. They were buried on the mountain behind the Xie family ancestral temple. Since there was no tombstone, this slave cannot specify the exact location."

Bang!

Yun Chu slammed the teacup in her hand heavily onto the table.

Her expression was icy. "It seems Mama He does not intend to tell me the truth. Someone!"

At her command, two coarse servant women from the courtyard brought a long bench forward and pressed He’s wife onto it. Then they picked up two long wooden planks.

He’s wife was terrified. "Madam, this slave is telling the truth..."

Yun Chu made a gesture.

The two servant women, one on each side, began to strike with the planks.

They were used to heavy labor, and their strength was astonishing. After three or four strikes, He’s wife was already weak.

"Mama He, I’ll give you one more chance." Yun Chu spoke slowly, emphasizing each word. "As long as you tell me where the children are buried, I will let you go."

He’s wife was in so much pain she almost fainted.

She knew very well that the mistress must have confirmed that the children were not buried in Ji Province, which was why she dared to openly interrogate her.

Sticking to her original story had no meaning.

"Madam, this slave... this slave doesn’t know either..." He’s wife struggled to speak. "Master ordered this slave to bury the young master and young miss, but before this slave could set off for Ji Province, Master took the children’s bodies away. This slave truly knows nothing..."

Yun Chu shook her head. "Continue."

The two servant women used all their strength to strike with the planks, and He’s wife screamed in agony.

After a while, she fainted.

Yun Chu’s face showed no emotion as she coldly ordered, "Splash water on her to wake her up, and continue."

A basin of ice-cold water was splashed on He’s wife’s face. Before she could regain her senses, the planks struck her body again, and the intense pain engulfed her.

Yun Chu tightly pinched her own palm.

She only wanted to know where the children were buried. Why had even this simple thought become a luxury?

What was the reason that made He’s wife too afraid to reveal the children’s whereabouts? What else was there that she didn’t know...

Never before had Yun Chu hated herself so much.

She hated her own weakness, hated her own stupidity for being deceived, hated that she was unworthy of being a mother...

Outside the courtyard, Xie Pin was anxious.

If this continued, He’s wife would either die or be half-dead.

She didn’t understand why He’s wife was so secretive about the burial place of two children who had died young!

She stamped her foot and turned to go to An Shou Hall.

Upon hearing that Yun Chu was punishing He’s wife, the old madam didn’t mind. But when she heard that Yun Chu was angry over the burial place of the deceased children, her expression turned unpleasant.

Those two children were already dead. Did it matter where they were buried?

The old madam, leaning on her cane, headed towards Yu Sheng residence. When she arrived at the entrance, she noticed that Yu Sheng residence had somehow become Sheng residence.

But now was not the time to ask about such trivial matters.

"Chu’er!" The old madam quickly stepped inside.

"What crime has He’s wife committed to deserve such a severe punishment?"

Yun Chu quietly looked at the old madam. "If the old madam knows where the children are buried, I can let her go."

"Children who die right after birth are considered inauspicious. No matter which family, they are buried in a random place to avoid affecting the family’s fortune." The old madam said, "Even in the royal family, if a prince or princess dies young, they are buried in a random place outside the city. Needless to say, for a mere fifth-rank official family like ours?"

"The old madam has many grandsons and granddaughters, so naturally, she doesn’t care about the deceased children." Yun Chu’s voice was extremely cold. "But I only have these two children. Not a day will pass in peace until I know where they are buried. If the children do not rest in peace, then the Xie family will forever be in turmoil!"

She stood up and walked into the inner room.

The old madam was so angry she almost fell backward. "She... what does she mean? How dare she be so disrespectful to her elder?"

"Old madam, since our mistress married into the Xie family, she has always been filial and respectful to you. This offense is because she is overwhelmed with grief." Tingshuang lowered her head. "The fact that the young master and young miss’s bodies are not in Ji Province was discovered by the mistress’s elder brother, who personally went to Ji Province to investigate. If the Xie family cannot provide an explanation, the Yun family will come to demand one."

The old madam’s heart lurched.

This was a clear threat.

She looked at He’s wife, who was sprawled on the long bench, and coldly said, "Quickly tell everything you know. Don’t ruin the marital relationship between the Xie and Yun families."

He’s wife bit her dry lips tightly.

If she told the truth, the Yun and Xie families would truly be finished.

Her son, An Ge’er, still needed to rely on the Yun family’s connection to enter the court. No matter how much she despised Yun Chu, she knew she couldn’t let Yun Chu abandon the Xie family...

"Old madam, Mama He is almost done for." Xie Pin couldn’t help but speak up. "Let’s call a doctor."

"Eldest young miss, don’t let your kindness lead to trouble." Tingshuang coldly said, "Without the mistress’s permission, no one is allowed to take He’s wife away."

The old madam’s expression was very grim.

Although she was an elder, if this granddaughter-in-law was determined to do something, she truly had no way to stop her.

The Yun family was a great mountain standing behind her granddaughter-in-law.

Thinking of this, the old madam turned around and left, leaning on her cane.

Xie Pin was very anxious but didn’t dare to show it too obviously.

She just didn’t understand why He’s wife caused so much trouble. If it weren’t for the fact that she had come from He’s wife’s womb, she wouldn’t even bother with this matter.

But since the old madam couldn’t control her mother, she, as a junior, could do even less.

The only option left was to ask her father.

Xie Pin hurriedly went to Qing Song Pavilion to find Xie Shian.

Xie Shian was writing, and he had already heard from the attending servant boy about what had happened at Sheng residence.

He calmly asked Xie Pin, "Do you know why your mother suddenly started caring about the children who died four years ago?"

Xie Pin shook her head.

"Last time, we were willing to believe a servant rather than her." Xie Shian looked at Xie Pin. "Perhaps your mother thinks that we, as non-biological children, are all ungrateful white-eyed wolves. So she remembered the pair of children who died young. At a time like this, if you still speak for He’s wife, your mother might be thoroughly disappointed in you. She probably won’t take you to any more banquets with the big families in the future."

chapters.title: Slapping Xie Jingyu
chapters.content:
Xie Shian lowered his head and continued writing.

Xie Pin pressed her lips together.

This younger brother was only one year younger than her, but he was far more mature and much colder than she was.

Heshu was, after all, their birth mother. Now, under the blows of the rod, she had nearly lost half her life, yet this brother hadn’t even furrowed his brow.

But she also knew that if she defended a servant in front of their mother, their mother would certainly become suspicious.

She said nothing more and turned to return to her own courtyard.

Xie Shian gripped the brush, barely managing to finish writing a piece of calligraphy. His dark eyes deepened, and he suddenly stood up and walked out.

"Prepare the horse!"

A servant led the horse to the gate of the mansion. He mounted it and rode straight toward the Yu residence.

Lord Yu was a third-rank official, and it seemed he was hosting a banquet, as the entrance was bustling with carriages and horses.

Xie Shian stopped under a large tree across from the Yu residence and waited silently.

Before long, the banquet finally ended.

He saw Xie Jingyu walk out with a dejected look. Xie Shian quickly went to meet him. "Father."

Xie Jingyu collected his dispirited expression and said in mild surprise, "Why are you here?"

"Something happened at home," Xie Shian said in a low voice. "Mother is interrogating Heshu, asking about the whereabouts of the two children who died four years ago."

Xie Jingyu's expression changed.

He took a deep breath. "What is the situation now?"

"Grandmother went to advise Mother, but Mother said that if Heshu doesn’t confess, then the Xie family will never have a day of peace," Xie Shian looked up. "Father, were those two children never properly buried? Is that why Heshu doesn’t dare to confess, for fear of Mother’s greater fury?"

Xie Jingyu looked at his son with a complicated expression.

If even twelve-year-old An Ge could guess this, then Yun Chu must have also thought of it.

If Yun Chu found out about those two children... she would probably hesitate to divorce him without a second thought, and his official career would likely come to an end as well.

"Mother is interrogating Heshu while waiting for Father to return home," Xie Shian continued. "If Father appears before Mother in this state, even if Father doesn’t say a word, Mother will still be able to guess something. The Xie family will truly be in turmoil."

Xie Jingyu took Xie Shian onto the carriage.

Inside the carriage, it was just the two of them. Outside, the sound of rolling wheels and the occasional chatter of passersby could be heard.

"Those two children... I ordered Heshu to throw them away..." Xie Jingyu closed his eyes. "They were never truly buried."

Xie Shian's heart sank.

He had indeed guessed correctly.

But he couldn’t understand why. Even though those two children had died young, they still carried their father’s blood. Even if they couldn’t be buried in the Xie family ancestral temple, they shouldn’t have been simply discarded...

But dwelling on the past was meaningless now. The key was how to handle the current situation.

"An Ge, I will return home now to deal with your mother. You must go as quickly as possible to the villages near the capital to investigate. The children who died young in the village are probably all buried in one place. Find a way to obtain two infant corpses..." Xie Jingyu placed his hand on Xie Shian’s shoulder. "I know this task is difficult for you, but right now, you are the only one I can trust."

Xie Shian’s expression was complex. "Alright."

He lifted the carriage curtain and got off, then rode away on horseback.

Xie Jingyu ordered the coachman to return to the mansion.

As soon as he arrived at the gate of the Xie mansion, the servant attending to him came forward. "Sir, the maids from Madam’s courtyard have come several times. They said that as soon as you return home, you must go to Shengju immediately."

Xie Jingyu nodded to indicate he understood.

He didn’t even change his clothes and went straight to Shengju.

Along the way, his mind was filled with various thoughts.

Soon, he arrived at Yun Chu’s residence. At first glance, he saw Heshu tied to a long bench in the courtyard.

Behind Heshu was a pool of blood. Her clothes were torn to shreds, and she looked pitiful.

But the two maids standing beside her did not let Heshu off. Instead, they splashed a basin of water on Heshu’s face. When Heshu woke up, they continued to strike her with the board.

"Stop."

Xie Jingyu coldly spat out three words.

The two maids quickly bent down and bowed. "Greetings, Sir."

Xie Jingyu’s expression was extremely complicated.

In his memory, Yun Chu had always been a gentle and tolerant wife, like the vast sky, able to accommodate everyone and everything.

In five years of marriage, he had never seen Yun Chu punish any servant.

This was the first time he had seen her anger.

This anger burned fiercely, making his heart feel a hint of unease.

He took a step up the stairs and walked to the door of Yun Chu’s bedroom. He lightly knocked on the door and said, "Madam?"

He heard footsteps, and immediately afterward, the door of the room was opened.

Before he could say anything.

Suddenly.

A gust of wind rushed over.

*Slap.*

A loud slap landed on his face.

Everyone in the courtyard was stunned. The surroundings fell silent, and only the sound of the wind could be heard.

Xie Jingyu’s face was filled with disbelief.

He had actually been slapped by a woman.

He was probably the first husband in this dynasty to be slapped by his wife.

This was simply a great humiliation!

Yun Chu’s palm was numb, and her eyes were red, as if they were about to spew fire. She stared intently at Xie Jingyu.

She said, word by word, "I will ask you only once. Where are the children buried?"

Xie Jingyu’s face burned with pain.

He tightly clenched his fists, suppressing the humiliating emotions.

He took a deep breath. "Madam, you are too emotional. Calm down, and we will talk."

Yun Chu coldly said, "You are my husband, so I naturally cannot interrogate you as I did Heshu. But I can ask my grandfather to intervene."

Xie Jingyu tightened his lips.

In the past, his grandmother had told him that if he married a woman from a noble family, he, as the husband, would be suppressed in every aspect.

But in five years of marriage, Yun Chu had never used the power of the Yun family to force him to compromise. He had always been grateful that Yun Chu respected him as her husband.

But now, Yun Chu had brought up Old General Yun.

She had no intention of continuing this marriage.

But he...

Lord Yu no longer favored him. The only thing he could rely on now was the Yun family.

He used all his strength to suppress all his emotions.

Then, he lifted his head again, putting on a humble and gentle appearance. "Regarding the burial of the children, I did indeed hide the truth from you, Madam. This is also something I cannot forgive myself for. The slap you gave me is what I deserve. Originally, I had planned to bury the children near the ancestral temple of the Xie family’s old residence. But later, I heard that burying children who died young near the ancestral grave would affect the fortune of the entire family. At that time, I had just established my footing in the court, and I was truly worried..."

Yun Chu’s patience had reached its limit. She coldly interrupted him, "You only need to tell me where the children are buried!"

"They were buried in a remote place in a village on the outskirts of the capital four years ago." Xie Jingyu lowered his gaze to hide the emotions in his eyes. "It’s getting late now, and it’s inconvenient to go there at this hour. Tomorrow morning, I will take you to see the children."

Yun Chu’s lips turned as pale as ash.

Her fingers trembled slightly as she uttered one word, "Get out."

Then, with a *bang*, she shut the door.

She leaned against the door and slowly slid down to sit on the floor.

Shouldn’t she be grateful? Grateful that Xie Jingyu had not abandoned the children’s bodies, grateful that the children had a place to be buried...

---

chapters.title: The Xie Family Wants a Divorce
chapters.content:
Xie Jingyu turned around and walked down the steps.

The servants in the courtyard secretly glanced at him and then quickly lowered their heads.

His face was red and swollen, extremely noticeable.

He walked up to Heshu and said, "Send two people to take Heshu back to the small temple."

The two maids exchanged a glance but did not move.

They had just fully understood that although this was the Xie mansion, the power to speak was in Madam’s hands.

Even though Madam had not borne a single child for the Xie family, even though Madam had just slapped the master across the face, the Xie family’s attitude toward Madam made it clear that she was the true person in charge of the entire Xie household.

Without Madam’s word, they dared not send Heshu away.

Tingshuang walked over and said, "You two, take Heshu back."

Only then did the two maids dare to go and lift the unconscious Heshu.

Xie Jingyu’s expression was extremely ugly.

He walked in front, personally leading Heshu to the small temple. Heshu was thrown onto the hard bed by the maids.

After being dragged all the way back, she regained some consciousness. Opening her eyes and seeing Xie Jingyu standing by the bed, hot tears rolled down her face. Her voice was hoarse as she said, "Master, I’m in pain..."

Xie Jingyu took out a bottle of ointment from his sleeve and handed it over. "This is a rare good medicine from the palace. Later, I’ll have a maid apply it for you."

Heshu raised her hand and trembled as she touched Xie Jingyu’s face. "How dare Madam hit you? Only a shrew would do such a thing... Master, divorce her. You should divorce her..."

Xie Jingyu dodged her touch and said, "She is just deeply missing the children. It’s understandable."

Heshu gritted her teeth. "Haven’t you noticed that Madam is completely different from before? She is no longer the Madam Xie who devoted herself to the Xie family. She seems to hold a grudge against the Xie family. Who hasn’t been punished by her? Even you have suffered a slap from her. In the future, what won’t she be capable of? No matter how high her status is, she is no longer suitable to be the mistress of the household. Master, cut ties where they need to be cut..."

Xie Jingyu looked out the window.

Of course, he had noticed Yun Chu’s strangeness. Previously, he hadn’t understood why Yun Chu seemed like a different person, but now he finally knew the reason.

Yun Chu must have long suspected the whereabouts of the children. After secretly investigating for a long time without finding where the children were buried, she had finally lost her temper...

"You did not reveal the truth even when she interrogated you so harshly. What happened four years ago should be buried in the past. Do not bring it up again." Xie Jingyu turned around. "You take good care of your injuries. Do not think wildly, and do not cause any more trouble. I will arrange for someone to take care of you. You will not live in hardship."

Heshu lay on the bed, tightly clutching the bottle of medicine in her hand.

Xie Jingyu walked out of the small temple and returned to his study.

The five finger marks on his face became more and more obvious. Almost every servant who passed by saw them.

Thus, the news that Xie Jingyu had been slapped by Madam in Shengju spread to every corner of the Xie mansion and naturally reached Anshou Hall.

"What?!" Madam Xie smashed the teacup in her hand. "Yun Chu actually dared to slap Jingyu. How dare she? Where did she get the courage?"

Yuan Shi advised, "Quarrels between husband and wife are common."

"Quarrels are quarrels, but who allowed her to lay a hand on him? She actually hit a man’s face. How is Jingyu supposed to go to court tomorrow?" The old madam was so angry that her chest was about to explode. "She can’t even bear children, which already violates the Seven Grounds for Divorce. To lay a hand on her husband, calling her a shrew or a wicked woman would not be an exaggeration. Such a woman is not fit to be the mistress of the household. In any other family, she would have been divorced long ago. How dare she be so arrogant?"

"Old Madam, we shouldn’t talk like this. What if someone hears?" Yuan Shi said. "Chu is a fortunate child. After she entered our family, my illness suddenly improved, and Jingyu’s official career has been smooth sailing. She brings fortune, and she can also bring prosperity to our Xie family. If we divorce her, where will we find such a good daughter-in-law?"

"That was when your illness was supposed to get better. What does it have to do with her?" the old madam said coldly. "Jingyu’s promotion is his own ability. Her Yun family hasn’t helped at all. This time, I will overlook it because she did it for the two children who died young. But if she continues to stir up trouble in the future, even if it means offending the Yun family, I will make Jingyu divorce her!"

Yuan Shi quickly said, "Chu is not an unreasonable person..."

While the two women were talking, the sky had already darkened completely.

Yun Chu’s emotions had gone through extreme ups and downs, and she felt as if all her strength had been drained. Exhausted, she lay on the bed.

Originally, she was supposed to practice her horse stance in the evening, but she truly couldn’t get up.

Closing her eyes, she kept hearing the pitiful cries of the children from her dreams. Eventually, she fell asleep at some point.

"Mother, where are you? We miss you so much."

"Mother, can you come and hold us? It’s so cold."

Yun Chu’s heart felt as if it were being twisted by a knife. Even though she knew this was a dream, she was unwilling to wake up. She really wanted to find her children, to hold them, to tell them that she had never forgotten them for a single day, that she missed them too...

She struggled forward through the mist in her dream.

The white mist enveloped everything, seemingly endless. She didn’t know how long she walked before a trace of light finally appeared ahead.

Yun Chu quickened her pace and ran toward it.

She saw a blue sky and a vast expanse of green grass. This place was filled with blooming flowers. Among the flowers sat two exquisitely beautiful children, about four years old.

A boy and a girl, they were lowering their heads, playing with something.

Yun Chu’s heart instantly softened. She carefully walked over, afraid that any sudden movement would wake her from this beautiful dream.

"Children, Mother is here..."

Her voice was as gentle as could be. She squatted down in front of the children.

The boy was the first to lift his head. A familiar face entered her vision, and she opened her mouth in shock. "Young Master?"

Why did her son’s face look like the young master of the Prince of Pingxi’s mansion...

"Mother!"

The child buried his head in her arms.

She jolted awake.

Only then did she realize that it was already dawn outside.

Tingshuang heard the movement and walked in. She softly said, "Madam, if you are not feeling well, sleep a little longer. I will have those who came to pay their respects leave."

Yun Chu pressed her temples. "Just say I’m ill. No need for anyone to come pay their respects for the next few days."

Tingshuang’s face was filled with deep concern.

She gently closed the door and walked outside. "Madam is unwell. Everyone, please leave. There is no need to come pay your respects for the next few days."

Tingyu held Xie Shiyou’s hand, her face showing surprise. "Wasn’t Madam fine just yesterday? How did she suddenly fall ill? Is it serious?"

Tingfeng felt that she was being extremely hypocritical. After what happened yesterday, how could Madam not be ill? Everyone in the mansion knew what had happened.

"Spring is still cold. Madam caught a chill." Tingshuang said indifferently. "Everyone, please disperse."

Everyone else left on their own accord. Tingyu pulled Xie Shiyou to stay behind and said, "Since Madam is ill, I can stay to attend to her. Madam dotes on You Ge the most. Let You Ge amuse Madam."

Tingshuang’s expression was very cold. "Madam is resting and does not need attendance. Concubine Yu, you may leave."

Tingyu lowered her gaze.

In the past, she had thought Madam was clever. Now, she only knew that Madam was extremely foolish.

A woman who couldn’t bear children should seize the existing children in the mansion and capture the man’s heart. But Madam had done the exact opposite.

Madam had slapped the master in broad daylight. The last bit of marital affection between the master and Madam was probably gone.

As Tingyu was thinking this, she saw Xie Jingyu, who had just returned from court, quickly walking into Shengju.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.content:
Xie Jingyu was dressed in the official robes of a fifth-rank officer, clearly having come straight from court without even changing clothes, rushing to Shengju.

A glimmer of joy flickered in Tingyu’s eyes.

Back when she lived in the mistress’s courtyard, sometimes the master would come to discuss official business with the mistress, and she would catch a glimpse of him.

But ever since she moved to the small courtyard, she hadn’t seen the master in a long time. She feared he had forgotten her, this concubine.

She pushed her son, Xie Shiyou, forward. "Yun’ge, weren’t you just talking about your father last night? Go greet him now."

Xie Shiyou immediately stepped forward and called out, "Greetings, Father."

Xie Jingyu gave a faint nod and walked straight into the Shengju courtyard, ascending the steps toward the side hall of Yun Chu’s residence.

Tingyu, ignored from beginning to end, clenched the handkerchief in her hand tightly.

She didn’t understand. The master had been slapped by the mistress, yet instead of blaming her, he had come rushing over.

Just because the mistress was the legitimate daughter of a great general, did that mean everyone had to fawn over her?

"What are you still doing here?" Tingfeng walked over, sneering coldly. "Don’t think that just because you gave the Xie family a young master, the master will treat you differently. Hmph, a servant who betrays her mistress, you’re doomed to be spat upon for life..."

Tingyu tightened her lips, grabbed her child’s hand, and turned away.

Xie Jingyu sat in the side hall for a while before Yun Chu finally emerged from the bedchamber.

She wore a plain white dress, with no hairpins or ornaments, and her face was bare of any makeup. Her simplicity only accentuated her natural beauty; glancing once, she was graceful and moving; glancing again, she seemed capable of toppling cities and nations.

An uncontrollable emotion surged in Xie Jingyu’s chest.

Yun Chu’s face remained expressionless. "Let’s go," she said coldly.

Xie Jingyu suppressed the inappropriate emotion and walked out with her.

At the estate’s gate, a carriage was waiting, and behind it was a cart. When they saw what was on the cart, Yun Chu’s face finally showed a flicker of emotion.

"This is a nanmu coffin I found last night. It never rots, even after a thousand years," Xie Jingyu said. "I failed the children. I will do everything I can to make it up to them."

Yun Chu lowered her eyelids and lifted her skirt to enter the carriage.

The journey to the outskirts of the city was smooth, taking about half an hour before they finally reached the village Xie Jingyu had mentioned.

Tingshuang and Tingfeng supported Yun Chu as she stepped down from the carriage.

Xie Jingyu looked at the mountain ahead. "The children’s bodies are on the mountain. The path is rough, so be careful, Madam."

He led the way, with Yun Chu and the two maids following behind. Behind them, four strong men carried the small nanmu coffins in pairs, and the group slowly made their way up the mountain.

It had rained for many days, leaving the mountain path muddy and treacherous. After just a few steps, Yun Chu’s shoes were soaked through, and the hem of her white dress was stained with black mud.

But she didn’t care. She didn’t need the maids’ support, taking each step forward on her own.

After nearly half an hour, they finally reached a slightly flatter area. Xie Jingyu stopped and said, "This is the place."

Yun Chu looked around. There wasn’t even a small mound here, just lush spring vegetation and blooming wildflowers. In one spot, the wildflowers had bloomed early, their vibrant purples and pinks unusually beautiful.

Her heart suddenly trembled.

Xie Jingyu spoke, "Madam, step aside."

Yun Chu shook her head. "Begin."

The four men approached with their tools, carefully clearing the wildflowers before starting to dig.

As soon as they broke the soil, underground water began to seep out.

Yun Chu thought of the dream she’d had; the children saying they were cold. Was it because they had been soaked in water all this time?

The thought of the children not even finding peace in death made her eyes sting, and tears streamed down uncontrollably.

Her appearance tugged at Xie Jingyu’s heart.

He stepped forward, trying to put his arm around her shoulder, but she dodged.

He withdrew his hand and said, "Madam, my father has an estate that is a feng shui treasure land. We can bury the children’s remains in a place with birdsong and flowers..."

"It’s unnecessary."

A cold voice interrupted.

Xie Jingyu turned to see Yun Ze leading a group of people up the mountain.

At the sight of Yun Ze, Yun Chu’s unsettled heart finally found peace. Her voice was slightly choked. "Big Brother."

Yun Ze raised his hand and gently patted her shoulder before turning to Xie Jingyu. "As an outsider, I shouldn’t meddle in the Xie family’s affairs. But Xie Jingyu, you’ve gone too far. Four years ago, if you had no intention of burying the children properly, you could have told me instead of carelessly burying them in some random mountain. These past four years, who knows how much the children have suffered, or whether their souls have found peace. If they cannot be reincarnated, it’s all thanks to you, their own father!"

Yun Ze, usually so gentle, delivered a harsh rebuke that left Xie Jingyu unable to lift his head.

He was twenty-eight this year, older than Yun Ze by a few years, yet he couldn’t utter a single word in his defense.

"Of course, I can understand you too," Yun Ze’s tone softened slightly. "At that time, you were on the rise in your career. How could you allow such a trivial matter to delay your progress? Besides, you already had three children, it’s only natural you wouldn’t care much about two more who had passed."

The softened tone carried words that struck straight to the heart. Xie Jingyu struggled to speak. "Big Brother, I..."

"Enough. No need to say more." Yun Ze’s imposing presence filled the air. "The children you Xie family do not cherish will be treasured by the Yun family. These two children will be buried in the Yun family’s ancestral land. There’s no need for Lord Xie to trouble himself."

The more than ten attendants Yun Ze had brought forward, pushing aside the four Xie family servants.

Xie Jingyu’s face darkened, but no one present cared about his feelings.

The Yun family guards carefully dug into the soil. Before long, they uncovered the remains of two infants, tiny, no larger than a palm.

Yun Chu’s tears fell like a broken dam, impossible to control.

Her knees buckled, and she slid downward.

"Chu’er, you are their mother. Kneeling to them will only bring them misfortune in their next life," Yun Ze pulled her up. "Tingshuang, support your mistress properly."

In his heart, Chu’er would always be the beloved young lady of the Yun family.

His sister, who should have had a lifetime of happiness and beauty; why did she have to endure the pain of life and death separation?

Yun Ze’s heart twisted in agony.

Yun Chu cried until she was nearly out of breath.

She clutched Tingshuang’s hand and slowly moved forward, stepping up to the small pit.

She crouched down, personally scooping up the tiny bones and placing the children into the new coffins with her own hands...

Her hands trembled the entire time, tears streamed endlessly, and her legs grew weaker...

After personally burying the children in the Yun family’s ancestral cemetery, Yun Chu lost consciousness, knowing nothing more.

---

chapters.title: Madam Xie Falls Ill
chapters.content:
Yun Chu fell ill after returning to the Xie residence.
