The illness struck like a collapsing mountain, her entire body ached terribly, and she couldn’t sleep peacefully.

In the morning, those who came to pay their respects waited in the side hall. Tingshuang stepped out and said softly, "Madam is ill. There’s no need to come pay respects for the time being."

Everyone knew this time, Madam was truly ill. Several physicians had been called, and the scent of medicine permeated the courtyard.

Jiang Concubine looked worried. "Shengju is in chaos. Why don’t I stay and take care of Madam?"

Tingshuang shook her head. "Madam has us servants to attend to her. There’s no need to trouble Concubine Jiang. Everyone, please return."

Xie Pin stood up. "Mother is ill. I shouldn’t bother her with trivial matters, but I truly don’t know what to do. Sister Tingshuang, can you help me make a decision?"

"Is it about Old Madam’s birthday celebration?" Tingshuang replied. "Madam has instructed that if Elder Sister truly cannot decide, she may ask Madam and Old Madam."

Xie Pin pressed her lips together.

She didn’t understand. They were just two children who had died four years ago, why had Mother suddenly started caring about them?

For the sake of those two dead children, she had slapped Father, and now she was feigning illness to avoid managing household affairs. Did she really want to completely turn against Father?

Was Mother not afraid of losing her authority as the mistress of the household?

After leaving Shengju, Xie Pin took the account books to Anshou Hall.

Old Madam and Madam Yuan were in conversation.

"Even though those two children died young, they were still blood of the Xie family. How could they be buried at the edge of the Yun family’s ancestral land?" Old Madam gritted her teeth. "Yun Chu is no longer a Yun family girl; she is the legitimate wife of the Xie family. How dare she bring such great humiliation upon the Xie family?"

Madam Yuan sighed. "If we examine this closely, it is indeed the Xie family’s fault."

Originally, the children’s bodies should have been taken back to the Xie family’s old residence in Ji Prefecture and buried near the Xie family ancestral shrine. But...

In the end, it was Jingyu who had not taken the deaths of those two children seriously enough. It was understandable that the Yun family had taken such drastic measures.

"Jingyu was supposed to be promoted to upper fifth rank, but because of this, he’s become the target of impeachment at court," Old Madam said, furious. "If it weren’t for Yun Chu’s sudden idea to rebury the children, how would the Xie family have ended up in this mess? She feigns illness and ignores everything, how comfortable for her, while Jingyu struggles at every step in court..."

Madam Yuan didn’t know what to say.

At this moment, Xie Pin stepped in, greeted the two elders, and said, "Old Madam, your birthday is approaching. There are still two matters I haven’t settled. I originally wanted to ask Mother for advice, but since she’s ill, I’ve had to come and trouble Old Madam and Grandmother."

Old Madam’s expression was far from pleasant.

The Xie estate was growing larger, and so were its trivial matters. Yun Chu actually couldn’t be bothered with something as important as a birthday celebration, leaving everything to Pin, an unmarried girl!

Was she determined to show that the Xie family couldn’t function without the mistress, as some kind of revenge for the family not properly burying the children four years ago?

She shouldn’t have given Yun Chu twenty thousand taels of silver to continue managing the household. It had only made Yun Chu think she had the entire Xie family under her thumb.

A cold smile appeared on Old Madam’s face. "Pin’er, what two matters haven’t been settled? Speak, and we’ll discuss them together."

Xie Pin replied, "One is the guest list, and the other is the menu for the banquet. I was thinking..."

She carefully laid out her thoughts.

She still wanted to invite some high-ranking officials and nobles. Whether they came or not was up to them, but they should at least extend the invitation. What if they were willing to come and show support?

Old Madam shook her head. "Because of yesterday’s incident, the Xie family has become a joke in the capital. Who would be willing to come to the celebration?"

Xie Pin didn’t dare say more and moved on to the second topic. "I want Old Madam’s birthday banquet to be extravagant, but a dozen tables would cost at least two thousand taels of silver. The household accounts don’t have that much..."

Old Madam didn’t hesitate before nodding. She only celebrated her birthday once a year, so naturally, it should be done well.

The banquets of the past three years had been especially grand, likely because Yun Chu had supplemented them with her dowry money.

This year, with Yun Chu feigning illness and ignoring these matters, if the banquet turned out poorly, the first to laugh at the Xie family would be the Yun family.

She turned to Mama Zhou at her side. "Give Pin’er three thousand taels of silver."

Xie Pin’s face lit up with a smile. "Thank you, Old Madam. I will definitely organize a magnificent birthday banquet for you."

If this banquet went well, her reputation as a capable manager would spread, and suitors would surely flock to the Xie family.

With the silver in hand, Xie Pin managed everything with even greater ease, devoting all her energy to the birthday banquet.

After three days of rest, Yun Chu’s body gradually recovered, though her spirits remained somewhat low. She spent her days sitting by the window reading, which worried her maids, Tingshuang and the others.

"Madam," Tingong plucked up her courage to enter and said with a bowed head, "You’ve rested for three days, and your illness is better. The matter of martial arts training cannot be delayed any longer."

Yun Chu closed her book. "Look at me, I actually forgot something so important. Let’s go, to practice."

She changed into a more comfortable outfit and followed Tingong to the courtyard to practice her horse stance.

Though it was spring, the air was still chilly. But after crouching in the courtyard for nearly an hour, her body quickly broke out in a fine sheen of sweat.

Tingong spoke up. "Madam, time is up."

Yun Chu remained still. "I can endure a little longer."

She had wasted three or four days and needed to make up for the lost time.

At first, she could hold her stance steadily, but gradually, her strength began to wane, and her body swayed occasionally.

Tingshuang tried to persuade her several times, but she refused, insisting on holding the stance for two full hours.

After the noon hour, Yun Chu finally stopped. Tingshuang helped her bathe, and after changing into fresh clothes, she finally regained some energy.

"Madam, Old Madam’s birthday banquet is in a few days," Tingshuang said as she dried her hair. "This year, the entire banquet is being handled by Elder Sister. I’ve heard a few things, and it seems there are many problems. Madam, you should guide Elder Sister a bit. Otherwise, on the day of the banquet, something might go wrong."

Yun Chu looked at her reflection in the mirror. "Spread the word. Say that Madam Xie is ill, so ill she cannot get out of bed."

Tingshuang hurriedly said, "Madam, you mustn’t curse yourself like that."

"If a casual remark could make it come true, wouldn’t that be chaotic?" A faint smile appeared on Yun Chu’s face. "If I’m ill, then whatever goes wrong with the banquet has nothing to do with me. Understand?"

Tingshuang’s eyes lit up. "This servant understands."

After drying Yun Chu’s hair, she quickly left the inner courtyard and called Chen Defu over to give him a few instructions.

The news that the eldest legitimate daughter of the General’s mansion, the wife of the Ministry of Revenue’s Xie Jingyu, had fallen ill instantly spread throughout the capital.

"Did you all hear about how Madam Xie recently reburied her deceased children, dragging two coffins all the way from the southern part of the city to the west?"

"Those Xie family people are truly shameless. Even though the children died young, they were still the blood of the direct line. How could they just bury them in some random mountain? Don’t they fear retribution?"

"A fine daughter of the General’s mansion, and she ended up marrying Xie Jingyu when he was only a seventh-rank official. I don’t know how the Yun family ever chose such a marriage alliance!"

...

"I heard from the owner of Shande Hall Pharmacy that the Xie family’s inner courtyard is in chaos, concubines poisoning each other to cause miscarriages. Madam Xie’s children who died young might have been harmed as well."

"I’ve heard people from the Xie residence say that Madam Xie is very ill. She can’t even manage Old Madam’s birthday banquet, and it seems she can’t even get out of bed. Could she have been poisoned by one of the concubines in the inner courtyard?"

"The mistress of the household cannot bear children, while those concubines have all given birth to sons. Perhaps they’ve developed wild ambitions, thinking that if the mistress dies, they might be elevated to her position."

"If Lord Xie can’t even manage the women in his own household, how can we expect him to be a good official?"

chapters.title: A Thief in the Bedroom
chapters.content:
The rumors from the streets and alleys reached the Xie household, and the old matriarch was so furious that she smashed two teacups.

Their humble Xie family, even if the lady of the house were to fall gravely ill, it wouldn’t have become common knowledge. The issue was that Yun Chu’s status was too special.

She was the eldest legitimate daughter of a first-rank general’s mansion, once the most celebrated jewel of the capital. Back then, countless suitors had nearly worn out the threshold of the Yun residence seeking her hand. Now, just as many were eyeing the Xie family’s inner quarters.

“She clearly recovered from her illness, who spread the rumor that she was dying?” the old matriarch said in a deep voice. “The servants in this mansion can’t keep their mouths shut anymore.”

Last time, the incident of He-shi poisoning Tao Concubine had also been leaked by someone.

With these two scandals spreading wildly, it made the Xie family’s inner quarters seem particularly chaotic.

As the old saying goes, *If one cannot sweep their own house, how can they sweep the world?* A man who cannot even manage the women in his household, would the imperial court promote him?

After a moment of hesitation, Zhou Mama said, “Ever since the lady fell ill, all matters big and small in the mansion have been decided by the eldest miss. Things have indeed been out of order.”

“Does that mean the Xie family can’t function without the lady of the house?” the old matriarch said coldly. “Zhou Mama, call Xie Pin over. I must personally oversee every detail of the birthday banquet. We cannot give people any reason to gossip.”

Zhou Mama took her leave to carry out the order.

The past few days had been clear, and the flowers in the Shengju Courtyard were in full bloom. Yun Chu sat in the flower hall reading a book.

Tingshuang came to report, “The eldest miss just took over household management and dismissed the servants and pages. They were very dissatisfied with her orders, whenever she assigned tasks, they only completed seven out of ten. The mansion is in chaos. However, this servant heard that the old matriarch plans to personally oversee the birthday banquet.”

Yun Chu smiled faintly.

The banquet was only three days away. Everything that needed to be prepared was already in place. Even if the old matriarch intervened now, she couldn’t change much.

“Elder Chen has handed over four or five of the Xie family’s shops to He Xu for management,” Tingshuang continued. “This time, the eldest miss entrusted He Xu with purchasing everything needed for the birthday banquet. That He Xu is truly bold, this servant did a rough calculation and found that he embezzled at least four hundred taels of silver.”

Even Yun Chu couldn’t help but click her tongue in shock. The old matriarch had only allocated three thousand taels for the banquet. If He Xu had taken four hundred, and other servants had also skimmed off the top, some taking thirty or forty taels, others fifteen or eighteen, then at most, only two thousand taels would actually go toward the banquet. That was already considered decent.

“He Xu gave a large portion of the embezzled silver to that person in the small temple,” Tingshuang said in a low voice. “He-shi has been injured, but lately, she’s been much more obedient.”

Yun Chu’s smile deepened. “Then let her rest well for a few more days.”

In a few days, He-shi wouldn’t have such peaceful days anymore.

Tingshuang already knew what Yun Chu intended to do. A shadow of worry crossed her brow. “Madam, do you truly intend to go through with this?”

Yun Chu took Tingshuang’s hand. “I’ve been married into the Xie family for five years. Do you think I’ve ever been truly happy?”

Tingshuang shook her head.

In the first month after her marriage, Madam had been full of hope. But then, she was coldly neglected by the master. Later, after the child’s death, she had never truly smiled from the heart again.

Over the years, Madam’s life had been the same day after day, seemingly calm, yet without any hope.

But recently, Tingshuang had finally seen a different spark in Madam’s eyes.

She worried for Madam.

She feared that something might happen, making Madam’s days even harder.

“Tingshuang, you and I are the same age. It’s time for you to marry,” Yun Chu said gently, looking at her. “If you have someone in mind, just tell me. If not, I’ll find a loyal and honest man for you…”

“Madam!” Tingshuang knelt down in fright. “This servant doesn’t want to marry! I want to stay by your side and serve you for the rest of my life!”

Yun Chu pulled her up.

Whether Tingshuang married or not, she couldn’t let her stay in the Xie mansion.

In this new life, no one knew if the tragedy would repeat. She feared that Tingshuang would die again in the devastating fire that had consumed the Xie mansion…

The sky gradually darkened. A maidservant brought in dinner.

Although Yun Chu no longer managed household affairs, she was still the lady of the house. Neither Xie Pin nor the other servants dared to cut her food rations.

As she ate, a sudden commotion erupted in the front courtyard. Tingfeng rushed in to report, “Madam, it’s not good! A thief suddenly appeared near the small gate in the southeast. All the pages and servant women have gone to catch them!”

Yun Chu frowned.

She had managed the household for four or five years, and the Xie mansion’s gates had always been well-guarded. Nothing this absurd had ever happened before.

She ordered, “Guard the door of Shengju Courtyard tightly. No one is to go out unless absolutely necessary.”

Night had fallen completely. The commotion about the thief had left some people uneasy.

But Shengju Courtyard had Qiutong there. The servants had all seen her martial arts skills before. With Qiutong standing at the door, everyone felt much more at ease.

After waiting for a long time, word came from the front courtyard that no thief had been found, and all the other courtyards were normal. The matter was dismissed as a false alarm. But Yun Chu didn’t let her guard down. She ordered the servants to form groups of three, with Qiutong leading them, to patrol the courtyard all night.

After bathing, Yun Chu entered the inner room and sat down at the dressing table.

Tingxue carefully removed her hair ornaments and combed her hair straight before bowing her head and retreating, gently closing the door behind her.

Yun Chu sat on the edge of the bed, took off her shoes, and lay down, pulling the blanket from the side over herself. Just as she was about to cover herself, she suddenly sensed something was wrong.

She held her breath and heard a faint breathing sound that wasn’t her own.

In that instant, her mind snapped to attention.

She carefully sat up and reached under the pillow, pulling out a dagger.

This was a gift from her grandfather for her coming-of-age ceremony. It was engraved with her name and was extremely sharp. She gripped the hilt with one hand and, with the other, suddenly threw the blanket open.

In the moment the blade was about to swing, her hand froze completely.

“Why is it you?”

Under the blanket was a delicate, fair-skinned child.

It was the young heir of the Pingxi Prince’s mansion.

“You, a woman, dare to point a knife at me! If you so much as harm a single hair on my head, my father, the prince, won’t let you off!” the child declared.

Yun Chu’s lips twitched.

She put the dagger away and said, “If your father finds out you snuck into someone else’s bedroom in the middle of the night, I doubt he’ll let you off either.”

Chu Hongyu huffed, “If it weren’t for the rumor that you were dying, I wouldn’t have come! You take kindness for granted!”

The little boy crossed his arms and turned his back to her, showing only one puffed-up cheek.

Yun Chu’s heart melted instantly.

So this child had come all this way, risking so much, just because he heard she was ill.

Truth be told, they didn’t have a deep friendship. For him to care so much was her fortune.

Perhaps it was because of that dream she had, where her own son’s face had turned into the young heir’s, that she felt a natural closeness to this child.

She couldn’t resist reaching out and poking his cheek.

Normally, Chu Hongyu hated it when people pinched his cheeks. Even the emperor would make him uncomfortable.

But now, he didn’t feel the slightest aversion. In fact, he even hoped she would poke him again.

Yun Chu knew when to stop. After one poke, she withdrew her hand and said, “My illness is already better. As you can see, I’m fine. I’ll have someone send you back to the prince’s mansion.”

The little boy’s eyes widened.

She wanted to send him away so soon after he’d arrived? How heartless!

Just as he was about to speak, footsteps suddenly sounded outside the door.

---

chapters.title: Let You Stay One Night
chapters.content:
“Master.”

The maids of Shengju Courtyard all knelt in greeting.

Xie Jingyu was exhausted.

That day at court, he had been impeached by the censor. What had once been a promising path to promotion to the fifth rank was now completely out of reach.

If the rumors on the streets grew worse, he feared he might even be demoted…

In the past, the Yun family had silently supported him as a marital connection, but this time, the Yun family showed the Xie family no favor at all. He had no support at court.

Dejected, he left the imperial palace and went to the Yu mansion again, but this time, Minister Yu wouldn’t even let him through the door. He waited outside the Yu mansion for several hours before finally accepting that Minister Yu had completely given up on him. Like a stray dog, he returned to the Xie mansion.

He stood at the door of Shengju Courtyard and asked Tingshuang, “Has the lady’s condition improved?”

Tingshuang lowered her gaze. “Madam appears to have recovered, but in truth, she suffers from a heart ailment. She can’t bring herself to do anything.”

Xie Jingyu removed his official hat.

Did he not know that Yun Chu’s illness was emotional?

But the child was already dead and properly buried. The past should be left in the past. Why dwell on it?

Her illness had thrown the entire Xie family into chaos.

He had never realized how much influence the lady of the house had over a family.

He asked, “Has the lady gone to sleep?”

“Madam went to bed about an hour ago,” Tingshuang replied. “If Master has any business, you may come back early tomorrow.”

Xie Jingyu said nothing more and turned to leave.

As he walked away from Shengju Courtyard, he saw Xie Shian on the path.

Xie Shian was clearly waiting for him. He cupped his hands and said, “Father, the rumors in the city have reached the academy. They must have reached the imperial court as well. Were you impeached by someone today?”

Xie Jingyu looked at his eldest son with admiration.

Despite only moving between the Xie family’s academy and home, his son had deduced the situation at court. He was truly a prodigy.

“What are your thoughts?” Xie Jingyu asked.

“The outsiders’ discussions focus on two points,” Xie Shian said slowly. “First, the burial of the twins four years ago in the Xie mansion. That matter is already settled, so the Xie family can only remain silent. Second, the rumors about Mother’s illness have grown more and more exaggerated. Soon, it will be Old Madam’s birthday banquet. If Mother attends, the rumors about the Xie family’s inner quarters being in disarray will collapse on their own.”

Xie Jingyu nodded. “Then, do you think your mother will attend the banquet?”

Xie Shian fell silent.

His mother had just suffered a great blow. Would she cooperate with the Xie family to dispel the rumors? He wasn’t sure.

Xie Jingyu sighed. “Even if we’re not sure, we have to try.”

Father and son continued talking as they walked farther away.

Only after their voices had completely faded did Yun Chu let out a breath of relief.

She looked at the child curled up in the blanket. “Let’s go. I’ll send you out of the mansion first.”

“I won’t go!” Chu Hongyu suddenly wrapped his arms around her waist, pressing his head against her chest, looking utterly stubborn.

Yun Chu persuaded him, “Young Master, if you’re not at home in the middle of the night, you’ll be discovered soon. Can you bear the Pingxi Prince’s wrath?”

She thought the child would be afraid, but to her surprise, the little boy proudly raised his eyebrows. “This evening, my father was ordered by the emperor to go suppress bandits. He won’t be in the capital for the next few days. I even found a child my age to impersonate me and stay in the prince’s mansion. Don’t worry, no one will notice I’m gone.”

Yun Chu: …

She had no idea what to say.

At that moment, the window was lightly tapped.

Before Yun Chu could get up to see what was happening, a pained cry came from outside the window.

“Which thief dares to lurk outside our Madam’s window!”

It was Qiutong’s voice.

Yun Chu glanced at the child on the bed and saw him scrambling toward the window, trying to push it open.

She grabbed the child and tossed him into the bed curtains, then raised her voice. “Qiutong, tie up the thief outside and send him to the authorities!”

“No, you can’t!” Chu Hongyu was so anxious that sweat beaded on his forehead. “He’s not a thief, he’s my guard. His name is A Mao. Don’t send him to the officials!”

Yun Chu deliberately kept a straight face. “Was the thief earlier at the southeast gate also your guard?”

The little boy’s face fell. “There were always people patrolling back and forth at the Xie mansion’s gate. I had no choice but to have A Mao pretend to be a thief to lure them away. A Mao really didn’t do anything bad.”

At his expression, Yun Chu’s heart softened.

She looked toward the window. “Qiutong, bring the man inside.”

She got out of bed, put on her shoes and outer robe, and led the child out of the inner room.

Qiutong and Tingshuang brought the guard in together. When they saw a child appear in the room, both of their eyes nearly popped out of their sockets.

Especially Qiutong; she was skilled in martial arts, yet she hadn’t noticed an extra person in Madam’s bedroom.

Yun Chu made a gesture, and Tingshuang quickly closed the door.

“Mmm! Mmm!”

The guard’s mouth was gagged, and he made muffled sounds.

Chu Hongyu quickly rushed over and pulled the rag from his mouth. “A Mao, are you alright?”

“I’m fine, Young Master.” A Mao looked his master up and down, then said with lingering fear, “Young Master, are you alright?”

Qiutong was stunned. “Madam, what in the world is going on?”

Tingshuang had already recognized the child and was equally shocked. “How did the young heir of the Pingxi Prince end up in Madam’s bedroom?”

“While it’s dark and the mansion is in chaos, Qiutong, take these two out,” Yun Chu ordered. “Don’t let anyone see them.”

If Xie Jingyu found out that the young heir of the Pingxi Prince had come to the Xie mansion, he would surely try every means to use the child to get close to the prince. She didn’t want a child to become a tool for Xie Jingyu’s rise to power.

“I said I won’t go! I won’t go!” Chu Hongyu scrambled onto Yun Chu with all four limbs, clinging to her. “I want to stay here. I won’t go, I won’t!”

Qiutong stepped forward, grabbed the back of the child’s collar, and lifted him up. “Young Master, even though you’re a child, you’re still an outsider. It’s improper for you to stay in Madam’s room. This servant will send you back to the prince’s mansion.”

“Waaah! I won’t go!” The little boy kicked his legs in the air. “I finally found a chance to sneak out of the prince’s mansion, finally managed to get into the Xie mansion, and you want to send me away so soon? I don’t want to like you anymore! You’re horrible! Waaah!”

A Mao chimed in, “A few days ago, when Young Master heard that Madam Xie was ill, he couldn’t eat or sleep well and lost several pounds. Only when Prince Xie left the mansion did Young Master finally find a chance to sneak out. Our Young Master has never had a mother’s love, Madam, please take pity on our Young Master…”

Yun Chu’s heart ached.

She pulled the kicking child into her arms.

She knew the young heir of the Pingxi Prince was four years old, but compared to Xie Shiyou, who was the same age, he was far too thin; he looked more like a three-year-old.

She said softly, “Then I’ll allow you to stay here for one night. But you must leave at dawn. Alright?”

The little boy stopped crying and buried his face in her embrace.

chapters.title: I Like You So Much
chapters.content:
The night was quiet.

Chu Hongyu was too excited to sleep, his arms and legs wrapped around Yun Chu. Yun Chu was overwhelmed; though she had raised Xie Shiyun herself, he had never dared to be so bold.

"Don’t close your eyes. Let’s talk."

The little one pressed against her, prying her eyelids open.

"Little Prince, do you know what time it is?" Yun Chu sighed, rubbing her temples. "Children who sleep early grow tall. Go to sleep."

"I’m Chu Hongyu. Call me Yu Ge’er, it sounds more affectionate." The boy wrapped his arms around her neck and whispered, "Then what should I call you?"

Yun Chu was at a loss. "Call me Auntie."

"No, Auntie sounds too distant." Chu Hongyu tilted his head, thinking hard. "How about I call you Mother?"

Yun Chu was startled. "Yu Ge’er, you can’t say things like that. If someone hears, I’ll be the one in trouble."

The boy quickly explained, "I know you’re already married, so you can’t be my real mother. But what if I call you Mother in private? Then no one will hear, and you won’t get in trouble."

"You—"

The refusal died on her lips. Yun Chu couldn’t bring herself to say it.

Her heart softened completely. She had pretended to be cold, hoping he would leave soon, but now she couldn’t control her emotions. She reached out and pulled the child into her arms.

"Mmm, you smell so good." Chu Hongyu closed his eyes. "Just like the mother in my dreams. I really like you so much..."

The child mumbled to himself before drifting off to sleep.

Yun Chu gently stroked his hair.

This child looked exactly like the one in her dreams. Her heart had already opened to him.

How she wished her own child were still alive, that he could sleep by her side... but it was all just a vain hope.

Yun Chu slowly fell asleep.

The next morning, a tickle in her nose made her sneeze, and she woke up.

She saw the little one holding a thread, deliberately tickling her nose. When she sneezed, he grinned triumphantly.

"Mother, you’re awake. Good morning."

The word "Mother" made Yun Chu unable to feel any resistance toward him.

She picked him up. "Yu Ge’er, put on your clothes. Let’s have breakfast first."

Chu Hongyu obediently let her dress him, then held her hand and followed her to the side hall.

Because she was ill, those who came to pay their respects were turned away at the courtyard gate by Tingshuang. The other maids in the courtyard were busy with their tasks, so only her most trusted maids remained in the side hall.

"Yu Ge’er, what would you like to eat?" Yun Chu asked gently. "These steamed buns with mutton and milk are delicious. Try one?"

Chu Hongyu lifted his chin. "I want you to feed me."

Expecting refusal, he was surprised when Yun Chu picked up a bun and brought it to his lips. He took a bite. The taste was similar to those at the prince’s mansion, but for some reason, it was especially delicious. He ate one, then another, and another, seven or eight in a row, all fed to him by Yun Chu.

"Mother, you’re so kind. I like you so much!"

He had never been this happy before. It felt as if he were soaking in a jar of honey, like a dream.

Yun Chu smiled at him. "Are you full?"

Chu Hongyu rubbed his round little belly. "I’ve never eaten this much before."

Yun Chu stood up. "If you’re full, then let’s go."

Her words struck like a bolt from the blue. Chu Hongyu froze in shock.

Had this woman been so kind to him just to make it easier to send him away?

The happier he had been, the more heartbroken he felt now.

His eyes blinked, and tears fell like golden beans.

Yun Chu hardened her heart. "The little prince stayed out all night. It’s time to go home."

"Wahhh—"

Chu Hongyu burst into tears, sobbing uncontrollably.

Tingxue spoke up: "Madam, early this morning, I went out to inquire. The Prince of Pingxi is currently at a mountain outside the city, dozens of miles away, suppressing bandits. He won’t be returning to the capital anytime soon..."

Back when the third young master had been raised by Madam, she had been the primary maid attending to him. She understood the nature of children this young. It was clear that the little prince genuinely liked their madam.

Madam had suffered so much. Having someone who truly liked her stay here wouldn’t be a bad thing.

She hoped the little prince could help Madam step out of the shadows soon...

Tingshuang also whispered: "The Prince of Pingxi’s mansion is peaceful now, which means no one has noticed the little prince’s disappearance. Madam need not worry."

Yun Chu sighed.

She suddenly felt sorry for the child.

He was only four years old, and no one in the vast prince’s mansion had noticed he was missing all night.

If he had a mother, how could his disappearance go unnoticed?

Tingfeng entered to report: "Madam, the master has arrived."

Yun Chu glanced at the time. It should be just after morning court. In the past, Xie Jingyu would handle official business after court, then socialize with colleagues, usually returning only at dusk. Now, with no official duties or social obligations, she could guess why he had come to Shengju at this hour.

She reached out and wiped Chu Hongyu’s tears clean, then said, "If you want to stay with me, you must behave and not let anyone outside this place discover your presence. Can you do that?"

Chu Hongyu’s eyes widened in disbelief. "Mother, you’re really not sending me away?"

"Only temporarily." Yun Chu ruffled his hair. "Stay quiet and don’t make a sound."

She stood and walked out of the side hall.

Standing on the steps, she saw Xie Jingyu under the eaves.

At twenty-eight, Xie Jingyu still looked like a dashing young man, able to attract the gaze of every maid.

In her past life, she had willingly raised so many illegitimate children, secretly hoping that one day, Xie Jingyu would notice her.

But now, in this new life, she felt nothing but disgust for this man.

"Master, why have you returned to the mansion so early?"

She asked, feigning innocence.

Xie Jingyu looked concerned. "Are you feeling better?"

Yun Chu nodded. "I’m fine."

Seeing she didn’t want to talk, Xie Jingyu didn’t press further. After a pause, he said, "The old madam’s birthday is in two days. Will you be attending?"

"These past few days, my appetite hasn’t been good. I’m afraid attending a banquet might affect the guests’ appetites. However—" she changed her tone, "Since the Xie family couldn’t host the flower-appreciation banquet this year, this birthday banquet is the only chance for everyone to gather and enjoy themselves. Naturally, I should make an appearance to greet the guests. Husband, rest assured."

Xie Jingyu breathed a sigh of relief.

He had expected to persuade her, but Yun Chu had agreed so readily.

He had misjudged her.

Just as he was about to speak, Tingyu entered the courtyard carrying a bowl of soup. "Madam has been ill for a long time. I specially made this tonic soup to bring to her. I didn’t expect Master to be here as well."

Xie Jingyu’s expression was indifferent. "Take good care of your madam."

With that, he turned and left Shengju.

Watching his retreating figure, Tingyu’s face was filled with disappointment. She had finally encountered the master, yet she couldn’t even exchange a few words with him.

Yun Chu was about to enter the side hall when she saw Tingyu holding a bowl of soup in front of her.

---

chapters.title: I’m Jealous of Him
chapters.content:
Yun Chu looked at Tingyu, her expression complex.

Tingyu and Tingshuang were born in the same year, both twenty now. Tingyu was already the mother of a four-year-old child.

As far back as she could remember, Tingyu and Tingshuang had been by her side, serving her. Tingshuang was steady, Tingyu was meticulous; they were like sisters to her.

When she was twelve, she had accidentally fallen into the water. Tingyu had jumped in to save her, but Tingyu herself hadn’t made it out in time and had been in a coma for over half a month.

Tingyu had saved her life, so even when Tingyu had climbed into Xie Jingyu’s bed behind her back, she had never truly blamed Tingyu.

But later, when the Yun family fell from grace, Tingyu had chosen to side with the Xie family and even ordered Xie Shiyun to deliver the cup of poison to her.

She couldn’t let go of the past.

Tingyu had saved her, but she had also betrayed her. The two canceled each other out, so Yun Chu treated Tingyu coldly.

Yet Tingyu kept coming back.

A greedy person would eventually suffer because of that greed.

"Mother!"

Just as she was thinking, Xie Shiyun threw himself into her arms.

This child had been sent to her side as soon as he was born. Apart from letting Tingyu nurse him, he had spent all his time with her.

It wasn’t until he was three that he moved out of her bedchamber to live with Tingyu in a side courtyard.

"Mother, it’s been so long since I’ve eaten with you or seen you." Xie Shiyun pouted. "Don’t you like me anymore?"

Yun Chu’s smile didn’t reach her eyes. "You’re older now. You should understand the rules."

Tingyu quickly pulled her son away. "I will make sure Shiyun behaves properly in the future. Madam, please drink the soup while it’s hot."

"Tingyu, you’re practically a mistress now. You shouldn’t be doing such rough work in the kitchen anymore." Yun Chu said coolly. "I’m tired. You may leave."

Tingyu nodded and took Xie Shiyun with her.

"Mother, why doesn’t Auntie pay attention to me anymore?" Xie Shiyun was deeply aggrieved. "It wasn’t like this before..."

Tingyu didn’t understand either. In the past, Madam had doted on Shiyun so much, but now she barely spoke to him. What had gone wrong?

Yun Chu entered the side hall. The moment she closed the door, Chu Hongyu rushed over from the side and hugged her.

The boy tilted his head up and asked, "That child just now called you Mother. Is he your son?"

Yun Chu chuckled. "Why do you ask?"

"I’m jealous of him." Chu Hongyu bit his lower lip. "Jealous that he can openly call you Mother. Jealous that he gets to see you every day. I want to be him."

Yun Chu softened her voice. "You are you. You don’t need to be anyone else."

"If it weren’t for my sister still at home, I’d never want to go back." Chu Hongyu looked up with his big, dark eyes. "Mother, my sister is very pretty and very cute, but she can’t speak. Would you like a child who can’t talk?"

Yun Chu was surprised.

Everyone in the capital knew that the Prince of Pingxi had a pair of children, but no one had ever mentioned that the young lady was mute.

Her voice grew even gentler. "If she’s as obedient and sensible as you, of course I would like her."

Praise made Chu Hongyu so happy his mouth couldn’t close.

Just then, Tingshuang came to report some matters. The boy, very sensibly, said, "I’ll go read a book over there so I don’t disturb Mother’s work."

He walked to a low table in the side hall, pulled out a book from somewhere, and began reading seriously. His short legs couldn’t reach the ground, leaving him dangling in midair.

A smile appeared on Yun Chu’s face, one she didn’t even realize was there.

She turned her head and said softly, "Arrange someone to watch the Prince of Pingxi’s mansion. If there’s any movement, report back immediately."

Tingfeng took the order and went to the front courtyard to make arrangements.

Tingshuang, holding an account book, carefully reported the income from the shops and estates outside the city from the previous month.

As Yun Chu listened to the numbers, she slowly furrowed her brows.

Just like in her past life, her estates outside the city were declining, slowly going downhill, until they were all sold off.

She needed to think carefully, aside from ice, what other businesses would be profitable...

While she was talking to Tingshuang, Chu Hongyu grew increasingly bored. He didn’t like reading, and being able to sit still for a quarter of an hour was already impressive. The main issue was that he didn’t recognize many of the characters in the book, so he couldn’t understand it. Pretending was exhausting.

"Mother, I need to pee."

The boy jumped down from the couch. Tingxue went over to take him to the outhouse at the back.

Because there was now a child in Shengju, Tingshuang had sent the older servants and maids in the courtyard to help with the birthday banquet preparations. The entire courtyard now only had the maids who had come with Yun Chu from the Yun family.

After Chu Hongyu relieved himself in the outhouse, he noticed a line of ants by the window. Curious, he followed them to the other side.

He didn’t know how far he had walked when he suddenly saw a group of people approaching. Remembering Yun Chu’s words, he quickly hid in the grass beside him.

The people ahead were the old madam and Lady Yuan. They were admiring the flowers in the courtyard.

"With you, Old Madam, overseeing everything, the birthday banquet preparations will be perfect. Nothing will go wrong." Lady Yuan smiled. "Jingyu said that Chu will also attend the banquet to help receive the guests. Then, those rumors in the streets will naturally disappear. Old Madam, you need not worry anymore."

The old madam coldly replied, "What? A junior attending an elder’s birthday banquet is treated like a favor? Should I be grateful?"

Lady Yuan didn’t know what to say. The old madam used to like Chu, but after these recent incidents, she had developed a bias against her. Nothing Lady Yuan said would help.

"She hasn’t given the Xie family any sons or daughters, that’s the first of the Seven Grounds for Divorce. Disrespecting her elders is the second. Feigning illness to avoid her duties is the third." The old madam said gravely. "And slapping her husband is the fourth. She’s committed four of the seven. Do you think the Xie family can still tolerate her?"

Lady Yuan bitterly smiled. Why had the conversation turned to divorce again?

Chu had only been a little willful recently. But for the past four or five years, she had been proper in every way, both inside and out. You couldn’t completely deny someone based on a moment of willfulness.

But she knew that if she tried to persuade the old madam now, it would only make her angrier. So she swallowed her words.

"She only has a slightly better family background. In every other way, how can she compare to our Jingyu?" The old madam said hatefully. "Jingyu is learned, talented, and handsome. There isn’t a second man in the entire capital who is as perfect as him. He’s the one who’s wronged by marrying her. And then she even slapped him! If I get the chance, I will make sure Jingyu slaps her back..."

Chu Hongyu, hiding in the grass, clenched his little fists.

Mother was better than that Xie Jingyu in every way. The old woman must be blind to say such ridiculous things.

And she actually wanted to slap Mother? What a pipe dream.

Chu Hongyu really wanted to jump out and curse at the old madam.

But he was afraid of being discovered. If he was, Mother would definitely not allow him to come to the Xie family anymore.

What should he do?

The boy’s eyes rolled, and an idea came to mind.

The old woman wanted to have a grand birthday banquet, did she? Well, he’d make sure it was a birthday she’d never forget.

chapters.title: Mother's Secret
chapters.content:
Shengju was very quiet.

Yun Chu reviewed the account books and felt it was too quiet.

She frowned. "How long has Yu'er been out?"

Listening Frost was also startled. She had been busy assisting the mistress and only now realized that the young master had been gone for an unusually long time.

At that moment, Listening Snow entered, drenched in sweat. "Mistress, the young master is missing. I searched all over Shengju but couldn't find him..."

Yun Chu's heart tightened, and she abruptly stood up, then quickly calmed down. "First, go to the front courtyard and see if Ah Mao is still there."

The child had come secretly, so perhaps he had also left secretly.

Ah Mao was staying in the side room of the front courtyard under the guise of being Listening Frost's distant cousin. Listening Snow hurried over and returned with a pale face. "Ah Mao is still there."

That meant the young master had not left the Xie residence; he was just somewhere unknown.

"It's all my fault!" Listening Snow knelt down. "Please punish me, mistress."

Listening Frost spoke up. "Now is not the time for punishment. Quickly think carefully; where did you lose the young master?"

"I was waiting outside the restroom when the young master went in. After waiting a long time without seeing him come out, I went in and found the window open. The young master must have climbed out the window." Listening Snow was so anxious she was almost in tears. "The path outside the window leads to the rear garden of the Xie family. I quietly searched the garden but didn't see the young master anywhere."

Yun Chu's heart sank. The rear garden had a small lake, if the child had fallen in...

Just the thought of that possibility made her heart suddenly suffocate.

She steadied herself and said, "Listening Frost, find some excuse to clear everyone out of the garden."

Listening Frost left to carry out the order.

Yun Chu took her personal maids and servants to the garden. The Xie family's backyard wasn't large, and the garden was even smaller. It had an artificial lake, a rockery, and the original flowers and plants had been replaced with date trees. The entire garden could be seen at a glance, but the lake was overgrown with water plants and lotuses, making it hard to see clearly.

Listening Snow was trembling all over.

If the young master had drowned in the lake, her worthless life wouldn't be enough to compensate. She would surely implicate the mistress...

She tied up her skirt and was about to jump into the water when a voice suddenly came from behind her.

"Sister Listening Snow, what are you doing in the water? Are you catching fish?"

Yun Chu turned abruptly.

She saw Chu Hongyu, dressed in brocade, climbing out from the hollow trunk of a large tree. The trunk was hollow for some reason, easily big enough to hide a child. No wonder they couldn't find him.

Yun Chu had been so anxious and scared a moment ago, but now she was furious.

She suppressed her anger. "What are you doing hiding here? Do you know how long we've been looking for you? Do you know how worried we were?"

"I didn't let anyone see me. I only came out of the tree hole when I saw there was no one else in the garden." Chu Hongyu grabbed her sleeve and shook it. "Mother, please don't be angry, okay? I know I was wrong. I won't sneak out alone again..."

Yun Chu took his small hand and led him back to Shengju. She left everything to Listening Frost to handle and personally took the child to read.

"This character you don't recognize, and this one either?" Yun Chu's face was stern. "You're four years old. Has your father not started your education yet?"

Chu Hongyu made a bitter face. "He... he did, but I don't understand what the tutor says. I can't learn it... Mother, if you teach me, I'm sure I can learn."

Yun Chu could clearly see that this boy was neglecting his studies because he was too playful.

But a four-year-old child, with no one at home to guide and discipline him, being a bit playful was normal.

However, if he was too playful and fell behind in his studies, lacking knowledge and understanding, he would suffer greatly when he grew up.

"Yu'er, why do we read books? Because books contain many great truths. The more books we read, the more truths we understand." Yun Chu said softly. "Before learning to read, you must first recognize characters. Recognizing characters isn't a boring and tedious task. Look at this character 'chu' (初), as in 'the beginning of man' (人之初), which is also the 'chu' in my name. It's written like this..."

She held the little guy's hand and wrote each stroke on the paper.

Chu Hongyu began to study seriously.

Surprisingly, those difficult characters that he couldn't recognize before, after less than half an hour of teaching, he not only recognized them all but also learned how to write them.

"Mother, you're amazing!" he exclaimed.

Yun Chu smiled. "It's because you're smart. Remember how it feels to recognize characters now, and follow this feeling in the future."

Chu Hongyu nodded vigorously.

Looking at Yun Chu's gentle smile, the little guy suddenly felt sad.

When he was hiding in that tree hole, many servants of the Xie family passed by the tree in groups. He had heard many secrets about his mother.

He learned that his mother had given birth to two children before, but both had died at birth, and his mother had been ill for a very long time because of it.

He learned that his mother and that Xie something-Yu had a very bad relationship. That man never spent the night with his mother, and all the servants of the Xie family sympathized with her.

He learned that the children who called his mother "Mother" were not her children at all...

He learned that his mother's days were very difficult...

Yet his mother smiled so gently, as if she had no worries at all.

"Mistress, the young servant outside the city has gathered some news. It's said that the Prince of Pingxi has successfully eliminated the bandits." Listening Wind entered to report. "Yesterday, the Prince of Pingxi led his men to capture over a hundred bandits alive. Some fled upon hearing the news, and the prince is in hot pursuit. He is expected to return to the capital the day after tomorrow."

"Those bandits are too weak." Chu Hongyu frowned. "How come they have no resistance at all and were so easily captured by my father?"

"Yu'er, it's not that the bandits are too weak, but that your father is too strong." Yun Chu looked at him. "Every extra day these bandits exist, countless common people's lives are threatened. Your father took down the bandits in one day, this is the will of the people."

Chu Hongyu nodded with a look of partial understanding. He tightened his lips. "Then I have to go back the day after tomorrow."

Yun Chu ruffled his hair. "While your father is out eliminating bandits, you should study hard. When your father returns, you can recite the *Sanzi Jing* perfectly for him. He will definitely be very pleased."

"Really?" Chu Hongyu's face lit up. "Will Father praise me?"

Yun Chu nodded. "He probably will."

The little guy took the book and sat to the side, reciting seriously. When he encountered a character he didn't recognize, he would actively ask, and when he didn't understand a sentence, he would ask until he did before continuing.

Listening Frost whispered, "The young master is so well-behaved. Why do people outside say he's unruly and beyond redemption?"

Yun Chu said, "A child is like a blank sheet of paper; whatever adults write on it is what it becomes. The Prince of Pingxi is a strict man, and there's no princess consort at home to guide him, so naturally, the young master is a bit willful and rebellious."

For the rest of the day, Chu Hongyu focused on memorizing his books.

In the evening, Listening Snow had someone bring in a very large screen. The screen was embroidered with all kinds of "shou" (壽, longevity) characters.

"Ugh, the characters on this are so ugly." Chu Hongyu glanced at it and made a face. "Who gave this screen to Mother? They have no sincerity at all."

Yun Chu laughed. "This is the longevity gift Mother is going to give to someone else."

The child kept calling her "Mother," and Yun Chu unconsciously began to refer to herself as such as well.

---

chapters.title: Lifting the House Arrest
chapters.content:
The screen before her was embroidered by the least skilled embroideress Yun Chu could find, completed in just one day.

This was the longevity gift she was going to give to Old Madam Xie. It had cost less than two taels of silver in total.

Over the past four or five years, every year on Old Madam's birthday, she had racked her brains to give gifts. The first year, she had given a coral basin worth 800 taels of silver. The second year, she had personally overseen the creation of a full set of emerald and gold thread hairpieces. The third year... In short, every birthday gift had cost her both time and money. Looking back, she felt it had all been a waste.

Look at this screen; though it was ugly, as long as she said she had embroidered it herself, no one would dare say anything. They might even praise her for being filial.

Yun Chu had the screen put away, and the maids served dinner one by one.

She ordered a table of light dishes that children loved, as well as a steamed fish. She personally picked out the fish bones and placed them in Chu Hongyu's bowl.

Chu Hongyu stood on a chair to help, stretching out his little arms to serve Yun Chu a bowl of chicken soup.

After dinner, the little guy picked up his book and continued reading. The *Sanzi Jing*, which he had previously struggled to read, he could now recite more than half of it, albeit with some stumbling.

Yun Chu had Listening Frost carefully accompany the child in his studies, while she herself went to the Xie family's small temple.

The temple housed only a young nun and He Shi. Fearing that He Shi would cause trouble again, Xie Jingyu had ordered two servant women to guard the entrance.

Upon seeing Yun Chu arrive, the two servant women quickly bowed. "Greetings, mistress."

Yun Chu asked indifferently, "Has He Shi been behaving these days?"

One of the servant women replied, "She spends all day lying in her room recovering from her injuries. No matter what food we send in, she eats it all. She's been quite well-behaved."

Yun Chu nodded and walked in. Listening Wind stepped forward to push open He Shi's door.

He Shi was lying down, embroidering something. When she saw Yun Chu, her expression changed, then she quickly got off the bed to greet her.

Listening Wind picked up the embroidery and handed it to Yun Chu.

Yun Chu glanced at it and smiled. "Madam He, even while under house arrest, you still think to embroider a longevity gift for Old Madam. It's rare to have such a thoughtful heart."

He Shi lowered her eyes. "This forehead ornament will be finished in half a day. At that time, could you please show mercy and have someone help deliver it to Old Madam?"

"Since this is your own embroidered gift, it's only right that you deliver it yourself." Yun Chu's voice was gentle. "Old Madam's birthday is a rare happy occasion. I'll lift your house arrest for one day, but remember, no causing trouble."

He Shi could hardly believe it.

She had gone to great lengths to frame the mistress for poisoning Concubine Tao, and that had led to her house arrest. Yet the mistress was now voluntarily lifting her house arrest for a day?

She didn't dare to be too happy, always feeling that something bad was waiting for her.

Yun Chu dropped this remark and walked out.

Back in Shengju, Chu Hongyu was already asleep. The little guy was still hugging his book, muttering in his sleep. Upon closer listening, he was still reciting the *Sanzi Jing*.

Yun Chu chuckled, gently took the book from him, removed his clothes, covered him with a blanket, and lay down beside him to sleep.

That night, she slept very soundly. When she woke up in the morning, it was already bright outside.

She turned her head, only to find the little guy beside her was gone, and her heart suddenly felt empty.

Listening Frost smiled. "The young master woke up very early. He said today is his last day at the Xie residence and wants to give you a gift, mistress."

Yun Chu followed Listening Frost quietly to the side hall, where she saw the little guy holding a piece of wood in one hand and a short knife in the other, carving a wooden sculpture.

He looked extremely serious, as if he were doing something of great importance.

Yun Chu also began to think; what should she give this child?

"Mistress, the concubines have all come to pay their respects."

Listening Frost stayed in the side hall to watch the child, while Yun Chu went to the front.

Jiang Concubine, Tao Concubine, Yu Concubine, along with several young masters and ladies, were all present.

"Mistress looks well. It seems you've fully recovered." Jiang Concubine smiled. "Just in time for Old Madam's birthday banquet."

"Speaking of the banquet, I should ask Sister Wan." Yun Chu said, "Is everything prepared for tomorrow? If there's anything you're unsure about, we can discuss it now."

Xie Wan replied, "Old Madam personally supervised the preparations for the banquet. Everything is ready. Mother need not worry about these trivial matters."

Old Madam had said that once the banquet was over, she would hand over all the household management rights from her mother's hands into hers. Before she married, everything in the Xie residence would be under her control. For an unmarried girl, being able to manage the household well would be a great advantage in marriage discussions...

Yun Chu didn't ask further about the banquet and instead inquired about the recent situation of the concubines and children.

Tao Concubine's pregnancy was becoming more noticeable; she was likely to give birth during the hottest time of the year.

Jiang Concubine had started teaching her daughter, Sister Xian, to recognize characters and read, as she was just beginning her education.

Yu Concubine wasn't to be outdone; she had sent her son, Yun'er, to the small private school within the residence to study with the tutor.

Xie Shiwei had become much more obedient after the last time he was punished with family discipline. During the greeting, he sat to the side without saying a word.

After chatting for a while, the group dispersed.

As they left Shengju, Xie Shiyun pulled at Listening Yu's sleeve. "Auntie, Mother doesn't like me anymore, is it because she has another child?"

Listening Yu shook her head. The mistress wasn't just cold to Shiyun; she had also grown distant from the first young master and the second young master. She had even slapped an adult...

To be honest, even though she had served the mistress since she was young and understood her habits like the back of her hand, she couldn't figure out what the mistress was trying to do now.

" Auntie, I saw another child in Mother's courtyard." Xie Shiyun whispered. "Yesterday, I was playing near Mother's courtyard and heard a child's voice inside. It was a boy's voice. I waited for a long, long time before seeing a boy come out of the side hall. He was about my age... It must be this child that's making Mother dislike me!"

This didn't sound like a fabrication. Listening Yu's expression was shocked. "You really saw him?"

Xie Shiyun nodded vigorously.

Listening Yu's hand suddenly tightened.

The child was most likely from a branch of the Yun family. Could it be that, since the mistress had no children of her own, she wanted to adopt one from the Yun family?

If the mistress really raised a child with the same bloodline, then her own Shiyun would never be able to win the mistress's favor again.

Did Old Madam know about this? Did the madam know? Did the master know?

Tomorrow was Old Madam's birthday banquet. Was the mistress planning to reveal this child to everyone at the banquet?

Listening Yu's mind raced with thoughts, but she didn't dare to do anything, because she wasn't sure what the mistress intended...

As soon as Yun Chu entered the side hall, the little guy hid what he was holding. "Mother, don't look at me. I'll give you a surprise later."

"Alright, then Mother will wait." She sat by the window and began to work on something with her hands.

She was also preparing a parting gift for the little guy.

This was the last day. Just thinking that the little guy would leave the Xie residence tomorrow filled her with a faint sense of reluctance.

chapters.title: The Old Madam's Birthday Banquet
chapters.content:
After dinner.

Chu Hongyu pulled Yun Chu into the room and, like offering a treasure, pressed a wooden carving into her hands. "Mother, do you like it?"

It was a palm-sized wooden figurine, barely recognizable as a woman in a skirt and blouse, this was Yun Chu.

Overjoyed, she examined the carving again and again. "Yu'er, thank you. Mother really loves it. Mother also has a gift for you."

She took out a sachet and handed it over.

Chu Hongyu couldn’t wait to open the sachet and pulled out a small doll made of stitched fabric.

The doll was only the size of a thumb, but its facial features and expressions were so lifelike that anyone could tell it was Chu Hongyu.

"Wow, Mother, you're amazing! I love this doll!" the little guy exclaimed excitedly. "If only this doll were a little bigger, I could hold it in my arms."

Yun Chu picked him up and placed him on her lap, softly saying, "I made it this small on purpose. You can keep it in your sachet and carry it with you every day. Remember, you must not let anyone know you’ve been to the Xie family, and you must not let anyone know you call me Mother. Otherwise, I will be in great danger."

Chu Hongyu nodded seriously, then hesitated after a moment. "Can I let my sister know?"

He had already said before that his sister couldn’t speak, and someone who couldn’t speak certainly wouldn’t reveal secrets. Yun Chu lightly nodded.

The little guy jumped up happily.

Yun Chu could see that the brother and sister had a very good relationship. That little girl must be as likable as he was.

Perhaps because they were leaving early the next morning, the little guy was especially clingy. He wrapped his arms and legs around Yun Chu, resting his head on her chest, refusing to close his eyes to sleep.

Yun Chu told him several stories and sang several songs. It was almost midnight before the child finally fell asleep.

In the dim light, she looked at the sleeping child in her arms. For some reason, she gently kissed his face.

After that one kiss, she felt as if the emptiness in her chest had been filled with something.

She held the child tightly and soon fell into a deep sleep.

The next morning, as the faint morning light just began to stream through the window, Yun Chu opened her eyes, but the child in her arms was gone.

She anxiously got out of bed.

"Madam, the young master got up and left at the Yin hour. Seeing you were in a deep sleep, he wouldn’t let us wake you." Tingshuang entered with a basin of water. "Today is the old madam’s birthday banquet. Everyone in the courtyards has gotten up to prepare. This servant will help Madam with her hair and makeup."

Yun Chu clutched the wooden carving in her hand, the only proof that the child had been there.

She sat in front of the mirror, putting great effort into pushing the child’s image out of her mind. Looking at her reflection, she said, "Make my hairstyle simple."

Tingshuang nodded, quickly styling her hair in the simplest way, inserting a plain jade hairpin. Then she applied Yun Chu’s makeup, covering her entire face with white powder. She skipped the lip rouge and didn’t draw her eyebrows, making her look pale and lifeless. Finally, she dressed her in a dark purple dress, which made her face look as white as paper.

Just as the styling was finished, those who had come to pay their respects arrived.

Because it was the old madam’s birthday, Xie Shian had not gone to school and was waiting in the flower hall with the others.

Yun Chu walked out, and everyone bowed to her.

Xie Shian looked up at Yun Chu’s face, hesitating before saying, "Mother, why is your face so pale? Are you feeling unwell somewhere?"

"I’ve had a headache since the middle of the night. Now my head feels like it’s about to explode." Yun Chu pressed her temples. "An'er, do you think I should go out to greet the guests like this?"

Xie Shian pursed his lips.

If his mother didn’t greet the guests, the rumors outside would only get worse.

But with his mother looking so sickly, the guests would also have various suspicions.

"Madam, I just happen to have brought some lip rouge." Tingyu stepped forward. "This concubine will apply some color to your lips. Your complexion should look better then."

Yun Chu nodded, allowing her to do as she pleased.

But after her lips were painted red, her face seemed even paler.

Xie Shian spoke up, "Mother is naturally fair-skinned. It would be better not to use lip rouge."

Tingyu awkwardly wiped off the rouge with a handkerchief.

Standing to the side, Tingshuang felt it was unfair for her mistress. These people were only worried about whether Madam’s appearance would cause the Xie family to be gossiped about. No one genuinely cared about Madam’s health.

She suddenly understood why Madam no longer got close to the Xie family’s children, because each and every one of them was an ungrateful wretch.

Even if Madam had poured out her heart to raise these children, she probably wouldn’t get a single word of thanks in return.

It would be better to be like the young master of the Prince of Pingxi’s residence...

Yun Chu stood up, smiling. "Let’s go. We’ll go wish the old madam a happy birthday."

The group bustled toward Anshou Hall.

The old madam was dressed in new clothes, looking energetic as she sat in the main seat. Yuan Shi had already arrived, as had Yun Chu’s father-in-law, Xie Zhongcheng.

Among all the masters of the Xie family, Yun Chu had the least interaction with Xie Jingyu’s father, Xie Zhongcheng, because this father-in-law mostly stayed at the manor outside the city, devoting himself entirely to managing the Xie family’s businesses.

She entered and greeted each person in turn, then looked at the old madam and smiled. "This daughter-in-law wishes the old madam a happy birthday. May you have the blessings of the East Sea, the longevity of the South Mountain, and may every year be as today, every birthday as joyous as this one."

Behind her, the concubines and young masters and misses stepped forward one by one to offer their birthday wishes.

The old madam beamed with joy. "Very good, very good. You all have filial piety. Our Xie family depends on you to bring glory to the family name!"

The Xie family had only this one branch in the capital. After the birthday wishes, the presentation of gifts began.

Xie Zhongcheng had gone to a temple to pray for a longevity charm for his mother. He claimed to have knelt for nine days and nine nights at Hanshan Temple, the most sacred temple outside the city, before obtaining it.

Yuan Shi gave the old madam a jade vase symbolizing longevity.

Xie Jingyu presented a painting of an immortal deer that he had drawn himself.

Next, it was Yun Chu’s turn to present her gift. Every year, Yun Chu’s birthday gift to the old madam was the most precious among all the gifts.

When the old madam saw Tingshuang and Tingxue carrying in a large object, she immediately knew it was a screen.

"Old Madam, this is a 'Hundred Longevity' embroidered screen that your daughter-in-law spent three months making for you." Yun Chu pulled off the red cloth. "Your daughter-in-law is the daughter of a general and is not skilled in needlework. I’ve tried to learn a little, but I’m not very good at it. I hope the old madam won’t mind."

Yuan Shi spoke up, "The importance of a gift lies in the sincerity, not in how well it’s made."

But when she saw the "longevity" characters on the screen, Yuan Shi found it hard to praise. They were simply too ugly.

If this screen were placed in a room, it would be a laughingstock. It could only be stored in the warehouse, but even there, it would take up space...

The old madam’s mouth twitched. Even the worst embroiderer in her room could do better than Yun Chu. If the embroidery was this bad, it would have been better not to embroider at all. Wasn’t this just embarrassing?

But embroidering a hundred "longevity" characters was indeed no easy task, especially for someone who wasn’t skilled in needlework. It must have been extremely difficult.

If she said anything displeased, it would hurt Yun Chu’s face. Who knew what outrageous thing this daughter-in-law would do then?

"Chu’er has put in the effort." The old madam said against her will. "You prepared this birthday gift while you were ill. Your filial piety is moving."

Yun Chu lowered her head in deference.

Next, the concubines and younger generations presented their gifts, clothes, shoes, or calligraphy and paintings, nothing particularly novel.

After the gift-giving, the old madam stood up. "It’s about time. We should open the doors to welcome the guests. Let’s go to the front courtyard."

---

chapters.title: Many Troubles
chapters.content:
By now, the sky was already bright.

The front courtyard had long been prepared with tables and chairs. Since it was a birthday banquet hosted by the women, there was no separation of men and women at different tables. Instead, each family sat together, and several dozen low tables were prepared.

Just as they passed through the front courtyard where the banquet was to be held, before the main gates were fully opened, a servant woman suddenly rushed over. "Eldest Miss, something has happened. You need to make a decision quickly."

Since Xie Pin was in charge of the birthday banquet arrangements, the servants came directly to her to report.

Xie Pin was somewhat annoyed. These servants really had no sense of propriety. With so many elders present, weren’t they deliberately trying to embarrass her?

She took a deep breath and asked, "What happened?"

The servant woman spoke, "Eldest Miss, when we were preparing the dishes just now, the kitchen discovered that the fish delivered early this morning were all only the size of a palm. That would be fine, but they were all dead. What should we do?"

"What?" The old madam could hardly believe it. "Who hosts a birthday banquet with dead fish?"

Wasn’t this inviting bad luck, cursing her to die early?

Xie Pin quickly said, "Take me to see."

The old madam’s right eyelid kept twitching. She felt uneasy. "It’s still early. The guests won’t arrive for a while. Let’s all go take a look."

Xie Zhongcheng and Xie Jingyu, along with Xie Shian, stayed in the front courtyard while the old madam led a group of women to the back kitchen.

When they saw the small fish floating on the water with their white bellies up, the old madam’s face completely darkened. "Who was in charge of purchasing the fish?"

A servant woman replied, "The kitchen purchases are all handled by Manager He."

Xie Pin tightly clenched her handkerchief.

She had trusted He Xu so much, entrusting most of the tasks to him. She never expected this bastard to cause such a huge problem for her!

The fish being small was one thing, but they were dead! How much silver had he embezzled to pull off something like this?

"Old Madam, I... I misjudged the person." Xie Pin lowered her head. "I’ll arrange for someone to buy fresh, large fish immediately."

Yuan Shi sighed. "By the time the fish are bought, the banquet will have already started. It’ll be too late."

Tao Concubine suggested, "Then we might as well skip the fish dish."

"We can’t have a birthday banquet without fish." Yun Chu said calmly. "These fish have been dead for about half an hour. If we make the flavor strong enough, it can cover up the lack of freshness."

The old madam looked at Yun Chu. "Are you sure it will work?"

"There’s a dish in the Yun residence called 'Sour and Spicy Crispy Fish.' After deep-frying at high temperatures and adding flavor with coriander and aged vinegar, most people won’t be able to tell the difference." Yun Chu explained. "Concubine Yu, you know how to make this dish. Leave it to you."

Her calm and composed manner made the originally panicked crowd feel as if they had found a pillar of support. The dead fish no longer seemed like such a big deal.

Tingyu stepped forward. "Yes."

Among the four senior maids by the mistress’s side, she was the one skilled in cooking. She felt she finally had a chance to be useful.

She handed her child to the wet nurse and strode into the kitchen. As she entered, she heard Yuan Shi speaking: "Chu’er, our family still needs you to take charge. It’s a good thing you’re here, or we really wouldn’t know what to do..."

Jiang Concubine added, "Madam has the talent of a steward. Such a small matter is naturally nothing to her."

Tingyu, who had just walked in, bit her lip. Clearly, it was she who was solving the current difficult problem, but everyone was only praising Madam, completely forgetting about her...

The old madam’s expression was complicated.

Originally, she had wanted to host a perfect birthday banquet to take back Yun Chu’s authority as the steward. But the banquet hadn’t even started yet, and already there was a problem that required Yun Chu to clean up...

She had to admit that the legitimate daughter of a general’s family was indeed stronger in every aspect compared to others.

"Check all the ingredients delivered this morning." Yun Chu said coldly. "They are all experienced people in the kitchen. Handle small matters yourselves. If you really can’t deal with it, report it immediately."

"Yes!"

The servants and maids in the kitchen all acknowledged the order in unison.

Only then did the old madam lead the women to the front courtyard to greet the guests.

A sarcastic smile tugged at Yun Chu’s lips.

She knew this birthday banquet wouldn’t go perfectly, but she never expected such a big problem to arise.

It hadn’t even started, and a whole basin of fish had died. Who knew how many more troubles were waiting ahead.

But did He Xu really have the audacity to purchase a basin of dead fish? She somehow felt that the fish had been deliberately suffocated...

The rough servant women in the residence might have many complaints about Xie Pin, but they shouldn’t dare to sabotage the birthday banquet.

Yun Chu thought to herself that perhaps the old madam was just unlucky...

The old madam, Yuan Shi, and a few of the younger masters and misses sat in the flower hall of the front courtyard to chat. The concubines were not allowed to attend such occasions. Yun Chu and Xie Jingyu, along with the eldest son and daughter, Xie Shian and Xie Pin, stood at the main gate to welcome the guests.

The first to arrive with congratulations was Hu Daren, a subordinate of Xie Jingyu, who came with his wife and daughter.

"Lord Xie, Madam Xie." Hu Daren cupped his hands in greeting. "I’ve brought a small gift. Please accept it."

Xie Jingyu returned the greeting. "Shian, take Hu Daren inside to be seated."

Hu Daren looked at Xie Shian and sighed. "Two years ago, when this official first visited the Xie residence, Young Master Xie was only this tall. Now he’s grown so much."

Xie Shian exchanged pleasantries with Hu Daren as they entered the front courtyard.

Yun Chu smiled and greeted Madam Hu.

Madam Hu looked at Yun Chu’s pale face. "I’ve heard that Madam Xie has been very ill, yet you’re still managing the birthday banquet. It must be very hard on you."

"Not at all." Yun Chu replied. "This time, the birthday banquet was entirely handled by my daughter. I only gave a little guidance. All the big and small matters were decided by her. With Eldest Sister helping me, things will be much easier in the future."

Madam Hu looked at Xie Pin in surprise. "Miss Xie is only thirteen or fourteen years old, yet she can handle such a big birthday banquet by herself?"

Xie Pin spoke up, "It’s all thanks to Mother teaching me well."

This implied that she was indeed the one who had handled the entire banquet.

Just then, many guests had arrived. Hearing that the banquet was organized by a thirteen-year-old girl, they couldn’t help but look at her with admiration.

Xie Pin accepted all these praises without hesitation.

At this moment, a servant woman hurriedly came from the back.

Her heart skipped a beat, and she quickly said, "This junior has some matters to attend to. Please excuse me for a moment."

She took the servant woman to the side and frowned. "What’s wrong now?"

"The eldest miss, the pork and mutton purchased for the back kitchen are each short by at least ten jin." The servant woman slapped her thigh. "It’s too late to send someone to buy more now..."

Xie Pin gritted her teeth in anger.

He Xu was her own uncle. How could he deliberately make things difficult for her like this?

She clutched her handkerchief. "Then just reduce the portion in each bowl slightly. Today’s guests are all well-off officials. They won’t miss one or two mouthfuls of meat."

The servant woman opened and closed her mouth, ultimately swallowing the words she wanted to say. She accepted the order and returned to the back kitchen to continue her work.

Xie Pin composed herself and returned to Yun Chu’s side to continue greeting guests.

Every lady who arrived would inquire about Yun Chu’s illness. Although Yun Chu said she was much better, her pale complexion and frail figure made it clear she was forcing herself to greet the guests.

At this time, the Yun family’s carriage arrived.

The last time the Yun family had stepped in to bury the Xie family’s deceased legitimate son and daughter next to the Yun family’s ancestral hall, it was equivalent to publicly slapping the Xie family in the face. Everyone was curious: now that Yun Chu was so ill, what would the Yun family’s attitude toward the Xie family be?

chapters.title: The Arrival of Marquis Xuānwǔ
chapters.content:
Yún Chū personally led the Yún family members inside to offer birthday congratulations.

The Yún family had three attendees: Madam Yún, Lin Shi, Yún’s eldest daughter-in-law, Liǔ Qiānqiān, and Yún’s second daughter, Yún Rán.

"Wishing the birthday star radiance like the sun and moon, and eternal youth." Lin Shi ordered the presentation of the gift. "A small token of our esteem, merely to express our heartfelt wishes."

The birthday gift was a large-bellied vase as tall as a person, its body adorned with exquisite peony flowers inlaid with gold thread, extraordinarily precious, worth at least five hundred taels of silver.

Yún Chū felt a pang of heartache at the expense, but there were many things she could not openly discuss with her mother. Saying too much would only make her mother worry about her life.

The surrounding ladies could tell from this gift that the Yún and Xiè families’ marital alliance would continue.

With the Yún family as a backing, the ladies’ attitudes toward Old Madam Xiè warmed slightly.

The women kept Old Madam Xiè company in the flower hall, while the men were entertained by Xiè Jǐngyù, with Xiè Zhōngchéng and Xiè Shì’ān keeping him company.

Soon, the time for the birthday banquet arrived, and everyone took their seats according to their rank and status.

Just then, the guard at the entrance suddenly announced loudly, "Marquis Xuānwǔ has arrived!"

Old Madam Xiè’s face showed shock.

Marquis Xuānwǔ was a noble of such high status that the Xiè family had no connection to him at all. She had not even sent an invitation to the Marquis’s residence, so why had the young marquis come?

Xiè Jǐngyù’s expression suddenly darkened, and he looked up uncomfortably at the newcomer.

Marquis Xuānwǔ had inherited his title just three years ago and was barely in his early twenties. Dressed in a silver robe and holding a paper fan, he exuded an air of refined elegance.

"I’ve come to wish Old Madam a happy birthday." Qín Mínghéng stepped forward, closed his fan, and presented his gift. "This is Snow Skin Ointment from the palace. When young women use it, their skin becomes as fair as snow, and for the elderly, it removes wrinkles. I wish Old Madam a joyous birthday and everlasting youth."

Hearing that it was a palace treasure, Old Madam’s eyes lit up. She hastily stood and said, "Marquis Xuānwǔ has gone out of his way to offer congratulations, this old one is truly honored."

"Old Madam, what are you saying? The Xiè Minister and I are close friends. It is only right that I come to celebrate." Qín Mínghéng looked at Xiè Jǐngyù. "Minister Xiè, why do you seem unwelcoming of my arrival?"

Xiè Jǐngyù clenched his fists tightly and said, "Marquis Xuānwǔ’s presence brings great honor to our humble home. Please, take the seat of honor."

As a marquis, his rank was above all officials, so Qín Mínghéng’s seat was placed above the Yún family’s, right next to the host, the Xiè family.

Between Yún Chū and the young marquis, there was only Xiè Jǐngyù and a pathway separating them.

Whether it was her imagination or not, she felt that since the young marquis entered, his gaze seemed to linger on her from time to time.

But whenever she looked his way, he was already speaking with someone else, as if she had imagined it.

Just as she thought she was overthinking, Qín Mínghéng suddenly turned to her: "I’ve heard that Madam Xiè is gravely ill. How is she faring now?"

Many guests had asked similar questions, so Yún Chū did not find it odd and was about to respond.

But Xiè Jǐngyù spoke first: "Thank you for your concern, Marquis. My wife merely caught a slight cold, it’s not as serious as the rumors suggest. She is much better now."

As the host, Xiè Zhōngchéng stood and said, "Thank you, honored guests, ladies, and young masters, for taking the time to attend my mother’s birthday banquet. Today, we have prepared a modest feast. If there is any lack in our hospitality, please forgive us. Now, let us raise our glasses in celebration!"

The guests all raised their cups.

But as the wine touched their lips, their expressions changed. For such a grand banquet, the wine was surprisingly ordinary.

However, as the saying goes, "When in Rome, do as the Romans do." The guests drank what was served without complaint.

Only Qín Mínghéng spoke up: "Tsk tsk, this is the first time I’ve tasted such bland wine. Minister Xiè, your family’s wine is just like you, far too mild."

Xiè Jǐngyù tightened his lips.

It was clear that Qín Mínghéng had come to pick a fight, but due to his status, Xiè Jǐngyù could not possibly ask him to leave.
