After He sent Xie Shiwei back, she returned to her own Bihe Yuan. Seeing that the fallen leaves in the courtyard had not been swept, she suddenly felt extremely weary in her heart.

She didn't understand how it had come to this...

chapters.title: The Rules of the Gambling Den
chapters.content:
He Shi was not someone who accepted her fate.

When her entire family had hit rock bottom before, hadn't she pulled herself up and returned to the capital?

Twenty years ago, her mother had supported the whole family with her exquisite embroidery. She, too, could use this skill to secure her place in the Xie household.

He Shi found a way to buy some silk threads and began embroidering handkerchiefs with extremely difficult techniques...

Yun Chu ordered her subordinates, "Buy some of He Shi's handkerchiefs. Keep the ones with unique stitching; I have a great use for them."

Tingshuang nodded and arranged for someone to purchase the handkerchiefs.

He Shi hadn't expected the handkerchiefs to sell so easily. She pondered making more valuable items, like folding screens.

That day, Chen Defu hurried in to report, "Madam, that He Xu has fled the capital after incurring a debt of ten thousand taels of silver. This old servant has already arranged for four men to follow him. What should we do next?"

A cold smile curled on Yun Chu's lips. "Next, naturally, we ensure he can never... function as a man again."

Chen Defu hesitated. "But if we hand him over to those people, they might just kill him..."

"Send a few men to handle it," Yun Chu said, her face as cold as ice. "If you take the money, you must pay the price. Isn't that the rule of the gambling den?"

When she had lent money to He Xu, he had signed a collateral agreement. Cutting off *that* would comply with the laws of this dynasty.

Though she was determined to seek revenge, she would not break the law.

Her grandfather had defended the Yun family's integrity and reputation until his death. She would not bring shame to the Yun name.

The next afternoon, Chen Defu returned. "Madam, it's done. We gave him the medicine. He survived, but he's still on the road. His destination is Jizhou."

Yun Chu nodded. "Have you found any information about He Lingyuan?"

Chen Defu shook his head. "There aren't many people in the capital with the surname He, and no one by that name."

"Then send someone to Jizhou to inquire." Yun Chu stood up, took a large box from the table, and handed it to him. "Chen Bo, you've worked hard for me these days. This is some tea, please accept it."

Chen Bo used to manage the shops with single-minded devotion. Though busy, he had been at ease.

Now, though it seemed he had no proper work, the mental pressure he bore was immense.

Chen Defu didn’t dare accept. He waved his hands. He was a born servant of the Yun family. The Yun family had shown him great kindness. Serving the madam was only natural; how could he accept such precious tea?

"If you refuse, how can I continue to rely on you? I’ll have to send you back to retire."

Hearing this, Chen Bo had no choice but to accept the tea.

Yun Chu then discussed the ice-selling business with him. Initially, Chen Defu had purchased large quantities of ice under the name of a southern merchant, without revealing the Yun family's involvement. Next, they would arrange for a southern merchant to open an ice shop in the capital. By the end of May, it would officially open for business.

These matters were handled by Chen Defu’s subordinates to avoid exposing their identities.

"Several of my dowry estates sold for a good price," Yun Chu said. "The money from them should be enough to buy a large estate."

The income from those estates had been declining year by year. Selling them now would still fetch a good price; waiting any longer would only make them less valuable.

Chen Defu looked up. "This old servant knows of several large estates in the outskirts of the capital. Shall I go and negotiate?"

Yun Chu shook her head. "I want the Wu family’s estate in the north of the city."

Chen Defu was shocked.

Over twenty years ago, the Wu family had been a rising power in the capital. The head of the family was an official, and their business ventures were thriving. But then, the family fell ill with a strange disease. From elders to children, none were spared. To pay for treatment, they sold countless properties. The once-great family dwindled until only the estate outside the city remained.

The estate wasn’t particularly large, but it included a mountain, a lake, and a small forest; it had everything. The last member of the Wu family sold it to the Zou family for twenty thousand taels of silver.

Soon after the Zou family took over, rumors of hauntings began. Their fortune declined, and they sold the estate at a loss in the middle of the night.

A merchant, refusing to believe in superstition, bought it. But as soon as he took over, he tried to sell it as quickly as possible.

By then, word of the hauntings had spread. No one dared buy it, so the estate remained unsold in the merchant’s hands to this day.

"Counting the years, that estate has been abandoned for over twenty years," Chen Defu said regretfully. "The land is fertile, perfect for crops, with excellent harvests every year. I don’t know how the rumors of hauntings started, but a good estate was ruined. Madam, please consider other estates, there are many better options."

Yun Chu thought of her past life. Around the time she turned thirty, a fire broke out at the Wu estate. The overgrown wild grass burned away, revealing a massive hot spring beneath. The spring was later claimed by a concubine in the palace, bringing in immense wealth every year.

As for the earlier hauntings, they had long been forgotten by time.

Since she had foreknowledge, she wouldn’t let that estate remain abandoned for so many more years.

She stood up. "Come, let’s go take a look at the estate."

Chen Defu was stunned. "Madam, do you really want to buy that estate? Please reconsider!"

"When the Zou family bought it, they paid twenty thousand taels. They sold it to the merchant for about fifteen thousand. Tell me, how much do you think I can buy it for?" Yun Chu smiled. "Price isn’t the issue. Let’s first see what’s really going on with the hauntings."

Though she was reborn, she still didn’t believe in ghosts. In her view, it was likely man-made.

Chen Defu’s brows furrowed deeply. "Madam, it’s getting late. Why not wait until tomorrow, when I can bring a few Taoist priests?"

"Ghosts only come out at night," Yun Chu said, rising and heading out. "But you’re right; we should bring more people. Have all the strong men and women from the residence come along."

Not only Chen Defu, but Tingshuang was also terrified.

She knew the madam had grown bolder lately, but she hadn’t expected *this* much boldness.

No family in the entire capital dared take over that haunted estate, fearing it would bring misfortune to their own luck. Yet the madam was doing the exact opposite.

But then again, the madam was already at odds with the Xie family, maybe this made sense?

Tingshuang gathered the sturdy women, claiming they were going to the madam’s dowry estates to retrieve some leftover items. She didn’t dare say they were going to the haunted estate, no one would have the courage to go.

As the sun set, Yun Chu led her group out of the city.

Upon hearing this, the Old Madam could hardly believe it. "I’m already this ill, and she doesn’t even come to see me, yet she’s leaving the city now?"

Week Mama lowered her head. "The madam sent ginseng this morning. She’s done her duty."

The Old Madam knew Yun Chu had done all she should. She used to like this granddaughter-in-law, but now she found fault with everything she did.

After drinking her medicine, she leaned against the bed frame. "So she’s sold all her estates?"

Week Mama said, "Perhaps the madam is short on money."

"Hmph. She took over twenty thousand taels from me earlier. She’s the richest in the family. Why would she sell her estates? A woman wouldn’t part with her dowry unless absolutely necessary." The Old Madam narrowed her eyes. "Why does she need so much money all of a sudden?"

Week Mama lowered her voice. "This servant speculates... The divine physician who treated the Empress has arrived in the capital. I think the madam is raising money to seek treatment for herself. What woman doesn’t want a child of her own?"

The Old Madam had heard of that divine physician. Due to his extraordinary medical skills, the demand for his services was overwhelming. He had raised his consultation fee to an exorbitant price, five thousand taels just to diagnose, and a single treatment could cost tens of thousands...

Yun Chu’s actions made sense. After all, if she recovered, any child she bore would still be of the Xie bloodline. Let her do as she pleased.

---

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Estate
chapters.content:
They traveled all the way to the northern part of the city.

After passing through the city gates, the road became uneven. After about half an hour, the sky had darkened, and they finally arrived at the estate’s entrance.

This estate had been haunted for over twenty years. Apart from the nearby farmers and those specifically hired to manage the estate, most people knew very little about the matter.

For example, the sturdy men and women Yun Chu had brought along stared curiously at the overgrown estate, wondering why no crops were planted.

"Madam, the entrance is overgrown with weeds. You shouldn’t go in," Chen Defu said. "Let this old servant take a few men to scout ahead."

Yun Chu carefully observed the estate’s entrance. A smile suddenly appeared on her lips. "At first glance, it does seem overgrown, but Chen Bo, have you noticed? The grass on the left and right sides parts to reveal a nearly invisible path. The people in the estate must use this path to enter and exit."

Chen Defu’s eyes widened in shock. "There are still people living here?"

Yun Chu only smiled in response.

People feared ghosts, but ghosts feared people even more. Even if there really were ghosts, there was no need to be afraid.

She took the lead down the hidden path. Her skirt was caught by the weeds, and with each step, threads were pulled loose, her skirt was ruined.

Chen Defu quickly stepped ahead to clear the way.

Tingshuang led the way with a lantern, while Tingfeng and Tingxue walked on either side of Yun Chu, lifting the hem of her skirt.

The men and women behind them followed in a rustle, only now realizing something was off. The sky was completely dark, why wasn’t there a single lantern lit in the estate?

Inside the estate, the weeds were as tall as a person. Moonlight filtered through, casting shifting shadows. The timid Tingxue’s face turned pale with fear.

Chen Defu and his men cleared a path and led Yun Chu into the main hall. He wiped a chair clean with his own clothes and respectfully invited Yun Chu to sit.

Tingshuang even brought tea from the carriage and began brewing it there.

Once the tea was ready, its fragrance filled the air, and the night grew deeper.

Chen Defu, Tingshuang, and the others gradually regained their courage. With so many of them, even a fierce ghost wouldn’t dare show itself.

"There’s too much tea. Everyone, have a few sips to wet your throats. We’ll have work to do soon," Yun Chu said with a smile, offering the tea to them.

The servants had only ever drunk coarse tea. Such fine, fragrant tea was a first for them, and they couldn’t help but drink several cups.

Before long, one of the women clutched her stomach. "Madam, this old servant needs to relieve herself. I’ll be right back."

Yun Chu nodded. "It’s dark outside. Take two people with you."

Two other women also needed to go, so the three of them left the main hall together. Outside, the weeds were as tall as a person, making it impossible to tell directions. They couldn’t find the outhouse, so they agreed to find a lush patch of grass, untie their belts, and squat...

Suddenly, they heard rustling sounds.

One woman shouted, "We’re over here! Go somewhere else to relieve yourselves!"

But the footsteps grew closer...

Yun Chu and the others, sitting in the main hall, soon heard the women’s successive screams.

Tingxue’s entire face trembled. "Could there really be ghosts?"

"Don’t talk nonsense," Tingshuang said, her voice also shaking slightly. "The madam has already sent Chen Bo over. Nothing will happen."

As soon as she finished speaking, Chen Defu had people carry the three women back. Two of them had fainted from fear, while the third babbled incoherently, "It was a ghost! A terrifying ghost with long fangs! It was going to eat us..."

The woman’s eyes rolled back, and she, too, fainted.

Chen Defu reported, "Madam, by the time we arrived, the thing had already fled. It ran too fast, it disappeared into the woods."

The woods were dense with tall trees and thick undergrowth. With the darkness, they would get lost if they ventured in.

The men and women in the main hall were all deeply shaken. None of them had expected there to actually be ghosts here. Each of them considered retreat.

Yun Chu stood up. "Let’s go take a look."

The men and women exchanged glances. They didn’t understand, wasn’t the madam afraid? How could she remain so calm, without a hint of panic?

But then again, a mistress was a mistress; not something they, as servants, could compare to.

With Yun Chu leading the way, they found their backbone. Their thoughts of retreat slowly faded as they surrounded Yun Chu and followed her out.

Chen Defu and four men led the way, quickly reaching the spot where the three women had relieved themselves. The weeds were flattened in one direction, and following it, they took a dozen steps to reach the edge of the estate’s small forest.

The forest was even darker, with denser trees. Entering it, even if they didn’t encounter ghosts, getting lost would be trouble enough.

Yun Chu closed her eyes and sniffed.

Earlier, she had added a nameless incense to the tea, a fragrance her mother had developed when she was a child. She had always loved it and often burned some.

Later, she discovered that this incense lingered for a long time. Even if drunk and then expelled from the body, it would retain its scent, and the scent would be stronger.

The women had drunk the tea, relieved themselves, and if the "ghost" had passed through here, it would have picked up the scent.

Yun Chu sniffed for a while, then opened her eyes and pointed south. "Chen Bo, this way."

Chen Defu nodded and, with the four men, went ahead to clear the path.

There was no sign of anyone passing through, but upon closer inspection, the weeds were systematically flattened in one direction. Someone familiar with the path could walk through without disturbing the grass.

Yun Chu led the group deep into the forest, where they found a thatched hut. Though located in the dense woods, it looked clean and showed signs of habitation.

Chen Defu couldn’t believe it. "So there really are people living here."

Tingfeng frowned. "Who would dare live here and play at being a ghost? Chen Bo, quickly capture them and interrogate them properly."

Yun Chu made a gesture to stop him.

She walked to the door of the hut and said softly, "Madam Wu, Young Master Wu, let’s meet."

Before deciding to buy this estate, she had already looked into its first owner, the Wu family.

After the Wu family fell ill with the strange disease, they had all died and been buried in the Wu ancestral graves. She had sent someone to investigate and found that, in the vast ancestral cemetery, two gravestones were missing.

Those belonged to the last madam of the Wu family and her son, who had been about a year old at the time.

In her past life, ten years later, a fire had broken out at the estate, presumably killing the mother and son. That was when the hauntings stopped.

Yun Chu’s words were met with silence from the hut.

She wasn’t in a hurry and continued, "A divine physician has recently arrived in the capital. Doesn’t Madam Wu want him to diagnose and treat Young Master Wu?"

At these words, there was movement inside the hut. Soon, a hunched woman emerged, leaning on a cane.

Yun Chu couldn’t help but be shocked.

The Wu madam had been around twenty when she gave birth. Twenty years later, she should be in her early forties, but she looked as if she were in her sixties. What hardships had she endured to age her so?

Before she could recover from her shock, another figure emerged from the hut, a person dressed in a black cloak.

The person’s face was covered in blisters the size of a baby’s fist. Some were broken and festered, making the entire face look terrifying. The person reached out to support their mother, and their hands were also covered in blisters, likely their entire body was the same...

Yun Chu knew this must be Young Master Wu, suffering from the Wu family’s hereditary disease.

chapters.title: Encounter with the Young Princess
chapters.content:
As they left the estate, it was nearly dusk. The capital city imposed a nighttime curfew from the second watch of the evening until the fifth watch of the morning. If they didn’t return now, they would have to wait until the next morning.

Tingshuang helped Yun Chu into the carriage and asked softly, "Madam, have you really agreed to treat Young Master Wu?"

Yun Chu nodded.

More than twenty years ago, the Wu family had fallen ill one by one, and in the end, only the youngest, Young Master Wu, had survived. Madam Wu had sold all their property without hesitation to seek doctors everywhere to treat her son. Penniless and homeless, they had moved into this estate.

This was an estate passed down by the Wu ancestors, and at that time, it was the only property the Wu family had left.

However, a family named Zou had schemed to force them to sell the estate at a low price. The estate had been as grand as an imperial garden, with ornate carvings, pavilions, rare flowers, and could have been sold for at least thirty thousand taels of silver. In the end, Madam Wu had only received twenty thousand taels.

After the Zou family acquired the estate, they immediately demolished the Wu family ancestral hall, and the small forest was about to be burned down. With nowhere to go, Madam Wu had come up with an idea: she pretended to be a ghost to scare people away.

Sure enough, the Zou family had been so frightened that they sold the estate at a low price. As for the Zou family's decline in fortune, that was purely a coincidence.

Later, when a merchant took over the estate, Madam Wu, along with her three or four-year-old son, continued to pretend to be ghosts, scaring the merchant into illness.

Not only that, Madam Wu would go out during the day to tell the neighbors that the estate was haunted. Soon, the rumor spread, and no one dared to take over the estate. Occasionally, the merchant would send someone to inspect, but they would be scared away by the growing Young Master Wu. He didn’t even need to disguise himself; his face and the foul smell from his festering wounds were enough to scare anyone unconscious...

"Madam Wu and her son are pitiful, having lived in darkness for more than twenty years," Yun Chu said. "This estate is the ancestral property passed down by the Wu ancestors. I bought this estate with the money earned from the Wu family's ancestral property. Treating Young Master Wu is not inappropriate."

Tingfeng spoke up, "But that divine doctor charges five thousand taels of silver for a single pulse diagnosis. It would take three to five years for this estate to earn that much money."

Yun Chu smiled.

Once the hot springs were opened, they could earn at least fifty thousand taels of silver this winter. Paying for Young Master Wu's medical expenses would be nothing.

She didn’t consider herself a great philanthropist, but she would help others when she could. Perhaps it was because of these good deeds that heaven had allowed her to return to the age of twenty.

"Madam should also get a pulse diagnosis," Tingshuang said with a sour heart. "You are still young. After curing your infertility, you can have another son..."

Before she could finish, a cry suddenly came from outside the carriage.

Yun Chu immediately said, "Stop."

The coachman tightened the reins, and the carriage slowly came to a halt.

Tingshuang lifted the carriage curtain, and Yun Chu looked out. It was already inside the capital city, and the curfew was about to begin. There were no pedestrians on the road, only a night watchman passing by.

The crying seemed to come from a small alley.

Without hesitation, Yun Chu got out of the carriage and walked towards the alley, followed by Tingshuang and the other maids.

The alley was dimly lit by the moonlight, and a small white figure could be vaguely seen crouching in the corner.

The crying was coming from this small figure.

Yun Chu quickened her pace and soon saw clearly that it was a girl of about three years old. Her long hair was messy, her head buried between her knees, her small shoulders shaking as she let out fragmented, cat-like sobs.

Yun Chu also noticed that the little girl wasn’t even wearing shoes.

Her heart softened, and she quickly picked up the child, gently asking, "Why are you alone outside? Where are your parents?"

The little girl lifted her face, revealing a pair of large, round eyes filled with tears that rolled down her cheeks. She looked at Yun Chu, first with confusion, then suddenly wailed and buried herself in Yun Chu’s arms, crying loudly.

Yun Chu was immediately at a loss, "Don’t cry, be good, or you’ll turn into a little cat."

But the little girl cried even harder, her tears soaking Yun Chu’s clothes.

Yun Chu’s heart ached inexplicably.

She loved Xie Shiyou the most, but even when Xie Shiyou was injured and crying, she didn’t feel this heart-wrenching pain.

She held the little girl, gently patting her back as they walked out of the alley. With difficulty, she climbed back into the carriage and sat down, softly singing a song. The little girl gradually quieted down in her arms.

Just as she was about to communicate with her, she saw the little girl’s big, beautiful eyes close, and she had fallen asleep in her arms.

Yun Chu’s heart softened. She said softly, "Tingshuang, you and Chen Bo go around and see if anyone is looking for a child. If everything matches, bring them over."

Tingshuang took the order and left.

The carriage pulled over to the side, leaving Yun Chu holding the child, with Tingfeng and Tingxue waiting outside, along with the coachman holding the horse.

At this moment, a group of people suddenly approached and surrounded the carriage.

Leading them was a nanny in her forties or fifties, who coldly stared at the carriage and said, "Search it."

Four or five guards immediately stepped forward.

"What are you doing?" Tingxue quickly blocked them. "Inside is our madam. Don’t offend our madam!"

The nanny’s expression was cold. "It’s abnormal for a carriage to stop on the side of the road in the middle of the night. Which proper madam doesn’t return home at night? Search it!"

Tingxue was almost anxious to death and was about to argue when a child’s cry suddenly came from inside the carriage.

The nanny’s face lit up with joy. "The princess is in the carriage!"

She pushed Tingxue and Tingfeng aside, climbed onto the carriage with the help of the guards, and abruptly lifted the curtain.

At a glance, she saw the little girl in Yun Chu’s arms. In one swift motion, she rushed forward, grabbed the child under her armpits, and pulled her out.

The little girl was already crying, and being yanked like this, she burst into even louder sobs.

Yun Chu’s eyes darkened. "Let go."

"It’s you who should let go!" the nanny glared angrily. "How dare you kidnap our princess! You must be tired of living. Regardless of which family’s madam you are, your days are numbered!"

With that, she hugged the child and pulled hard.

Yun Chu was holding the little girl’s waist and, seeing this, didn’t dare to pull back, so she let go.

The little girl struggled in the nanny’s arms, crying so hard she could barely breathe. Her originally fair little face turned purple.

"Let go of the child!" Yun Chu’s voice suddenly rose, her aura fully unleashed.

The nanny wasn’t intimidated by her aura but was frightened by the princess’s purple face. She softened and placed the child on the soft cushion of the carriage.

"It’s alright, don’t cry..." Yun Chu’s voice was extremely soft. "Can Auntie hold you?"

The nanny’s face sank. "What qualifies you to be our princess’s aunt..."

Before she could finish, the little girl stretched out her short arms and hugged Yun Chu’s neck tightly.

Yun Chu placed her on her lap and pointed at the nanny, softly asking, "Do you recognize this person? Is she from your family?"

The little girl only held onto her, not making a sound.

Yun Chu looked up. "If she says she recognizes you, I’ll let you take her away."

The nanny couldn’t believe it. To take her young mistress away, she actually needed a stranger’s permission.

But the young mistress was so dependent on this madam, and she couldn’t use force.

She said, "Our princess can’t speak. According to Madam, I can’t take the princess away today?"

Yun Chu was taken aback.

This child can’t speak?

Wait!

She remembered. Brother Yu had told her that he had a sister who couldn’t speak. Wasn’t Brother Yu’s sister the princess?

Was the little girl the daughter of Prince Pingxi?

But Prince Pingxi’s child was already four years old, and this little girl looked only about three...

---

chapters.title: Someone Wants to Jump into the Well
chapters.content:
As the two groups were at a stalemate, the sound of galloping horses approached.

A dozen or so horses stopped in front of the carriage. Leading them was a sweating blood horse, on which sat a formidable man in a black cloak.

Yun Chu looked up and recognized him; it was Prince Pingxi, Chu Yi.

Chu Yi dismounted and walked to the carriage, stopping in place without coming closer. He said, "So it’s Madam Xie."

Yun Chu, holding the child, got out of the carriage and said, "Greetings to Prince Pingxi. I would like to ask, in such a large prince’s mansion with countless servants, how could a child so young be out of the mansion in the middle of the night?"

She knew that the affairs of Prince Pingxi’s mansion were none of her concern.

But thinking of how Brother Yu had stayed at the Xie mansion for several nights without anyone coming to look for him, and how such a young girl had gone missing at night, she felt distressed for the two children.

Moreover, the biological father was right in front of them, yet the little girl in her arms showed no reaction. This was simply abnormal.

Overcome with emotion, she couldn’t help but question him.

Even if the other party was the renowned Prince Pingxi, she was not afraid at all.

Chu Yi met her gaze, his voice somewhat hoarse. "Recently, I’ve been busy with official duties and neglected the child. This is indeed my failure as a father."

The attendants of Prince Pingxi’s mansion were all shocked, their eyes wide.

They had followed the prince for many years, and in all that time, they had never seen the prince apologize to anyone with such humility. Madam Xie was the first.

Yun Chu hadn’t expected the prince to be so gentle.

She looked down at the child in her arms. "Your father has come to find you. Go home with him."

The little girl didn’t even glance at Chu Yi. She clung to Yun Chu’s shoulder, wrapping her arms and legs around her, clearly unwilling to leave.

"Changsheng, Father will take you home," Chu Yi said, trying to soften his tone, but it still sounded deep. "You said you wanted to raise a cat. Father agrees, alright?"

The little girl immediately lifted her head from Yun Chu’s shoulder, slowly looking at Chu Yi with a hint of disbelief in her dark eyes.

Chu Yi nodded. "Father won’t lie to you. Be good, let Father hold you."

The little girl seemed to think for a long time before finally spreading her arms and reluctantly going into Chu Yi’s embrace.

Yun Chu’s arms suddenly felt empty.

The little girl weakly hugged her father’s neck, looking back at Yun Chu with great reluctance, her big eyes slowly filling with misty tears.

Yun Chu smiled and gently patted her head. "There are many bad people outside at night. Don’t run out like this again in the future."

The little girl pursed her lips and nodded slightly.

Chu Yi looked at Yun Chu. "Thanks to Madam Xie. If there’s anything Madam Xie needs help with, feel free to ask."

Yun Chu curtsied. "It was a small effort, no need for thanks."

Chu Yi nodded to her, then with the child in his arms, mounted his horse.

The little girl, holding Chu Yi’s neck, stared at Yun Chu with wide eyes until Yun Chu’s figure slowly disappeared into the night before she finally looked away with disappointment, nestling into Chu Yi’s arms.

Back at the mansion, Chu Yi gathered all the servants in the front courtyard. Dozens of people stood trembling.

He sat on a chair, his presence commanding without anger, and said coldly, "Speak. How did the princess leave the mansion in the middle of the night?"

While he was at the Jingzhao Yin interrogating bandits overnight, someone from the mansion had suddenly informed him that Changsheng was missing. His heart felt as if it had been thrown into a vat of boiling oil, filled with unbearable pain.

He immediately dispatched a team of guards to search the entire city, and fortunately, they found the child. Thankfully, nothing had happened to her.

Long before this, Changsheng had wanted to raise a cat, but because she was frail and would break out in rashes when near cats, he had never agreed. Tonight, Changsheng had insisted on staying with that Madam Xie, so he had no choice but to use the promise of a cat to get her back into his arms. But that didn’t mean Changsheng had left the mansion because of the cat.

The servants trembled as they stood in the courtyard.

Chu Yi’s gaze fell on the nanny who personally attended to the child.

The nanny could only speak up. "In the evening, this slave saw the princess painting a woman and wrote the words 'mother' next to it. She even cried for a while. This slave speculates that the princess left the mansion at night to find her mother..."

Chu Yi’s eyes darkened slightly.

He could fulfill any request for his children except this one.

He suppressed his emotions and said coldly, "The princess is only four years old. How could she leave the mansion just because she wanted to? From her courtyard to the outside, she would have to pass through at least five gates. Tell me, what exactly happened?"

While Chu Yi was interrogating the servants in the courtyard,

Chu Hongyu ran into his sister’s room, ordered the maids to leave, and climbed directly onto the little girl’s bed.

He pulled his sister into his arms and spoke softly.

"Changsheng, I know you miss Mother too. Let me tell you a secret, okay? I’ve actually found Mother. It’s just that going to Mother’s house is a bit troublesome, so I’ve never dared to tell you..."

"But it was wrong of you to sneak out of the mansion in the middle of the night. If you promise me not to do it again, I’ll take you to see Mother."

The little girl’s long eyelashes fluttered, and her big eyes sparkled with lively light.

She used both hands to make several gestures in succession.

Chu Hongyu smiled. "Big Brother won’t lie to you. I really found Mother. She’s very beautiful, gentle, and really likes me. She’ll definitely like you too."

The little girl started gesturing excitedly.

"Father agreed to let you raise a cat. That’s great. But you can’t touch the cat, or you’ll get a lot of rashes. They’ll be very itchy. The cat will be raised in my courtyard..."

The siblings talked and slowly fell asleep.

That night, Yun Chu couldn’t sleep well. In her mind, she alternately saw images of Brother Yu and the little princess, their figures overlapping, sometimes laughing, sometimes crying, and both calling her "Mother."

Before dawn, Yun Chu woke up.

She got up and picked up the wooden carving from the table, carefully caressing it, feeling much more at ease.

After finishing her toiletries, the people who came to pay their respects had arrived.

Xie Shian was dressed in new clothes, waiting in the side hall. Only then did Yun Chu remember that the imperial examination was today.

She had been so busy with various things that she had temporarily forgotten about this.

Back then, she had even specially prepared many things for Xie Shian, such as "success porridge," "top scholar soup," "first-place banquet," and "moon palace golden osmanthus wine..."

Yun Chu picked up a cup of tea and personally handed it to Xie Shian. "After entering the examination hall, the most important thing is to stay calm. This is a cup of clear tea. Drink it, and you will be able to discard impetuousness and achieve the top score."

"Thank you, Mother."

Xie Shian took the tea and drank it.

The other concubines in the room also said auspicious words, and the children wished him success in becoming a scholar. The atmosphere was harmonious for a while.

He Shi secretly slipped a talisman she had obtained into Xie Shian’s hand.

Yun Chu smiled and said, "Shian, today your father and I will take you to the examination hall. Your father should be waiting in the front courtyard. Let’s go."

Xie Shian nodded.

Just as they were about to leave, a servant woman suddenly rushed into Shengju Hall, her face filled with alarm. "Madam, it’s not good! Someone wants to jump into the well!"

He Shi angrily said, "Can’t you see that the young master is about to take the imperial examination? Why are you talking about such inauspicious things at this time? Get out!"

If this kind of nonsense affected her son’s examination, she would kill this servant woman.

The servant woman looked anxious. "Madam, we just pulled her back from the well. Then she tried to crash into the wall and looked for scissors to kill herself. What should we do?"

Yun Chu frowned. "Who wants to take their own life?"

The servant woman said, "It’s Jiu’er from the second young master’s courtyard."

At this, Yun Chu remembered. In her past life, it was also on this day that a maid in Xie Shiwei’s courtyard had made a scene about wanting to die. At that time, she had been in a hurry to take Xie Shian to the examination hall and had asked Tingshuang to handle it. But she hadn’t expected that Tingshuang wouldn’t be able to stop her, and in the end, the maid had jumped into a lake and died.

In the end, she had taken the initiative to give Jiu’er’s parents a large sum of money for the funeral, but she had never looked into why Jiu’er had wanted to take her own life.

chapters.title: Xie Shian's Institute Examination
chapters.content:
"Listen to the Wind, Listen to the Snow, the two of you take turns guarding Jiu'er. Do not leave her side until I return to the mansion."

"Listen to Frost, take my token and thoroughly investigate what happened."

Yun Chu gave clear and orderly instructions.

"Qi Pozi, take some people to the Second Young Master's courtyard and tie up the Second Young Master. Wait for me to come and deal with him!"

Xie Shian, standing to the side, was shocked. "Mother, what does this have to do with Shiwei?"

Yun Chu calmly replied, "It was a maid in his courtyard who tried to take her own life. How can it have nothing to do with him? An'er, you still have your examination. Don't be late. Go."

He Shao forced a smile. "Madam will surely make a fair judgment. Eldest Young Master, just focus on your exam."

Xie Shian knew this wasn’t his place to worry. He nodded and followed Yun Chu to the front courtyard, where he met Xie Jingyu.

The three of them boarded a carriage, which slowly made its way to the examination hall. This was the triennial institute examination, and many scholars came full of ambition.

In this dynasty, there was a rule: any scholar studying under the Imperial Commissioner of Education in the capital did not need to take the child scholar examination and could directly take the institute examination. If they were students of the Imperial College, they didn’t even need to take the institute examination and could directly participate in the provincial examination.

Xie Shian got off the carriage and cupped his hands. "Thank you, Father and Mother, for seeing me off. I'll go in now."

Xie Jingyu nodded, his eyes fixed on his son as he entered the examination hall.

Yun Chu's expression was calm, showing no particular emotion.

At that moment, a voice reached her ears. "Madam Xie."

She turned her head and saw Qin Mingheng, the Marquis of Xuanwu, standing beside her in his official robes. She quickly took a step back and greeted him. "Greetings to the Marquis."

Hearing the voice, Xie Jingyu immediately walked over and subtly positioned himself in front of Yun Chu. "This official greets the Marquis."

Seeing his action, Qin Mingheng's expression immediately darkened. He smiled and said, "This time, I am the supervising official for the western district of the institute examination. May I ask in which district Young Master Xie is taking the exam?"

Xie Jingyu's fingers tightened. An'er was in the western district.

Ever since he and Yun Chu had their marriage arranged, he and Qin Mingheng had been at odds.

Fortunately, the Marquis of Xuanwu had a title but no real power. Otherwise, Qin Mingheng would have suppressed him in every possible way in the officialdom.

Xie Jingyu cupped his hands. "The Marquis has to supervise the exam. This official will not delay the Marquis any longer. Farewell."

He led Yun Chu towards the carriage.

Qin Mingheng closed his eyes and sniffed the air, catching the same scent as the handkerchief. He took a deep, satisfied breath.

Once in the carriage, Xie Jingyu's expression was still poor.

Yun Chu was not concerned about what had happened between the two of them. She asked, "Today is your rest day, husband. Do you have any other arrangements later?"

Xie Jingyu was surprised. This was the first time Yun Chu had asked about his schedule. Did she want him to accompany her for something?

His expression softened slightly. "Just some official business, minor matters. Why does Madam ask?"

"When we left the house this morning, the wet nurse reported that a maid in Wei'er's courtyard was making a scene, trying to take her own life." Yun Chu said slowly, "Last time, I disciplined Wei'er according to family rules, which displeased the Old Madam. I couldn’t do anything more, so I thought of asking you to handle it."

Xie Jingyu frowned. "If a disobedient maid wants to die, just sell her off. Why go through so much trouble?"

Hearing this, Yun Chu laughed outright. "Without a proper investigation, you would just convict the maid?"

Her laughter made Xie Jingyu feel an inexplicable sense of mockery.

Mockery of him for being a scholar in name only, mockery of his poor household management, mockery of him, mockery of the Xie family... Her laughter contained too much.

"Then, husband, go attend to your official business. I won’t trouble you with the matters of the inner courtyard again."

As soon as Yun Chu finished speaking, the carriage arrived at the Xie mansion. She lifted the curtain and got out, not waiting for Xie Jingyu, and walked straight in.

Xie Jingyu pinched the space between his eyebrows and sighed deeply.

Over the past five years, the matters of the inner courtyard had been left to Yun Chu to manage. This was the first time she had asked for his help. No matter how busy he was, he had to make time to look into it.

He jumped out of the carriage and followed Yun Chu into Xie Shiwei's courtyard.

Old Madam Xie, Yuan Shi, and several concubines were already in the courtyard. Tingshuang stood at the door of a side room, her expression grave.

"Jingyu, you're finally back!" The Old Madam, weakened by a recent illness, stood up with the help of a wet nurse. "Look at what your wife has done! She actually had people tie up Wei'er. I wanted to untie him, but she said it had to wait until she returned. She may be the mistress of the Xie household, but she is not the Emperor!"

The Old Madam was truly furious.

Wei'er had indeed been a bit naughty in the past, but he had been much better behaved recently. Why should he be punished just because a maid tried to take her own life?

Last time, during the birthday banquet, there was a mishap. Yun Chu had taken it upon herself to discipline Wei'er, thinking the Xie family couldn’t do without her. Was she becoming more and more unscrupulous in her actions?

"Your daughter-in-law dare not presume to be the Emperor." Yun Chu walked over and slowly curtsied. "Your daughter-in-law greets the Old Madam. Today’s matter coincidentally happened on the day of An'er’s institute examination, so there was no time to inform the Old Madam. Please, take a seat. Let my husband handle this. Tingshuang, come and explain what happened."

Tingshuang walked over, her head lowered. "Madam ordered me to investigate, so I questioned all the maids, wet nurses, and young servants in the Second Young Master's courtyard. It turns out that not a single maid in the Second Young Master's courtyard has escaped his punishment..."

He Shao, standing behind the Old Madam, couldn’t help but interrupt. "It is only natural for a master to punish his servants. What is there to say?"

Tingshuang sighed and gave the maids a look.

All the maids rolled up their sleeves and pulled open their collars, revealing shocking scars.

Yun Chu tightened her lips.

In her past life, several maids in Xie Shiwei's courtyard had died unnatural deaths. Later, he had taken seven or eight concubines, four of whom had died in bed.

In fact, many maids had come to her to report this, but every time she tried to investigate, He Shao, who was then known as Mama He, would cover it up. With the Old Madam’s indulgence and Xie Jingyu’s turning a blind eye, she, as a non-biological mother, couldn’t press the matter further...

Recalling this, she knew that at least a dozen or more women had died at Xie Shiwei's hands.

"Please, Madam, stand up for us!" one maid pleaded. "Whether the Second Young Master is happy or not, he takes it out on us. There isn’t a single good spot left on our bodies."

"The Second Young Master likes to whip people. My back is covered in whip marks. If we made a mistake, it would be one thing for the Second Young Master to punish us. But we have always followed the rules and never made any mistakes. Yet we are beaten every day. We can’t go on like this."

"The Second Young Master made me stand with a flowerpot on my head all day. When I couldn’t hold it steady, he punished me by making me soak in a water vat all night."

The several maids serving Xie Shiwei poured out their grievances one after another.

He Shao coldly retorted, "Isn’t it because you maids don’t serve the Second Young Master wholeheartedly? Otherwise, why would he punish you? Besides, the Second Young Master is only eight years old. Even if he whips you, how bad can it be..."

"Shut up!" Xie Jingyu roared. "A concubine like you has no right to speak. Get out!"

He Shao was taken aback.

She was Wei'er’s mother. How could she not have the right to speak? What had she said wrong?

Xie Jingyu’s hands behind his back were clenched tightly.

Over the past few years, he had been busy with promotions and official duties, leaving home before dawn and returning late at night. Even on his rest days, there was a pile of things to handle. He had indeed neglected the upbringing of his children. He had always thought that Wei'er was just not fond of studying and not making progress, and that with An'er around, it would be enough. He never expected Wei'er to do something like this!

He finally understood why Yun Chu had asked him to handle this.

Because this was no longer something Yun Chu could handle alone.

---

chapters.title: Whipping Xie Shiwei
chapters.content:
Old Madam Xie also realized the seriousness of the situation.

In noble families, the treatment of servants was always lenient and kind. If word got out that they were harsh and abusive to their servants, their reputation would suffer greatly.

This matter must not be allowed to spread.

Before she could speak, Xie Jingyu coldly ordered, "Bring Jiu'er out. I want to hear why she tried to kill herself."

Jiu'er was brought out from the room in disheveled clothes, her face ashen as she collapsed to the ground.

She was only eleven years old, a young girl just beginning to develop. She looked at Yun Chu and sobbed, "Madam, this servant really doesn’t want to live anymore. Please grant me a quick death."

Yun Chu walked over and helped her up. "Jiu'er, the adults are here. If you have any grievances, tell the adults."

Jiu'er looked at Yun Chu and saw a firm yet gentle light in her eyes, as if it gave her a surge of strength.

She didn’t speak but lowered her head and undid the buttons on her collar, revealing her small frame. On her body were whip marks, both new and old, crisscrossing in a horrifying display.

"It’s just a few whip marks. It’s not worth dying over." The Old Madam glanced and said gently, "You girls are young and may not be efficient in your work. It’s not improper for your master to punish you. The Second Young Master is young and doesn’t know the weight of his actions. It is indeed our family’s fault for not disciplining him properly. How about this: I’ll give each of you ten taels of silver for medical expenses and transfer you to another courtyard. How does that sound?"

Although her voice was gentle, it carried an implicit threat.

These maids should know better than to take the money and let the matter drop. If they continued to pursue it, things wouldn’t be so simple.

Yun Chu gave a cold laugh.

In her past life, Xie Shiwei’s offenses had been covered up in this very way. Until her death, she had never seen Xie Shiwei receive the punishment he deserved.

She looked at Xie Jingyu. "Does the Old Madam’s word represent my husband’s will?"

Xie Jingyu’s hands clenched tightly behind his back. He knew he had to take a stand. Otherwise, Yun Chu would no longer bother to discipline the children in the future.

He was too busy. He needed Yun Chu, his capable wife, to keep the Xie family running smoothly.

He stared at Jiu'er and coldly asked, "Is it because the Second Young Master whipped you that you no longer want to live?"

Jiu'er raised her arm. With the thumb and index finger of her other hand, she pulled hard on her arm. Suddenly, a silver needle appeared at her fingertips, and a needle hole appeared on her arm, oozing a few drops of blood.

"The Second Young Master wanted to know how many needles could be inserted into a person’s body. He used me as an experiment." Jiu'er sobbed. "Half a year ago, the Second Young Master started inserting needles into me. The first time, he inserted ten into my back. After that, he added one more each day. There are now nearly two hundred needles in my body. If I move even slightly, it hurts terribly all over. If I dare to secretly remove any needle, what awaits me is the Second Young Master’s whip... I feel like those needles have already entered my internal organs. It hurts so much every day. I really don’t want to live anymore..."

The courtyard fell into complete silence.

Only the sound of Jiu'er’s sobs could be heard.

Even the maids who shared a room with her had no idea that every night she was called to the Second Young Master only to have needles inserted into her.

The Old Madam opened and closed her mouth, at a loss for words.

He Shao had long known about her son’s antics and wasn’t the least bit surprised. She just didn’t understand why this matter had blown up so much...

Tao Concubine, who was pregnant, was so frightened by the scene that she could barely stand.

Yun Chu’s heart trembled.

Xie Shiwei was only eight years old this year. An eight-year-old child could come up with such cruel methods. She dared not imagine what the concubines who had died at Xie Shiwei’s hands in the future had gone through. Whether they were tortured to death by Xie Shiwei or driven to suicide, their lives were filled with bloody and desperate despair...

"Bring that unfilial son out!" Xie Jingyu, who was usually gentle in public, suddenly roared.

Two wet nurses immediately pushed the bound Xie Shiwei out of the side room. His mouth was gagged, and he looked at the Old Madam with muffled pleas for help.

Before the Old Madam could say anything, Xie Jingyu coldly ordered, "Bring the Second Young Master’s whip!"

The people below immediately brought the whip.

It was a soft leather whip suitable for children to play with. Although it wasn’t as lethal as a hard whip, the pain it inflicted was not much lighter than a board.

Xie Jingyu raised the whip and struck Xie Shiwei.

With his mouth gagged, Xie Shiwei couldn’t scream no matter how much it hurt. His hands and feet were bound, and he writhed on the ground like a worm.

*Crack! Crack! Crack!*

Xie Jingyu showed no mercy and lashed out seven or eight times in a row, focusing on one spot. Xie Shiwei’s back was torn open, his clothes stained red with blood.

"Master!" He Shao could no longer bear it. She rushed forward and threw herself on Xie Shiwei, blocking the fierce whip.

She knew she shouldn’t show too much concern for her children in public, but no mother could bear to watch her child being beaten like this.

"The Second Young Master is still young. Master, please show mercy!" He Shao held Xie Shiwei tightly and pleaded.

Only then did the Old Madam come to her senses. She stood up and said, "Jingyu, if you keep beating him like this, the child will be beaten to death. The matter has already happened. What good will it do to beat him to death? You should think about how to properly educate Wei'er, how to treat Jiu'er’s illness, and how to minimize the impact of this incident..."

Xie Jingyu, a scholar, was not skilled at whipping someone. By now, he was already out of breath from the effort.

He threw the whip aside and coldly declared, "Xie Shiwei, your behavior has brought me, your father, immense shame. I am ashamed to have you as my son!"

How could the Xie family, which had been scholarly for generations, produce such a good-for-nothing?

If this good-for-nothing were allowed to grow up like this, the reputation of the Xie family, built up over three or four generations, would be destroyed completely.

"I fear the Xie family cannot educate you properly!" Xie Jingyu’s voice was harsh. "I will send you to the military!"

Hearing this, the Old Madam was horrified. "No, absolutely not! The military is a place for the poor and desperate. It’s hard and exhausting. If he goes to the front lines, his life could be in danger with one wrong move."

Xie Jingyu took a deep breath. "The military has strict discipline. Only there can Wei'er’s nature be corrected. Otherwise, in the future, if he commits murder or arson, the Xie family will not be able to cover for him. Madam, my father-in-law has many confidants in the capital. Could Madam please help find a good place for Wei'er?"

A smile appeared on Yun Chu’s lips.

She truly hadn’t expected this scene to come seven or eight years earlier than in her previous life.

In her past life, she had unhesitatingly agreed, sending Xie Shiwei to the Yun family’s camp stationed at the outskirts of the capital, making Xie Shiwei a confidant of the Yun family army. The consequences had been too tragic. She would never try that again...

"Husband, you are unaware." Yun Chu spoke with difficulty. "A few days ago, Wei'er wanted to learn martial arts. I had Qiutong check his physique. He doesn’t have the talent for martial arts. If sent to the military, he would only be a common soldier. A common soldier in the military is like the lowest-ranked maid in a household. Husband, can you bear to send him?"

Before Xie Jingyu could speak, the Old Madam immediately said, "Wei'er is only eight years old. Sending him to the military as a common soldier would be like sending him to be bullied. Even with the Yun family army protecting him, they can’t protect him all the time. What if something happens when they’re not around?"

He Shao quickly added, "Master, the Second Young Master has already promised Madam that he will study hard. He has changed, truly changed."

Xie Shiwei nodded desperately.

chapters.title: I Have Said All I Need to Say
chapters.content:
Xie Jingyu’s proposal to enlist in the army was merely a desperate choice made under duress.

After calming down and reconsidering, he indeed had many reservations.

He coldly stared at Xie Shiwei, who was being held by He-shi. "Have you truly decided to study properly?"

He-shi quickly pulled the cloth out of Xie Shiwei’s mouth.

"Father, I was wrong, I know I was wrong, I won’t dare do it again," Xie Shiwei sobbed. "I will definitely study hard, just like Eldest Brother, with diligence and effort. Father, please don’t send me to the military camp!"

The torment of learning martial arts from Autumn Tong in his mother’s courtyard had made him deeply fear being bullied. As long as he could stay in the manor, he was willing to study properly.

Disregarding the whip marks on his body, he crawled to Xie Jingyu and begged, "Father, please give me one more chance."

"Husband, please give Wei another chance. Even if he must enlist, he is still too young. If he doesn’t study well, we can send him later," Yun Chu bent down, helping Xie Shiwei up. "Wei, your father whipped you for your own good. You must not hold a grudge against him in your heart. Since you’ve promised to study hard, from now on, you must not be lazy. You will go to the school at the beginning of the Chen hour and may only return to your courtyard at the end of the Shen hour. Can you do that?"

At this point, what else could Xie Shiwei refuse? He nodded repeatedly.

Yun Chu continued, "Even if you and Yun start studying at the same time, you are much older than him. If you can’t even keep up with Yun, it will prove you haven’t studied properly. If your father decides to send you to the military camp next time, I won’t stop him."

"Mother, I will definitely study hard!"

Xie Shiwei was in so much pain he felt dizzy. No matter what the demand, he only knew to nod.

He-shi, heartbroken for her son, quickly said, "Master, Madam, the Second Young Master’s back is bleeding so much. Let me take him to apply medicine."

The Old Madam spoke up, "Zhou Mama, quickly go fetch the physician!"

Xie Shiwei was taken into the bedroom, and both the Old Madam and the Madam followed to check on him.

Xie Jingyu turned his gaze to Yun Chu. "There are still some loose ends to tie up, and I’ll have to trouble you, Madam. If there’s anything that requires my involvement, feel free to speak up."

Yun Chu lowered her head. "I can handle the remaining matters. Husband, you may go attend to your business."

Xie Jingyu rubbed his fingers. The few lashes he had given had also blistered his palm. At this moment, he slightly regretted hitting so hard.

He only hoped that Wei would truly study hard. He didn’t need to bring glory to the family name; he just needed to grow into an upright and honorable man.

Yun Chu looked at the maidservants attending to Xie Shiwei’s courtyard and had them all stand up. "The Old Madam promised you ten taels of silver each. Later, I will have someone deliver it to you. If you wish to work in another courtyard, feel free to come and ask. If you no longer wish to stay in the Xie family, I can also return your contract of servitude."

The few maidservants were terrified at the thought of the Second Young Master. They feared that once he recovered, he would seek revenge on them. The Madam couldn’t protect them forever.

Except for Jiu’er, the other three maidservants unanimously decided to take their contracts and leave the manor.

These few maidservants had been purchased by Yun Chu from the slave market after the Xie family had added members. Their contracts were in her hands.

She immediately had someone fetch the contracts and handed them one by one to the maidservants. In addition to the ten taels promised by the Old Madam, she secretly added five more taels for each. After arranging for a physician to examine and prescribe medicine for the maidservants, she arranged for their departure.

Yun Chu held the last contract and stood by Jiu’er’s bed. "Do you truly wish to remain in the Xie family?"

Xie Shiwei was a highly vengeful person. These few maidservants who had reported him would all suffer retaliation, especially Jiu’er, who had escalated the matter.

She didn’t understand why Jiu’er insisted on staying.

The physician had just removed dozens of silver needles from Jiu’er’s body. She was extremely weak, lowering her gaze to hide the emotions in her eyes. "This servant has no father or mother. Besides the Xie family, this servant has nowhere else to go. Furthermore, this servant believes that after this ordeal, the Second Young Master will definitely change for the better. Madam, this servant is willing to stay and continue serving the Second Young Master."

Yun Chu smiled.

Jiu’er was too much like her.

When she had first been reborn, she had the same mindset: to rise again from where she had fallen, rather than flee far away.

She spoke gently, "There are still many silver needles in your body. You will need at least three more treatments to completely remove them. We can discuss your future then. For now, focus on recovering. I will arrange for a matron to take care of your daily needs."

Jiu’er’s eyes were filled with guilt.

She had stayed with different intentions, yet the Madam had still been so kind to her.

If only she had been in the Madam’s courtyard from the beginning... Even if her body recovered, it was already ruined. Her life was destroyed...

Yun Chu went to check on Xie Shiwei.

Although Xie Jingyu had been heavy-handed, he was a scholar at heart. The injuries looked severe, but in reality, they were just superficial wounds. The physician had prescribed a topical medicine and instructed him not to touch water. In about three or four days, the scabs would form, and he would be mostly healed.

Yun Chu sneered coldly.

Jiu’er had nearly lost her life, yet Xie Shiwei had only received such a light punishment.

Since the Xie family refused to properly teach Xie Shiwei how to be a decent person, then perhaps it was time to let outsiders do the teaching. When that time came, it wouldn’t be just a few lashes...

After three days of rest, Xie Shiwei was able to get out of bed.

He didn’t dare to stay in his room and slack off any longer. On the third day, despite his injuries, he hurried to the manor’s small school to attend class.

Jiu’er had undergone three or four sessions of needle removal, yet not all the silver needles had been taken out.

Yun Chu sighed silently.

Xie Shiwei was truly too cruel. He was practically a demon.

"Madam, this servant feels a bit better," Jiu’er knelt on the ground. "This servant cannot repay Madam’s great kindness and can only kowtow to you."

She knocked her head three times before continuing, "This servant will go attend to the Second Young Master now."

Yun Chu had her stand up. "If you return to Wei’s side, he will inevitably make things difficult for you. How much more abuse can your frail body endure? I know what you intend to do."

Jiu’er looked up in disbelief.

Yun Chu met her gaze. "Continuing to endure in silence will only lead to more harm for yourself. When the time comes to strike, do so swiftly. I have said all I need to say. You may go."

After leaving the Shengju Pavilion, Jiu’er still couldn’t believe it.

The Madam clearly knew she intended to take revenge on the Second Young Master. Why hadn’t she driven her out of the manor? Instead, she had urged her to strike quickly...

Why? What was the reason...

Yun Chu arranged for a matron to secretly follow Jiu’er to prevent the girl from being harmed again. Since she had saved Jiu’er, she would see it through to the end.

By now, it was almost evening. Yun Chu set aside her tasks and walked to the front courtyard. Xie Jingyu had been waiting for a while, clearly anxious.

The three-day imperial examination had ended, and Xie Shian would soon exit the examination hall. As a father, it was natural for him to be tense.

The two of them boarded the carriage together. Yun Chu looked out the window. Xie Jingyu tried to speak a few times but didn’t know what to say. They remained silent until the carriage reached the examination hall’s entrance.

"There are too many people over there. I won’t go," Yun Chu casually remarked. "I’ll wait for An here."

Xie Jingyu didn’t overthink it. He nodded and went to the main gate where the crowd was thickest.

---

chapters.title: Negotiating for the Estate
chapters.content:
Yun Chu sat in the carriage and took a sip of hot tea. Before long, she indeed heard a man’s voice from outside the carriage: "Madam Xie, I am the owner of the Dou family’s trading firm. Might I trouble Madam for a moment of your time?"

The haunted estate had originally been sold by the Wu family to the Zou family. The Zou family later sold it cheaply to the Dou family’s trading firm, where it became a burden in the Dou family’s hands.

She remembered that in her past life, after the fire, the estate had been directly taken by the family of a palace concubine. Merchants were the lowest class, even worse off than ordinary farmers. How could they dare to oppose the imperial family? In the end, they had no choice but to hand over the estate to the palace concubine’s family.

Yun Chu lifted the curtain.

Standing below the carriage were two people: Master Dou and Madam Dou, both in their forties.

She took Ling Shuang’s hand and stepped down. "Three nights ago, I took some people to your Dou family’s estate. I apologize for the intrusion, but I’ve been too busy these past few days to come and offer my apologies in person..."

"That’s understandable. With Young Master Xie taking the imperial examination, Madam Xie must be very busy," Madam Dou quickly replied. "That estate was already abandoned. It was its fortune to have Madam Xie rest there for a while. I hope it didn’t frighten Madam Xie too much?"

Yun Chu sighed. "Actually, I had the intention of buying a large estate. I heard that one has mountains and water, so I went to inspect it. Who would have thought..."

She shook her head and didn’t continue.

Madam Dou’s face, however, lit up with joy.

For so many years, no one had shown interest in that estate. Finally, a sucker had appeared.

But she had also heard that Madam Xie had entered with a group of people and left carrying three or four injured individuals. It was clear they had been badly frightened.

To persuade Madam Xie to buy the estate would require some effort.

Madam Dou paused before speaking. "Madam Xie may not be aware, but the rumors about the estate being haunted are not true. The neighboring farmers were jealous of the estate’s fertile land, so they spread lies about ghosts to scare people away. Back when our Dou family lived there, those farmers would always come to cause trouble. We are merchants, the lowest of the four classes. How could we dare to stand up to farmers? Since the Dou family doesn’t lack this bit of money, we simply let the estate fall into disuse."

Yun Chu smiled.

If they truly didn’t lack money, they wouldn’t have come to her.

In this era, a farmer’s annual income was only two taels of silver. This estate had cost at least ten thousand taels. Anyone would feel the loss of such a sum.

Master Dou added, "Initially, our Dou family bought the estate from the Zou family for twelve thousand taels of silver. If Madam Xie is truly interested, we can let it go for eight thousand taels."

Yun Chu shook her head.

The Dou family was indeed greedy.

This estate had been abandoned for over twenty years, and they still wanted eight thousand taels? If it had been maintained all these years, she wouldn’t mind paying ten thousand.

An opening price of eight thousand was clearly taking advantage of her as a noblewoman who didn’t understand business. They saw that she had personally visited the estate and decided to take the opportunity to swindle her.

"Eight thousand taels is already a very good price. However—" Yun Chu lowered her voice, "my husband does not approve of me buying that estate. He says it’s bad luck and fears it will affect his official career. Even if I truly like it, there’s nothing I can do."

Ling Shuang, standing beside her, added, "Our Madam really likes the mountains of that estate. She once considered using her private funds to buy it, but her private funds are not enough..."

Madam Dou quickly asked, "May I ask how much private money Madam Xie has?"

Yun Chu extended three fingers.

Madam Dou’s smile froze on her face. She had thought Madam Xie was an easy mark, but she hadn’t expected her to haggle so fiercely.

Business had been difficult lately. The Dou family’s trading firm had closed several branches and urgently needed silver to keep afloat. If not for this, the couple wouldn’t have come here specifically to intercept Madam Xie.

Master Dou was a merchant, skilled in bargaining. He immediately said, "Final offer: five thousand taels of silver. We can handle the deed right now."

Yun Chu shook her head. "I only have this much."

The estate had been abandoned for over twenty years and was supposedly haunted. Even if she acquired it, aside from the at least ten thousand taels needed for repairs, changing people’s perceptions of it would not be simple.

Most importantly, she didn’t have much silver on hand.

Just as the Dou couple hesitated, Yun Chu’s expression changed. "My husband is coming. Forget it. I won’t buy it. You should leave quickly."

Master Dou and Madam Dou: "..."

They had just thought three thousand taels was too little, but now, even that three thousand was gone.

But Xie Jingyu had already arrived with Xie Shian, so the Dou couple, no matter how reluctant, had to step aside and wait for another opportunity.

Xie Jingyu curiously glanced at the backs of the Dou couple. "Who were those two?"

Yun Chu smiled. "Merchants who have done business with the Yun family. They came to pay their respects to me."

She turned to Xie Shian. "An, how did your exam go?"

Xie Shian smiled. "I should have no problem being in the top three."

Upon returning home, the Old Madam saw Xie Shian’s confident demeanor and knew that this great-grandson would definitely become a Xiucai in one go. At just twelve years old, this was even more outstanding than Jingyu had been at that age.

Xie Pin, sitting to the side, asked, "If Shian becomes the top scholar, will our Xie family hold a banquet?"

Xie Jingyu took a sip of wine. "Of course."

The Old Madam shared the same sentiment. "The youngest top scholar in the entire capital, this is something to be proud of. Why wouldn’t we hold a banquet? Chu, what do you think?"

Although the Old Madam currently disliked Yun Chu, in such a major matter, she was still in the habit of listening to Yun Chu’s advice.

"Many noble families in the capital have painstakingly cultivated their children, yet none can compare to An. If An truly takes first place this time, it will bring honor to the Xie family. Moreover, there have been many criticisms of our family lately. Holding this banquet will naturally silence those voices." Yun Chu smiled. "If the Old Madam trusts me, I can arrange the banquet. Would that be acceptable?"

The Old Madam was more than willing. "Then I’ll have to trouble you, Chu."

Xie Pin looked at Yun Chu. "Mother, may I learn alongside you?"

After the incident at the last birthday banquet, she had stopped learning household management from her mother. She had avoided it for so long, but it was time to face it.

This time, the top scholar’s banquet would naturally be even livelier than the Old Madam’s birthday banquet. She was determined to clear her name at this event.

Although the imperial examination results had not yet been announced, the Old Madam was already convinced that Xie Shian was the top scholar. In her joy, she couldn’t help but sigh, "If only Wei could study as well as this..."

Xie Shian, upon returning from the examination hall, had heard about what had happened in the manor. Wei had been whipped more than ten times by their father and had been bedridden for two days before going to school today.

"An, go see your younger brother," Yuan Shi spoke up. "Seeing how accomplished you are now, perhaps Wei will start to apply himself."

Xie Shian nodded and walked toward Xie Shiwei’s courtyard.

All the servants in the courtyard had been replaced with sturdy matrons. One matron was standing at the entrance, boiling medicine. When she saw him approaching, she was about to bow in greeting.

He made a gesture for silence and quietly pushed open the door. He saw Xie Shiwei lying on the bed, reading a book.

As an elder brother, seeing his younger brother from the same mother becoming motivated brought him a sense of relief. He felt that his father’s lashes had been well worth it.

But as he approached, his expression suddenly darkened. He snatched the book from Xie Shiwei’s hands. "Is this the kind of trash you read all day?"

The book was filled with illustrations of small figures, depicting various bloody scenes as part of a story.

"Eldest Brother..." Xie Shiwei was terrified. "Please don’t tell Father and Mother. I beg you, Eldest Brother."

Xie Shian threw the illustrated book onto the candle holder on the table. Soon, it caught fire.

Suppressing his anger, he said, "Father punished you so severely, yet you still refuse to change. It seems you truly are beyond hope!"

"Eldest Brother, I didn’t mean to... The tutor’s assignments were too difficult..." Xie Shiwei racked his brain for excuses. "I wrote for a while and wanted to relax, so I picked up this book. I really have changed. I’ve changed for the better..."

Xie Shian looked at the crooked, poorly written characters on the table.

chapters.title: You Dare to Hide
chapters.content:
Xie Shian simply couldn’t believe someone could write such ugly characters.

At the age of three, his own handwriting had been far better than that of his eight-year-old younger brother, Xie Shiyou.

"At eight years old, you still can’t even write 'Men at their birth are naturally good' properly. Don’t you feel ashamed?" Xie Shian was so angry he spoke without restraint. "No wonder Father beats you. If it were me, I’d strangle you to death!"

Xie Shiyou feared two people most in the world: his father, Xie Jingyu, and his eldest brother, Xie Shian. His elder brother was too outstanding, making him seem like a good-for-nothing by comparison.

He grabbed Xie Shian’s sleeve and pleaded, "Eldest Brother, I really want to study, but it’s too hard. It’s really too hard. No matter how much I try, I can’t learn. I have no choice… Mother said if I can’t even compare to Yun Ge’er, she’ll send me to the army. Eldest Brother, please help me. I don’t want to die on the front lines…"

Xie Shian pushed him away and snapped, "If you can’t study and don’t want to join the army, do you want to be a failure your whole life?"

"I… I could learn to do business?" Xie Shiyou racked his brains. "I may be slow, but I’m still young. If I take my time, I’ll eventually learn…"

Xie Shian pressed his lips together.

The Xie family would only grow larger in the future. While someone needed to uphold the family’s reputation, there also needed to be someone managing the business in the background to provide sufficient funds.

He couldn’t trust just anyone with this task, only his full-blooded younger brother, Shiyou, would do.

After a moment of thought, he said, "Mother wants you to compare with Yun Ge’er. All you need to do is outperform him. If you can’t even handle this, then you deserve to go to war and have the enemy chop off your empty head."

With that, he flicked his sleeve and left.

Xie Shiyou rushed to the desk and picked up the burned picture book, but it was already gone. He was so furious that he pounded his chest in frustration.

As he looked up, he saw a figure entering the room. He grabbed a candle holder and hurled it at them. "You little wretch! This is all your fault!"

The person who entered was Jiu’er.

She sidestepped and avoided the candle holder, which crashed to the ground with a loud *bang*.

"You dare to hide!" Xie Shiyou roared. "Wretch! Who gave you the courage!"

Jiu’er lowered her head and said, "In response to Second Young Master, the madam has arranged for a physician to check my pulse every other day. If I have new injuries, the madam will surely hold Second Young Master accountable. I was also worried that Second Young Master’s old injuries haven’t healed, and I didn’t want you to add new ones."

Hearing this, Xie Shiyou grew even angrier.

But indeed, he no longer dared to lay a hand on Jiu’er.

Jiu’er bent down to pick up the candle holder from the floor and began her work in earnest.

While Xie Shiyou was suffering, the Xie mansion was filled with joy.

Old Madam Xie had already ordered Yun Chu to begin preparations for the banquet celebrating Xie Shian’s first-place finish in the county examination.

Other families wouldn’t dare make such preparations before the results were announced, but the Xie family had the confidence to do so.

Yun Chu was experienced in hosting such banquets. Most tasks didn’t require much thought; she could simply delegate them to Tingshuang. The only thing that needed careful consideration was the guest list.

She drafted a list and sent it to Anshou Hall.

The Old Madam took one look and was stunned. This daughter-in-law was incredible; she even wanted to invite the Sacrificial Officer of the Imperial College. He was a third-rank official in the court; how could he possibly attend a banquet at the home of a fifth-rank official?

Yun Chu smiled and explained, "Old Madam, you may not be aware, but the Academy of Political Studies where An Ge’er studies was established under the leadership of the Imperial College. Every year, the Academy selects two outstanding students to enter the Imperial College. Since An Ge’er has become the top scholar in the county examination, he is the most outstanding student at the Academy. This autumn, he will definitely enter the Imperial College. The Sacrificial Officer values talent, so naturally, he will come to show his support."

The Old Madam knew of the Academy of Political Studies and the Imperial College, but she hadn’t realized that students from the Academy could enter the Imperial College.

Her eyes widened in shock. "If I recall correctly, the students at the Imperial College are all royal relatives, nobles, and dukes. Can An Ge’er really get in?"

Yun Chu smiled. "As long as An Ge’er is this year’s top scholar, it’s a certainty. The Emperor wants to find outstanding students to serve as study companions for the princes, to encourage them to work harder and study better."

"Amitabha Buddha, may the heavens bless us!" The Old Madam pressed her palms together in prayer, then looked at Yun Chu. "You’re the one who thinks of everything. Now that we’ve invited the Sacrificial Officer to drink with us, he will surely take good care of An Ge’er in the future."

Yun Chu continued, "We should also invite all the teachers from the Academy of Political Studies, as well as An Ge’er’s classmates. What do you think, Old Madam?"

The Old Madam quickly nodded. "Most of the students at the Capital’s Academy of Political Studies are children of official families. These people will be An Ge’er’s future connections in the officialdom. We must invite them."

Yun Chu spoke again, "There’s one person… the young marquis of the Xuanyu Marquis’s mansion. At the Old Madam’s birthday banquet last time, he took the initiative to come and offer his congratulations. Should we invite the marquis for An Ge’er’s celebration this time?"

The Old Madam admonished, "Last time, we didn’t send an invitation to the Xuanyu Marquis’s mansion. That was our oversight. We must not make the same mistake again. This time, we’re inviting so many dignitaries, so the banquet must be generous. Prepare some new dishes. Also, you must personally supervise the kitchen; we can’t have a repeat of last time’s incident."

Yun Chu nodded in agreement.

Returning to her courtyard, she tossed the guest list aside, sat at the desk, and began to paint.

The haunted estate was already as good as hers. Now, she needed to plan how to renovate and improve it once it was in her possession.

Everything would revolve around the hot spring as the core, building a villa for the noble and wealthy families to enjoy.

As Yun Chu was drawing, she suddenly heard Feng walking in to report, "Madam, Concubine Yu and Third Young Master have arrived. It seems there’s something important."

She put down the brush and closed the drawing paper. "Let them in."

Tingyu entered the flower hall with Xie Shiyun, and the mother and son both greeted her with a bow.

"Madam, this concubine has something to report." Tingyu lowered her head. "Today at noon, I went to the school to deliver clothes to Yun Ge’er. I personally saw Second Young Master bullying Yun Ge’er. Second Young Master is tall and strong; he pushed four-year-old Yun Ge’er to the edge of the lake. He almost fell in! Madam, you must seek justice for Yun Ge’er."

Yun Chu frowned. "Yun Ge’er, is this true?"

Xie Shiyun lowered his head and said nothing.

"Tingshuang, have Second Young Master come over."

By now, school had already ended for the day. Tingshuang went directly to Xie Shiyou’s courtyard and brought him over.

After several incidents like this, Xie Shiyou had come to fear one more person: Yun Chu.

As soon as he entered Shengju, he became meek and submissive, with none of his usual arrogance and domineering attitude.

"Greetings, Mother." Xie Shiyou cupped his hands in respect. "I don’t know why Mother has called for me."

Yun Chu spoke, "Concubine Yu says she personally saw you try to push Yun Ge’er into the lake. Is this true?"

Xie Shiyou feigned shock. "Yun Ge’er is my younger brother. How could I possibly harm him? Concubine Yu must have seen wrong."

Tingyu raised her head. "Second Young Master, how can you deny what you’ve done? Not only did I see it, but my maid also witnessed it with her own eyes!"

Xie Shiyou put on an innocent face. "But my maid also saw that I didn’t push Yun Ge’er. Mother, although I have a stubborn nature, I would never lay a hand on my own younger brother. Besides, I’ve already changed. Please, Mother, give me justice!"

---

chapters.title: Xie Shian, Top Scholar
chapters.content:
Yun Chu’s lips twitched.

It was easy to change the world, but not one’s nature. Xie Shiyou would never truly change.

After a beating, he had only learned to pretend.

Yun Chu spoke, "Concubine Yu says you pushed him, and you say you didn’t. Each of you has your own reasoning. Why not let Yun Ge’er speak for himself?"

Xie Shiyun kept his head down, twisting his hands together.

Tingyu was so anxious she wanted to stomp her foot. "Yun Ge’er, Madam is here. Just tell Madam the truth. Madam dotes on you the most and will surely seek justice for you."

Xie Shiyou’s mouth twitched. "Yun Ge’er, the teacher said that children must not lie."

"Mother, Second Brother didn’t bully me…" Xie Shiyun buried his head even lower. "It… it was my concubine mother who saw wrong."
