Tingyu couldn’t believe it. She wanted to say more.

Yun Chu set down her teacup. "Shiyou says he didn’t push, and Yun Ge’er also says he didn’t. Concubine Yu, isn’t this a case of making something out of nothing?"

Tingyu opened her mouth to argue. "Madam, this concubine did not—"

"I have many things to attend to. You may all withdraw." Yun Chu picked up a book and began to read.

Tingshuang made a gesture for them to leave.

Tingyu took Xie Shiyun and left, her face cold. "I clearly saw him bullying you. Why won’t you admit it in front of Madam?"

Xie Shiyou walked over from the side. "What is Concubine Yu talking about? Actually, Yun Ge’er and I were just playing around. It was Concubine Yu who took it seriously and even brought it to Mother’s attention. Mother is so busy every day; she doesn’t have time to deal with such trivial matters."

As he spoke, he put his arm around Xie Shiyun’s shoulders. "Yun Ge’er, the teacher has assigned homework. Let’s go write together."

Once Tingyu was far behind them, Xie Shiyou’s voice turned dark. "Today, you performed well in front of Mother. I’m very satisfied. Remember this: in the future, the Xie family will be managed by my eldest brother. If you don’t obey me, once my eldest brother becomes the head of the family, I’ll have him expel Concubine Yu from the Xie mansion. I’ll make her a prostitute on the streets, and you’ll never be able to hold your head up again!"

"Second Brother, I’ll listen, I’ll obey you!" Xie Shiyun’s eyes welled up with tears at the thought of his mother being driven out.

Now, even Mother didn’t like him. If the only person protecting him, Concubine Yu, also left, what would he do?

With tears in his eyes, he wrote the homework assigned by the teacher. Normally, he wrote carefully, stroke by stroke, but with Xie Shiyou watching, he could only scribble like a mess, not even knowing what he was writing…

Xie Shiyou nodded in satisfaction. He only needed to write slightly better than Yun Ge’er. Then, Father and Mother would no longer scold him.

As May arrived, the temperature gradually rose.

Early in the morning, Yun Chu’s forehead was already covered in a thin layer of sweat.

"Just last month, it was as cold as winter. How did it suddenly get so hot?" Tingfeng looked at the sun. "The next half month will probably be all clear skies."

Yun Chu knew that it wouldn’t just be half a month. For the next four or five months, until October, it would only get hotter. Fortunately, there would be occasional heavy rainstorms; otherwise, a drought would surely cause a famine, and the common people would suffer even more.

She asked, "Is there any news?"

Today was the day the county examination results were to be announced. She had sent two young servants to check the list, so the news should have come by now.

As soon as she finished speaking, Tingxue rushed in, breathless. "Madam, the yamen has sent someone to deliver the good news. Young Master has passed the county examination and is truly the top scholar!"

A smile appeared on Yun Chu’s face, though it did not reach her eyes.

So many big and small things had happened in the Xie mansion recently, yet Xie Shian had still managed to secure first place. She had to admit that the boy was a natural-born scholar.

If it weren’t for the fact that Xie Shian would turn against the Yun family in the future, she wouldn’t want to ruin such a pillar of the nation.

She spoke, "Quickly, gather Old Madam, Madam, Master, and all the concubines, young masters, and young ladies. Let’s go together to the front gate to welcome the good news!"

Xie Zhongcheng, who was usually not in the mansion, had already returned to wait for the news. As soon as he heard that the yamen had sent someone to deliver the good news, he was the first to rush forward, quickly making his way to the front gate of the Xie mansion. Xie Jingyu had already brought Xie Shian to the steps of the Xie mansion.

The four yamen runners who came to deliver the news beat drums and gongs, attracting the attention of everyone nearby.

"To pass the county examination at just twelve years old and even become the top scholar, truly impressive for one so young."

"A few years ago, Master Xie was personally selected by His Majesty as the top scholar in the imperial examination. I don’t think Young Master Xie will be any worse. Perhaps in the future, we’ll see a family with two top scholars."

"Master Xie and Madam Xie have raised their son well. With the Yun family as their backing, I believe Young Master Xie will surely achieve the highest honors in the imperial examinations and hold a high position among the officials!"

The onlookers discussed animatedly, their eyes filled with admiration as they looked at Xie Shian.

Xie Shian stood tall and proud. At this moment, he was full of spirit, as if he could see himself ten years in the future, even if he wasn’t the highest-ranking official, he would surely become a high-ranking minister…

Old Madam Xie had each of the four yamen runners given a large red envelope containing a full ten taels of silver, a very generous amount.

Xie Zhongcheng cupped his hands toward the onlookers and said, "The Xie family will choose an auspicious day to host a banquet. If you have time, please come and drink a cup of wine to share in our joy."

The crowd naturally agreed.

After the well-wishers dispersed, the entire Xie family surrounded Xie Shian.

Old Madam Xie patted his head. "An Ge’er, the future of our Xie family now rests on your shoulders."

Xie Zhongcheng spoke, "When your great-grandfather was your age, he wasn’t even a *tongsheng* (a student who had passed the county-level examination). Seeing you become the top scholar in the county examination is like fulfilling your great-grandfather’s dream. You must continue to study hard and strive to become the top scholar in the provincial examination next."

Yuan Shi was overjoyed. "An Ge’er is so promising. Shiyou, you must not fall behind. And neither should Yun Ge’er!"

He Shi was so happy she was moved to tears.

When An Ge’er was three years old, his teacher had said he had great potential in his studies and told her to find him a good teacher.

At that time, An Ge’er had no status and could only attend the most ordinary private school. To get him into a better school, she had repeatedly proposed that An Ge’er be recognized as part of the Xie family. Fortunately, all her schemes had been worth it. An Ge’er had lived up to expectations, and his future was bright.

With tears in her eyes, she looked at Xie Shian, laughing and crying.

Tao Concubine, standing to the side, frowned slightly. While it was a joyous occasion that Young Master had become the top scholar, as a concubine, wasn’t she a little *too* happy?

If it were like Madam, who had no children of her own and treated Young Master like her own son, then her happiness would be understandable.

But she had her own child. While she was happy, she couldn’t help but worry that the adults would pay too much attention to Young Master and neglect her own child…

Why was Concubine He so excited?

Yun Chu, who was in charge of rewarding the servants of the entire mansion, asked, "Old Madam, when should we hold the banquet?"

The Old Madam looked at Xie Jingyu.

"Tomorrow is a day of rest for all officials. It would be the perfect time to host a grand banquet for guests." Xie Jingyu turned to Yun Chu. "I wonder if Madam can prepare everything in time?"

Yun Chu nodded. "Everything has been prepared these past few days. We can host the banquet at any time."

Yuan Shi sighed. "With Chu’er in charge of the mansion’s affairs, we basically don’t have to worry about anything. Pin’er, you should learn from your mother."

Xie Pin quickly lowered her head. "Yes, Grandmother. I will learn well."

Since the banquet was to be held tomorrow, there was a lot to do. Yun Chu had Tingshuang take Xie Pin to handle the remaining tasks.

Tingshuang was a head maid personally trained by her mother, so Yun Chu trusted her completely with the work.

Just as she finished giving her instructions, a servant came to report that Madam Dou sought an audience.

chapters.title: The Illegitimate Sister’s Marriage Discussion
chapters.content:
Yun Chu had someone bring Madam Dou in.

Madam Dou was the wife of a merchant. In this dynasty, merchants had extremely low status and were generally not allowed to enter the residences of official families.

After entering the estate, Madam Dou kept her head lowered, not daring to look around. After passing through several gates, she finally arrived at the flower hall of Shengju.

"Greetings to Madam Xie."

Madam Dou bowed as low as she could, paying her respects.

"Madam Dou is too polite. Please, have a seat. Tingxue, serve tea."

After drinking tea, Madam Dou felt more at ease. She smiled and said, "I came without sending a calling card. I hope I haven’t disturbed Madam Xie."

Yun Chu said gently, "Last time, I entered your Dou family’s estate without permission, and Madam Dou didn’t blame me, did you?"

Madam Dou felt that Madam Xie was very approachable. She got straight to the point. "Last time, Madam Xie mentioned three thousand taels of silver. After discussing it with my husband, we feel that it’s not impossible."

Yun Chu said, "Madam Dou must know that my son has just become the top scholar in the county examination. Our Xie family is currently at the peak of our fortune. I’m afraid that estate might affect our luck, so..."

Madam Dou regretted it extremely.

That day, when Madam Xie mentioned three thousand taels of silver, she should have agreed. Although the money wasn’t much, in a sense, it was a way to cut her losses. Otherwise, holding onto that estate would only bring more losses.

However, since Madam Xie was willing to let her come to the door, she must still have the intention to buy the estate.

She tentatively said, "How about two thousand taels of silver?"

Yun Chu pondered.

Madam Dou became restless.

After a long time, Yun Chu finally spoke, "In business, it’s about mutual agreement. Two thousand taels of silver is clearly a loss for the Dou family. If you regret it in the future, it would be our Xie family’s fault. Let’s settle on three thousand taels. I’ll have someone go with you to the notary office to handle the deed. However, I must ask Madam Dou to keep this quiet."

Madam Dou was overjoyed. Yun Chu had Chen Defu and a person from the Dou family go handle the procedures.

After finishing these matters, Yun Chu took the Xie family’s calling card and personally went to the Yun family to invite her family to the banquet.

"An Ge’er’s future is limitless." Yun Ze sighed. "In the entire capital, there isn’t a second child as outstanding as him."

Lin Shi followed, "After all, this child is not your own. Chu’er has raised him for several years, and he isn’t very close to our Yun family. Although Xie Jingyu is despicable, it’s not An Ge’er’s fault. You should put in more effort. You’ll have to rely on An Ge’er for the second half of your life."

Yun Chu tightly clutched the handkerchief in her hand.

In her past life, her mother, elder brother, and sister-in-law had all advised her like this, telling her to pour her heart and soul into the Xie family’s children. They hoped that the Xie family’s children would support her in her old age.

But the children she had raised with all her heart and soul had ultimately sent her and the Yun family to their doom.

"Last time, I found two families for Ran’er. Mother chose the Dai family. This time, I specially invited Madam Dai and Young Master Dai to the Xie family. Later, Mother can chat with Madam Dai, and I’ll take Ran’er to meet Young Master Dai." Yun Chu smiled. "In the end, it’s up to Ran’er to agree before the marriage can be considered successful."

Yun Ran stood to the side, her small face blushing.

Yun Chu changed the subject. "There’s another matter. A divine doctor has come to the capital and is currently staying in the palace to treat the Empress. I wonder if Mother can help invite the divine doctor out for half a day?"

Lin Shi’s face lit up with joy. "Chu’er, you’ve finally come to your senses. As long as you’re willing to seek treatment, no matter how much effort it takes, I will help you invite the divine doctor."

She dreamed that Yun Chu would have a child of her own.

Yun Chu did not deny it.

Let her mother be happy for now. There was no need to always worry about her.

When she returned to the Xie estate from the Yun family, it was already dark. Yun Chu did not return to Shengju. Instead, she went to the back kitchen to check that all the preparations were in place before returning to her courtyard to eat.

Upon returning to her room and seeing the wood carving on the windowsill, Yun Chu sighed. She hadn’t seen the little guy in a long time and inexplicably missed him.

There was also the little princess who had gone missing that night. She remembered that the Prince of Pingxi had called out "Changsheng." Was her name Chu Changsheng? It was a good name.

Various thoughts filled Yun Chu’s mind as she fell asleep. The next day, before dawn, Tingshuang entered quietly to wake her.

She put on a slightly more formal skirt and blouse, styled her hair in a cloud bun, and inserted a red gold pearl hairpin. She applied a touch of light makeup.

After she was dressed, Xie Bao was the first to come and pay her respects. This was because Yun Chu had ordered her to wake up early. Since the banquet was being prepared in a hurry, there were bound to be some oversights. Waking up early would allow her to address all potential issues.

Xie Bao followed behind Yun Chu. Seeing Yun Chu enter the kitchen, calling all the servants and personally checking on everything, even tasting the ingredients to see if they were fresh...

Xie Bao couldn’t help but feel ashamed.

Last time, when she was in charge of the old madam’s birthday banquet, she had never done such things herself. She had always just ordered the maids and servants to handle everything.

No wonder her mother managed the household so well. There was still so much for her to learn.

After Yun Chu made a round of the courtyard, the sky was already bright. The Xie family members gradually woke up and went to the front courtyard, but there was no sign of Xie Shiwei.

Xie Jingyu frowned. "It seems I was too lenient last time."

"Husband, today is a good day. Don’t be angry." Yun Chu said, "I’ll go wake Shiwei up."

She went to Xie Shiwei’s courtyard and saw Jiu’er standing at the bedroom door. She said, "Go in and wake up the second young master."

Jiu’er lowered her head obediently. "Last night, the second young master drank a lot. When he got up half an hour ago, he said he had a headache. I’m afraid he..."

Yun Chu looked at Jiu’er. "Is this your idea of revenge?"

Jiu’er’s face stiffened. How did the madam know that she had deliberately plied the second young master with alcohol?

She had wanted the second young master to miss the eldest young master’s banquet, provoking the master’s anger so that the second young master would receive another beating.

"Not pain, not itch, better not do it." Yun Chu shook her head. "Today, many dignitaries and nobles will come to the Xie estate. As a legitimate son of the Xie family, you must go out to greet the guests. No matter what method you use, you must wake the second young master within a quarter of an hour."

Jiu’er quickly went in to call someone.

Soon, Xie Shiwei came out dressed in new clothes, though his face was slightly swollen from drinking the night before.

Yun Chu said calmly, "You’re only eight years old, yet you drink and get a hangover. If your father finds out, he will make you kneel in the ancestral hall. Today is your elder brother’s celebration banquet, so we’ll let this matter slide. Pull yourself together and greet the guests properly. Many dignitaries and nobles will bring their young masters. You must accompany them, talk, and play with them. Remember, those are people of high status. Be careful not to offend them."

Jiu’er, standing to the side, furrowed her brows slightly.

She seemed to suddenly understand what the madam meant...

Yun Chu took Xie Shiwei to the front courtyard.

The old madam and Yuan Shi were waiting for the female guests in the back courtyard.

Xie Zhongcheng was in the front courtyard, responsible for receiving the male guests.

Yun Chu and Xie Jingyu, along with their children, stood at the entrance of the Xie estate, respectfully welcoming the guests.

The first to arrive were Lord Yuan, Madam Yuan, and Young Master Yuan. The family of three alighted from their carriage in unison.

"Congratulations, Lord Xie." Lord Yuan approached, cupping his hands. "Today, I have specially brought my son to attend the banquet. I hope he can learn from Young Master Xie. I don’t expect him to become the top scholar, but if he can pass the examination to become a xiucai, it would be a blessing from our Yuan family’s ancestors."

Although being a xiucai was not a particularly remarkable title, it was the first step into the officialdom, making it very important.

Xie Jingyu made a gesture of invitation. "Lord Yuan, please come in. Shi’an, you take Lord Yuan and Young Master Yuan inside."

Yun Chu had Xie Bao take Madam Yuan inside.

After the Yuan family entered, Xie Jingyu quietly ordered a nearby servant, "Keep an eye on this family of three. Report any suspicious movements to me immediately."

Last time, it was the Yuan family who had caused trouble, making the Xie family lose face completely. This time, if the Yuan family dared to act again, he would not show mercy.

chapters.title: Xie Shiwei Causes Trouble
chapters.content:
The guests arrived one after another.

The front and back courtyards gradually became lively.

Before long, the carriage of the Marquis of Xuwu arrived, and Xie Jingyu's expression turned somewhat ugly.

But as a minor fifth-rank official, even if he despised the Qin family, he had to welcome them with a smile: "Marquis, Madam, Young Master, your presence honors our humble home. Please, come in."

Qin Mingheng arrived with Madam Luo and their eldest son. The young master of the marquis's household was about six years old and very fair-skinned.

"I remember that before I was married, I went with my mother to the young master's full-month celebration," Yun Chu said with a smile to Madam Luo. "In the blink of an eye, the young master has grown so much."

Madam Luo's face was warm with a gentle smile: "Back then, I also went with the Marquis to the Yun residence for your wedding banquet."

With this exchange, the two women felt an inexplicable closeness.

Because of Madam Luo's high status, Yun Chu personally led her to the inner courtyard. The women in the inner courtyard quickly stood up to greet her.

Madam Luo was kind-hearted and did not put on airs, so she quickly blended in.

Yun Chu continued to the front gate to welcome more guests.

Around the same time, the Yun family arrived. Since they were relatives by marriage, except for the old general who was too elderly and the generals stationed at the front lines, everyone else came.

Madam Yun, Lin Shi, the eldest young master Yun Ze, his wife Liu Qianqian, their eldest son and daughter, and Yun Chu's three younger half-siblings, all arrived, giving the Xie family great face.

Yun Chu led her family in and deliberately seated Lin Shi next to Madam Dai. The two women chatted happily.

Lord Dai was a fifth-rank civil official in the court. His second son, now nineteen, had passed the imperial examination as a xiucai two years ago. Compared to Xie Shian, he was far behind, but for most people, this was already quite impressive.

For example, the sons of the noble families in the capital either inherited their titles and family businesses or directly participated in the metropolitan examination. Before entering the examination hall, no one knew their true abilities... Those from less prestigious families were different. Passing the xiucai examination proved that one could make a living as a scholar and that the person was hardworking and studious, far better than the average spoiled young master.

Lin Shi was quite satisfied with Dai's second son and also felt that Madam Dai would be a good in-law. Madam Dai was naturally a hundred percent satisfied with the Yun family's daughter. Neither side could find any faults, so the marriage was more or less settled.

Yun Chu walked over: "Jing'er, come with me to fetch some fruit wine for the ladies to taste."

Yun Jing stood up and obediently followed Yun Chu.

She followed Yun Chu to the gate with hanging flowers, the place where the outer and inner courtyards met. There was a long corridor here.

From a distance, they could see Xie Shian leading some young masters and sons in conversation.

Yun Chu softly said: "That one in the green robe, the taller one, is the second young master of the Dai family. What do you think?"

Yun Jing glanced up, then quickly averted her gaze. Her ears turned red to the roots, and she nodded almost imperceptibly.

Yun Chu couldn't help but recall the past when her mother had taken her, hiding behind a screen, to secretly glance at Xie Jingyu.

Back then, Xie Jingyu was truly a dashing young man. She had taken one look and immediately nodded, agreeing to marry into the Xie family. Thus, she became the wife of the Xie family.

Because she had been caught in the rain, she would protect her sister from such things.

The Dai family was the best one she had selected from hundreds of families. If Jing'er married into it, she should have a worry-free life.

After Yun Jing expressed her satisfaction, the next step was for Yun Chu to lead Yun Jing past there, allowing the second young master of the Dai family to catch a glimpse. Only then would the matter be completely settled.

Along the way, Yun Jing's face was extremely red, like a ripe persimmon.

Yun Chu went to the front courtyard to welcome the last group of guests. By this time, it was almost noon, and the banquet officially began.

The men were in the front courtyard, but some of the younger boys, whether seven or eight years old, who were still too young to understand, all stayed in the back courtyard.

Some of the higher-status madames sat in the seats of honor, and Yun Chu and Old Madam Xie personally accompanied them.

Among those madames, some had attended Old Madam Xie's birthday banquet before and had been worried about another incident. But halfway through the banquet, they finally let their guard down. This banquet was indeed well-organized, and compared to the banquets held in their own residences, it was just as good, if not better.

After three rounds of drinks, Madam Luo couldn't help but say: "Master Xie is a zhuangyuan (top scholar), and it seems that Young Master Xie will also become a zhuangyuan. Not to mention the good feng shui of the Xie family, but the most important thing is that the Xie family knows how to educate their children. Madam Xie, could you share how the Xie family usually disciplines their children?"

Yun Chu quickly replied: "Madam overpraises us. They say that children of five or six are so mischievous that even dogs dislike them. I see that the young master is obedient and sensible, which clearly shows Madam's excellent teaching."

"He is just a little troublemaker," Luo shook her head. "Everyone in the household, from top to bottom, is afraid of him. He can even pluck two feathers from a bird as it flies by. Can you imagine how naughty he is? I think in the future, he will be one of the most notorious spoiled brats in the capital!"

"Mother!" The young master of the marquis's household, who was sitting nearby, showed his displeasure on his face when he heard his mother speaking about him like this in front of others.

"Children have thin faces," Old Madam said with a smile. "Wei'er, you are about the same age as the young master. Why don't you take the young master to play?"

Xie Shiwei pursed his lips. The young master was only about six years old, a little brat. He disliked playing with small children the most; they were always sniffling.

He instinctively wanted to refuse, but then he felt Old Madam's cold gaze.

Old Madam wished she could grab his ear and tell him that the person in front of him was the young master of the Marquis of Xuwu. Befriending the young master of the marquis's household would only bring benefits, not harm!

Although Xie Shiwei didn't understand these twists and turns, he knew that if he didn't agree, after the banquet ended, Old Madam would definitely scold him, and then his father would be furious, leaving him in a terrible state.

He quickly stepped forward: "Young Master, I'll take you to the back courtyard. There are many fun places there."

The young master of the marquis's household had long been impatient. He wasn't interested in what the madames and old ladies were talking about and was eager to change places. He immediately followed Xie Shiwei to the back courtyard.

Yun Chu turned her head: "Jiu'er, you follow the second young master and the young master closely. Be careful not to let them fall or get hurt."

Jiu'er lowered her head and quickly followed along.

While the women in the back courtyard were chatting, the banquet in the front courtyard was also coming to an end.

In the front courtyard, there were court officials and some young men. Xie Shian took the young men of similar age to the garden to play a game of pitching arrows into a pot, while Xie Jingyu arranged a tea-tasting and poetry-reciting session for the scholars.

After two rounds, Lord Yuan stood up: "All the poems are about romantic themes like wind, flowers, snow, and moon. It's too common. I heard that Master Xie's residence has a grove of jujube trees. Jujube trees have excellent symbolism. Why don't we go to the jujube garden and compose poems with jujube as the theme?"

Who among the scholars present didn't know that the symbolism of jujube trees was early birth of a noble son? Lord Yuan was mocking the Xie family for not having a true legitimate eldest son.

They were also colleagues and friends of Xie Jingyu, so naturally, they wouldn't respond to this.

At this moment, Qin Mingheng laughed loudly: "I heard that this jujube garden was planted by Madam Xie. It's rare that she didn't just pretend to be cultured. Let's go and take a look."

The highest-ranking person present had spoken, so the others naturally followed.

---

chapters.title: This is Too Much!
chapters.content:
The Xie residence was not large, so the jujube garden was not far away.

Even before approaching, one could see the large patch of jujube trees planted along the courtyard wall. Although they had not been planted for long, they already showed vigorous vitality, with lush branches and leaves rustling in the wind.

Under the jujube trees, a group of children were playing. The older children were playing the arrow-pitching game with Xie Shian in the front courtyard, while the children under seven or eight were playing wildly here.

"A jujube tree with dense green leaves on its branches, a clear sky with a gentle breeze calling the birds," a gentleman couldn't help but recite a poem. "When these jujube trees grow up, the scenery here will be even more unique."

Lord Yuan smiled: "With so many jujube trees planted in the residence, Master Xie and Madam Xie's wishes will surely come true."

Qin Mingheng's expression darkened.

Did that woman still hope to have a child with Xie Jingyu?

Did she know that the two children she had given birth to had been thrown at the door of his Marquis of Xuwu residence by Xie Jingyu?

The two children, not yet dead, were as small as the palm of a hand. On a snowy night with the north wind howling, they were only wrapped in a thin, tattered bed curtain. Their small faces were frozen purple...

If she knew about this, would she hate Xie Jingyu?

No, she would hate him even more for almost sending the children to the underworld.

While Qin Mingheng was lost in thought, he heard his son's voice. He looked up and saw his son having a dispute with the second young master of the Xie family.

The young master of the Marquis of Xuwu stared at the cricket held in Xie Shiwei's hand and angrily said: "I saw this cricket first. It's mine!"

He reached out his hand, ordering Xie Shiwei to hand it over.

"Clearly, I caught it first!" Xie Shiwei humphed. "Who told you to be slow?"

The six-year-old young master of the Marquis of Xuwu was furious: "How dare you defy me! Who gave you the courage? I'll say it again, hand it over!"

He carried the aura unique to the noble families. Xie Shiwei suddenly realized that the other party was the legitimate eldest son of the Marquis of Xuwu, a great figure that even his father couldn't afford to offend.

If he offended the young master of the Marquis of Xuwu, his father would definitely give him a severe scolding.

Realizing this, he looked reluctantly at the cricket in his hand, hesitating whether to hand it over.

"Second Young Master, this cricket was found in the Xie residence, so it belongs to the Xie family," Jiu'er stepped forward and whispered in his ear. "Although the young master of the marquis's household has a higher status, he cannot just take away the Xie family's belongings. What about the Xie family's dignity?"

This remark hit the spot for Xie Shiwei. It was indeed the Xie family's property, and moreover, it was the cricket he had caught. Why should he hand it over?

He held up the cricket: "If the young master wants it, come and take it yourself."

He was taller and held the cricket high up. The young master of the Marquis of Xuwu couldn't reach it at all and pushed Xie Shiwei hard in anger.

Xie Shiwei instinctively pushed back. He was two years older and stronger. With this push, the young master of the Marquis of Xuwu was directly pushed over and let out a miserable cry.

Xie Shiwei looked over and saw that the young master of the Marquis of Xuwu had hit his hand on a stone, and it was bleeding a lot.

He was scared stiff for a moment, then immediately walked over, bent down, and was about to help the other up. At this moment, a large hand suddenly pushed him away from behind.

He was pushed to the ground and looked up to see the enraged Marquis of Xuwu, Qin Mingheng.

"M-Marquis..." Xie Shiwei stammered.

The next moment, Qin Mingheng's boot-clad foot heavily stomped on Xie Shiwei's knee.

Crack.

A crisp sound came from the joint, and Xie Shiwei's face suddenly turned pale, followed by a painful howl.

Back in the inner courtyard.

Yun Chu and Madam Luo of the Marquis of Xuwu were chatting and laughing. Lin Shi and Madam Dai were sitting together, talking about their children. Old Madam Xie and Yuan Shi were also chatting happily with several other madames.

The atmosphere here was harmonious.

At this moment, a servant woman came in with a panicked look on her face: "Madam, something has happened."

From the start of the banquet until now, as it was about to end, Old Madam Xie had been in a good mood because the things she had been worried about had not happened. Just as her heart was about to settle, the servant's words "something has happened" struck like thunder in her chest. She was truly afraid that something as absurd as the last birthday banquet would happen again.

Yun Chu's expression remained calm: "What happened?"

The servant lowered her head: "The young master of the Marquis of Xuwu's hand is bleeding a lot..."

Old Madam Xie's heart settled a bit, and she let out a breath: "Children of five or six are at the mischievous age. It's normal to accidentally injure a finger. Has a doctor been called..."

Madam Luo suddenly stood up, interrupting Old Madam's words: "How could his finger get injured?"

"It was the second young master..." The servant's head was lowered. "The second young master pushed the young master, and he fell on a stone, so his finger started bleeding."

"What?!" Old Madam Xie stood up so suddenly that she knocked over the stool. She held onto the table, speaking one word at a time: "Was it Wei'er who caused the young master to be injured?"

Seeing the servant nod, the old lady's vision began to darken. If it weren't for the servants supporting her, she might have collapsed to the ground immediately.

Last time, that kind of incident had only caused the Xie family to lose face.

But injuring the young master of the Marquis of Xuwu was equivalent to offending the Marquis of Xuwu. The consequences were too terrible to imagine.

Old Madam Xie was so scared that she was about to faint. She looked up and saw Yun Chu's calm face. For some reason, it was as if she had found a pillar of support, and her limbs gradually regained strength.

"Madam, please don't be anxious. Let's go and take a look first," Yun Chu said. "The jujube grove is over there."

Lin Shi felt a heaviness in her chest.

The Marquis of Xuwu had only one wife and no concubines or mistresses in the inner courtyard. Madam Luo had only given birth to this one legitimate son over the years. The couple doted on their only son extremely, treating him as if he were made of glass, afraid he might break, or like a treasure in their mouths, afraid he might melt. But now, this precious treasure had shed blood in the Xie residence. This matter was unlikely to end well.

Lin Shi also followed.

When they arrived at the jujube grove, they heard the doctor coming out of the room to report: "The young master's fingers are not severely injured, but he has lost a lot of blood and needs to rest well for a month... The second young master of the Xie family's leg is somewhat troublesome. Even if it heals, he will walk differently from ordinary people in the future."

Xie Jingyu's body staggered.

He glared at Qin Mingheng with fiery eyes.

The young master of the marquis's household had only scraped his finger and bled a little, yet Qin Mingheng had stomped and broken his son's leg. Wei'er was only eight years old. His future was ruined.

Qin Mingheng coldly looked at him: "A mere illegitimate son of the Xie family, even if raised under the main wife's name to become a legitimate son, is not worthy to be mentioned in the same breath as my young master of the Marquis of Xuwu. Even if his limbs are all broken, it is not enough to appease the anger in my heart. This matter cannot be settled just like that. Master Xie, by indulging your beloved son in bullying the young master of the marquis's household, you have allowed a subordinate to offend a superior, which is a great act of treason. I will ask His Majesty to uphold justice!"

Upon hearing the words "His Majesty," Old Madam Xie could no longer support herself and fainted at the entrance of the courtyard.

Xie Jingyu's fists were tightly clenched.

Although the marquis's household did not have much real power, they were extremely close to the royal family. If Qin Mingheng said a few words to the emperor, it would be enough to cause the Xie family great trouble.

Wei'er's leg being crippled was already a fact. He couldn't let the entire Xie family be dragged into this.

He loosened his fingers and cupped his hands: "It is this official's fault in teaching his son. The Xie family is at fault for injuring the young master. Please, Marquis, be magnanimous..."

Qin Mingheng's face was cold, clearly very dissatisfied with his apologetic attitude.

At this moment, Yun Chu walked in from the doorway and approached Qin Mingheng. She slowly bowed: "Marquis, please calm your anger..."

chapters.title: Listen to Mother
chapters.content:
Yun Chu’s pupils contracted sharply, and her breathing stopped.

"Madam, what’s wrong?" Xie Jingyu felt a flicker of unease at her strange expression.

Yun Chu withdrew her gaze and steadied her voice. "An’ge’s words are not without reason. As for how to handle Weige, my lord and the old madam can discuss it further. I have a headache, so I’ll take my leave first."

With that, she turned and walked out.

Outside, she saw Jiu’er kneeling in the courtyard, looking as if she was awaiting punishment at any moment.

"There’s nothing for you here," Yun Chu said to her. "The second young master is injured and in a bad mood. Don’t go near him for now. My courtyard is short a maid to sweep the floors. You can help me for a couple of days."

Before Jiu’er could respond, Yun Chu hurried away.

This was the side courtyard closest to the jujube tree grove, located at the very back of the Xie residence. Beyond its outer wall lay a small alley in the capital.

After the guests had dispersed, the Xie family servants had all gone to the front courtyard to clean up, leaving this place completely deserted.

"Huh? Didn’t they say the Xie family was hosting a banquet today?" Chu Hongyu peeked over the wall, looking left and right. "Why isn’t there a single person around?"

"S-Small Prince!" A Mao’s voice came from below. "You and the little princess stay put on the wall. This humble one is going to let go!"

Chu Hongyu quickly scrambled up the wall and grabbed his sister’s hand. "Changsheng, hold onto this brick. Just push off with your legs and you’ll be up."

The little girl’s delicate fingers clung to the brick, straining as she tried to climb. Her face turned red from the effort, but she still couldn’t make it up.

"Changsheng, if you can’t get up, we won’t be able to see Mother," Chu Hongyu said, reaching down to help her while calling to the man below, "A Mao, higher! A little higher!"

A Mao’s face twisted in frustration. No matter how much he stretched, his short stature made it impossible.

Fortunately, the little girl made one final effort and finally pulled herself onto the wall.

A Mao let out a long sigh of relief. He exhaled onto his palms, then pressed his feet against the wall and, like a flying cat, leapt up beside them. Seeing no one inside the courtyard, he jumped down and stretched out his arms. "Little Princess, jump down. Don’t be afraid. This humble one will catch you."

This was the first time Chu Changsheng had ever done something like this.

She stood up shakily and looked down, instantly feeling dizzy with fear.

But the moment she thought of her mother living just beyond this wall, that she would see her mother soon, she was filled with courage.

Her long, feather-like lashes fluttered, then she closed her eyes, spread her arms, and jumped, landing safely in A Mao’s embrace. He carefully set her on the ground and looked up. "Small Prince, come down quickly. This humble one thinks I heard voices."

Chu Hongyu nodded. Just as he was about to stand, he spotted two figures rounding the corner. He was about to hide when he realized the person in front was Yun Chu.

A grin split his face, and he opened his mouth to call out to her.

Yun Chu quickly raised her hand, pressing a finger to her lips in a gesture for silence.

The Xie family members were all nearby. If the small prince made any noise and alerted them, it would give the Xie family a chance to cling to the Prince of Pingxi’s household.

"Shh!" Chu Hongyu mimed the same gesture.

Perhaps from excitement, he lost his balance and tumbled forward.

Yun Chu’s heart nearly stopped.

Luckily, A Mao was standing right below the wall and caught him in time.

"Brother Yu, didn’t I tell you last time not to sneak into the Xie residence anymore?" Yun Chu deliberately scolded, though her face was stern. "And now you’ve even brought the little princess to climb the wall with you. What if you’d fallen?"

Chu Hongyu held up his fingers. "My sister dreams about Mother every night. Since Father isn’t here, I brought her to see Mother. Mother, look, this is my sister. Her name is Chu Changsheng."

Before he could finish, the usually timid little girl rolled into Yun Chu’s arms like a snowball.

Yun Chu’s face softened as she lifted her up. "Changsheng, I’ve missed you too, after all these days apart."

Chu Hongyu’s eyes widened in disbelief. "Mother, when have you ever met Changsheng before? How come I didn’t know?"

"She snuck out of the residence a few nights ago, and I happened to run into her." Yun Chu took Chu Hongyu’s other hand. "This isn’t the place to talk. Let’s go back to my courtyard."

Tingshuang had already cleared the servants from this path, so they encountered no one on the way back.

Once they were in the familiar courtyard, Chu Hongyu relaxed even more. He grinned. "Mother, my father received an imperial decree and went to Jizhou on business. He won’t be back for half a month. So for the next half month, my sister and I will stay here with you."

Yun Chu frowned. "Half a month is too long. That won’t work."

"Then how long can we stay?" Chu Hongyu wrapped his arms around her neck. "Mother says how many days, and we’ll stay that many. We’ll listen to you."

The little girl climbed onto her lap and hugged her neck from the other side. Though the two children were small, they pulled with surprising strength, each seemingly determined to have her neck turned toward them. Yun Chu felt her neck being twisted back and forth, almost cramping.

Chu Hongyu was a little annoyed. He was willing to share their mother, but his sister insisted on having her all to herself. He should have known better than to bring her along.

But then he saw the new light in his sister’s dark eyes, and he felt the trip had been worth it.

His sister had been frail since childhood. Even at four years old, she was smaller and weaker than most three-year-olds, and she still couldn’t speak.

The imperial physician said there was nothing wrong with her throat; it was another condition caused by her long-term poor health. She refused to communicate with others, as if she couldn’t see anyone else. In her tiny world, there was only him, her brother. Occasionally, she noticed their father, but only if he happened to say something that struck a chord with her.

This was the first time he had seen her accept someone else so readily.

He loved their mother so much. He just knew his sister would feel the same.

"Just two days," Yun Chu said, fondly embracing both children. "If you stay in the Xie residence, you’ll have to stay in my courtyard. No going out on your own. Can you do that?"

Chu Hongyu answered loudly, "Yes!"

The little girl blinked her big eyes and nodded.

Yun Chu booped both of their noses. "You two turned into little mud monkeys climbing that wall. Go bathe first."

She had to admit, she was impressed. These two had snuck in, and even had A Mao carry a bundle of spare clothes.

She had Tingshuang and Tingxue help Chu Hongyu bathe, while she personally bathed the little girl. But when she removed the girl’s dress, her heart was instantly gripped by an invisible hand.

She knew the girl was thin, but not like this, nothing but bones, with no flesh at all. The only meat on her seemed to be on her face, which was what made her so adorable.

Upon closer inspection, she noticed the girl’s entire body was covered in tiny needle marks.

These marks were very obvious, not like signs of abuse, but rather the lingering traces of frequent acupuncture.

"Changsheng, Changsheng..." she murmured, vaguely understanding why the Prince of Pingxi had given the little princess such a name.

With complicated emotions, she bathed the little girl. Just as she was busy, Tingshuang’s voice came from outside the door: "The master has arrived. He says he has urgent matters to discuss with Madam."

Yun Chu lifted the little girl from the bath, dried her off, and dressed her. Smiling, she said, "I’ll be right back."

The little girl clutched at her sleeve, her big eyes fixed on her, as if afraid she would leave and never return.

"Be good. I’ll be back in a moment."

Only then did the little hands loosen their grip.

---

chapters.title: No Way Out
chapters.content:
Xie Jingyu was waiting in the side hall outside.

After a long while, Yun Chu finally emerged from the inner room.

He stood with his hands behind his back, his voice deep. "I’ve discussed it with the old madam. We’ve decided to send Weige to the manor in the outskirts of the capital. What do you think, Madam?"

"Not a bad idea," Yun Chu replied, lifting her gaze. "Let him suffer a little, and he’ll learn his lesson. When does my lord plan to send Weige away?"

Xie Jingyu spoke deliberately. "Now. Immediately."

Yun Chu asked, "Won’t you wait until Weige has recovered a bit more?"

"Lord Xuanwu is still furious. If the Xie family doesn’t take a stance now, he will hold a grudge forever." Xie Jingyu pressed his lips together. "We’ll have to ask Weige to endure this hardship."

Yun Chu scoffed inwardly.

Xie Jingyu and Xie Shian, father and son were cut from the same cloth. Both were well-read, and both were selfish and heartless.

In her past life, she hadn’t been treated unfairly either. Xie Shian had been able to abandon his own younger brother, so what did it matter that she, with no blood ties, was his legal mother?

"After Weige is sent away, the Xie family will still have to pay a visit to apologize." Xie Jingyu looked at the woman across from him. "Madam, you will come with me."

Since they had decided to bow to the Xuanwu Marquis’ residence, they might as well bow completely. Whether the marquis humiliated or insulted him, cursed or ridiculed him, he would endure it. In a few more years, once An’ge had grown into a great man, the Xie family would reclaim its lost face.

Yun Chu knit her brows slightly.

She had no desire to go with Xie Jingyu to the Xuanwu Marquis’ residence to read their expressions.

As she and Xie Jingyu spoke, two fuzzy little heads popped out from behind the screen in the side hall.

"Changsheng, look at that man. He’s Mother’s husband," Chu Hongyu whispered. "Tell me, what’s so good about him compared to our father? Why did Mother marry him instead of Father?"

Chu Changsheng blinked her innocent big eyes, looking equally confused.

*Pffft, *

A strange sound came from Chu Hongyu’s rear.

Chu Changsheng wrinkled her delicate little nose, then immediately covered it in disgust.

*Pffft. Pffft.*

Two more sounds followed in quick succession.

Xie Jingyu was waiting for Yun Chu’s response when he caught a strange noise from behind the screen. At the same time, a foul odor wafted over.

He frowned. "Smells like spoiled food."

Unconsciously, he began walking toward the screen.

Yun Chu immediately spotted the two small figures moving behind it.

Her head ached. Surely, Hongyu had disobeyed and brought Changsheng out of the inner room.

"My lord!" Yun Chu called out to stop Xie Jingyu.

"And so tomorrow, I will go with you to the Xuanwu Marquis’ residence to apologize. My lord, remember to prepare the gifts for the apology."

Xie Jingyu halted, his gaze falling on Yun Chu. "Thank you, Madam."

Yun Chu only hoped he would leave quickly. "My lord, aren’t you still sending Weige to the manor? It’s getting late. If you delay any longer, you won’t make it in time."

At that, Xie Jingyu finally left.

The moment he was gone, Yun Chu hurried to the screen. She had intended to keep a stern face, but when she saw Chu Hongyu with his knees pressed together, one hand clutching his stomach and the other his rear, stomping his feet in place, his face flushed red, she couldn’t help but laugh. "Come on, Mother will take you to the outhouse."

At the same time, Xie Jingyu led a group of people to Xie Shiwei’s courtyard.

He surveyed the entire room. Ever since Shiwei had been punished a month ago, Yun Chu had ordered all the furnishings removed from this courtyard.

Yun Chu had said that when Heaven was about to place a great responsibility on a person, it would first exhaust their spirit. But even in such sparse conditions, Shiwei had shown no improvement at all.

A few days ago, when Shiwei had mistreated a maid, he should have sent the boy far away. At the very least, he should have locked him in the ancestral hall for a few months. Then, perhaps, today’s disaster could have been avoided.

But it was too late for regrets now.

Xie Jingyu’s expression was grim as he entered the inner room. He looked at Xie Shiwei, who lay pale-faced on the bed. "Shiwei," he said slowly, "you have disappointed me greatly. I have given you chance after chance, yet you have shown no remorse, making mistake after mistake. Today, I am having you sent to the manor in the outskirts to live. You will recover from your injuries there, and more importantly, reflect deeply. I hope that the next time we meet, I can look at you with newfound respect."

Xie Shiwei was still in agony from his broken leg. When he saw his father enter, he had assumed it was out of concern.

But he never expected to hear such words, that his father was sending him away to the manor!

He looked at Xie Shian standing behind Xie Jingyu. "Big Brother!" he cried out. "Please, beg Father for me! Tell him I’ve changed, I really have... This was all an accident. The Xuanwu Marquis’ son tried to take my things first. He pushed me first..."

"Enough!" Xie Jingyu roared. "At this point, you’re still shifting the blame! Do you even know where you went wrong?"

Xie Shian sighed. "Shiwei, Lord Xuanwu said that even if all your limbs were cut off, it wouldn’t ease the hatred in his heart. Sending you to the manor is to spare your life. It’s Father’s last resort. You must understand his good intentions."

Xie Shiwei’s face turned ashen.

His leg was already broken, and yet the Xuanwu Marquis was still unsatisfied; he wanted all his limbs?

If he were sent to the manor in the outskirts, wouldn’t it be even easier for the marquis to take his life?

"Father, I was wrong..." Xie Shiwei rolled off the bed, his voice choked with sobs. "I truly know I was wrong. Please, Father, give me one more chance..."

He Shao wept, "Master, Shiwei is still young. He can still be disciplined..."

"Father, I will change, I promise!" Xie Shiwei sobbed, barely able to breathe. "As long as you don’t send me away, I’ll do anything!"

He was only eight years old. His leg was broken, and now they were sending him far away. This was leaving him with no way to survive...

"Someone!" Xie Jingyu said coldly. "Take the second young master to the carriage."

Two young servants entered, lifting Xie Shiwei between them and carrying him out.

A carriage was waiting in the courtyard. Xie Zhongcheng sat inside, sighing. "Shiwei, from now on, you will live quietly with your grandfather at the manor. The manor isn’t so bad. If you can change your ways, your father will naturally bring you back to the capital."

"No, I don’t want to go!" Xie Shiwei thrashed violently. The moment his leg touched the ground, the pain was so excruciating it felt like his heart was being torn apart. "I don’t want to go to the manor! Father, give me one more chance! Mother, Mother, save me..."

He had completely lost control, turning toward He Shao as he cried out for his mother.

Xie Jingyu’s eyes darkened. The two servants dared not delay any longer. They lifted Xie Shiwei and threw him into the carriage. When he continued to struggle, they tied him up with ropes and gagged his mouth with a cloth.

Tears streamed down He Shao’s face.

She hadn’t even come to terms with the fact that Shiwei had lost a leg, and now she had to endure the pain of separation from her son. Her heart felt as if it had been split open, and she cried until she was on the verge of fainting.

A group of concubines stood not far from the courtyard gate, all wearing puzzled expressions.

Tao Concubine was the first to speak. "Don’t you all think Concubine He seems a little too concerned about the young masters? Last time, when the eldest young master passed the imperial examinations, she was happier than anyone. Now that the second young master is being sent away, she’s more heartbroken than anyone. Is it because she’s so devoted to the master that she’s extended her love to his sons as well?"

Ling Yu and Jiang Concubine said nothing. They merely tightened their grip on their children’s hands, silently warning them not to cause any trouble...

chapters.title: A Complete Family
chapters.content:
Xie Jingyu waited in the side hall outside.

After a long while, Yun Chu finally emerged from the inner room.

He stood with his hands clasped behind his back, his voice deep as he said, "I have discussed it with the old madam. We have decided to send Weige to the manor in the outskirts of the capital. What do you think, Madam?"

Yun Chu raised her gaze. "It is indeed a good place. Let him suffer a little, and he will learn his lesson. When does my lord plan to send Weige away?"

Xie Jingyu spoke slowly, word by word: "Now. Immediately."

Yun Chu asked, "Shouldn’t we wait until Weige has recovered a bit more from his illness?"

"The Marquis of Xuanwu is in a rage right now. If the Xie family does not take a stance at this moment, the Marquis will hold a deep grudge against us." Xie Jingyu pressed his lips together. "We will have to trouble Weige for a while."

Yun Chu let out a cold laugh in her heart.

Xie Jingyu and Xie Shian, father and son, were truly cut from the same cloth, both well-read, both selfish and heartless.

In her past life, she had no reason to feel wronged either. Xie Shian could abandon his own younger brother, so what about her, who had no blood relation to him?

"After Weige is sent away, the Xie residence must still pay a visit to apologize." Xie Jingyu looked at the woman across from him. "Madam, you will go with me."

Since they had already decided to bow to the Marquis of Xuanwu, they might as well bow completely. No matter how the Marquis humiliated or insulted him, he would endure it. In a few more years, once An’ge had grown up, the Xie family would reclaim their lost face.

Yun Chu slightly furrowed her brows.

She certainly did not want to go with Xie Jingyu to the Marquis of Xuanwu’s residence to read others’ faces.

As she spoke with Xie Jingyu, two fluffy little heads popped out from behind the screen in the side hall.

"Changsheng, look at that man. He is Mother’s husband," Chu Hongyu whispered, lowering his voice. "Tell me, what is better about this man compared to our father? Why did Mother not marry Father but instead married him?"

Chu Changsheng blinked his innocent, confused eyes, also expressing incomprehension.

*Plop, *

A strange sound came from Chu Hongyu’s rear.

Chu Changsheng wrinkled his delicate little nose, then immediately covered it with a look of disgust.

*Plop, plop, *

Two more sounds followed in succession.

Xie Jingyu was waiting for Yun Chu’s reply when he heard some movement behind the screen, accompanied by a strange smell.

His brow furrowed. "It smells like spoiled food."

He unconsciously walked toward the screen.

Yun Chu caught sight of the two little figures swaying behind the screen at a glance.

Her head ached. It must be that Yu’ge had disobeyed and brought Changsheng out from the inner room.

"My lord!" Yun Chu called out to stop Xie Jingyu.

"Then tomorrow, I will go with you to the Marquis of Xuanwu’s residence to apologize. My lord, remember to prepare the gifts for the apology."

Xie Jingyu stopped in his tracks, his gaze falling on Yun Chu. "Thank you, Madam."

Yun Chu only hoped he would leave quickly. "My lord, aren’t you going to send Weige to the manor? It’s getting late; if you delay any longer, it will be too late."

Hearing this, Xie Jingyu finally left.

As soon as he was gone, Yun Chu quickly walked to the screen. She had intended to put on a stern face, but she saw Chu Hongyu with his knees pressed together, one hand covering his stomach and the other his bottom, stomping his feet in place, his entire face flushed red from holding it in.

She couldn’t help but laugh. "Come on, Mother will take you to the restroom."

At the same time, Xie Jingyu led people to the courtyard where Xie Shiwei resided.

He looked around the entire room. Ever since Shiwei had made a mistake and was punished with family discipline a month ago, all the belongings in this courtyard had been moved out by Yun Chu.

Yun Chu had said that when Heaven is about to place a great responsibility on a person, it must first torment their mind. But even though the living conditions were already quite harsh, Shiwei had still shown no improvement.

A few days ago, when Shiwei had mistreated a maid, he should have sent Shiwei far away, or at the very least, locked him up in the ancestral hall for a few months. Then, today’s disaster might not have happened.

But it was too late to say these things now.

Xie Jingyu’s expression was grim. He walked into the inner room and looked at Xie Shiwei, who was lying on the bed, pale-faced. He spoke slowly, word by word: "Shiwei, you have greatly disappointed me. I have given you chance after chance, but you have not shown the slightest remorse, making mistake after mistake. Today, I will have someone take you to the manor in the outskirts of the capital to live. You will recover from your illness there and also reflect deeply. I hope that the next time we meet, I can look at you with new respect."

Xie Shiwei was still in pain from his broken leg. Seeing Xie Jingyu approach, he thought his father had come to check on him out of concern.

But he never expected to hear such words, that his father was actually going to send him to live at the manor!

He looked at Xie Shian, who was standing behind Xie Jingyu, and cried out in shock: "Elder Brother, quickly plead with Father for me! Tell Father I’ve changed, I really have... This incident was just an accident. It was the Marquis of Xuanwu’s son who first tried to snatch my things, and he was the one who pushed me first..."

"Enough!" Xie Jingyu roared. "At this point, you are still shifting the blame and do not know where you went wrong!"

Xie Shian sighed. "Shiwei, the Marquis of Xuanwu said that even if your arm were cut off, it would not be enough to appease his anger. Sending you to the manor is to save your life. It is something Father has to do. You must understand Father’s hardships."

Xie Shiwei’s face turned pale with fear.

His leg was already broken, yet the Marquis of Xuanwu was still not satisfied and wanted to cut off his arm...

If he were sent to the manor in the outskirts of the capital, wouldn’t it be even easier for the Marquis of Xuanwu to take his life?

"Father, I was wrong..." Xie Shiwei rolled off the bed. "I really know I was wrong. Please, Father, give me one more chance..."

He Shao wept, saying, "Master, Weige is still young. He can still be disciplined..."

"Father, I will definitely change!" Xie Shiwei sobbed, out of breath. "As long as Father doesn’t send me away, I will do anything."

He was only an eight-year-old child, and his leg was already broken. Sending him far away was like giving him no chance to live...

"Someone!" Xie Jingyu said coldly. "Take the Second Young Master to the carriage."

Two young servants entered, lifting Xie Shiwei from both sides and carrying him out.

A carriage was waiting in the courtyard. Xie Zhongcheng was already sitting inside. He sighed and said, "Weige, from now on, you will obediently live with your grandfather at the manor. The manor isn’t so bad. Slowly change your mindset, and your father will naturally bring you back to the capital."

"No, I don’t want to!" Xie Shiwei struggled violently. The moment his leg touched the ground, the pain was so excruciating that he screamed, "I don’t want to go to the manor. Father, give me one more chance. Mother, Mother, save me..."

He completely lost control, looking toward He Shao’s direction and crying out, "Mother!"

Xie Jingyu’s eyes darkened. The two servants dared not delay any longer. They lifted Xie Shiwei and threw him into the carriage. Seeing him struggle violently, they took out a rope to tie him up and stuffed a piece of cloth into his mouth.

He Shao’s tears streamed down.

She hadn’t even accepted the fact that Weige had lost a leg, and now she had to endure the pain of separation from her son. Her heart felt as if it had been split open, and she cried until she was on the verge of fainting.

Several concubines stood not far from the courtyard gate, all showing puzzled expressions.

Tao Concubine was the first to speak: "Don’t you think that Concubine He seems to care a little too much about the young masters? Last time, when the Eldest Young Master passed the imperial examination, she was happier than anyone. This time, with the Second Young Master being sent away, she is more distressed than anyone. Is it because she is deeply in love with the Master, and thus extends that love to his sons?"

Lingyu and Jiang Concubine remained silent, only tightly holding their children’s hands, secretly instructing them not to cause trouble...

---

chapters.title: Prince Pingxi Searches the Residence
chapters.content:
Yun Chu entered the flower hall with Tingyu.

Looking at the pastries on the table, she said, "I remember the mung bean cakes you make are softer than usual. If you have time, make some and send them to me."

Tingyu’s face lit up with a smile. "Yes, Madam. This servant will go make them right now."

As long as Madam was willing to use her, she would eventually be able to return to Madam’s side, just like before. Then, who in the residence would dare to give her any trouble?

Yun Chu nodded. Tingyu was about to leave when a servant woman rushed in, looking anxious: "Madam, Prince Pingxi has brought many people and come to search the Xie residence."

Yun Chu’s fingers, which were holding a teacup, suddenly stiffened.

The people from Prince Pingxi’s residence had arrived so quickly, which was somewhat unexpected. Fortunately, Qiutong and Tingshuang had already left with the two children.

Tingyu looked confused. "Even though Prince Pingxi holds a high position and great power, he doesn’t have the authority to search a private residence, does he? Unless there are thieves on the run, and that’s why Prince Pingxi..."

"It’s Prince Pingxi’s young son and young lady who have gone missing," the servant woman hurriedly explained. "The Master has already gone to the front gate to welcome Prince Pingxi. He specially sent this servant to inform Madam so that the concubines and young ladies in the residence can avoid him."

Yun Chu nodded and immediately ordered someone to notify the women of the household.

Just as she gave the order, she heard many voices. It turned out that Prince Pingxi’s people had already searched their way to the back courtyard.

In the entire capital, only Prince Pingxi would dare to do such a thing.

The Grand Prince was the Crown Prince and needed the support of the people. He would never randomly search private residences and risk being impeached by the officials.

The other princes lacked the power and influence, so none of them would dare to do such a thing.

Seeing Xie Jingyu accompanying Prince Pingxi as they drew nearer, Yun Chu, as the mistress of the household, naturally could not avoid them like the concubines.

She stood up and went to greet them. "Greetings, Your Highness."

Chu Yi’s gaze fell on Yun Chu.

For some reason, he thought of that night when she had been holding Changsheng.

In the moonlight, her skin had been as white as porcelain. That night, in a daze, he had felt that her beautiful eyes resembled Changsheng’s.

Now, in the daylight, he could see even more clearly. Not only were their eyes alike, but even the shape of their lips seemed to have been carved from the same mold.

He paused for a moment before speaking. "Madam Xie, forgive the intrusion."

At this moment, the four guards who had searched Shengju’s quarters came out and shook their heads at Prince Pingxi.

He slightly narrowed his eyes.

Two hours ago, just as he was about to leave for Jizhou, the Crown Prince had suddenly fallen ill. The Emperor had sent successive imperial edicts summoning him back. After returning to his residence, he had been about to take his eldest son, Yu’ge, to the Eastern Palace to visit the Crown Prince when he discovered that Yu’ge had gone missing, and so had Changsheng.

He immediately gathered his people and began a city-wide search.

The first residence they went to was the Grand Princess’s residence, because Yu’ge was close to the Grand Princess.

The second place they came to was the Xie residence. Perhaps it was because that night, Changsheng had been reluctant to part with Madam Xie. He vaguely felt that the two children might have come here.

But they had not found them.

"Lord Xie, Madam Xie, sorry for the disturbance."

Chu Yi turned to leave.

Just at that moment, a child’s voice rang out: "There’s a shoe over there!"

Yun Chu turned her head and saw Xie Shiyun, who had been held by Tingyu all along, suddenly dash forward and point at the flower bushes.

Following Xie Shiyun’s finger, she looked over, and her breath suddenly caught in her throat. It was Yu’ge’s brocade boot.

Chu Yi also stopped in his tracks, looking at the shoe. Busy with official duties, he naturally did not personally dress his children, but the shoe looked somewhat familiar to him.

"That’s not my shoe," Xie Shiyun’s childish voice rang out. "Whose shoe is this, left here?"

Tingyu immediately noticed the change in Yun Chu’s expression. She quickly pulled her son back.

Xie Shiyun pursed his lips tightly.

He had already said that there were other children in his mother’s courtyard, which was why his mother no longer liked him. But his mother had not believed him.

Now, he had finally found evidence. Since Prince Pingxi was here, he could use Prince Pingxi’s people to find the children in his mother’s courtyard.

Tingyu covered her son’s mouth, her peripheral vision sweeping over the shoe.

It was indeed not Shiyun’s shoe, but it was clearly the size of a three- or four-year-old child. In the entire residence, the only boy of that age was Shiyun.

This proved that there were indeed other children in Madam’s courtyard.

Was Madam really going to adopt other children?

Tingyu’s emotions were extremely complicated.

Yun Chu’s expression only changed slightly before returning to normal. She quickly walked over and picked up the small shoe from the flower bush. "Yesterday, I had the maids in the courtyard looking everywhere for a shoe. So it was here. It’s for my nephew from my maiden home. His birthday is coming up, so I specially had someone make it in the most fashionable style in the capital."

Chu Yi nodded. "We have troubled you. This prince takes his leave."

He left quickly with his guards.

Just then, Yun Chu saw Qiutong and Tingshuang entering from outside. The two of them nodded to her, and her suspended heart finally settled back into her stomach.

Chu Yi reached the gate and was about to go to the next place to search when a servant came to report: "Your Highness, the young master and young lady have been found. They had sneaked out of the residence to wander the streets, with Guard Mao following them."

As soon as he finished speaking, the two young masters were carried over by two wet nurses.

The two little ones knew they had done something wrong. They clung tightly to the wet nurses’ necks, burying their heads and not making a sound.

Chu Yi looked at Chu Hongyu, his gaze involuntarily moving downward to his feet. Then, his eyes narrowed. "Where are your shoes?"

Chu Hongyu rubbed his little feet together. "I... I don’t know where I lost them."

"Oh?" A cold smile appeared on Chu Yi’s lips. "Then tell me, how did your shoe end up at the Xie residence?"

Chu Hongyu’s little face suddenly paled. He instinctively denied it. "No, I didn’t go to the Xie residence..."

Chu Yi’s voice grew colder. "I never said you went to the Xie residence. You’re incriminating yourself. You—"

Before he could finish his sentence, the little girl, who had been lying in the wet nurse’s arms, suddenly came to her senses. She opened her watery, large eyes and stretched out her two short arms toward him.

At that moment, Chu Yi’s heart softened instantly.

For the first two years of her life, Changsheng had spent most of her time in a daze. After she turned two, she finally improved, but she had to undergo acupuncture frequently. Every time she had acupuncture, she would cry bitterly, and she became increasingly resistant to him, the father who forced her to receive treatment.

By the time she turned three, her illness had finally improved, but her eyes had lost their light.

She would not take the initiative to look at him, her father. She would not let him, her father, hold her. She was unwilling to spend even a moment with him...

This was the first time in history that she had taken the initiative to reach out to him for a hug.

Chu Yi let Chu Hongyu off and took his daughter into his arms.

Chu Hongyu let out a long sigh of relief.

He was somewhat surprised.

In the past, even if he had been scolded by his father until he was covered in blood, his sister would not have reacted at all if she heard it.

But now, his sister had actually taken the initiative to help him out of trouble.

After spending some time with their mother, his sister seemed a little different.

chapters.title: Keep This Secret for Me
chapters.content:
The sky had already darkened.

Yun Chu's gaze fell on Xie Shiyou. "Yun'er, your mother asks you, whose shoe do you think this is in my courtyard?"

Her voice was calm, without any fluctuation, but Tingyu could sense the hidden anger in the madam's tone.

She quickly spoke up, "Madam, Yun'er, he—"

"I am asking Yun'er. Aunt Tingyu, please step aside for now." Yun Chu's voice was very light. "Yun'er, you know that your mother dislikes children who lie the most."

Tingyu was so anxious she could barely breathe.

But Tingshuang stood beside her, coldly staring at her, so she didn't dare make any move.

Xie Shiyou stood in front of Yun Chu with his head lowered.

A month ago, every time he came to Yusheng Courtyard, he would be held on his mother's lap. Back then, as long as he made her happy, she would give him many nice things.

But lately, his mother had grown increasingly cold toward him.

He hadn't done anything wrong, so why had he lost his mother's favor?

He felt wronged, truly wronged.

At the thought, tears welled up in Xie Shiyou's eyes, rolling down his cheeks. He lifted his head and sobbed, "Mother, have you taken in another child? Is that why you don't want Yun'er anymore?"

Yun Chu steadied her mind and asked, "What do you mean by taking in another child?"

"Mother, don't lie to me. I saw it all." Xie Shiyou wailed. "I saw a boy about my age in your courtyard. You held him and smiled at him. Will he be your son now? Will you stop caring for me?"

Yun Chu's fingers tightened.

As expected, she had guessed that Yun'er must know something. Otherwise, with his timid nature, he would never have mentioned the shoe in front of Prince Pingxi.

She turned to Tingyu. "Did Aunt Tingyu see it too?"

Tingyu's fingers twisted together tightly.

She bit the tip of her tongue and said, "In reply to Madam, this concubine saw nothing. Yun'er must have seen wrong. This concubine will make sure Yun'er doesn't say anything reckless in front of the old madam and the master."

Yun Chu lowered her gaze.

Her courtyard was no longer safe. She absolutely could not let those two children come to the Xie residence again.

She took a sip of tea and sighed. "Yun'er did not see wrong. There is indeed a child from the Yun family in my courtyard, prepared to be adopted under my name as my legitimate son. But I have always felt it was improper, so I haven't mentioned this to the old madam and the master. Aunt Tingyu, until I make a decision, you must keep this secret for me."

Tingyu could hardly believe it.

The truth was indeed as she had suspected. Madam really intended to adopt a child with Yun family blood.

This was truly improper and against propriety!

But once the Yun family decided, the Xie family would have no choice but to accept. No matter how improper it was, it would become a fact.

She clenched her handkerchief tightly. "This concubine is forever Madam's. I will keep this secret for you."

Yun Chu looked at her quietly.

She had given her the opportunity. It was up to Tingyu to cherish it.

Later, someone from outside reported that Prince Pingxi had taken the young heir into the palace. Yun Chu knew that this matter was finally over.

The next morning, as soon as she woke up, Yun Chu felt a wave of heat.

The servants of the residence came as usual to pay their respects. The absence of Xie Shiwei seemed to change nothing.

Yun Chu assigned the tasks of the Xie residence and continued to study the layout and facilities of the hot spring villa. After the hour of Chen, Xie Jingyu returned from court. She changed her clothes and went to the front courtyard.

Xie Jingyu had already changed out of his court robes and was holding a gift box in apology. "This is a fine ink stone. Do you think it will do, Madam?"

Yun Chu said, "The Marquis of Xuanyu's residence lacks nothing. What he wants is an attitude."

Xie Jingyu agreed.

The husband and wife got into the carriage and sat facing each other, very close.

Yun Chu slightly turned her head. She lifted the carriage curtain a little and looked at the bustling street outside.

Xie Jingyu looked at her fair profile. For some reason, he felt that Yun Chu seemed to be drifting further and further away from him, like a cloud on the horizon, visible but untouchable.

If she still had even the slightest expectation of him, he would be willing to try to forget the night she had lost her virtue.

But the light in her eyes when she looked at him was already gone. The affection between them as husband and wife had, at some point, become thinner than paper.

He knew the price of bringing her to the Marquis of Xuanyu's residence, yet he had still brought her.

"Madam."

Xie Jingyu's voice was tight.

He couldn't help but call out.

Yun Chu let down the curtain and turned back. "Husband?"

"All these years, have you ever blamed me?"

Hearing this question, Yun Chu almost laughed.

In her past life, of course she had blamed him, resented him, hated him. But so what?

In the face of family blood feuds, what did these things matter?

"Husband, what are you talking about?" Yun Chu said gently. "I am the wife of the Xie family. The honor and disgrace of the Xie family are more important than my life. Coming to the Marquis of Xuanyu's to apologize is my duty. How could I blame you?"

Xie Jingyu's voice was hoarse. "Madam, you know that's not what I'm asking."

Yun Chu lowered her gaze. "It is also my duty to bear children for the Xie family. Since I am unable to do so, it is only natural that you do not come to my room. I do not harbor any resentment."

"I want to make up for my mistakes." Xie Jingyu looked at her eyelids. "Tonight, I will come to Yusheng Courtyard..."

Yun Chu's fingers tightened. Without lifting her head, she said, "Husband, my body is somewhat indisposed."

Xie Jingyu's expression gradually faded.

Whether she was truly indisposed or not, he could see that she did not expect him to come to Yusheng Courtyard at all.

In that case, there was nothing to feel guilty about in bringing her to the Marquis of Xuanyu's residence.

The carriage traveled smoothly to the gate of the Marquis of Xuanyu's residence.

After getting out of the carriage, Xie Jingyu presented his calling card. The guard at the gate took the card and went in to report.

Qin Mingheng was in the courtyard playing with a dog. He threw a flying disc, and the dog leaped up to catch it, then wagged its tail as it came back.

"Marquis, Lord Xie requests an audience."

Qin Mingheng glanced at the calling card and sneered. "Let him wait outside."

He had attended the Xie family's matriarch's birthday banquet because he had heard that Yun Chu was seriously ill and had taken the opportunity to see her.

As for Xie Shian passing the imperial examination as a Xiucai, it was because Yun Chu had invited him, and he had naturally given her this face.

He had always looked down on Xie Jingyu as a despicable and shameless man.

Qin Mingheng continued playing with the dog.

At this moment, he heard two young servants nearby whispering, "Lord Xie has offended our marquis. He will have no good days ahead."

"The eldest daughter of the Yun family was once the most famous in the capital. I don't know why she married Lord Xie. The legitimate daughter of a first-rank family now has to accompany him to the marquis's residence to apologize. How pitiful."

Qin Mingheng's movements suddenly stopped. He asked, "Madam Xie is also here? Why didn't you say so earlier?"

It was so hot, and she had been standing outside in the sun for so long. Her fair and tender skin couldn't withstand such exposure.

He immediately said, "Let them in."

The young servant hurried toward the gate.

---

chapters.title: Request the Marquis to Clarify
chapters.content:
The sun in May was indeed getting fiercer.

Just like in Yun Chu's past life, April was still chilly, but as soon as May arrived, the temperature soared, making people dizzy with heat.

They had been standing for less than a quarter of an hour when a young servant ran out and said, "Lord Xie, Madam Xie, please follow me inside."

Yun Chu had thought that the Marquis of Xuanyu would deliberately make things difficult for Xie Jingyu, but she didn't expect him to let them in so quickly.

This was the first time in both her lifetimes that she had entered the Marquis of Xuanyu's residence.

Pavilions, water features, carved beams, and painted rafters; it was clear that the Qin family ancestors had been people of great taste.

The young servant led them into the garden. It was summer, and the flowers were in full bloom, with butterflies fluttering everywhere. As soon as they entered, a dog barked.

A huge dog as tall as a person rushed out from the side, barking continuously at Xie Jingyu. Xie Jingyu, a scholar, had never seen such a scene and was so frightened that he kept retreating.

Yun Chu stood still. The dog had a leash around its neck and couldn't reach them.

"Madam Xie truly has courage!" Qin Mingheng walked out. "Lord Xie, a grown man, is not as brave as a woman. Tsk, tsk."

Xie Jingyu's face darkened.

He bowed his head and cupped his hands. "Marquis, this official and Madam have come to plead for forgiveness. Yesterday, you honored the Xie family by bringing the young heir to drink with us. But this official has failed in teaching his son, causing the young heir to be injured. My son's leg is ruined for life, and I have sent him to the manor to reflect. He has received the punishment he deserves. I beg the marquis to be magnanimous and give this official a chance to atone."

Yun Chu took the ink stone from Tingshuang and presented it with both hands. "This is an extremely rare pine flower ink stone. I beg the marquis to accept it."

Qin Mingheng disliked reading and didn't care for pine flower ink stones, but this was an ink stone presented by Yun Chu herself.

He walked over, took the ink stone, and examined it. Then he held it in his hand, playing with it, and glanced at Xie Jingyu. "Lord Xie, you don't think that just because you brought Madam to apologize, I will let this matter go, do you?"

Xie Jingyu's fingers tightened secretly. "I beg the marquis to clarify."

"Five years ago, Lord Xie came to my door, asking for an extremely rare divine medicine." Qin Mingheng's lips curled into a smile. "Does Lord Xie still remember what price he paid at that time?"

Xie Jingyu's heart sank heavily.

Five years ago, on the eve of his wedding to Yun Chu, his mother, Lady Yuan, suddenly worsened. She coughed up blood continuously and spent most of her time in a coma.
